items.statement: Cash and equivalents of INR 1,700 crores as of June 2024; evaluating inorganic acquisition opportunities in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; no promoter exit intention
items.quote: currently, our cash and cash equivalents as mentioned in our earnings presentation, it's around INR 1,700 crores. And as of now, we have not yet decided it how do we deploy it? We are still looking at a lot of inorganic opportunities

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 1,041 crores as of June 2024 vs net debt of INR 565 crores a year ago
items.quote: Aster India, net cash stands at INR 1,041 crores as on 30th June, compared to net debt of INR 565 crores as on 30th June 2023

items.statement: Mature hospitals (6+ years) delivered 23% EBITDA margin and 30% ROCE in Q1 FY25; core hospital segment at 21% EBITDA margin
items.quote: our mature hospitals (with more than 6 years in operation) contributing to almost 73% of our hospital segment revenue, delivered our operating EBITDA margin of 23% in Q1 FY25, with the ROC E standing at 30%

items.statement: O&M hospital EBITDA margin target of 15-20% (currently 11-12%); ROCE accretive at 15-20%
items.quote: we are expecting in a range of 15 %, in that around that range, 15% – 18%, or if you can take it to 20%, well and good. But at present, we are aiming to take it, some of the hospitals are at around 11% now, 11%- 12%

items.statement: Kerala cluster (55% of hospital revenue) grew 14% YoY revenue, 30% YoY EBITDA; ALOS reduced to 3.1 days; ARPOB at INR 42,000 (+12% YoY)
items.quote: The Kerala cluster delivered operating EBITDA margins of 22.7% aided by reduction in ALOS to 3.1 days and price growth. The APROB of Kerala cluster also witnessed an optimum growth of 12% YoY at INR 42,000 in Q1 FY25

items.statement: Karnataka/Maharashtra cluster (34% of hospital revenue) grew 38% YoY revenue, 55% YoY EBITDA; occupancy improved to 62% from 55% YoY
items.quote: The revenue of the cluster grew by 38% YoY and operating EBITDA grew by 55% YoY in Q1 FY25 while delivering an operating EBITDA margin of 21.2%. With the scaling performance of a new Whitefield Hospital at Bangalore location, the cluster witnessed a notable improvement in occupancy levels, rising to 62% in Q1 FY25 from 55% in Q1 FY24

items.statement: Price increases of 3-3.5% targeted annually; spread across geographies and departments based on market position and case mix.
items.quote: Around three, three and half percentage is something which we always look for price increase growth.

items.statement: ARPOB expected to grow 7-8% CAGR over next 3-4 years driven by case mix change and non-metro pricing headroom.
items.quote: We see that still in the future, I'm talking about medium term, between three to four years, we should be really able to grow at least 7 to 8 percentage.

items.statement: Kerala cluster EBITDA margin can mature from 22.7% to 25% via brownfield expansion and manpower optimization.
items.quote: We see that with the current EBITDA margin of 22.7%, it can really mature at 25% so that is something which is possible for Kerala cluster.

items.statement: Karnataka-Maharashtra cluster EBITDA margin can reach near 30% as Whitefield matures and occupancy improves.
items.quote: If you are something at INR 70K specifically in Karnataka, Maharashtra, you can look at my EBITDA margin something like near 30%.

items.statement: Andhra-Telangana cluster target mid-teens EBITDA margin initially, eventually closer to 20%.
items.quote: The target is to take the EBITDA margins to the mid-teen and eventually all our efforts is to see if we can take it beyond 20%, or close to our, not beyond, at this point, closer to 20% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Capex requirement ~INR 1,000 crore for 1,700 bed expansion; greenfield non-metro INR 1-1.4 crore/bed, brownfield/leased INR 60-75 lakh/bed.
items.quote: The CAPEX requirement that we have is nearly INR 1000 crore for all these 1700 beds.

items.statement: No immediate equity raise needed; cash from GCC sale and operating cash flows sufficient for capex and M&A; dilution only if share swap for platform merger.
items.quote: we do not need immediate further funding for our investment plans. So basically, any thought on dilution, we are definitely not looking at unless dilution is happening naturally as Alisha was highlighting, you know, if ther e are some share swap opportunities

items.statement: Whistleblower complaint under investigation; relates to undisclosed related party transactions and conflicted business activities; financial impact not significant.
items.quote: So, that is still under investigation actually, so nothing is in finalized actually, once we get the investigation report, only the board will take appropriate decisions.

items.statement: Strong super-specialty growth in Kerala: oncology +31%, cardiology +26%, gastro/liver transplant +21-22%; high-end cases rising.
items.quote: So almost a 31% oncology growth we have, and specifically th e cardiology department has grown by 26%. Gastro, right, basically where we do liver transplant, that has grown by more than 21, 22

items.statement: Shift to daycare surgeries and single-room upgrades driving ARPOB growth; insurance penetration improving affordability for quaternary care.
items.quote: most of the tertiary, quaternary care work is migrating towards daycare activity. That sense it puts less pressure on the system in terms of manpower, equipment and other resources required to sup port this

items.statement: Promoter pledge reduction targeted by end of current financial year; overseas loan structure makes pledge appear higher than required.
items.quote: We are hoping towards the close of this year. So, Damayanti, I think our efforts are towards reducing the pledge definitely. There is a goal towards kind of reducing it towards the close of the year.

items.statement: Brownfield expansions at Medcity (80% occupancy, +100 beds) and Kannur (95% occupancy, +100 beds) to be margin-accretive.
items.quote: Aster Medcity is where I have 80% occupancy, near 80% occupancy, with a 750 bed hospital, I'm adding 100 beds. So and also in Kannur, where I'm 95% occupancy, I'm adding another 100 beds.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Kerala ~55%, Karnataka-Maharashtra ~38%, Andhra-Telangana ~11%; Karnataka share may exceed 40% in future.
items.quote: Kerala's 55% and Karnataka and Maharashtra is around 35%, 38% revenue contribution and 11% is the Andhra and Telangana.

items.statement: Management aims to sustain current gross margins and expects EBITDA margin improvement to follow as investments gain leverage
items.quote: My take right now, would be, say, let's sustain these gross margins and then take the next leap forward in sometime.

items.statement: No major greenfield capex planned beyond Hyderabad plant; only regular maintenance and NPD capex expected
items.quote: Our large capex was on Hyderabad plant, which we've done. Our purpose is to now leverage that. As of now the regular capex of NPDs and expansions and capacity improvements and other things that we do, any large capex as of now, not yet.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 249 bps YoY to 33.1% driven by price increases, mix improvement and cost savings
items.quote: Gross margins expanded by 249 basis points year-on-year, and 237 basis points quarter-on-quarter sequentially, and stands at 33.1%, driven by a combination of price increase, mix and cost savings.

items.statement: Implemented two price hikes in fans category totaling 3-3.5% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We've done price increase in our fans category in two tranches in quarte r 1. One was early April and the other one was in June, largely in the ball park tune of about 3% to 3.5% is what we passed on to the consumers

items.statement: ECD segment grew 5.8% YoY in Q1 but 14.5% over Jan-Jun period; fans grew high-teens over Jan-Jun
items.quote: Our mark-to-market performance is better. For this period of January to June, we've grown at about 14.5% in ECD and high -teens in fans.

items.statement: Lighting business grew 10.2% with high-teens volume growth in consumer lighting and deep double-digit B2B growth
items.quote: Overall, our Lighting and Switchgear business has grown by 10.2%.

items.statement: Export degrowth due to geopolitical issues in African markets with high dependency on one country
items.quote: We degrew in exports because we were slightly dependent on one African country where there have been geopolitical situations.

items.statement: Large size inquiries and tenders in lighting B2B segment have started regenerating post-elections
items.quote: Large size inquiries and tenders have started regenerating post -elections.

items.statement: Hyderabad Industry 4.0 plant commenced commercial production; will take couple more months to stabilize operations
items.quote: We've initiated commercial production at our greenfield Hyderabad plant designed as an Industry 4.0 facility. This plant would deliver superior products at competitive costs and offer proximity to South and Western India markets. It will take a couple of more months to stabilize the operations.

items.statement: Spark Sanchay program delivering ~2% annualized cost reduction; McKinsey costs to cease from Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our Spark Sanchay program aimed at driving cost leadership is deeply ingrained in the organization, consistently delivering approximately 2% annualized cost reduction and helping us in mitigating commodity and pricing risk.

items.statement: Added 250-300 LFR stores in Q1; cover all national accounts and 40-45 of ~80-84 regional accounts
items.quote: We've added close to about 250 to 300 more stores in quarter one. So we're increasing our penetration within the account as well as the breadth of accounts that we deal with.

items.statement: Employee cost at INR 77 crore includes increment impact and wage variability; senior onboarding complete, no major restructuring planned
items.quote: So Achal, this quarter, the employee costs had impact of the increments and other things. Over a period of time, as I said, we've made investments on the structure, and I think is this the going rate.

items.statement: TPW fan contribution ~25-30% of industry; company in line with industry mix
items.quote: Firstly, the industry, depending on brand to brand, would hover between 25% to 30% as TPW contribution to the overall fans.

items.statement: Lighting market share gains consistent over last few quarters; team execution driving outperformance
items.quote: In lighting, we've been seeing a consistent market share gains over the last few quarters, and we are inching up, and that's a good encouraging sign for us.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected to be higher than Q4 FY24's 5%, targeting high single digit to double digit; EBITDA margin expansion guidance of 100 bps maintained
items.quote: Our guidelines has been that we want to grow EBITDA by at least 100 basis points, even in the current really difficult market condition, we are committed and you look at this quarter also the EBITDA has gone up by 100 basis points and is now close to 13%.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth target of 12-15%
items.quote: Medium term, we would love the growth rates to move to 12% to 15%, but we are hoping for the market to correct, and we are also very watchful on profitable growth.

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs 100 crores for FY25, largely for Tommy Hilfiger COCO stores, IT and store renovations
items.quote: So, our capex is likely to be in the range of 100 crores, largely to be spent on some COCO stores on the PVH side, some IT capex and some renovation of stores.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 80 bps to 55.2% in Q1 FY25 driven by better price realization, premiumization and sourcing efficiency
items.quote: GP has moved up to 55.2%, a gain of 80 basi s points with dual benefit of better price realization as well as lower, more efficient product cost

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to ~12.9% post-IndAS in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Most of these GP gain has flown into EBITDA which saw nearly 20% growth to Rs. 123 crores versus last year value of Rs. 103 crores.

items.statement: Wholesale channel grew >15% in Q1 FY25 after delayed spring-summer billing to align with season
items.quote: We have seen growth across brands and in every channel. There is growth in volume as well as in price realization. A key highlight was control on discounting where we delayed EOSS to end of June, while industry had been discounting by mid-June.

items.statement: Market conditions remain subdued due to elections, heat wave, fewer wedding dates; expect slightly better conditions ahead
items.quote: Markets have been difficult for a couple of quarters. Summer, there were some specific issue linked to elections for example. The global warmin g or warming in India is the reality, May saw that. The markets are sort of challenging and subdued currently

items.statement: Adjacent categories (footwear, womenswear, kidswear, innerwear) now >20% of AFL revenue, growing double-digit; USPA adjacent share ~30%
items.quote: The share of adjacent category like footwear, womenswear, kidswear, innerwear has crossed 20% revenue share of AFL and has grown in the last one year at double digit.

items.statement: Footwear category facing regulatory changes; monitoring policy developments and preparing supply chain
items.quote: As far as the footwear results is concerned, there are some regulation changes, and we are in touch with the policymakers and we are making sure that our supply chain is geared for whatever the change required.

items.statement: Net retail space addition target of 15% for FY25; added 40,000+ sq ft net in Q1 with ~30 new stores
items.quote: We remain committed to growing net retail space by around 15%, and hopeful of furt her acceleration of build-up in square footage in times ahead

items.statement: Online D2C business grew >60% YoY in Q1 with improved channel profitability; online contribution ~25% of revenue
items.quote: There is handsome growth in online direct -to-consumer b usiness that has grown more than 60% year -on-year and delivered higher channel profitability as well

items.statement: Arrow brand at low single-digit EBITDA, targeting mid-single digit in near term; Flying Machine ~1 year behind Arrow in turnaround
items.quote: Arrow remains in a low single digit brand and our first task is to take it to mid-single digit brand and in the current market condition believe the wedding dates are in the second half that the performance will improve.

items.statement: US Polo approaching Rs 2,000 cr scale, double-digit pre-IndAS EBITDA; expected to match Tommy/CK profitability in medium term
items.quote: U.S. Polo is very close and it's also double digit pre IndAS EBITDA brand of scale that we are talking about. So, in medium term, I can say confidently it will be a similar profitability brand.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 225 crores end-Q1; may rise ~50 crores next quarter due to seasonal inventory build; committed to debt reduction from free cash flow
items.quote: Our net debt was around 225 crores. There is a seasonality, next quarter it could go up by 50-odd crores here because we have to build the inventory for the season and a bigger scale.

items.statement: 60 Tommy Hilfiger stores converted to COCO model; no CK stores converted
items.quote: We have 60 stores in Tommy Hilfiger which are now COCO stores.

items.statement: A&P spend ~3% of revenue in Q1; typically 3-4% for full year
items.quote: So, in Q1, typically it is slightly lower than 3% because the campaigns happens towards the end of season. So, we are in between that 3% to 4% spend, but for this quarter it was around 3%.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 15% for FY25 stands; long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% sustainable ex inventory gain/loss
items.quote: No, I think on a long -term basis, 12% to 13% EBITDA margin is sustainable. This quarter was impacted slightly by product mix.

items.statement: Bihar plant to be operational by January adding 45,000 tonnes capacity; debottlenecking of 35,000-40,000 tonnes at existing plants over 3-4 quarters
items.quote: we expect Bihar to be operational by January, which will add -- so previously, we had guided for end of quarter 4, and we have tried our best to prepone that. So we are confident by January, we will be able to commercialize production at Bihar facility, which will help us have a strong March quarter in the current financial year, which would be a production capacity of around 45,000 ton nes, which

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 9.6% impacted by adverse agri-heavy product mix and higher A&P spend (>2.5% of revenue); long-term 12-13% sustainable
items.quote: The two major reasons for that one has been product. While we have grown across segments, both have been higher in the agriculture space where the -- of course, it's a volume driver, but the margins are slightly lower. And second is also the A&P costs have significantly increased, which is a conscious effort.

items.statement: April-May demand robust; June-July saw destocking due to PVC price decline but last-mile demand remains strong on affordable raw material, real estate and infrastructure growth
items.quote: Of course, in June, towards the end, we saw some weakness in PVC prices, which always means that there will be destocking in the channel. And that trend has continued in July. But I have always maintained that any restocking or destocking averages out over 12 months. What is important is the last mile demand. And that, I believe, continues to be strong because of the confluence of many factors lik

items.statement: Agri share of revenue increased Y-o-Y in Q1; plumbing and SWR also grew but agri was major contributor
items.quote: Correct. So agri has increased that at the gross margin level, their product mix is there. But as the EBITDA margin with increase in advertising expenses as well as losses in bathware, we have ended up with a lower EBITDA margin compared to normal.

items.statement: CPVC raw material prices to remain range-bound with no major upside; PVC prices affordable and range-bound, anti-dumping duty already factored in
items.quote: No, I believe that's already actually factored into the pricing. So it's tough to predict raw material prices, but I think even CPVC, there is no major upside. Most of the variables have been factored in. So I think CPVC raw material prices should continue to be range bound from here onwards because PVC also is becoming extremely affordable.

items.statement: PVC raw material manufacturers struggling at current spreads; government support possible but timing uncertain
items.quote: I believe that current PVC prices not be sustainable for PVC raw material manufacturers. If you look at the spreads between the feedstock and PVC are at very, very low prices, and I don't see feedstock prices correcting. So current prices of PVC, most PVC raw material manufacturers will really be struggling. So maybe you could see some support given by the government.

items.statement: Bathware revenue ~Rs.5 crore, water tank revenue ~Rs.10-12 crore in Q1; bathware net loss ~Rs.4 crore; A&P spend Rs.14 crore vs Rs.11 crore YoY
items.quote: So bathware would be around Rs.5 crores for the quarter. Water tank, just give me a minute. Water tank is around Rs.10 crores to Rs.12 crores exact number Karl will share post -- but Rs.10 crores to Rs.12 crores of water tank and Rs.5 crores of bathware.

items.statement: Aquel bathware annual run-rate expense Rs.15-18 crore (Rs.5-6 cr manpower + Rs.10-12 cr branding); gross margins higher than piping once in-house manufacturing scales
items.quote: So annual level, I would say, Rs.5 crores to Rs.6 crores on manpower and Rs.10 crores to Rs.12 crores on branding. This will slightly increase because we are now expanding our footprint to south and east over the next couple of quarters. But around -- you can take around Rs.15 crores to Rs.18 crores on a 12-month basis.

items.statement: Working capital improved to 80 days (from 95 days Mar'24); receivables 61 days (from 83 days); inventory 70 days (from 52 days); channel finance sanctions increased to Rs.155 crore
items.quote: Our overall working capital stood at 80 days in June as compared to 95 days in March 2024. As we had guided, Receivables have shown marked improvement at 61 days in June '24 from 83 August 02, 2024 Transcript - Prince Pipes and Fittings Limited Q1 FY25 Earnings Call days in March end. Inventory days stood at 70 days in March as compared to 52 days

items.statement: No inventory gain or loss in Q1; industry-wide phenomenon as price increase concentrated in late May/June
items.quote: This is not only for Prince, we are not the only industry player. If you see across players, this has been the situation because the price increase was not across the 3 months. It was mostly in the end of May or in June

items.statement: ROE to return to ~16% in 2-3 years as new capacity ramps up; gross block asset turn to improve with capacity additions
items.quote: So we are a growing organization, and we intend to keep adding the capacity, which will go back to gross block, which will not immediately give the top line and the contribution. So in next 2 to 3 years, we'll be again back to 16% as we add capacity and we start realizing the output from it.

items.statement: No plans for OPVC capacity; focus on distribution-driven products and private projects; selective about new segments
items.quote: So at this point of time, we do not have any plans for OPVC. We have always been more focused on distribution and private projects. And we believe there is enough and more room for growth, and we are adding capacity. And we have enough on our plate with now water tanks and bathware being the 2 new segment.

items.statement: Debottlenecking capex across Jaipur, Silvassa, Kolhapur, Haridwar, Chennai; Bihar plant has land for significant expansion over 2-3 years
items.quote: And the existing debottlenecks that we're doing around 35 to 40 KT additional will be at the existing plant. So it would be a combination of Jaipur, Silvassa, Kolhapur, Haridwar, Chennai across facilities because the good part is the demand is not coming from 1 or 2 geographies.

items.statement: Lucknow 450-bed tower expected to cost around Rs. 700 crore plus
items.quote: So, I think this will be around Rs. 700 crore plus for the beds.

items.statement: Mohali 250-bed hospital on 50-year lease; developer bears building cost, Max provides equipment and security deposit
items.quote: We will be providing the medical equipment, the security deposit, which is interest bearing, and loose furniture. The entire project cost will be incurred by the developer, including the land and building, etc.

items.statement: Nanavati Phase I (241 beds) structure up this month, completion expected by end of FY25
items.quote: For 241 beds in Nanavati (Phase I), the hospital structure will be up in this month and the project completion is expected by end of this fiscal year, as communicated earlier.

items.statement: Max Smart Saket (375 beds) fast-tracked, completion expected by Q1 FY26
items.quote: For 375 beds at Max Smart (Saket Complex), the project was fast-tracked in Q4 and we expect its completion by Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Mohali 155 beds on schedule, completion expected by Q1 FY26
items.quote: For 155 beds at Mohali, work on the 2nd floor slab is underway, while the work on ramp area side is reaching ground level. All high-side equipment has been ordered and the project is on schedule. We expect the completion by Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Sector 56 Gurgaon Phase I (300 beds) basement slabs nearing completion, completion expected by Q2 FY26
items.quote: For 300 beds at Sector 56, Gurgaon (Phase I), basement slabs are nearing completion and the project is progressing as per plan. Orders for all high lead-time items have been placed. We expect completion of the first phase by Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Max Vikrant Saket Phase I (415 beds) facing delay due to forest approval litigation, expected couple of quarters delay
items.quote: We expect some delay due to ongoing litigation involving DDA and Delhi Government regarding cutting out trees in the eco-sensitive zone near Asola Bhati Wildlife Sanctuary and the Ridge areas without approval.

items.statement: Dwarka hospital (303 beds) expected to break even at EBITDA level by Q4 FY25 (8-9 months from launch)
items.quote: We do think that by the 8th to 9th month we should be in a breakeven state, which means that in Q4, we should start to see breakeven numbers at EBITDA level for Dwarka hospital.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin 26.5% in Q1 FY25 on like-to-like basis, down 2% QoQ due to merit increase, GST on variable fee, lower immigration footfalls
items.quote: Network operating EBITDA stood at Rs. 487 crore, reflecting a growth of 12% year-on-year while declining by 2% quarter-on-quarter. Operating EBITDA margin stood at 26.5% for the quarter.

items.statement: ARPOB for existing network improved 7% YoY and 3% QoQ to Rs. 80,100 driven by oncology, orthopedics, renal, robotics and tariff revisions
items.quote: Average Revenue Per Occupied Bed (ARPOB) for the quarter improved to Rs. 80,100, growing by 7% year-on-year and 3% quarter-on-quarter. Year-on-year improvement in ARPOB was largely due to growth in oncology, orthopedics and renal sciences as well as increased number of robotic procedures. This was coupled with tariff revisions for self-pay, insurance and institutional segments.

items.statement: Occupancy at 77% on existing network, up from 74% YoY and 75% QoQ; occupied bed days grew 5% YoY and 2% QoQ
items.quote: Our average occupancy for the network increased to 77% from 74% in Q1 last year and 75% in the trailing quarter. While occupied bed days grew by around 5% year-on-year and 2% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Higher-end clinical mix (more robotics, oncology) lowers EBITDA margin percentage but raises EBITDA per bed; surgical vs medical mix shift improves ARPOB
items.quote: We have clearly seen a change in the clinical mix. It's moved to a higher-end clinical mix. And like I've mentioned in the past, when you do higher -end surgeries, you do more robotics and more oncolog y, etc., they typically have lower margins in percentage terms, but higher margins in value terms

items.statement: International patient revenue Rs. 158 crore; muted growth due to political situations and credit-risk actions in some countries; immigration footfalls down 48% due to visa changes in Canada, UK, Australia
items.quote: The international patient revenue stood at Rs. 158 crore. There was a temporary impact on patient flows from some countries due to political situations and credit-risk management related actions taken by us, which accounted for the muted growth in this segment.

items.statement: Lucknow and Nagpur acquired hospitals ramping well: 60% avg occupancy, Rs. 99 cr revenue and Rs. 18 cr EBITDA in Q1, ARPOB Rs. 45,300, annualized EBITDA per bed ~Rs. 30 lakhs
items.quote: For Q1, these hospitals contributed Rs. 99 crore to the revenue and Rs. 18 crore to the operating EBITDA, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 21% and 64% respectively. And more importantly, this was done within the first three months of us acquiring these facilities. Collectively, their ARPOB stood at Rs. 45,300 and annualized EBITDA per bed at approximately Rs. 30 lakhs.

items.statement: Tax rate 22.8% overall; Q1 rate 26% due to losses in Sahara entity where DTA not recognized; expected to normalize around 22%
items.quote: That's right. So, overall rate is 22.8%. The rate has gone up this quarter because we have losses in the new ent ities, mainly the Sahara hospital entity. Sahara hospital transaction was Rs. 993 crore. We funded this by Rs. 840 crore of loan into the entity. And as Abhay alluded to in his speech, we are changing the cost and capital structure in the company. So, since we have losses in the company

items.statement: Non-MF revenue share target of 20% in 3-3.5 years, growing ~2% per year (~0.5% per quarter)
items.quote: We still reaffirm our commitment to grow this, scale this to at least 20% in the next 3, 3.5 years. I believe we are on track. We'd like to grow this by about 2% every year. So about 0.5% every quarter.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue expected to grow mid- to high-20s, possibly up to 30% for next quarter or two
items.value: mid- to high-20s, maybe up to 30%
items.quote: We've said earlier that we'd like to scale MF 15%, non-MF 20%, non-MF to scale 31%. And I think for a quarter or 2, we could expect mid- to high 20s, maybe up to 30% growth from non-MF.

items.statement: Cloud migration net margin impact not expected to exceed 0.5% at any point, positive from year 4-5
items.quote: We do not expect, at any point of time, the not impact margin to be more than 0.5%. It could be higher in the initial one or two years closer to 0.5%. But going forward, because of the rationalization that is going to happen on the various resources that we are using for this platform, we expect that from the fourth or fifth year, this will become, in fact, very positive to us from an overall marg

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 45.4%, up 320 bps YoY despite absorbing annual salary increments
items.quote: We had -- we have completed the quarter with a INR150-plus crores EBITDA for the first t ime, which is a 45.4% quarter. You will also understand that April is the time when most of the company goes through its annual salary increment(28.50). Traditionally, the impact of the increment has been upwards of 2 percentage of revenue. So even eating that cost, we are able to kind of come to an operating

items.statement: MF yields stable with <1% quarterly depletion; equity mix >3% supporting yields; no disproportionate price discounts
items.quote: You've seen that play out actually, and the leads have been largely stable with the quarter-on-quarter depletion being less than 1%, right? it's 0.7% depletion in yields. And we also had said that there's not going to be a disproportionate reduction in price or price discounts. And kind of the last few quarters have been in line with what we have guided.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 55%+ YoY; equity net inflows INR90,000 crore (70% of industry); NFO collection 82% (INR20,000+ crore); SIP registrations ~90 lakh (100% YoY growth)
items.quote: see crossed INR90,000 crore s in the quarter, this was 70% of industry's equity net inflows. And of the INR1,27,000 crores, this was INR90,000 crores, so a strong number. Within this new fund offerings, we were at a staggering 82% collection. So this is a number upwards of INR20,000 crores, upwards of 82% collection and just vindicates the overall direction in terms of the market share and market

items.statement: Non-MF revenue grew 31% YoY, outpacing MF (26%) for second consecutive quarter; KRA 100%+, Pay 44%, Account Aggregator 100%+ on small base
items.quote: the non-MF revenue grew by 31% year-on-year, driven largely by a very impressive growth that we are seeing in both Pay as well as in The AIF and Rep(28.00) revenue growth is a little muted, but you've heard the plans that we have for both, especially with the Rep with the Bima Central going live only in April and more and more integration is happening. We expect that the revenue growth will be mor

items.quote: The only thing we don't like about the market is that pricing is significantly lower just competitive price. items.statement: Vikas loan pricing to reduce from 28% to 26% or 24.99% from August 1
items.quote: Currently 28%, which we are operating to less than would be 26% or 24.99%that is from 1st of August.

items.quote: So from here on, we see our overall cost of funds moving from 7.6% to somewhere close to 7.90% and thereabouts.

items.statement: Target microfinance:retail assets mix 55-45 near term, 50-50 medium term
items.quote: In the first stage, we would want to reach 55-45. As a steady state in the medium term, we look at a 50-50 split between microfinance and retail asset -- secured retail assets.

items.quote: we see stress in Gujarat, pockets of Gujarat, pockets of Orissa, pockets of UP in places where we operate. Otherwise, we largely don't operate in the largely affected areas -- the big, affected areas, we do not operate

items.quote: Yes. I think we will have capital requirements somewhere around 15 to 18 months, and we do have that in mind, and we are focusing on that requirement.

items.quote: Rs. 5,000 crores to Rs. 7,000 crores.

items.quote: Balance promoter contribution required to be made for our operational HAM projects or under construction HAM projects put together, of which we are expecting contribution of Rs. 600 crores in this year.

items.statement: Food delivery GOV growth of 20%+ expected to continue near term; currently trending at 27%-28% YoY

items.quote: However, the overall expectation from a longer-term perspective is still that we should at least grow at 20%.

items.statement: Blinkit expected to remain profitable; long-term confidence in achieving food delivery-like margins
items.quote: At this point, we don't think that will happen, and that's why we have said that we believe the business will remain profitable.

items.statement: Capex increase driven by Blinkit store scale-up and Hyperpure warehousing capacity expansion
items.quote: It's a combination of the Blinkit store scale-up and partly, we're increasing some warehousing capacity on the Hyperpure side.

items.statement: Target of 2,000 Blinkit stores by March 2026; 113 stores opened in Q1 FY25
items.quote: you have explained it quite well in the letter, but these 2,000 stores, I think you are saying latest by March 2026.

items.statement: No specific demand concerns in food delivery; no caution from restaurant partners

items.statement: Blinkit SKU count expanding; some stores at 25,000 SKUs with goal to maintain 10-minute delivery
items.quote: Two years ago, we used to serve up to 5,000 SKUs in the same neighborhood; now we are at 25,000.

items.statement: Platform fee of Rs 5-6 implemented in food delivery; will experiment with dynamic vs static pricing
items.quote: We have implemented a platform fee, or you can call it a convenience fee, of Rs. 5 to 6 in food delivery, which was almost zero last year.

items.statement: Social security benefits for delivery partners: no clarity yet; impact not expected to be meaningful
items.quote: There is no clarity on these topics at this point. Different states are taking different views on how these welfare benefits should be administered.

items.statement: Express Parcel volumes expected to grow in line with e-commerce market at 15-20% annually
items.quote: I anticipate that our steady state volumes will continue in line with what we forecasted, which is sort of annual growth rates in the e-commerce market of between 15% and 20%. And our numbers should be broadly range bound as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex was Rs 80 crores; full year FY24 capex was ~Rs 550 crores with seasonality weighted to H2
items.quote: the CapEx in the Q1 was about Rs. 80 crores, the fresh CapEx that was done. And while last year, I think, we would have done CapEx of close to about Rs. ~550 crores for the full year.

items.statement: Express Parcel service EBITDA stable at 18% Y-o-Y, up 60 bps Q-o-Q; PTL service EBITDA improved to 3.2% from 2.2% Y-o-Y; SCS service EBITDA at 4.4% down from 6% Q-o-Q
items.quote: Express Parcel service EBITDA margin has held constant on a Y-o-Y basis, while it has expanded by about 60 bps on a Q-o-Q basis. Part truckload service EBITDA margin continues to improve as we improve our customer mix and efficiency in operations and it is at 3.2%.

items.statement: PTL yield improved 8% Y-o-Y from pricing and mix efforts; Express yield up 5.5% Y-o-Y from heavy goods mix
items.quote: Part Truckload saw a revenue increase of 25% Y-o-Y and a freight tonnage of 16% Y-o-Y, coupled with 8% yield improvements, which has resulted in 1% improvement in our service EBITDA margin in this business to 3.2%. Yield improvement has been an outcome of efforts on pricing and mix improvement in this business.

items.statement: Peak season indications show decent growth; SCS pipeline robust across auto, electricals, FMCG; integrated fulfillment demand rising
items.quote: The next quarter, as you're aware, Sachin, is also going to contain the peak period, and at least indications so far are that the peak period is likely to be a period of fairly decent growth for the industry.

items.statement: Heavy goods mix driving Express yield expansion; multi-tenant dark store network launched for rapid commerce; PTL and Express networks fully integrated
items.quote: This yield has primarily increased on back of a higher mix of heavy goods category. There are certain initiatives that we are undertaking, which could potentially further increase the mix of heavy goods in our business.

items.quote: SCS business growth was 26% Y-o-Y due to a seasonally strong quarter for air conditioning customers and we have a robust pipeline of customers across several sectors like auto, electricals, and FMCG.

items.statement: Critical Power business grew ~16% YoY driven by lithium-ion battery solutions and hybrid power solutions for telecom renewable energy uptake
items.quote: Our Critical Power business grew roughly 16% year-on-year based on consistent demand for our lithium-ion battery solutions and various types of power management solutions, particularly hybrid power solutions because of uptake of renewable energy in the telecom sector.

items.quote: Today because there is no cell manufacturing in India directly every company has no option but to import, but in time to come when there is local manufacturing then the business strategy will have a cost associated with it in terms of custom duty, but not as of today.

items.quote: In Q1 '25,the bus vertical booked 3.84 million passenger segments, generating a grosstransaction value of Rs. 376.5 crores. This represents a 13% increase in segment

items.quote: we are expecting that to accelerate a bit in the second half of the year. items.quote: Our Consumer Product vertical has demonstrated revenue growth after 4 quarters. We have also managed a few price hikes and streamlined some of our discounting schemes as our products gain greater acceptance with our customers.

items.quote: We have also managed a few price hikes and streamlined some of our discounting schemes as our products gain greater acceptance with our customers.

items.quote: The Lighting installations vertical continues to do well and has delivered double -digit EBIT margins with promise to continue to do better in succeeding quarters.

items.quote: And the gross margin actually it's improved by about 1.5 percentage points over last year. So, that's a function of our product mix and premiumization continue to happen in certain pricing actions we have taken.

items.quote: Morphy Richards is also delivering high-teens revenue growth since the past few quarters.

items.quote: My view is sitting on about 2 percentage points of logistics savings, percentage points in terms of percent of sales. That should come into our books by end of this year.

items.quote: Cash from operations in Q1 was Rs. 155 crores, which is a testament of our rigor on operational excellence. Strong balance sheet with surplus cash as on 30th June 2024, is Rs. 442 crores.

items.quote: We don't give forward guidance in numerical terms, whether it's double digit, single digit. But I will just emphasize what we put in our note and what I said in the opening comments, we are seeing definitive green shoots.

items.statement: Alternate channels contribute ~39% of revenue (E-com ~13%); alternate channel margins not lower than general trade
items.quote: E-Com is contributing about 13%. And overall, if you look at alternate channel, it is contributing close to about 39%.

items.statement: Fan growth below industry due to high sub-economy share; premium segment acceptance a journey; NEX brand to drive premium growth from next year
items.quote: Our growth in fans, while we have had growth, I would say it has been below industry growth. And the reason for that is our share of contribution from sub -economy continues to be very high.

items.statement: Warranty and service costs declining due to quality improvements; product costs up from R&D investment; pricing recovery expected by next year
items.quote: That's very visible and quantifiable metrics for us. And as a result of that, our actual servicing costs, of this, our product replacement or spare part replacement costs are coming down.

items.statement: Distribution moat eroding with e-commerce; focus shifting to product differentiation and weighted distribution in urban counters
items.quote: With the advent of online platform, e -commerce, etcetera, the importance of distribution moat has somewhat been coming down because every new company can also reach every part of India through online platforms.

items.statement: Management expects clarity on syrup and B-Heavy molasses policy for 2024-25 within four weeks.
items.quote: we are hoping that they will allow Syrup and B-Heavy for the year '24-25. items.statement: No expansion plans for 2024-25; no real capex seen for the next six months.

items.statement: Rainfall has been good so far; hoping it stays for the next eight weeks.

items.statement: Sugar contributed 60.6% of EBIT in Q1 FY25, up from 29.7% a year ago.

items.statement: Engineering division order book stood at INR 3,394 crores at end of Q1 FY25

items.statement: UP contract residual value of Rs. 813 crores planned for significant execution by end of current financial year

items.statement: Radio EBITDA margin at 21.8% excluding digital in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the year, excluding digital, stood at INR20.5 crores as compared to INR19.2 crores in Q1 FY '24. EBITDA margins were at 21.8%.

items.statement: Radio pricing increased ~5.8% YoY in Q1 FY25 due to political business, prices stabilized
items.quote: There was some bit of price increase, about 5.8% of price increase. But I would not read much, it's one time because of the political event. Good part to say on the pricing, it has stabilized, and we don't see any further drop.

items.statement: Gaana subscription price doubled to INR599 from July 1, blended price impact gradual as existing users renew
items.quote: Our pricing earlier used to be INR299, which was not feasible. But recently, you would have seen from 1st July, we have increased the price to INR599.

items.statement: H2 FY25 pricing optimism, potential price increases from September, no price declines expected
items.quote: Generally, media, not just radio, any media, the price is based on supply demand in the H2, we believe, starting September could have a chance where we could look at certain price increases as the business comes back and the media is always skewed towards H2.

items.statement: Cash balance INR355 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains robust with a cash balance of INR355 crores as of June 30, 2024.

items.statement: Inventory utilization at 72% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The inventory utilization for this quarter is about 72%.

items.statement: Multimedia solutions grew 10%, activations grew 42%, original content pushed to next quarter for margin discipline
items.quote: Otherwise, other business of multimedia solutions has grown 10%, activation has grown by about 42%. Just as I said, this is the one business where we believe we wanted to have a much better margin because that remains our guiding principle across the company, and that's the reason we have pushed that business to this quarter.

items.statement: Gaana investment front-loaded in Q1-Q2 FY25, costs expected to decrease in subsequent quarters
items.quote: So, it's a planned expense. I would say for the first quarter, it's a little on the higher side. But as we see for the next quarter, this cost will come down.

items.statement: Management expects similar quarter-on-quarter growth going forward
items.quote: Yes, we can see a similar growth quarter on quarter. Yes.

items.statement: Margins under pressure due to new contracts and higher coal mix; expected to improve as ash share rises
items.quote: The major reason in the first instance being the coal and ash handling business because there are new opportunities, new businesses coming up. We are taking time to learn and understand the actual cost involved in every tender.

items.statement: Margin improvement expected as ash handling becomes majority and contract efficiencies kick in
items.quote: Going forward, this margin will get better and also the mix of coal and ash also will get better with ash taking over majority where we will have a larger margin. The margin will get better going forward.

items.statement: Immediate capex of about INR100 crores for EV and ash/coal fleet combined; may increase with business growth
items.quote: Currently, I think we immediately have current capex which is close to about INR100 odd crores for both the fleet, both EV and just put together. But going forward, yes, as the business goes, this might grow also.

items.statement: Ash handling fleet expansion to 1,500-1,600 vehicles would require INR75-100 crores capex for owned fleet (10-15%)
items.quote: So, even if you double the capacity to 1,500 or 1,600 vehicles from the band 800, we'll be about 150, 160 fleet will be owned fleet, which will be about INR75 crores to INR100 crores of capex requirement, if at all we own those fleets.

items.statement: New large public sector power plant clients added; expect 7,000-10,000 tons/day additional volume in 2-3 months
items.quote: I think we are looking at another addition of about 7,000, 8,000 to 10,000 tons per day going forward in two to three months to add.

items.statement: Legacy pond ash of 1.7 billion tons must be cleared in 3-6 years; fly ash generation of 185 million tons/year
items.quote: The legacy pond ash has to be cleared within the next three years. There is already a fine and penalty being imposed by Ministry of Environment. But looking at the volume, I think it might go up to five to six years to remove the legacy ash.

items.statement: Strategic focus shifting to ash handling over coal trading due to larger growth potential
items.quote: Yes, our focus is more majorly on ash, because that's one area which we think is going to grow a lot in the country. So, major focus will be on ash going forward.

items.statement: INR1,000 crore enabling resolution for future working capital needs; no immediate deployment plan
items.quote: We don't need to go to a process because we are a very fast -growing c ompany. If there's a potential requirement, this will only be an enabling factor

items.statement: Sherisha Technologies (promoter) loan repayment of INR27 crore done; balance INR19 crore by Sept 15 for working capital
items.quote: This loan out of the total INR46 crore loan, INR27 crore of the loan has been repaid as on day and balance also will get repaid by 15th of September.

items.statement: Ash handling realization varies by distance and disposal avenue: INR400/ton at 100km, INR800-900/ton at 200km
items.quote: Different customer, different location has different pricing depending on the number of kilometres you have to dispose the ash for. So it ranges if it's 100 kilometres it is INR400 a ton if it's 200 it's INR800, INR900 a ton

items.statement: Green mobility revenue INR5.47 crore from 539 EVs; target 2,000 vehicles by March 2025 with ~INR7-8 lakh/vehicle/year yield
items.quote: This year like we said last time by end of this year it will go up to 2000 vehicles by March next year. And the potential revenue could be roughly about yield per vehicle could be roughly about 7 to 8 lakhs per vehicle on a yearly basis.

items.statement: Green mobility gross profitable; EBITDA profitability expected as fleet scales and corporate costs absorb
items.quote: So I think we are on the gross level we are profitable. I think as we increase the fleet and then the corporate expense and the total team expenses get divided, we'll be profitable even at the EBITDA level.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 60-90 days (payables 15 days, receivables 60-90 days); no improvement expected
items.quote: Currently, working capital cycle is between 60 to 90 days. Where our supplier, we pay on a 15-day basis. But from the customer, we get between 60 to 90 days.

items.statement: Real estate segment saw sales of 1.15 million square feet and revenue of INR 1,086 crores in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: In Q1 FY'25, the real estate segment saw sales of 1.15 million square feet and revenue of INR 1,086 crores.

items.statement: Overall price realization reached INR 9,483 per square foot, the highest till date.
items.quote: The overall price realization continued its upward trajectory coming in at INR 9,483 per square foot this quarter, which is our highest till date.

items.statement: Strong demand continues for new launches and under-construction properties with end users as largest buyer segment.
items.quote: We are still seeing strong demand for new launches as well as under construction properties. In our key markets, end users remain the largest buyer segment.

items.statement: Leasing portfolio stands at 8.7 million square feet with consistent office rental collections.
items.quote: In Q1 FY'25, the Brigade leasing portfolio stands at 8.7 million square feet with consistent office rental collections.

items.statement: GCCs, flex space operators, PFSI and technology firms continued to drive office leasing activities.
items.quote: Across the office segment, GCCs, flex space operators, PFSI and technology firms continued to drive leasing activities.

items.statement: Management does not provide presales guidance for FY25.
items.quote: We have not given guidance, and we actually don't share guidance.

items.statement: Launch trajectory remains same as previous quarter; launches skewed towards second half of FY25.
items.quote: As we had shared in the previous quarter. The launches trajectory remains the same. Whatever we have launched has been replenished in the land bank as well.

items.statement: Q2 launches expected to be similar to Q1 levels, subject to approvals.
items.quote: Similar to what we achieved in first quarter. Or maybe we're not sure because of approvals.

items.statement: Commercial pipeline includes 1.48 million sq ft of upcoming launches across Chennai, Bangalore, Trivandrum, Kochi and Gujarat.
items.quote: So basically, we have we Brigade Padmini Tech Valley, which is A block. So that's around 300-odd thousand square feet. And I think Kochi Infopark, again, this is all in the upcoming in the next 4 quarters, which has already mentioned, Kochi Infopark as mentioned last quarter, is about 150,000 square feet. And those are the main 2, I think Brigade Gujarat has already been mentioned, the Phase 2 of

items.statement: Land bank stands at 517 acres with overall GDV of INR 50,000 crores, Brigade share INR 39,000 crores.
items.quote: In terms of the data points, whether it is the GDV, etcetera, similar to what we mentioned in the last earnings call, we had about overall INR 50,000 crore s number for the GDV, of which Brigade share is about INR 39,000 crores

items.statement: Launch pipeline guidance of INR 10,000-11,000 crores GDV for FY25 remains unchanged.
items.quote: Yes, that is similar to what we mentioned earlier.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR 1,113 crores, EBITDA INR 328 crores, PAT INR 83 crores for Q1 FY25.
items.quote: Consolidated revenue, including other income for quarter 1 FY'25 stood at INR 1,113 crores. Consolidated EBITDA for quarter 1 FY'25 stood at INR 328 crores. Consolidated PAT after minority income for quarter 1 FY'25 is at INR 83 crores.

items.statement: Q1 sales lower than Q4 due to seasonal pattern and election-related approval delays.
items.quote: It's fairly typical for Q1 to be running at a lower rate than Q4. In fact, across the industry, Q4 tends to be the highest in the year. So we're not too worried about it. Also, there were some slowness in approvals due to elections, etcetera.

items.statement: Strategy remains land-driven; mid-segment pricing has moved up to INR 90 lakhs-1.2 crores in Bangalore.
items.quote: Now I would say that's comfortably upward of INR 90 lakhs to INR 1.2 crores. So there is an overall change in the market itself in terms of what qualifies as mid-segment, and that's due to multiple factors, mainly affordability and growth in per capita income as well.

items.statement: Hospitality revenue grew 13% YoY in Q1; occupancy up 9%, ARR strategy balanced with occupancy focus.
items.quote: The revenue that we have seen has actually gone up by 13% if we compare it to Q1 of last year. So there was growth and a typical hospitality strategy varies between an occupancy versus an ARR strategy.

items.statement: Brigade Twin Towers awaiting OC; one tower (0.6M sq ft) to be strata sold, other for leasing.
items.quote: Twin Towers, yes, we are still awaiting OC. So I cannot say it's completed just yet, we're still awaiting OC, and that should be we should be able to get in the next couple of months.

items.statement: Mahan Energen Phase II 1600 MW ultra-supercritical expansion targeted for completion by June 2027
items.quote: Speaking of the future, the Mahan Energen Phase II Ultra-supercritical expansion project of 1600 megawatt capacity is well underway to achieve its targeted completion by June2027.

items.statement: Advanced preparation started for three 1600 MW projects at Raipur, Raigarh, and Mirzapur
items.quote: We have started advanced preparation for setting up three more projects of 1600 MW each at Raipur, Raigarh, and Mirzapur.

items.statement: Awaiting NCLT approval for Lanco Amarkantak and Coastal Energen acquisitions adding 1800 MW operating and 1320 MW under-construction capacity
items.quote: We are awaiting NCLT approval of the resolution plans for Lanco Amarkantak and Coastal Energen, which will expand our operating capacity by 1800 MW and add another 1320 MW of under-construction capacity.

items.statement: Target capacity of 30.67 GW by FY29-30 including brownfield expansions of 4800 MW and inorganic opportunities over 1000 MW
items.quote: In addition to this, we are also evaluating further brownfield expansion projects of 4,800 MW and inorganic opportunities of more than 1,000 MW, which together will take our target capacities to 30.67 GW by FY 29-30.

items.statement: Government estimates peak demand growing from 250 GW to 400 GW by 2031-32 requiring 80-90 GW additional thermal capacity
items.quote: The government has revised its power demand projections within just two years. It estimates that peak demand will grow from 250 GW currently to 400 GW by 2031-32.

items.statement: Three states have invited bids for 6400 MW thermal supply with 25-year PPA duration
items.quote: Bids for supply of 6400 MW from thermal power have already been invited by three states, while more b ids are expected from other states soon

items.statement: Merchant revenue realization Rs 7.45/unit, fuel cost Rs 2.89/unit, contribution Rs 4.56/unit vs Rs 3.71/unit last year
items.quote: In merchant sales, we had a revenue realization of Rs. 7.45 per unit on an average for the quarter and the fuel cost was Rs. 2.89 per unit, so there was a contribution of Rs. 4.56 per unit.

items.statement: Carbon tax would be change in law and passed through under PPA, citing Rs 400/tonne GST Compensation Cess precedent
items.quote: See, any carbon tax would be a change in law and therefore it would be passed through under the PPA.

items.statement: Strategy to keep 80% capacity under long-term PPAs and 15-20% for merchant sales
items.quote: As per our internal assessment, we are keeping around 20% under merchant. That should be a sort of balancing act, whereby we don't want to expose ourselves to market risk for more than the 20%.

items.statement: Bangladesh PPA for 1500 MW for 25 years, receiving regular payments with 4-5 months average arrears
items.quote: have signed the agreement for 1500 megawatts and the PPA is for 25 years. So, there is no question of future as regards to the already concluded agreement. As far as payment is concerned, we have started getting good payments from last few months and every process is well

items.statement: Green ammonia co-firing pilot study at Mundra in technical feasibility stage
items.quote: We are carrying out a pilot study. So first we have to establish whether the green ammonia can be co-fired with the coal or not.

items.statement: Credit available for merchant capacity from banks and financial institutions based on standalone viability
items.quote: Credit is available nowadays even for merchant capacity also. There is a clear indication from Government of India that since now the rates in the market are quite attractive, the financial institutions and banks should look at standalone viability of the capacity now since the merchant market is quite matured.

items.statement: Q1FY25 had a slow start due to general elections and lower movie releases; 476 movies released vs 581 in Q1FY24 and 550 in Q4FY24, an 18% YoY and 13% QoQ decline.
items.quote: Q1FY25 had a slow start, due to the general elections campaign in April and May and a lower number of movie releases. During the quarter, 476 movies were released (including different versions/languages), compared to 581 in Q1FY24 and 550 in Q4FY24, reflecting an 18% decline year-over-year and a 13% decline quarter-over-quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR 945 mn, EBITDA INR 66 mn, net loss INR 42 mn in Q1FY25.
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for Q1FY25 was INR 945 million, up from INR 853 million in Q1FY24. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 66 mn, compared to INR 163 mn in Q1FY24. Net loss of INR 42 mn in Q1FY25, compared to a Net profit of INR 25 mn in

items.statement: Upcoming release lineup includes Auron Main Kahan Dum Tha, Stree 2, Vedaa, Khel Khel Mein, The Goat, Devara, Joker, Vettiyan, Deva, Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3, Singham Again, Sitare Zameen Par, Pushpa 2.
items.quote: Looking ahead, with the continued success of 'Kalki 2898 AD' in July and an exciting lineup of upcoming releases across languages, including 'Auron Main Kahan Dum Tha,' 'Stree 2,' 'Vedaa,' 'Khel Khel Mein,' 'The Goat,' 'Devara,' 'Joker,' 'Vettiyan,' 'Deva,' 'Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3,''Singham again,' 'Sitare Zameer par, and 'Pushpa 2,' we are hopeful for a positive turnaround in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Nova Cinema: license secured for one screen in UP; three screens under construction, two completed; first launch expected mid to late this month in Meerut.
items.quote: Yes, the license to operate one of the screens in UP has been secured. As mentioned earlier, three screens are under construction, and two of them are now completed. For one of the screens, we're just waiting for the right movie release, likely by mid to late this month, to officially launch it in UP.

items.statement: Product sales revenue grew 84% YoY to INR 26.5 crore with 20-22% operating margin; cost of goods sold increased INR 9 crore.
items.quote: Our revenue from product sales has grown by 84%, from INR 14 crores last year to INR 26.5 crores this quarter, carrying an operating margin of approximately 20-22%. Correspondingly, the cost of purchased goods has also gone up.

items.statement: Central government ad allocations remain under a cloud; no meaningful revenue received this quarter; uncertainty persists until new government establishes approach.
items.quote: Yes, the challenges with central government allocations for cinema networks persist. We haven't received meaningful revenue from them this quarter. Given the election period, even regular spending by the central government would have been low , making this a particularly dry qua rter for central government funds

items.statement: TSR network acquisition integration expected by Q3FY25; currently paying fixed fee ~INR 3.3 crore per quarter; revenue ramp-up underway.
items.quote: As discussed earlier, our multiplex network of ~2,000 screens adds significant value to our ad network but comes with associated costs. For single screens or lower-end multiplexes, we typically use a revenue-sharing arrangement, where we give around, let's say, 25% of earnings.

items.statement: Ad revenue share percentage expected to normalize to 45-48% range as advertisement revenue grows; TSR integration to stabilize by Q3.
items.quote: As advertisement revenue increases, the fixed nature of the revenue share will cause the percentage to naturally decrease to around 45-48%, which aligns with our typical range.

items.statement: Corporate ad revenue expected to perform well with strong film lineup; state government traction positive; significant traction expected in next two quarters.
items.quote: advertising, we have a strong lineup of films that should drive revenue in this sector. Additionally, our recent tie -up for South screens has increased our network strength there. As mentioned earlier, our overall product mix is improving with the addition of more multiplex screens. Given these factors, we expect to see significant traction in the next two quarters

items.statement: Advertisement screen network grew to 3,769 screens as of June 30, 2024, up 17% YoY with addition of 535 screens; slight 2% QoQ decline.
items.quote: On the screen network front, our advertisement screen network grew to 3,769 as of June 30, 2024, compared to 3,234 as of June 30, 2023, marking a 17% year-over-year increase with the addition of 535 advertisement screens.

items.statement: Company remains net cash positive with INR 1,066 mn cash balance; net cash position ~INR 50 crore after maintaining reserve for opportunities.
items.quote: Regarding the consolidated funds position, the balance at the end of the quarter stood at INR 1,066 mn. As of June 30, 2024, the company continues to be n et cash positive, even after considering outstanding debt

items.statement: Caravan ad business has good margins but limited scale; revenue tied to number of vans; not a major revenue driver like core ad network.
items.quote: However, from a pure modeling perspective, expectations should be tempered. The revenue potential of the caravan business is directly tied to the number of vans in operation, unlike our core advertising network where the infrastructure is already in place.

items.statement: NeuralGarage partnership for VisualDub AI lip-sync technology for dubbed films; revenue-sharing with no direct costs; pricing mechanisms still being determined.
items.quote: The partnership involves a revenue-sharing arrangement with no direct costs for us. VisualDub not only enhances the viewing experience but also provides practical benefits in film production.

items.statement: SG&A up 2% YoY; employee benefits up 14% due to normalization after converting 20% fixed salary to variable pay last year.
items.quote: SG&A has only seen a marginal 2% YoY increase, and employee benefits have risen by 14%. Although this 14% might seem high, it's due to last year's adjustment in our payout structure, where we converted 20% of fixed salaries into variable pay.

items.statement: Government ad revenue grew 55% YoY to INR 59 mn in Q1FY25 driven by political ads (~INR 4 crore); central government allocations remain low.
items.quote: While state government spending was also lower this quarter due to elections, political parties still see cinema as an effective medium for their campaigns. This quarter, we generated about INR 4 crores from political advertisements.

items.statement: No additional capex for NeuralGarage partnership; no fixed commitment; revenue-sharing model only.
items.quote: In terms of costs, no. The partnership is a revenue-sharing arrangement, so there won't be any additional expenses. There's no fixed commitment from the company in this business arrangement.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 9-10% for remaining quarters of FY25
items.quote: This has been extraordinarily good quarter. So, my sense is that last year, we had a margin of 8.2%. This year 10.8% and I feel that anything between 9% to 10% is something which we think we will be able to maintain in rest of the quarters.

items.statement: Animal Feed EBIT/MT expected around ₹2,000 for rest of FY25
items.quote: I think we should be able to maintain it around ₹ 2,000 in rest of the quarters, because I'm very confident because we are definitely covered as far as major raw materials are concerned, where most of the movements take place during the season.

items.statement: Astec CDMO revenue guidance maintained at ₹260-270 crore base growing 60-70% YoY in FY25
items.quote: See typically, I think we maintain our guidance on the CDMO revenues for the full year. As I have repeatedly mentioned, we should not look at CDMO revenues on a quarterly basis. So we maintain the same guidance that from last year, ₹ 260 crores- ₹ 270 crores number. We'll continue to grow that number by 60% to 70% this year, and we are well on target to achieve those numbers.

items.statement: Astec enterprise demand expected to recover fully by end of FY25, export prices to firm up in 1-2 quarters after
items.quote: On the enterprise side, as I mentioned, the demand is likely to come back or we are seeing some green shoots in the demand starting this quarter, specifically from the domestic market. And I would say, by end of this year, the demand is likely to come back fully, and the prices might take another quarter or 2 to firm up.

items.statement: No new capex committed for Astec beyond debottlenecking, quality, environmental projects; Herbicide 2 plant near completion
items.quote: So definitely, there is a big change. The discussion here is that have we run the full life cycle of some of our old triazole products, and in case we get an idea that rather than setting up new capex, we might modify some of our old plants to fit in some new molecules which might come, which may defer the investment by another year or 1.5 years. But we still don't know. It will take another 3 to

items.statement: GAVL FY25 capex includes ₹70-80 crore for OPP refinery plus Herbicide 2 capitalization and routine capex
items.quote: Point number two is capex this year, definitely, we are going to have one more refinery in OPP. And with these attachments, etcetera, of ₹ 70-80 crores. Apart from that, there is a capitalization of herbicide. Money is already invested 99% of that. And then routine capex, everything will be managed through internal accrual easily.

items.statement: Dairy Value-Added Products salience improved from 36% to 42% of sales in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The salience of Value-Added Products has improved from 36% of total sales in Q1 FY'24 to 42% in Q1 FY'25, reflecting our successful portfolio optimization efforts.

items.statement: Bangladesh JV operations temporarily halted due to political unrest; expected to resume in 1-2 days as essential service
items.quote: My sense is within a day or two, we will start our factory. And we have a meeting post this, where we will assess the situation and take a decision if can start our factories, because they got closed day before yesterday. The other thing I must say is that we are classified in essential services there, so I think as soon as the new government takes charge, somebody responsible is there, they will

items.statement: Astec took ₹18 crore inventory write-down and ₹4-5 crore credit notes in Q1 due to 10-12% export price deterioration
items.quote: Yes. We have taken inventory write-downs in Q1 on tune of almost ₹ 18 crores. We brought all the inventory to the existing pricing level in the market. So, any kind of uptick in prices as we get into the subsequent quarters will have a positive impact on our profitability.

items.statement: Animal Feed volumes impacted by subdued milk prices and lower placements; Maharashtra recovery starting July
items.quote: I think if you ask me, this impact has been all around, but the major impact was Maharashtra, but I think that has certainly started improving, particularly from the month of July.

items.statement: Domestic Crop Protection margins expected to match last year's profile despite late season uncertainty
items.quote: Yes. I think Q1 and some part of Q22 is always our in -house products. And then we will start now quarter 2 second half and quarter 3 will be our in -licensing products. And some in -house products like double and combined. So, my sense is that our change in strategy and improvement in our in-licensing product, will definitely make sure that we come to similar margin profile as last year.

items.statement: Godrej Tyson 100% acquisition enables faster decisions on branding, M&A, restructuring
items.quote: We felt that we would be better off managing it alone and that is what, I would say, motivated us to go for acquiring 100% stake in this business. Now having said that, apart from the opportunities which we can capture in this business because of agility and investments, etcetera, yes, there is other, I would say, freedom. This thing gives us our ability to do M&A or restructure this business, tak

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 25% CAGR maintained
items.quote: I would say that I have always claimed that we have had a growth of 25% CAGR always, we work to see that how is it that we can continue to maintain this or better this.

items.statement: API capacity expansion from 100 KL to 250 KL with Rs. 60 crores capex
items.quote: Our current production capacity stands at 100 KL, and we plan to expand it to 250 KL with an estimated CAPEX of around Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: CCS facility at Dahej with Rs. 90 crores capex, initial capacity 1,800 MTPA scalable to 3,600 MTPA
items.quote: We are in the process of setting up a CCS facility at Dahej which is located 1 kilometer from the original unit. This facility would be dedicated for the production of Cross Carmellose and complex excipient products. With an estimated CAPEX of nearly Rs. 90 crores, the initial production capacity will be 1,800 metric tonnes per annum, which will be scalable up to 3,600 MTPA.

items.statement: O&M segment EBITDA margin typically 21% to 23%
items.quote: Yes, it's usually between 21% to 23% EBITDA.

items.statement: MCC pricing moderate this quarter, stable but not increasing, focused on volumes
items.quote: And coming to pricing, this pricing is little in this quarter this is on moderate, there is no not much growth in pricing because we are concentrating on the volumes to our capacities. And going forward it will increase.

items.statement: MCC market expected to grow 7-9% up to 2035 in Southeast Asia
items.quote: See, there are market research studies which indicate that MCC market is expected to grow, especially in the Southeast Asian region it's expected to grow between 7% to 9% up to 2035.

items.statement: Target revenue mix: API 35-40%, O&M 20-25%, excipients balance, food & nutrition <5%
items.quote: I believe, that at least 35% to 40% of our revenue should be coming in from the API, operations and management should add in to around 20%, 25%, and the balance should be from the excipients, not just MCC because we will also have Cross Carmellose sodium. So, it will be combination of excipients, and the balance should add up from the excipients. And food and nutrition should be maybe a little les

items.statement: Healthy six months order book in place for MCC
items.quote: We have a healthy six months order book in place.

items.statement: Saudi JV $180M sales target deferred due to working capital constraints
items.quote: Now when we look at it deeper, we realized that we need to be gradual in this because $180 million, there is market potential available. But for that, for the kind of bid bond, for the kind of tender valuation which we have to put in money, it will be tremendous and probably our working capital and our cash flow will not permit us to put in that level of funding upfront.

items.statement: Dahej and Jhagadia MCC expansion 95% complete, Rs. 50 crores spent from internal accruals and debt
items.quote: Manav, this Dahej and Jhagadia almost it is in the flag, maybe 95% already we have spent. That Rs. 50 crores were allotted for Dahej and Jhagadia, that is almost incurred.

items.statement: Debt to reach near zero by end of FY25
items.quote: Yes, definitely by end of this year, almost debt would be zero level would be there.

items.statement: API regulated market revenue miniscule in FY25, CEP approvals expected in 9 months
items.quote: Revenue in the API segment in the current financial year, revenue from the regulated markets is going to be miniscule. We might still have some exports in the ROW markets, but revenue from the regulated markets is going to be very small, insignificant actually.

items.statement: No new capex planned for Middle East JVs in next 2-3 years
items.quote: No, none at this moment.

items.statement: Bottom line margins to be maintained in near term, improvement later as capacity utilization increases
items.quote: Yes, Naman, for time being we will maintain, the sustainability is there. And then going forward it will increase. But immediately there is no increase, bottom line margins we will maintain, it will be maintained.

items.statement: MCC capacity utilization dropped to 66% in Q1 due to new capacity additions, expected to reach full utilization by FY26
items.quote: Overall, it is 66%. This is because the expanded capacities, we have increased the capacities in Jhagadia and Dahej by 7,000 metric tonnes, around 3,600 metric tonnes each at Jhagadia and Dahej. This we are yet to occupy. This is the 1st Quarter, going forward we will occupy this, by next year we will occupy full, FY '26.

items.statement: CCS environmental clearance expected within 4 weeks after Gujarat Pollution Control Board review
items.quote: So, just four days back we have had another review by the Gujarat Pollution Control Board EC Committee, and I believe we have cleared all their queries. I do not foresee any further queries coming in. So, that should imply that in the next four weeks we are expecting to get the EC clearance document.

items.statement: Bromine production target for FY25 is 22,000 to 25,000 metric tons including captive requirements
items.quote: We aim to produce nearly 22,000 to 25,000 metric tons of Bromine for the year, including captive requirements.

items.statement: Salt volume guidance for FY25 maintained at 4.5 million metric tons range
items.quote: Yes, it has been in 4.5 range.

items.statement: SOP sales expected to start in Q3 FY25 with meaningful contribution in H2 FY25
items.quote: So, it is a work in progress as we have said before and we continue to expect meaningful contributions in H2.

items.statement: Acume subsidiary expects healthy contribution in FY25 with sales starting in H2 FY25
