items.statement: Management states margins will be maintained at a high level beyond 20% territory.
items.quote: So these numbers will more or less will be in between and maintained at a high level beyond 20% territory in any case.

items.statement: New PPF second line expansion of 300 LSF underway, expected to go on stream in FY26 Q2.
items.quote: Last quarter, we took a call of expanding the PPF second line by 300 LSF further.

items.statement: De-bottlenecking of older lines in progress to cater demand until new PPF line comes online.
items.quote: In between, there are many things which happen behind the doors like we are upgrading some of the older or smaller lines, which are little older for us. And there we are doing de-bottlenecking.

items.statement: Focus on maintaining order flow to run both PPF lines at optimal capacity.
items.quote: So our focus is to maintain the order flow for that line.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by product mix shift to high-end products (99% IR rejection) and new line capabilities, not commodity price gains.
items.quote: No, I explained that in detail like this was a product mix, which we have been with the sustained efforts we have been able to do.

items.statement: Specialty products in IPD segment now contribute around 20% of total IPD margins.
items.quote: So some of the good margins you see for these kind of additional products only up to around 20% I can say as we speak we have been able to make 20% margins out of total IPD business margins from these products.

items.statement: Sun Control Films portfolio shifting toward top-range products (99% IR rejection) which carry nearly 2x margins of bottom-range products.
items.quote: So the products which come at the top of the range, they are almost two times margin than the something which is at the bottom line.

items.statement: Architectural segment traditionally export-heavy (Europe #1 market); domestic growing faster from low base with new Spectra Pro and DecoVista series.
items.quote: Yeah. So it is more exports traditionally, but now the, with the introduction of Spectra Pro series & DecoVista series. So these two products are actually aimed only for architectural and both of them and especially they are working very good on export market and domestic market actually if you see the base in domestic market on architectural was pretty low.

items.statement: PPF line running at 121-125% capacity utilization; Sun Control and IPD also at near 100% utilization.
items.quote: So capacity utilization is, I mean, it is more than 100 % or close to on 121%, 125% in PPF. In Sun Control, depending on the product mix, it is almost running 100 %

items.statement: Inorganic opportunities evaluated but targets lack state-of-the-art facilities; focus remains on organic growth and backward integration.
items.quote: So in that we evaluated many but we don't find people who are up for such kind of cooperation with us in, I mean, which are not qualitative means we are looking for the state of the art facilities, whereas whatever we have been evaluating or getting for such kind of offers are things which are like 15, 20 years old.

items.statement: Branded vs private label sales split is approximately 50-50.
items.quote: It's typically 50-50 for us.

items.statement: PPF backward integration in progress; Sun Control already 100% backward integrated.
items.quote: Yes, since he has asked, I'll just answer the question that the see PPF we are Sun Control, we are 100% backward integrated. On PPF it is in the process.

items.statement: CPD revenue split: Sun Control ~50%, PPF ~20% of total revenue.
items.quote: So this Sun Control is somewhere around close to 49% or 50%. Right. And balance around roughly 20 % comes from PPF.

items.statement: Fertilizer margins expected to remain same unless subsidy revision; IP segment positive results expected in Q2/Q3
items.quote: Fertilizer business, the margins are more or less same. Until a nd unless there is any subsidy revision, I don't foresee any changes in t he raw material prices presently

items.statement: INR1,000 crores capex this year for HX Crystal, Sulphuric Acid, Urea Revamping and Solar Power projects
items.quote: So in this year, we will be capitalizing the project amounting to INR1,000 crores. Three plants are under the capitalization or i n this particular financing year only

items.statement: HX Crystal project capex INR100 crores; expected revenue INR100 crores with good margin
items.quote: Our HX Crystal project plan, that will be produced at -- that will produce HX Crystal, and it will be sold in the market. It will generate INR100 crores revenue and a good amount of margin

items.statement: Fertilizer average margin INR2,000-2,500 per metric ton; DAP negative contribution; Urea margins lesser due to energy penalty
items.quote: We're talking about the average margins, it is nearly INR2,000 to INR2,500 per metric ton. However, as I told that in the DAP, there is no margin available, even the contribution is in negative

items.statement: DAP negative contribution dented bottom line by ~INR42 crores in Q1; expected to remain negative next quarter
items.quote: I think in the current quarter, we see that there is a dent in the bottom earning amounting to INR42 crores approx

items.statement: IP segment reported INR4 crores loss; caprolactam negative contribution, melamine positive contribution
items.quote: So over all, IP product or the IP segment this year, if you see the segment, we have reported INR4 crores loss in the IP segment.

items.statement: Robust fertilizer demand expected due to favourable rainfall and accelerated Kharif cultivation
items.quote: The acceleration of Kharif cultiv ation has been facilitated by the favourable rainfall that is being experienced this year. Improv ed seasonal prospects are expected to maintain the robust demand f or fertilizers during forthcoming quarters

items.statement: Chinese dumping of cheap caprolactam, melamine, nylon-6 hurting IP segment margins; capro-benzene spread down to $582/ton
items.quote: In IP segment, domestic prices remained subdued due to dumping of cheap Chinese caprolactam, melamine and basic nylon 6. Capro-benzene spread on Y-o-Y basis reduced from $730 per metric ton to $582 per metric ton.

items.statement: Urea energy penalty 35% provisioned; requested government to reduce to 30%; revamping project to address
items.quote: They will impose and we have already requested the government to reduce it up to the level what it was earlier 30%. But let us see how the government reacts. And we are already puttin g INR450 crores for revamping of Urea II

items.statement: Accumulating sufficient DAP inventory for forthcoming Rabi season anticipating NBS subsidy increase of INR3,500/ton
items.quote: If you see there -- on the archives there w as news about increasing the subsidy by INR3,500 per metric ton for DAP. And from the government, still notification is awaited

items.statement: Projects progressing per schedule except few months delay in HX Crystal and Urea Revamping; full year impact next financial year
items.quote: All projects are progressing well as per the schedule except few months delay in HX Crystal Project and Urea Revamping Project. However, we will be commencing HX Crystal, Sulphuric Acid Project and Urea Revampin g Project up to the end of this financial year. Full year impact on turnover, margins will be seen in the next financial year

items.statement: Expect Rs 400 crore EBITDA bump-up from new capacities if conditions persist
items.quote: even if the margin profile remains the same, the capacity which is getting commissioned as we speak through the year, next year should give us at least Rs. 400 crore bump up in the EBITDA

items.statement: Additional 70,000 tons bicarb in India expected by mid-October; total bicarb capacity 290,000 tons
items.quote: Yes, 70,000 tons has already come on stream. I think another 70,000 tons will come somewhere around mid of October ahead

items.statement: UK margins to run at similar level through year; range Rs 30-45 crore quarterly loss
items.quote: run rate will continue. It may be less. See, the issue in UK is that if, the renewable power generation there reduces, we would probably be closer to 30 odd figure if the renewable power does not reduce, they have high level of wind energy and generation, it will be close to about Rs. 45 crore, that is the kind of range it will fluctuate between in negative terms

items.statement: Kenya margin decline due to higher shipping/transport costs; expect normalization
items.quote: The Kenya margin in terms of the per ton margin, is in sync with the market pricing and is in sync with what we are seeing across the board. But however, there was a slightly higher variable cost mainly due to the realiasation cost ie., shipping and transportation cost was slightly higher this quarter. We expect them to normalize.

items.statement: Bicarb demand driven by feed, food, pharma and flue gas desulphurization; first 70k tons absorbed this year, second by Q1 FY26
items.quote: Full utilization should happen through the year. So, we expect the first stream should get fully absorbed during the year and the balance maybe by Quarter 1 of next year.

items.statement: India and US volumes to be better or at least same as last year; market not a constraint
items.quote: Except in UK, we do believe that we should either be better in volume terms or at least at the same level as last year in all the geographies. In fact, India and US will show, if we run ou r operations well, that is within our own remit and what we need to do. Market is not the constraint for us to deliver higher volumes

items.statement: Surplus cash to be deployed towards debt repayment
items.quote: every surplus we have, we will deploy towards debt repayment. These remain our priorities

items.statement: Management projects annual revenue growth of approximately 10% and EBITDA margin of 14-15% for FY25.
items.quote: We had indicated a rough estimate for the overall year where we had projected an annual growth of approximately about 10%. And we would like to stick to that guidance for the whole year. And for the bottom line, our estimated EBITDA was roughly a range of between 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Company plans to invest approximately INR50 crores to open 30 company-owned retail stores by March 2025, funded through internal accruals.
items.quote: In addition to our existing footprint, we will initiate new retail projects with the launch of approximately 30 new fast fashion and ethnic wear retail outlets separately in tier 1, 2 and 3 cities by March 25 with an investment of approximately INR50 crores. These stores will be funded through internal accrual.

items.statement: Per store capex estimated at INR1.25-1.5 crores with similar inventory investment per store.
items.quote: So, these stores will require about anywhere between about INR1.25 to INR1.5 crores for capex and an inventory would also be in that range, one, one and a half crores per store.

items.statement: Expects INR100 crores revenue from the 30 new stores in FY26 (first full year of operation).
items.quote: So, the revenue growth for these 30 stores, I mean in this year it is difficult to say because it is all opening month on month but in the next year, we can estimate a revenue top line of about INR100 crores from these 30 stores.

items.statement: Anticipates consumer demand recovery from Q3 FY25 driven by festive and wedding season after Shradh period.
items.quote: We anticipate that consumer demand will begin to increase from third quarter driven by upcoming festivities.

items.statement: New retail expansion comprises ~20 fast fashion stores (mass value, family format) and ~10 ethnic wear stores (menswear, mid-price), both company-owned and outsourced manufacturing.
items.quote: So, these are approximately 30 stores and in these approximate 30 stores, fast fashion would be approximately 20 and the ethnic wear would be approximately about 10.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 10.3% from 8.6% YoY; PAT margin 3.6%. New stores may pressure margins in near term.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is INR34 crores as compared to INR31 crores in quarter 1 financial year 24. An increase of 11% year on year basis and EBITDA margin for the quarter is 10.3%.

items.statement: Management acknowledges Bangladesh situation too early to assess; may bring short-term gains but long-term impact uncertain.
items.quote: So, it is too early to comment on what is happening in Bangladesh at the moment. Of course, there might be some short-term gains that we expect but how it plays out will be seen more in the long term.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 total income declined 9% YoY to INR331 crores due to weak demand, heat wave, and election disruptions.
items.quote: Our total income for the quarter 1 financial year 25 is INR331 crores as compared to INR362 crores in quarter 1 of financial year 24. A decline of 9% year on year basis. This decline in revenue can be attributed to the continued weakness in the consumer demand.

items.statement: Price realizations stable; Q1 revenue decline driven by volume drop and product mix changes, not pricing.
items.quote: Price realizations are generally quite standard and it is more to do with change in product mix. So, it is largely a volume decrease.

items.statement: Other income of INR24 crores in Q1 FY25 includes ~INR13 crores capital subsidy (cash basis) and ~INR11 crores operational income (interest, rent).
items.quote: This is also cash basis. What I said, as soon as we know that assurance is that we are getting that money, then only we recognize. Because this is the capital subsidy received from the state government on the eligible machineries

items.statement: Management expects to achieve full capacity utilization within three years instead of four years
items.quote: we do feel that we will be able to achieve this within three years instead of four years.

items.statement: No CAPEX planned for current year; next expansion will be Brownfield taking six months to one year
items.quote: We don’t expect, sir, any CAPEXs in the current year. So, the board has not approved anything. We don’t need any CAPEXs right now currently. And anyways, everything will be Brownfield expansion which will probably take six months to on e year

items.statement: Rieco has a healthy order book with comfortable contribution
items.quote: we have seen the current order book, Rieco is having the healthy order book and also the contribution from the order book seems to be comfortable.

items.statement: Gross margin of 47% expected to remain in similar range subject to raw material variability
items.quote: I expect this gross margin to remain in this range, subject to the raw material variability what we have already seen in the past.

items.statement: EBITDA margins should improve towards 17-19% range through operational leverage as volumes ramp up
items.quote: Directionally you are on the right are a. I would say, whether the gross margin would be in this area or slightly ahead, but the ma in advantage would be through operational leverage. So, as we ramp up our volumes , we should be able to improve our EBITDA

items.statement: Q1 saw normal demand increase; overseas demand improvement and increased customer inquiries after competitor insolvency
items.quote: We have seen in Q1 is a normal demand increase. And normally Q4 is a seasonality effect and a strong quarter. We see demand improvement in the overseas geographies. After the second pigment player insolvency filing in April, there is a clear increase in the customer enquiries for samples and product approval process getting

items.statement: Inquiries mainly for new products and existing products on coatings and plastics side; results expected from Q2 onwards
items.quote: So, this quarter we are seeing our normal demand coming. And we expect, as we ramp up through this year, we will see the numbers stepping up, right.

items.statement: Specialty pigment sales grew 11% to Rs. 402 crores; non-specialty grew 7% to Rs. 187 crores
items.quote: Specialty pigment sales stood at Rs. 402 crores as compared to Rs. 362 crores in the same period last year, higher by 11 percent. Non-specialty sales for the quarter is at Rs. 187 crores, which was higher by 7% as compared to the same period

items.statement: Freight cost increases can be passed on to customers; not a challenge for margins
items.quote: freight cost, raw material cost, it's a little easier to pass on. And so we will be able to pass on the increase in cost, we have to absorb certain costs. But going forward, we will be able to pass on the increase in freight cost. We don't see that as a challenge for margins.

items.statement: Rieco transformation to start in September; expect positive year-end and sustainable EBITDA improvement over 2-3 years
items.quote: Going forward this year we don't expect to have a negative impact on the numbers. But going forward, we would definitely look at, I guess, we should give it a two to three years transformation time, and the transformation we're going to kick start in September.

items.statement: Long-term rating upgraded from AA(-) Stable to AA Stable by India Ratings; EcoVadis Gold Medal achieved at 97th percentile
items.quote: I am happy to inform that the long-term external rating of the company has been upgraded by India Rating, a Fitch group company from AA(-) Stab le to AA Stable. While our short-term rating of the company remains affirmed at A1+. This rating upgrade demonstrates strengthening of the business profile, improvement in the financial performance and healthy financial

items.statement: Peak revenue from new CAPEX estimated at Rs. 1,200-1,400 crores at current prices
items.quote: our peak revenue on the new CAPEXs would be about Rs. 1,200 crores to Rs. 1,400 crores.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs. 375 crores; net debt to EBITDA at 1.28x; debt-to-equity at 0.3x
items.quote: The net debt of the company stands at Rs. 375 crores in Q1 at FY '25, down from Rs. 395 crores in Q4 at FY '24. Net debt to EBITDA stands at 1.28x as compared to 2.1x in Q1 FY '24. Debt-to-equity stands as 0.3x as at June 30, compared to 0.5x in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Exit quarter EBITDA margin target of 15% maintained for FY25
items.quote: If you can read my transcript of last quarter also, I have always maintained that H2 will see profitability and exit quarter at 15% is what I have guided for which I still maintain.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to reach 50% by exit quarter FY25 after one more quarter of pressure
items.quote: Gross margin is definitely going to be around 50%.

items.statement: Gross margin to inch up from current 44% to 50% by exit quarter with September quarter remaining under pressure
items.quote: One more quarter of pain, like September should be around this, but from December onwards it should start improving.

items.statement: Target to return to 55% gross margin in FY26
items.quote: Historically we used to be in the range of 50% to 55%. In FY26 our endeavor is to go back to 55%.

items.statement: Festive season and travel portal data indicate better demand despite subdued Q1
items.quote: If I have to talk about the demand indicators, barring Quarter 1, we still feel that festive season, and if you see the travel portal results, everything is pointing towards better demand indicators.

items.quote: The soft luggage inventory has reduced by Rs. 80 crore. So today as we speak number of pieces it is around 6 lakhs, and we are selling 1.5 lakh pieces approximately a month. So, that's where most of this old inventories will get cleared by September.

items.statement: Bangladesh factories in EPZ zones largely unaffected; only 3 days shutdown in 40 days; all factories running normally
items.quote: In fact, in last 40 days of unrest, only three days our factory was shut. Even as we speak, all our factories are up and running. All the employees are present, production is happ ening as desired and Material movement is also happening

items.quote: The worrisome is only the freight rate, which is almost quadrupled compared to what we have seen quarter before so, that's only a cost element to keep in mind when we are looking into a price calibration.

items.statement: Expect to maintain healthy double-digit EBITDA margin supported by energy cost savings and EPR income
items.quote: However, I must admit, demand remained fairly robust. We are sweating our assets and capacity utilizations remain much higher than before. items.quote: In Phase 1, the total capacity of crumb rubber that we will set up will be to the extent of about 40,000 tons to 50,000 tons.

items.statement: New reclaim rubber technology commercialization expected in Q2 FY25, commercial volumes from Q3 FY25 targeting 50% utilization by year-end
items.quote: As announced earlier, our new technology based on lower CO2 emissions and improved product quality are under evaluation with several customers. items.statement: Will not exceed debt-to-EBITDA of 2.5x, current debt-to-EBITDA ~1.6x, debt-to-equity ~0.7x
items.quote: I think we are very clear that we will not exceed debt -to-EBITDA of more than 2.5. I mean that is something that we would be fairly comfortable up to that level. Anything beyon d that, we may not be comfortable taking on

items.quote: We also have approval of the shareholders to raise rights issue of up to INR 40 crores. items.quote: In our efforts to transition to a renewable energy sources to get to about 50% of our stated target, our energy cost savings through a combination of wind mills, biofuels, etcetera, have amounted to about INR 1.65 crores or INR 16.5 million in the current quarter.

items.statement: EPR income of INR 6 crores in Q1 FY25, price range INR 2-4.5 per credit, credits sold on realized basis

items.statement: Expect EPR income every quarter going forward
items.quote: Rohit: So probably, every quarter, we will have some income from EPR, right? Harsh Gandhi: That's fair to assume, yes.

items.statement: Overall asset turn on INR 150 crore capex expected at 2.5-3x minimum on annualized basis
items.quote: So I mean the overall 150 is expected to generate an overall asset turn of between, I would say, 2.5 to 3 at the minimum on a full -- or annualized basis at the minimum.

items.statement: Recovered carbon black at nascent stage, will use continuous process technology, evaluating standards set by tyre companies
items.quote: We will ensure that the technology that we deploy will be,, environmental friendly. It will -- in most -- in all likelihood be a continuous process and will be an environmentally friendly process.

items.quote: The other reason for the likely spurt in the demand is also could be attributed to the high prices of natural rubber and synthetic rubber. items.statement: One-time employee costs of INR 1.2-1.3 crores for 50-year celebrations
items.quote: There were certain one-offs on account of employee costs. I mean, there have been -- as part of the company completing 50 years, there were onetime costs in rewarding several employees across the organization and costs associated with that were partly one-off.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 15-25% maintained for next year
items.quote: Yes, I think we have maintained growth of 15% to 25% in that range going forward, next year also.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to stay at 10-11% for at least a year
items.quote: I think for the time being 10% should be the number you should consider.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow target of Rs 10,000-11,000 crores
items.quote: So, Rs. 10,000 – Rs. 11,000 crores should be okay.

items.statement: FY25 capex target of Rs 150-200 crores

items.statement: International tender pipeline of around Rs 10,000 crores
items.quote: International, very specifically, I can tell you. Around Rs. 10,000 crores. Marine and there is other job also in Middle East around Rs. 10,000 crores.

items.statement: Bangladesh project worth Rs 1,500 crores over 2.5-3 years, FY25 exposure Rs 300-400 crores, currently on hold

items.statement: Overseas projects target higher margins due to fixed-price nature and risk provisions
items.quote: Yes, of course, but the question what you have asked, that is our profession. As a business, we do all these risk analysis, keeping provision, how much margin, which are to target, which are not to target.

items.quote: No. We are not going to solar EPC. For solar EPC, if there is infrastructure required, if they require a big pile foundation, definitely we are there.

items.statement: Targeting capacity utilization in high 90s over next 12-18 months
items.quote: I think we should be looking at utilizing our capacities and taking the utilization levels over, I would say, 90% levels, over the course of the next year. So, I would say 12 to 18 months, that's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Management resists giving specific quarterly or annual growth guidance per IR policy; triple-digit Q1 growth not a standard
items.quote: However, June ‘24 quarter, triple-digit growth percentage should not be taken as a standard. But, there are a variety of reasons and factors , intensified heat wave and climate change whether in the country or globally as we see everywhere will help us a lot.

items.statement: No overhead reduction capex needed for Australia; lease expiry by June 2025 will complete CODB plan
items.quote: We will finally be able to execute everything by June 2025 i.e. when our lease expires. Until then, we will still bear some overhead, which we don't need but from thereafter, there will be almost no overhead that or no CODB that we don't need and our entire CODB reduction plan would have sort of fallen in

items.statement: Australia had orders but logistical delays prevented execution; potential to surpass last year's sales by FY end
items.quote: However, we believe that this is due to - we had the orders, which we could have done certainly better than this , but there were delays (logistical delays), which did not permit us to execute many of the orders that we already had.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin doubled to 21% in Q1 FY25 from 9.3% in Q1 FY24 driven by gross margin expansion and operating leverage
items.quote: So, in June '23 quarter, EBITDA margin was 9.3%, which has grown to 21.0% on account of improvement in gross profit margin by 1.5% at a consol. level, while employee cost, advertisement and sales promotion, freight, rent, travel and other expenses have seen decent positive, mainly on account of huge increase in top line.

items.statement: Strategic price increases planned for some models going forward; no across-the-board hike
items.quote: Yes, yes, yes. Of course, of course. It will all be strategic pricing, there will be price increases in some models and in some, there may not be. So it is all going to be at what serves us best in the market.

items.statement: Demand broadening beyond traditional markets; non-traditional regions like South, East, Northeast seeing strong air cooler demand
items.quote: Very much so. Very much so. We are seeing sort of demand and actions across the country. So as Nrupeshbhai said a little while ago, there was a time when there was a feeling that sun seems to be setting on this category. And this summer has proven that, it is far from true. And we have seen demand for this from markets where we've never seen demand like this . Non-traditional markets like the Sout

items.statement: Launched 17 new air cooler models across 6 ranges (4 new formats) for summer 2025; entered storage water heaters with 3 ranges (SPA, SOUL, SAUNA) featuring PUROPOD filtration and AI smart controller
items.quote: For the coming summer season, we are introducing 17 new models as Nrupeshbhai mentioned and these are spread across 6 product ranges out of which 4 ranges are completely new formats, new performance levels that we are coming up with.

items.statement: Demand-supply mismatch in Q1 left ₹60-80 crore of sales unfulfilled; learnings being implemented for future seasons
items.quote: In fact, we could have done better, and we would have done better had there not been a demand/supply mismatch. We actually maybe left ₹ 70 – 80 crores, ₹ 60 -70 crores, anybody's guess worth of sales on the table.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of ₹71.40 crore at ₹2,500/share (10% of net worth) plus interim dividend of ₹1/share (50% face value) totalling ~₹78 crore; total payout including tax ~₹97 crore
items.quote: So today morning in the board meeting, the Board of Directors has approved buyback amounting to ₹ 71.40 crores, i.e. 10% of the net worth at a price of ₹ 2,500 per share, in addition to interim dividend at 50% i.e. ₹ 1 dividend on a face value of ₹ 2 amounting to about ₹ 7 crores. So all in all, total payout of about ₹ 78 crores and in addition to that, at company level, there we will buy back tax

items.statement: GSK China repaid ~₹7 crore of ₹59 crore loan in Q1 FY25 + July; outstanding now ₹52 crore; further repayment visibility from current business plan
items.quote: And also happy to share that out of about ₹ 59 crores of loans granted by Symphony to GSK China, in June quarter, plus in the month of July so far, ~ ₹ 7 crores has been repaid and hence remaining outstanding is ₹ 52 crores and considering current year's business plan of GSK, we are quite hopeful and there is a decent visibility of additional repayment of loan.

items.statement: Inventory below normal levels at trade and company level across India, Mexico, Brazil, and GSK China
items.quote: In GSK China, Symphony Brazil, IMPCO Mexico as well as Symphony India, the inventory is below normal level , at a trade level as well as at a company level.

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico revenue grew 46% YoY to ₹112 crore; PAT grew 77% to ₹17 crore; first quarter above ₹100 crore revenue
items.quote: For IMPCO Mexico, it is for the first time in any of the quarters, it touched or crossed the turnover of ₹ 100 crores, up from ₹ 77 crores to ₹ 112 crores and PAT up from ₹ 10 crores to ₹ 17 crores.

items.statement: Climate Technologies Australia revenue declined to ₹44 crore from ₹51 crore; PAT contained due to Part 1 transformation execution
items.quote: For Climate Technologies, it is subdued performance, turnover down from ₹ 51 crores to ₹ 44 crores. However, as you can see, still we could contain the PAT, mainly because of part 1 of the transformation has been executed.

items.statement: GSK China revenue grew to ₹16 crore from ₹12 crore; PAT rose to ₹3 crore from ₹1 crore after interest on Symphony loan
items.quote: About GSK China, turnover up from ₹ 12 crores to ₹16 crores. And at a PAT level from ₹ 1 crores to ₹ 3 crores after providing for interest on Symphony loan.

items.statement: Consolidated trailing 12-month revenue ₹1,385 crore (+19% YoY); PAT ₹212 crore (+92% YoY); PAT margin improved ~600 bps; capital employed flat at ₹301 crore
items.quote: if we see the picture in totality of trailing 12 months at a consol. level, the top line stands at ₹ 1,385 crores, up by 19 % and PAT stands at ₹ 212 crores, up from ₹ 110 crores, i.e. 92% growth and PAT margin has improved almost by 600 bps

items.statement: Standalone trailing 12-month revenue ~₹1,000 crore (+17% YoY); PAT ₹207 crore (+35% YoY); capital employed ₹24 crore; treasury ₹491 crore vs ₹342 crore
items.quote: And on trailing 12 months basis, for a stand-alone basis, i.e. 1st July '23 to 30 June '24, top line is almost about ~ ₹ 1,000 crores, up by 17 %; PAT at ₹ 207 crores, up from ₹154 crores i.e. 35% YoY growth. And capital employed in stand -alone business is just about ₹ 24 crores. And now as on 30 June, treasury stands at about ₹ 491 crores versus ₹ 342 crores

items.statement: Expects minimum 15% growth in FY25 and double-digit growth going forward
items.quote: Up to 15% minimum growth will be there. Vinod Sharma: Double digit

items.statement: Export OEM growth expected at least 15% YoY this year and 15-20% next year, continuing for next 3 years
items.quote: Export OEM growth this year compared to last year will be at least 15% more. And the next year, it will be another 15% to 20%. It will keep on growing at least 15% in the next 3 years.

items.statement: BMW order of 35,000 meters expected to be full-fledged by October or November
items.quote: Already started. And by I think -- by October or November, we will get full -fledged order of 35,000 meters.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by export OEM mix, domestic OEM supplies, cost reduction and efficiency improvements
items.quote: Margin expansion is one thing is export business, specifically OEM and then some domestic also, like Volkswagen we are supplying here, like MGR we are supplying here, like bikes -- this thing. So, we have good margin there. Now you can say the reason is one is the product mix, and other is we are working very hard to reduce the costing and as well as increase the efficiency on growth.

items.statement: PVC prices increased 5% due to rising PVC and plasticizer costs
items.quote: In PVC, we have increased on prices because of the PVC raising and plasticizer prices, we have increased 5%.

items.statement: Domestic OEM volume grew 7-8% YoY in Q1 FY25; export OEM volume down but compensated by general export growth
items.quote: Around 7 -8% domestic OEM has increased. OEM export is down but it is compensated by general export.

items.statement: PU plant operating at one-fifth capacity; working with foreign brands for footwear and leather goods; currently incurring losses
items.quote: PU plant is -- we are almost one-fifth we are using and we are working with a lot of big foreign brands to introduce our materials in the footwear and leather goods. And we are

items.statement: Established Lithuania subsidiary for European trading activities in general and furnishing segment
items.quote: Further to start general and furnishing segment business in European regions, we are also going to start trading activities soon through newly established subsidiary company, Lithuania, to cater and supply our products to nearby countries in Europe.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs. 1800 crores to be achieved once three new packing plants are activated
items.quote: In my last concall, I had put a target of Rs. 1800 crores to start with. This is the first target we want to achieve. And we plan to achieve it moment these three plants will be activated.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to return to historical 8-14% range in coming quarters
items.quote: Regarding the margins, if you look at the history of our balance sheets, we normally operate on an EBITDA of between 8% to 14%. So, you can see similar EBITDA margins in the future also.

items.statement: Target EBITDA of Rs. 10 per kg for full year average
items.quote: Normally like we have told in the past also, we work on a margin of Rs. 10 per kilogram. And current inventory June end quarter was Rs. 280 crores. And we are fast finishing that inventory also.

items.statement: Three new packaging units in Karnal; first unit operational in 2-3 months, second in 3 months after, third 3 months after that
items.quote: So, Akash Ji, the first u nit, like I said, three new units are coming up. So, we have completed the flooring of the first unit and in next two to three months, the first unit is going to get operational

items.statement: Each packing unit can add Rs. 70-80 crore quarterly revenue at normal efficiency, up to Rs. 150 crore at full efficiency
items.quote: No, this will be quarterly, but this is the maximum I am saying this is 100% efficiency. Normally, you can take about Rs. 70- Rs. 80 crore every quarter, be on the safer side. This is for one unit, yes.

items.statement: Inventory of Rs. 288 crore mostly order-backed, expected to be liquidated in coming quarter before new season
items.quote: Moreover, our inventory levels were at Rs. 288 crore, which is mostly order backed and is expected to be by and large liquidated in the coming quarter itself before we move into new season.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 8.9% impacted by softening basmati prices and geopolitical issues lowering contract spreads
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at Rs. 32 crores and our margins stood at 8.9% impacted by softening of basmati prices, along with the geopolitical issues leading to some of our new contracts being negotiated at relatively lower spreads.

items.statement: Raw material cost expected 10-15% lower this year with better head grain recovery adding to profit
items.quote: Raw material cost will be lower this time. And I think if the head grain recovery will be better, that means that will be adding to the profit.

items.statement: Freight costs stabilizing after 5-6 months of increases; shifting buyers from CIF to FOB basis
items.quote: Now the freigh t problem also is solving because it's been going on from last five, six months. So, that also is becoming stable, or it is coming down

items.statement: Export volume grew 38% YoY to ~35,000 MT in Q1; domestic business grew 70% to 13% of overall revenue
items.quote: our strong relationships. Our exp ort volume grew by almost 38% y -on-y in Quarter 1, to approximately 35,000 metric tons. This quarter has also seen significantly growth in our domestic business growing by a healthy 70% resulting in an improvement in share to 13% of our overall business

items.statement: Increasing focus on domestic market with dedicated team for premium products like brown rice and dry-heat powder
items.quote: We have put some persons especially to be focused on this thing. And the product, definitely we have better than a lot of our competitors, whether it is brown rice or it is dry-heat powder.

items.statement: Minimum Export Price (MEP) at $950 vs Pakistan's $700 hurting competitiveness; government considering removal
items.quote: The minimum export price you have made 950. And Pakistan very cleverly made their prices MEP 700. So, they have a small crop as compared to India. They will get first opportunity to sell in the international market.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and Red Sea logistics disruptions pressuring margins; FOB model limits freight pass-through
items.quote: This year, because of a problem from Ukraine, then in the Middle East, Red Sea, the logistic cost has gone up. My company works on FOB basis. That is true. But when the rate from $500 coming $4,000, so buyer is not ready to give better price.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of 2 million shares at Rs. 300 per share totaling Rs. 62.04 crore via tender route with promoter participation
items.quote: I am pleased to also announce that this quarter our board has approved a buyback of 2 million shares at Rs. 300 per share, totaling Rs. 62.04 crore. The proposed buyback price is 35% higher compared to yesterday's closing price.

items.statement: Cash and liquid investments of Rs. 150 crore as of June 2023 with near debt-free status
items.quote: As of June 2023, the company had Rs. 150 crore of cash and liquid investments and almost a debt-free status.

items.statement: Q1 was slow due to export postponement and sluggish domestic demand; demand improving since June with Q2 expected to be stronger than Q1
items.quote: So I think quarter 2, we expect it to be -- from the demand side, to be better than what quarter 1 has been.

items.statement: GVT salience rose to 56% from 46% YoY; GVT volumes grew 54% YoY in Q1
items.quote: This 360-degree approach of new products plus sales push plus advertising has driven our vitrified tile salience to 56% versus 46% of last year

items.statement: Gross margins expanded ~1% YoY; EBITDA improved ~2% YoY on like-to-like basis excluding brand spend
items.quote: Thus, driven by improved product mix and lower costs, our gross margins expanded by roughly 1% on a Y-o-Y basis, while the EBITDA too improved by roughly 2% versus last year.

items.statement: ASP down 1% YoY but up 3% QoQ; discounts increased to stay competitive; gas cost blended 40-45 Rs/scm; net fuel cost ~36-38 Rs with biofuel mix
items.quote: On an average, our gas cost would have been between 40-45 across locations. If I count my blessings on AFR, etcetera, biofuels, etcetera, that we use in our spray dryers, you can say INR6-INR7 rupees cheaper there as well.

items.statement: No capex on the table currently; may consider Greenfield, M&A or Brownfield later in the year if aligned
items.quote: Nothing on the table right now.

items.statement: Project sales ~20% in Q1; government projects slowed due to election cycle; private project sentiment more positive for H2
items.quote: So we did 20 in quarter 1.

items.statement: Morbi permanent shutdowns increased to ~290 units (40-50 more); export freight rates up 4-5x causing shipment postponements
items.quote: The number that I saw for July, I think it was 290 or so. Yes, 40-50 more shutdowns, permanent shutdowns.

items.statement: Net debt INR 41 cr for Dora GVT line; repayments start after 1-year moratorium; comfortable with leverage if deployed in productive assets
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, we stay comfortable with net debt at INR41 crores, largely money borrowed to fund the new line, the Dora GVT line.

items.statement: Brand awareness up 50% since Dec 2023 TV campaign; marketing spend 4.2% of revenue in Q1 vs 3.3% YoY; plan to maintain ~4% spend
items.quote: So it shows that there has been a 50% increase in our brand awareness. We still have a long way to go.

items.statement: Dora GVT plant utilization not up to expectations; significant delta remains to be addressed over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: No, it is not up to our expectation. Obviously, there's a lot of work to be done when we are doing that.

items.statement: Solar PPA of 7 MW at Sikandrabad commenced 19 June; Hoskote has existing solar PPA; Dora evaluating options
items.quote: Happy to share that the power flow commenced on the 19th of June. This should help us save more money going forward for our biggest manufacturing facility in North.

items.statement: OBT boutiques grew to 19 new in Q1; OBT share of sales slightly below 50%; OBT dealers get ~10% better margins than project-focused dealers
items.quote: We did 19 new OBTBs, Oriental Tile Boutiques in quarter 1. We expect to do better in quarter two.

items.statement: Antibacterial patented tile targeting institutional/healthcare segment; slow ramp, not expected to contribute meaningfully in near term
items.quote: It will take time, and it will be a slow month. So it is not going to be, so it is more of having a, we agree to do something which is different, and which is nice, but not something which is going to, like, contribute to, say, this quarter or next quarter's revenue.

items.statement: Outstanding order book is about Rs 2,050 crores, roughly 2x FY24 revenues, providing two years of revenue visibility
items.quote: Our outstanding order book remains healthy at about Rs 2,050 crores, roughly, which translates to about 2x of our FY24 revenues and provides a good revenue visibility for two years.

items.statement: Expect to add Rs 500-1000 crores of new orders in FY25
items.quote: As I said that we are expecting to earn anywhere between Rs 500 crores - Rs 1000 crores in terms of new orders.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected in 11-14% range for current order book
items.quote: The margins in these orders are already assured. So, they're already logged in. So, EBITDA margins would be in the double digit, ranging from anywhere between 11% to 14% range.

items.statement: Government focus on hydropower and pump storage with 18,000 MW target by 2032 and 103 GW potential
items.quote: The Union Ministry of Power has said th at government of India has drafted out guidelines of pump storage projects in March 2023 to generate 18,000 megawatts of electricity to bring stability to grids and also meet the peak power demand by 2032

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting from Jal Jeevan Mission and irrigation towards hydropower and pump storage projects
items.quote: In the past, because the mix of revenue in the past two, three years has been from Jal Jeevan Mission and irrigation projects. Going forward, I see this mix more skewed towards hydropower and pump storage projects.

items.statement: Bank guarantee requirement of 10-15% of order value for new projects
items.quote: So, for any project, we require anywhere between 10% to 20% of the order book, of the order value as new bank guarantee limits. So, if you take on an average between 10% to 15% also, that's the level.

items.statement: Bhilwara Jaipur toll road arbitration award reinstated after Commercial Court dismissed PWD appeal; PWD appealed to High Court double bench
items.quote: The appeal made by PWD Government of Rajasthan has been dismissed by the Commercial Court and hence the arbitration award has been reinstated. PWD Government of Rajasthan has appealed against the dec ision of the Commercial Court in the High Court of Rajasthan and more specifically in the double bench because of current rules of arbitration act

items.statement: Bandra project slum clearance timeline uncertain; dependent on Valor Estate
items.quote: Bandra, we don't know in terms of timelines when it is going to -- when the slum is going to be cleared, because it's all a guess work right now.

items.statement: Real estate portfolio expected to realize 100% value in next 2-3 financial years; no new real estate projects planned
items.quote: In the next two to three financial years.

items.statement: Last two quarters of FY25 may witness good progress and strive to match or surpass FY24 levels
items.quote: Last two quarters may witness good progress and we are all striving to match 23-24 levels or surpass it with relevant success support.

items.statement: Hydro-mechanical equipment bid success rate of 30-40%
items.quote: If it's hydro mechanical equipment's, we have a fairly strong share of success there. Our success rate is almost 30% to 40% there.

items.statement: Target AUM of INR 300,000 million by FY27
items.quote: We are well positioned to drive growth and are on track to achieve our target of INR300,000 million AUM by FY27.

items.statement: Expect AUM of INR 200,000-210,000 million in FY25
items.quote: So we would be able to achieve INR 200,000 – INR 210,000 million in FY25, I think we are well within our target to reach INR 300,000 million by FY27.

items.statement: Expect ROE of 10.5%-11% for FY25 and further improvement of 2%-2.5% next year, targeting 15% ROE in FY27
items.quote: In 1QFY25 we are likely to report ROE, in the range of about 10.5% to 11% for FY25. And we believe that next year, ROE should improve further by another 2% to 2.5%. And from there, once we achieve a scale of about INR 250,000 million plus, by then, I think we will be more or less in a steady state in terms of our branch expansion also on the incremental investment in the technology and data scienc

items.statement: Expect insurance distribution net fee income of more than INR 20 crores in FY25
items.quote: We are looking to generate more than INR20 crores in net fee income from insurance distribution in FY25.

items.statement: Plan to add about 50 gold loan branches in current financial year
items.quote: So gold loan segment, we might add about 50 branches in the coming year.

items.statement: Intend to open about 70 micro LAP branches in next 3 quarters, 27 already live
items.quote: We intend to open about 70 branches in next 3 quarters. And already 27 branches have gone live, and we will start seeing some portfolio, but initial few months are the phase where we will build up these branches.

items.statement: AUM reached INR 174,579 million in Q1 FY25, up 56% YoY
items.quote: We maintained a strong growth momentum in Q1 FY25 with our AUM reaching to INR174,579 million, with an increase of 56% year-on-year.

items.statement: Disbursement was INR 56,197 million in Q1 FY25, up 109% YoY
items.quote: Our disbursement was INR56,197 million during the quarter, reflected 109% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Yields at 16.3%, up 70 bps QoQ; spreads at 7%, up 60 bps QoQ
items.quote: Our yields were at 16.3%, an increase of 70 basis points and our spreads reached to 7%, increase of 60 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: NII increased 18% QoQ and 27% YoY to INR 3,013 million
items.quote: The net interest income or NII during Q1 FY25 came in at INR3,013 million, an increase of 18% quarter-on-quarter and 27% year-on-year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 64.6% in Q1 FY25 from 70.5% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: the effect of this already started to reflect in our cost -to-income ratio, which has improved to 64.6% in Q1 FY25, down from 70.5% in Q4 FY24, marking an impro vement of 5.9% in this quarter

items.statement: Cost of funds expected to remain in 9.3%-9.6% range, may increase only 10-20 bps which can be passed on
items.quote: So I think cost of funds in this year should remain by and large in this range. But I believe that cost of funds should not increase. If at all it increases, it will not be more than 10 to 20 basis points, which we should be able to pass on to all the new disbursals, which are happening now.

items.statement: MSME and housing finance growth to resume from Q2 after technology transition stabilization
items.quote: However, we are confident that our growth momentum will be back from Q2 onwards and will continue in coming quarters.

items.statement: Co-lending AUM increased to 16.4% of total AUM from 11.7% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Our co-lending AUM continued to surge during Q1 FY25, increasing to 16.4% of AUM compared to 11.7% in Q4 FY24 and 6.2% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Technical write-off of INR 280 million in construction finance; expect 80-90% recovery
items.quote: Our credit cost increased in Q1 FY25 due to one-off slippages in our construction finance book, resulting in a technical write-off of INR 280 million. However, based on our experience, we are confident of recovering the entire amount.

items.statement: Board approved fund raise of INR 20,000 million via equity, debt or convertible securities
items.quote: Our Board has also approved fund raise of INR 20,000 million by way of equity, debt or convertible securities through rights issu e, preferential allotment or QIP

items.statement: Target double-digit consolidated revenue growth and hold operating margins at FY24 levels in FY25
items.quote: we continue to gun for a double -digit consolidated revenue growth this year by driving outperformance vis -a-vis category and market share gains in the domestic core portfolios, accelerated growths in the foods and the premium care portfolio, and healthy momentum in International business, which will be supplemented by a favorable pricing cycle in key domestic portfolios.

items.statement: Expect digital-first brands to exit FY25 at Rs. 550-600 crores run rate and achieve double-digit EBITDA margin by FY27
items.quote: We expect the digital first brands to exit FY '25 at a Rs. 550-600 crores run rate this year and striving to achieve double -digit EBITDA margin by FY '27.

items.statement: Expect composite share of foods and premium personal care to cross 25% by FY27 with visible profitability improvement
items.quote: We will sustain the aggression to drive 20-25% CAGR in these portfolios and expect the composite share of foods and premium personal care portfolio to cross 25% by FY '27, accompanied by a visible improvement in their profitability.

items.statement: Expect Parachute volume growth to increase gradually from Q2 to Q4 with mid-single-digit growth
items.quote: we expect parachute volume growth to increase gradually as we move in the quarter 2 to quarter 4. And yes, you can expect mid -single-digit volume growth definitely coming in.

items.statement: Pricing growth to pick up from Q2 as Saffola oil price drops move into base and mild copra inflation expected
items.quote: Pricing growth is likely to pick up through the year with Saffola oil price drops moving into the base completely from Q2 and mild inflation expected in some commodities in Q2, particularly copra, which will further aid domestic revenue growth through the course of the year.

items.statement: May take another round of Parachute price hikes if copra prices rise further in H2
items.quote: The pricing growth on account of actions taken so far will flow through entirely from Q2 and we could take possibly another round of price hikes in case of any further rise in copra prices during the course of the next second half of the year.

items.statement: Committed to hold gross and operating margins at FY24 levels in FY25 despite commodity inflation
items.quote: we are definitely committed to hold the gross margins at the levels of FY '24 and similarly at operating margin level, we would hold operating margin in FY '24.

items.statement: Expect volume trends to sustain improving trajectory aided by stable retail inflation, healthy monsoon, and rural budgetary allocation
items.quote: We expect volume trends to sustain the improving trajectory, aided by stable retail inflation, a healthily progressing monsoon season, and the government's budgetary allocation towards boosting the rural economy.

items.statement: Beardo to hit double-digit EBITDA margin in FY25; Plix and Just Herbs scaling with minimal cash burn
items.quote: Beardo will hit double -digit EBITDA margin this year. Just Herbs is tracking well ahead of the Rs. 1 billion ARR mark while the traction in Plix Personal Care portf olio has been encouraging

items.statement: Kaya collaboration expected to be Rs. 100 crores revenue opportunity over next 4 years
items.quote: We believe this is a Rs. 100 crores revenue opportunity over the next 4 years.

items.statement: Project SETU Phase-1 launched in 6 states with promising initial results; will scale up and expand to more states this year
items.quote: launched Phase-1 of Project SETU in 6 states comprising a mix of stronghold and opportunity markets. The initial results have been very promising with direct coverage expansion in urban and rural markets. These new outlets have responded well to the core and new portfolios. During the course of this year, we will scale up Phase -1 markets as well as expand into some more states

items.statement: Export business scaled to $25 million with healthy run; broad-basing reducing Bangladesh concentration risk
items.quote: The export business has scaled to $25 million and continued its healthy run. The broad-basing of the business has not only strengthened the growth prospects of the business but has also added margin upside potential in the medium term and also consistently reducing the concentration risk in Bangladesh business over the last three to four years.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of 30% growth for FY25 and adjusted EBITDA margin of 32-33% maintained
items.quote: Our revenue increased by 26% over the last year and is in sync with a guidance of 30% revenue increase in FY'25. Our EBITDA increased by 9% and is currently at 33% of the revenue which again is in sync with the guidance that we have been giving for our adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: Music licensing plus artist management revenue to grow minimum 25-26% in FY25
items.quote: Overall, we aim for the music vertical - which includes licensing as well as artist management - to grow its revenue by a minimum 25% - 26% during the year.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue excluding Carvaan to grow at 30% CAGR over next 3 years; PBT to double over next 3-4 years
items.value: 30% CAGR revenue growth; PBT to double
items.quote: At the consolidated company level, we expect revenue, excluding Carvaan, to grow at a CAGR of 30% over the next 3 years and PBT to double over the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 32-33% despite step-up in content charge-off
items.quote: On the EBITDA side, we maintain our adjusted EBITDA guidance of 32% to 33% with the strength of -- the IP that we own, a long -term strategic thinking, adequacy of capital on our balance sheet and a fast -growing digital footprint.

items.statement: YouTube revenue pressure in April-May due to political and IPL advertising; stable growth from June onwards
items.quote: On YouTube revenue front , quarter 1 saw some pressure on account of most advertising actually coming from the political advertising or was IPL advertising. June onwards we started seeing very stable growth.

items.statement: Carvaan revenue was INR 24.7 crores in Q1 FY25; shifting to e-commerce and modern trade only, exiting individual retail stores
items.quote: As promised earlier, from this quarter onwards, we have started sharing the Carvaan revenue number separately. This quarter, Carvaan revenue was INR24.7 crores, which is a significant drop over Q1FY24.
