items.statement: Rs 150 crore CAPEX plan on track, 70% for backward integration, 30% for capacity expansion
items.quote: Company is poised to capitalize on the Rs. 150 crore CAPEX plan announced in the last Quarter

items.statement: Backward integration of key intermediates to complete by H1 FY25, capacity expansion by end Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are on track to complete the backward integration of key intermediates by first half of FY25 and increase our production capacity by end of Q4FY 25.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross margin 35%, EBITDA margin 20% (up 104 bps YoY, 670 bps QoQ), PAT margin 10%
items.quote: Notably, our gross margins remain ed strong at 35%, up yearly and sequentially , w hich can be primarily attri buted to lower raw material prices and improved product mix.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 20% for FY25 vs 17% last year, 3% improvement driven by backward integration
items.quote: Last year it was 17%, EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Healthy demand for products, off-patent opportunities, multiple growth opportunities over next 3-5 years
items.quote: With increased healthy demand for our products and off-patent opportunities in the short term, we anticipate multiple growth opportunities over the next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Sustained growth expected in ARVs, anti-diabetic, ibuprofen supported by stable raw material prices and expanding customer base
items.quote: We anticipate sustained growth in our key market segments, particularly in ARVs, anti-diabetic products and ibuprofen supported by stable raw material prices and an expanding customer base for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Revenue growth led by anti-diabetic and ibuprofen segments, anti-diabetic has >50% market share in Europe
items.quote: Our Revenue Growth was led by robust growth in anti -diabetic and ibuprofen segments.

items.statement: Anti-diabetic, anti-ARV, ibuprofen are key therapeutic areas; 5-6 products backward integrated to KSM level
items.quote: Around 5 to 6 products.

items.statement: Backward integration projects for Sitagliptin (8 stages in-house, up from 2) and Tenofovir (1-2 stages)
items.quote: Right now, we are planning to do around 8 stages in-house for Sitagliptin.

items.statement: Ibuprofen margins lower due to commoditization, anti-retroviral margins thin (CMO), anti-diabetic mid to lower teens
items.quote: definitely ibuprofen margins will be on the low side because being a commoditized product, it will be definitely much lower and again, even anti-retroviral also it is CMO based. So, margins there also will be quite thin.

items.statement: Targets minimum 20-25% year-on-year revenue growth going forward
items.quote: going forward that is our target, at least grow by a minimum of 20% year-on-year.

items.statement: CAPEX split approximately 70% backward integration (Rs 70 crore), 30% capacity expansion for existing products
items.quote: probably percentage wise I think maybe 70% will be for backward integration and I think around 30% for capacity expansion for the existing products.

items.statement: Board approved subsidiary for CRO services for peptides, preliminary stage, smaller investment
items.quote: The Board of Directors has principally approved our decision to set up a subsidiary company in India for Contract Research Organization (CRO) services for peptides, which we believe shows high growth potential.

items.statement: Reducing dependency on Chinese suppliers for key intermediates via backward integration
items.quote: we are trying to see where we reduce our dependency on some Chinese customers, and we want to bring these products in-house.

items.statement: Capacity utilization currently 70%, targeting ~80% by end of FY25
items.quote: Our current capacity utilization is within the range of 70% and by end of FY25, we anticipate crossing a utilization rate of around 80%.

items.statement: Guided for 20% EBITDA margin for full-year hospital business and well on track
items.quote: So, consolidated margin for the full Hospital business , we have guided 20% EBITDA margin, and we are well on track on that.

items.statement: Targeted around 19% EBITDA margin for Q1 hospital business and achieved that level
items.quote: 1st Quarter, we have targeted around 19% EBITDA margin, and we are around that level.

items.statement: Planned brownfield expansions at Faridabad, Anandpur, Shalimar Bagh, Noida; Manesar 350-bed facility to be operational in ongoing quarter
items.quote: We are progressing well on our brownfield expansion planned for this year, and we will be adding capacities across our key facilities, including Faridabad, Anandpur, Shalimar Bagh and Noida. In addition, we expect the 350 -bed Manesar facility that we acquired in Financial Year ‘24 to be operational in the ongoing quarter.

items.statement: Manesar facility to start with 100 beds and ramp to full 350 beds in ~18 months
items.quote: So, Manesar, the facilities have a total capacity of around 350 beds. So, we will be initially operationalizing around 100 beds. And once we reach a particular occupancy level of 100 beds, say, 60%, 65% occupancy level, then we will open up the balance beds. So, it will be gradual. And in our estimate, if things go as per our plan, we will be able to operationalize all 350 beds in, say, 18 months'

items.statement: Hospital EBITDA margin improved 330 bps YoY to 18.5% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The Hospital business operating EBITDA was Rs. 287 crores, resulting in improvement in margins by a strong 330 basis points from 15.2% in Q1 of Financial Year ‘24 to 18.5% in Q1 of Financial Year ‘25.

items.statement: Hospital ARPOB grew 9.7% YoY to Rs 2.41 crore per annum in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our Hospital Business saw a 9.7% increase in ARPOB, reaching Rs. 2.41 crores per annum.

items.statement: Diagnostics took small price increase on B2C walk-in business at end of Q4 FY24; impact not significant due to discounting
items.quote: So, in fact, we have taken a small price increase around the end of Q4 of last year. That's only on the B2C business, on the walk -in business, and also only in some of the segments that we have taken. So, overall, the impact is not very significant, as we also do some discounting on that business at this point of time for brand promotion.

items.statement: Hospital occupancy improved to 67% in Q1 FY25 from 64% YoY; occupied beds up 4.6% to 2,715
items.quote: Generally, Q1 is a relatively softer quarter , however, our hospital occupancy improved to 67% compared to 64% in Q1 of Financial Year ‘24. This translated into occupied beds increasing by 4.6% to 2,715 compared to 2,595 in Q1 of Financial Year ‘24.

items.statement: Key specialties (oncology, neuro, cardiac, ortho, gastro, renal) grew 15.7% YoY and contributed 63% of hospital revenue
items.quote: Collectively, these specialties achieved a 15.7% year-on-year growth and contributed 63% of the total hospital revenues, which is on the similar lines as Q1 of Financial Year ‘24.

items.statement: Legal costs expected to remain high in FY25 as court order awaited and potential appeals possible
items.quote: Not really, because just the hearing is completed. I don't know what will be the reaction of Daiichi, whether they will appeal in the higher court and things like that. And we have not come out from the woods completely. We have yet to receive the order. So, all those things will determine the legal cost. So, my estimate is legal cost will continue to be high in this year.

items.statement: Digital channel revenues grew 52% YoY and 17% QoQ, contributing ~30% of hospital revenue in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Revenues from website, mobile applications, and digital campaigns witnessed a 52% year -over-year growth and 17% quarter-on-quarter growth in Q1 of Financial Year ‘2 5. R evenues from digital channels contributed almost 30% to overall hospital revenues versus 23% in Q1 of Financial Year ‘24.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR5,600-5,700 crores for FY25, implying 15% YoY growth
items.quote: Well, so we are looking at an order -- top line close to around INR5,600 crores to INR5,700 crores for this fiscal year which will be a 15% growth on the year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Target to become $1 billion revenue company by FY27 with order book of INR25,000 crores
items.value: $1 billion revenue, INR25,000 crores order book
items.quote: And we want to be a $1 billion revenue company by FY '27 with the order book of around INR25,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 15-16% in coming 6-8 quarters, up from current 14-15%
items.quote: With similar margins of like 14% to 15% what we are getting in the last 4, 5 years, we expect going forward in coming 6 to 8 quarters, our margins will improve from 14% to 15% to 15% to 16%, 1% which is more.

items.statement: Order book of INR19,820 crores as of June 30, 2024 with metro 26%, elevated corridors 39%, road/tunnel 24%, others 11%
items.quote: The total order book as on 30th June '24 stood at INR19,820 crores. The order book includes metro projects contributing around 26%, elevated corridor flyovers contributing around 39%, road and tunnel projects contributing 24%, and others contributing around 11%.

items.statement: Already L1 on projects worth INR6,500 crores, targeting INR8,000 crores order inflows for FY25
items.quote: Alok, this year, we have already bagged -- we are already L1 projects worth around INR6,500 crores. And we are looking at an order book close to INR8,000 crores for this financial year.

items.statement: Capex of INR450-500 crores over next 2 years for Chennai and GMLR projects, Q1 FY25 capex was INR28 crores
items.quote: But in the coming 2 years, we are expecting a capex of INR450 crores to INR500 crores, mainly coming in from Chennai and GMLR 2 projects.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 14.4% vs 14.3% YoY, PAT margin at 6.7% vs 6.4% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margin in Q1 stood at 14.4% as compared to 14.3% in previous year. The net profit for Q1 FY '25 grew by 19% to INR86 crores, and the PAT margin stood at 6.7% as compared to 6.4% in Q1 of FY '24.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline of INR20,000-30,000 crores over next 9 months across metro, road tunnels, elevated corridors, irrigation
items.quote: So we are expecting additional orders to be booked in the range of -- additional orders to be bidded in the coming 9 months to the range of around INR20,000 crores or INR30,000 crores.

items.statement: Debt level guidance of INR700-750 crores for FY25 and FY26, internal threshold to keep debt-to-equity below 0.5x
items.quote: So FY '25, we are looking at a debt level of INR700 crores to INR750 crores. And going forward, in FY '26, it will totally depend upon the cash flow of the project. So we feel that we should be able to maintain the debt level to INR700 crores to INR750 crores for FY '26 as well.

items.statement: Board passed enabling resolution for QIP fund raise for growth capital and capex, no timeline initiated yet
items.quote: This is an enabling resolution for raising fund in form of QIP. And we are seeing a lot of work inflow or order inflows coming in. So we are preparing ourselves for the right moment to -- and we don't want to over -dependent on the banks as well.

items.statement: GMLR project: TBM PAT test in Jan and Mar, full execution post-monsoon, 50% revenue share via SPV consolidated
items.quote: The PAT test for the TBM machine is going to be in the month of Jan for first TBM and, yes, in the month of March for the second TBM. As well as all the drawings has been submitted with preliminary designs, the GAD, the segment design submission.

items.statement: Chennai project: Avoided 11-11.5% mobilization advance cost by using 9% bank CC limit, saving 2.5-3%
items.quote: So for Chennai, it's like we are getting from SBI at 9%. And the other rate, it's going to be with NHAI. Considering the bank guarantee charges and all, it would have gone to around 11%, 11.5%. So that's why we have gone in Chennai for CC limit.

items.statement: Working capital cycle target of 120-125 days, currently at 126 days in Q1 FY25
items.quote: So we intend to maintain a net working capital cycle close to around 125 days. So currently, in this quarter, it is 126. But if you look at FY '24, it was -- on an annual basis, it was 123.

items.statement: Cash position of INR640 crores as of June 30, 2024, up from INR630 crores in March
items.quote: INR640 crores is the precise number. Yes.

items.statement: Metro opportunities in Patna, Bhubaneswar, Indore, Bhopal, Nagpur, Pune, Mumbai Line 10; underground metro projects of INR1,500-2,000 crores
items.quote: So there are new projects that are coming up in Patna, in Bhubaneswar, in Indore, in Bhopal. Nagpur is coming up with new line. This Pune is coming up with an additional line. Bombay Metro has Metro Line 10, which is going to come up.

items.statement: MSRDC project LOI expected by month-end, work to start post-monsoon, revenue likely from FY26
items.quote: In Board meeting, like it will be taken forward. And like accordingly, they are in the process of finalizing the contract. So by this month end, we are expecting the LOI from them.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 order booking grew 40% y-o-y to a record ₹6.36 billion, with exports contributing 66%.
items.quote: Order booking for the quarter grew by 40% to ₹6.36 billion, with exports contributing 66% of the overall order booking.

items.statement: Total consolidated outstanding order book stood at ₹17.26 billion as of June 30, 2024, up 23% y-o-y.
items.quote: The total consolidated outstanding order book stood at ₹17.26 billion as on the 30 th of June 2024, which is higher b y 23% when compared to the previous year

items.statement: Export outstanding order book rose 65% to ₹10.05 billion, now 58% of closing order book.
items.quote: And the export outstanding order book stood at ₹10.05 billion, up 65% and now contributes 58% of our closing order book.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded ~240 bps to 24.8% in Q1 FY25 driven by export and aftermarket mix.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter increased by 36% to ₹1.15 billion in the Q1 FY 25 as opposed to ₹843 million in Q1 FY 24, and margins increased by 240 basis points to 24.8% as against 22.4% in the period of the last year.

items.statement: Management expects margins to remain robust due to higher export and aftermarket share in order book.
items.quote: Margins have not been a problem, and as we have spoken about in our previous conference calls, we do not see margins as being the biggest issue as the composition of our order book, and therefore, the resultant composition of our revenue will be skewed more towards exports and aftermarkets, which offer us better margins.

items.statement: Domestic enquiry book grew ~14% y-o-y; order finalisations expected to pick up in coming quarters after election-related delays.
items.quote: The enquiry book has grown by about 14%, but you have to recogni se that we have had a fall in enquiry book sometime last year the same period. Having said that, overall, on a y-o-y basis, we do see growth

items.statement: Domestic customers now asking for shorter deliveries, indicating urgency in capex decisions.
items.quote: We are, in fact, seeing customers wanting shorter deliveries, and we think that the domestic market will be a source of growth for Triveni Turbines, not only in the coming quarters, but in the years to come.

items.statement: U.S. subsidiary investment may incur ~₹20 crore loss in FY25; hiring local talent driving early enquiry growth.
items.quote: But it's an investment-heavy strategy where we are going to probably incur a loss of maybe ₹20-odd crore on the subsidiary this current year.

items.statement: Product range extended beyond 120 MW targeting large integrated steel, oil & gas, pulp & paper; commercial sales expected soon.
items.quote: As going forward, we have to see how these enquiries queue up and take us to that level.

items.statement: Aftermarket order booking grew 3% to ₹1.5 billion; turnover up 21% to ₹1.56 billion (34% of total).
items.quote: The Aftermarket segment order booking for the quarter stood at ₹1.5 billion, which is a growth of 3% when compared to the corresponding period of the previous year.

items.statement: Order intake is lumpy; management cautions against extrapolating Q1's 74% export order growth for full year.
items.quote: this growth of order book to ₹6.36 billion is truly remarkable, I would caution you when extrapolating this for the rest of the year, though we are confident that we will have good growth in both order booking as well as revenue for this current year

items.statement: Order book visibility now stretches into FY26 due to larger MW orders with longer delivery cycles.
items.quote: The end order book for Triveni T urbines gives us comfort not only for the revenues for FY 25, but in fact, actually, because of some of the larger megawatt orders that we have in our order book, this provides us visibility stretching into FY 26 as

items.statement: Commodity price volatility has ended; better predictability enables longer-term supplier contracts and cost visibility.
items.quote: More than that, the volatility that we have seen in commodity prices over the COVID period has come to an end. It is not as if there isn't any commodity inflation, but the predictability of that is far more, and so we can have longer term and better contracts with our partners and suppliers and vendors, which gives us visibility into costs as we go forward.

items.statement: R&D spend to increase on new product introductions, higher MW ranges, blade tech, and adjacent rotating equipment technologies.
items.quote: We will increasingly be spending more on R&D. And those are data that will come out through our annual report, so you'll be able to see what the investments are.

items.statement: Dividend policy consistent; capex to remain asset-light but will invest for customer proximity and localisation.
items.quote: We are consistent on our dividend policy, and I think that that's something that will continue. The capex, we will continue with our strategy of being asset light. But wherever investments are required for us to be close to the customers, we will not shy away from that.

items.statement: Export market share gains confirmed as overall market stable; API segment still low share but growing.
items.quote: Yeah. Well, pretty much we could sa y that since we are seeing the overall market to be quite constant, this is obviously market share gain

items.statement: Targeting 6-8 new restaurant openings by end of FY25, with 3-4 almost ready for Durga Pooja
items.quote: We are looking at between six to eight restaurants, which are under fit outs, three, four of them almost, some by Durga Pooja in Calcutta, some in terms of, you know, Borivali, Oberoi Mall, we have two, three restaurants, thr ee restaurants there

items.statement: Bare minimum 7-9 new restaurants by end of FY25 depending on real estate readiness
items.quote: So 25 end, we are looking at bare minimum of around seven to nine, depending on Borivali Mall, which can supply us because that's been delayed beyond our comprehension.

items.statement: New restaurants take 9-12 months to break even, impacting near-term EBITDA
items.quote: all the EBITDAs if you see that there's a little coming down from the expected le vels is because of the fact that these restaurants have opened and they take anywhere between 9 to 12 months to break even

items.statement: Targeting 20-24% EBITDA margin range, with internal goal to reach 20-22% by FY26
items.quote: We would target to be plus 20%, 22%, but in the range of 20% to 24% of EBITDA, sir.

items.statement: Confident of improving EBITDA margins as efficiency improves and corporate costs decrease
items.quote: I'm sure of the fact that the margins will improve.

items.statement: Food costs increased due to supplier constraints; pricing lever not fully pressed yet, expect price hikes in Q2
items.quote: in the second quarter, we will have to go up by nothing less than not just an in flationary pressure. The price play and the lever has not been pressed as yet

items.statement: Revenge eating headwind affected Q1 across industry; elections caused 3-4 day closures in some cities
items.quote: There's been one headwind from the market, which is the last thing I want to express, that the revenge eating, which used to be there, if you see the, I'm not saying that just because the others have not done so well, we should have also not done well, but it's an overall headwind, which has gone into the market.

items.statement: Renovated outlets show 15-25% dine-in revenue growth; liquor contribution doubled from 6-7% to ~13-14% post-renovation
items.quote: Wherever we have undergone a renovation and introduced a new menu, new branding, new bar, we have seen anywhere between a 15 to 25 percent growth in the dine-in revenue.

items.statement: Sweet Bengal brand expanding via FMCG partnerships for shelf-stable sweets; products targeted by end of FY25
items.quote: By the end of this fiscal year, we should have the products ready, available at different stores, online retailers, and so on.

items.statement: Warrant forfeiture brought INR 52 crores; invested in mutual funds and deployed for renovations and new restaurants
items.quote: Post the forfeiture, the amount which has come is INR52 crores f rom the warrants issue. We currently are having those invested part of the money which has been invested into mutual funds, and partly being utilized for the objects in the issue of renovation and the new restaurants

items.statement: No inorganic acquisitions unless target has positive EBITDA and potential; avoiding past mistakes of over-expansion and cannibalization
items.quote: We are not in QSR. So even QSR, one of the burger brands which we were talking about growing very fast, but they were unable to actually get into a level of profitability in next three years, four years.

items.statement: Hiring external CEO by end of FY25 (max March) to independently run operations and report to board
items.quote: we are going to be inducting a CEO. Finally, we've been able to get somebody of choice. So maybe within th is fiscal, by the end of the year, you will see somebody very competent who's coming in , to independently run the company and get us

items.statement: Cash balance of INR 163.84 crores as of June 30; fully diluted equity capital INR 48.23 crores post warrant conversion
items.quote: Sir, as of 30th June, we have INR163.84 crores.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of 2,191 MW with 217 MW executed in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We have an unexecuted order book of 2,191 MW and we have successfully executed 217 MW during first quarter of FY2025.

items.statement: Expect to execute roughly 75% of leftover order book (~1.8 GW) over next 9-12 months
items.quote: If you take 2.1 gigawatt and if you take 75%, we should be somewhere around 1.8 gigawatt roughly.

items.statement: Stable EBITDA margin model at 15% range, currently above 17% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The most stable margins is in the 15% kind of a range. Though this quarter also we have not beaten and we have been at higher than 17%.

items.statement: Bid pipeline currently at 15.5 GW across renewable energy projects including BESS, hybrid, RTC
items.quote: Current bid pipeline is, today as we speak, is 15.5 gigawatt.

items.statement: No significant capex needed; can scale 3x without additional capital expenditure
items.quote: We are like a platform. If you want to give me today, like I have got 2 gigawatt, if you want to give me 3x business, I can deliver 3x business without adding any additio nal capital expenditure

items.statement: Module procurement is back-to-back locked at order confirmation; margins protected from price volatility
items.quote: As soon as we get an order and our margins are visible there, we immediately lock in prices for modules. And it's back to back.

items.statement: Order book split 30-35% with module, 65-70% balance of systems; 5B Maverick deployment expected in couple of months
items.quote: We normally tend to be in the range of 30% to 35% with module and 65% to 70% without module, which we call as balance of systems as our projects.

items.statement: No significant risk seen in upcoming quarter except monsoon rains; no bank guarantees invoked to date
items.quote: Except for monsoon rains, we don't see any significant risk in the upcoming quarter that we need to address.

items.statement: IPP portfolio generated ~7.5 crore revenue in Q1 FY25; 40 MW capacity
items.quote: So, we have generated seven and half crores, little less than 7.5 crores for our IPP plants revenues in first quarter.

items.statement: 5B Maverick partnership exclusive for domestic market; test production completed, deployment expected in couple of months
items.quote: 5B Maverick has completed its test production, etc. In coming couple of months, we might see some of the deployments in terms of 5B Maverick in Waaree Renewable.

items.statement: Target to reach pre-COVID EBITDA margin of ~8.5% by end of FY26 with two consecutive years of ~10% SSG
items.quote: We did guide towards growing at two consecutive years of around 10% SSG or high single-digit SSG to reach that level by then we should be able to get back to the pre-COVID EBITDA margin level of around 8.5%.

items.statement: LimeRoad EBITDA loss to reduce quarter-on-quarter; full year loss expected to be less than 50% of prior year
items.quote: We will definitely want to improve the quarter-on-quarter performance in terms of losses, but the full year number should definitely be lesser.

items.statement: INR 26 crores spent in Q1 FY25 on new store openings and refurbishments
items.quote: On the capex side, we spent INR 26 crores during the quarter or paid out INR 26 crores majorly on new store openings and store refurbishments.

items.statement: Plan to open 50-odd stores gross in FY25, mostly in Q2 and Q3; only 3-4 regular closures expected
items.quote: The runway for the year is still mai ntained at 50-odd stores, a large part of which will be open between quarter 2 and quarter 3. Most of the unprofitable store closures have already been completed now

items.statement: Offline gross margins to remain at FY24 levels; focus on rupee margin growth via volumes not percentage expansion
items.quote: On a full year basis, the gross margins from offline business would remain at similar levels of last year as we continue to drive giving higher value to our customers and focusing on growth through volumes.

items.statement: Q1 V-Mart core EBITDA 13.4%, Unlimited 18%, entity 12.6% including INR 10 cr LimeRoad loss
items.quote: Moving on to EBITDA for the V- Mart core business, EBITDA for the quarter was 13.4% with u nlimited at 18%. At the entity level, the EBITDA stood at 12.6% which includes a loss of INR 10 crores coming in from

items.statement: Apparel ASP declined 3% YoY due to product mix (zero weddings in North) and strategic value pricing in South; price correction complete, ASPs to stabilize
items.quote: The apparel ASP de grew by 3%, largely due to the product mix change as a fallout of zero weddings during the quarter in north. While in south, the ASP degrowth was a fallout of the strategic shift towards sharper and more value-driven product pricing.

items.statement: Focus on Gen Z fashion, quality, agility; freshness index improved ~10%; assortment shifting to trend-driven, agile model
items.quote: We've really worked very highly on the whole freshness index. And the freshness is the inventory freshness and that has been key to us. And that is also resulted due to some margin losses because we've also come on inventory prior to liquidate inventory at a discount. So, our freshness index has bettered by almost 10%.

items.statement: Inflation ~5% on high base still pressures households earning INR 20k-35k; competitive pressure in premium and value segments
items.quote: But still the inflation rate continues around 5%, still on the high base, so that is still a problem to a n Indian consumer into a normal household, which is earning between INR 20,000 and INR 35,000

items.statement: Marketing spend cut 59% YoY to INR 12 cr; offline marketing down ~44%; NPS >60, 5L+ Google reviews at 4.4+
items.quote: In line with our strategy on making the LimeRoad business sustainable, we cut down on the marketing spend, which impacted the top line growth, which reduced by 33% year-on-year to INR 12 crores from INR 17 crores last year.

items.statement: Manpower cost up 17% YoY due to increments, higher ESOP and incentive payouts; largely variable and linked to performance
items.quote: The manpower cost was up by 17% on the back of the annual increments slightly higher ESOP expenditure and also increased incentive payouts in line with the sales growth.

items.statement: Inventory down INR 144 cr QoQ; free cash flow INR 43 cr; working capital improvement seasonal but trending better each quarter
items.quote: Inventory reduced by INR 144 crores quarter-on-quarter helping improve the working capital cycle and also it will help in improving freshness for the upcoming festive season even more. Free cash flow for the quarter stood at INR 43 crores.

items.statement: Management refrains from giving quarterly or annual guidance due to market volatility and geopolitical tensions.
items.quote: giving guidance on one particular year or one particular quarter, I think that's something which is difficult and now as you are seeing that geopolitical tensions, etc, are heightened and there is a lot of volatility in the market, and we refrain from giving any quarter or even annual guidance per se.

items.statement: Long-term strategy targets outperforming industry growth over the next 5 years.
items.quote: However, we would, in the long term, be outperforming overall industry growth like we have. And on a long-term basis, we can expect a very good outperformance.

items.statement: TREM V norms for tractors/off-highway deferred to 1 April 2026; OEM nominations on track.
items.quote: the time lines have been modified for 1 April 2026. And so far, all the OEMs have nominated in developing the products on track for 1 April 2026.

items.statement: Exports currently less than 2% of sales; targeting commercial vehicle emission components, off-highway adjacencies, small genset emissions, and sub-100HP tractors in US/Europe.
items.quote: exports currently is less than 2% of sales. And what makes us confident is that we are one of the only emission companies in the world who can cater to this market.

items.statement: Export margins higher than domestic but working capital needs also higher; ROCE similar or slightly better.
items.quote: the margins are much better in exports than in Indian business. However, the working capital requirement in exports is also higher than India n business. On a net basis, if you neutralize a higher margin and higher working capital requirement, from a ROCE perspective, it is similar or maybe slightly better

items.statement: Genset emission systems export market booming in US driven by data center demand; already supplying to top global player.
items.quote: genset market is going through a boom right now in the U.S. It is something that is growing very, very fast. It's something we didn't expect also that gensets would become so prominent in the U.S., but that's backed by the data center book.

items.statement: M&A focus on powertrain-agnostic products; no debt needed currently; land parcels available for monetization alongside cash reserves.
items.quote: we are not planning to do something that will be significantly large, at least unless it fits right into our strategy. So most likely, we would not require any debt at this juncture and funding any kind of for M&A. And we do have additional land parcels available, which we are looking to monetize and that, of course, is in addition to

items.statement: Incremental cash reserves to be returned to shareholders via dividends or buybacks; intention not to hold cash much beyond current levels.
items.quote: intention is not to keep cash reserve much beyond what we have already. So all the incremental cash reserve that keeps coming in would be returned back, and that can be in the for m of dividends, buybacks or anything else

items.statement: Export RFQ pipeline strong with multiple OEMs in various discussion stages; initial orders will be pilots growing over time.
items.quote: we have a very good RFQ pipeline, we've added and built a very good team, which is focused on exports. We do expect good customer additions. But of course, exports is also about building trust. So initial orders will be pilots and will grow over time.

items.statement: Zero market share in 3-4L commercial vehicle ICE segment; technology and product now ready to target competitor's domain.
items.quote: Currently, we have no market share. So now we have the technology and product ready. So we will be looking to increase market share substantially in that segment.

items.statement: Lightweighting vertical (currently ~8% of sales) capital allocation decisions based on ROCE; new control arm plant for new platform, margins too early to comment.
items.quote: all our capital allocation decisions are taken with ROCE in mind, right? So this project is looking good from the ROCE perspective. In terms of individual margins and product margins, that's something which I will not comment for the time.

items.statement: Buyback of 10,27,777 shares at Rs.1,800/share completed for Rs.185 crores; cash reserve Rs.778 crores as of June 30, 2024.
items.quote: The company has bought back 10,27,777 equity shares at Rs. 1,800 per share, totalling to Rs.185 crores. Following the completion of this buyback, the company's remaining cash reserve stands at Rs.778 crores as of June 30, 2024.

items.statement: Management withdrew FY25 volume growth guidance of 8% after 15% degrowth in Q1 and expects to struggle to match last year's volumes in Q2; will reassess after monsoon
items.quote: We already had 15% degrowth in Q1, right? Keshav: Right. Deepak Khetrapal: Q2, as of now, I think we'll struggle to make the same as last year. So if the first half of the year does not give us the required growth, obviously, the full year forecast needs to be relooked at

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at INR200-300 crores vs earlier INR1,000 crores guidance; Chittapur INR100 crores, Sarni INR25-30 crores, Rajasthan land INR100 crores, Devapur forest clearance payment INR150 crores
items.quote: Again, the first question sorry I just say a couple of maybe INR200 crores to INR300 crores not more than that.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton increased to INR750 in Q1 FY25 from INR650 in Q1 FY24 despite 15% volume degrowth, driven by stable pricing and lower fuel costs
items.quote: I don't think there's any one company in the industry which would have reported an increase in EBITDA per ton over last year's same quarter. And we were at about INR650 last year, we were around INR750 this year

items.statement: Power and fuel cost per ton of cement fell to INR1,337 in Q1 FY25 from INR1,571 in Q1 FY24 and INR1,351 in Q4 FY24; blended fuel cost INR1,785 per million kcal vs INR2,100 last year
items.quote: In Q1, the power and fuel costs for us are down to the INR1,337 per metric ton of cement, which is down from INR1,571 in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Cement prices in July down 2.5-3% sequentially; July and early August volumes and pricing remain very soft due to persistent rains
items.quote: I would say it is in the region 2.5%, 3% in July over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Q1 demand severely impacted by national elections, extreme heat wave halting construction, and heavy June rains across all markets; Telangana and Karnataka seeing high double-digit degrowth, Maharashtra down 5.5%
items.quote: What's unusual about Q1 quarter this year has been the fact that even Maharashtra, total demand, including Mumbai city, the demand is down over last year.

items.statement: Management expects sharp demand recovery post-monsoon due to pent-up construction and repair work from heavy rain damage, but signals of pickup in Telangana yet to emerge
items.quote: We do expect the demand to rise sharply once the rains stop, because the construction activity has been held up. There's a lot of pent-up, catch-up work that needs to be done

items.statement: Premium cement share reached 23% of total sales in Q1 FY25, nearing 25% target; OPC share remains high at 45-47% of unblended cement due to weak trade demand
items.quote: In Q1 of this year the overall proportion of our premium cements put together has reached 23% and we are very close from the beginning when we started, our target initially was 10%, then we said we want to go to 25%

items.statement: Industry leaders' aggressive capacity additions (organic and acquisitions) and volume-first strategy keeping prices low; pan-India utilization struggling to reach 70%
items.quote: The only way prices become stable is when people accept the fact that trying to sell to the market more volume at a lower price does not help anyone.

items.statement: Green power share reached 24% in Q1 FY25 (highest ever) from 12% last year; waste heat recovery contributed INR9 crores, solar INR2.5 crores in Q1; Chittapur solar expected by mid-September
items.quote: Our total, I would say, green power component in Q1 has reached a high of 24%, which is ever highest for us

items.statement: Chittapur expansion (3 mt cement) and Sarni grinding unit (2 mt) combined capex ~INR2,000 crores; Devapur expansion (2 mt clinker + 1 mt grinding + WHR + wagon tippler) estimated INR1,700-1,800 crores later
items.quote: Chittapur was INR1,500 crores and 500 for Sarni. So, then in terms of project, the y are two different projects, the total capex will be about 2,000

items.statement: Chittapur environment clearance application submitted; expects committee hearing by end-August; Sarni term alteration informally approved by MP Power Gen Board, awaiting formal letter; Devapur forest clearance at Minister level in Telangana
items.quote: We are still expecting that, hopefully, in the meeting that they will hold perhaps towards the end of August, our applications would be coming up before the committee for presentation.

items.statement: Maintained price realizations stable (down only ~1% YoY) while industry lost realizations; refused B2B orders below contribution threshold; aligned trade prices with Category A brands
items.quote: We've seen industry results. And I think any company which operates in our markets, if you look at, they have actually lost realizations per ton on the cement they have sold. We have more or less kept it stable.

items.statement: Trade share 44%, B2B 56% in Q1; lead distance 300-320 km maintained; July volumes very soft, struggling to match last year's Q2 volumes
items.quote: Trade share for us -- I did mention that B2B sales is perhaps 56% and balance 44% would be Trade, yes.

items.statement: Rajasthan limestone land acquisition still in negotiations, no deals closed; Devapur forest clearance payment of INR150 crores critical for Stage 2 conversion this year
items.quote: No, we have still -- we are in negotiations, but we've not closed any deals for the land in Rajasthan. Not till now.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin guidance maintained at around 18% for FY25
items.quote: But as is basis, currently, we are maintaining our guidance of around 18%.

items.statement: Full-year gross margin guidance increased to 62%-62.5% for FY25
items.quote: in our last call also, we have shared that our gross margin for the full year increased in the range of 62% to 62.5

items.statement: India business growth guidance in line with market at 8%-10% for FY25
items.quote: I'm expecting the mark et to grow somewhere between 8% to 10% and should be similar for us as well

items.statement: US business expected to grow at single-digit for FY25
items.quote: So in terms of our U.S. growth, I've always maintained, we are looking at a s ingle-digit growth from U.S. market

items.statement: Non-US business expected to grow at mid-teens over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So I maintained the non-U.S. business, we would see mid-teens kind of growth even in the coming years, and that is what we are focusing on.

items.statement: Full-year tax rate guidance revised to 11%-13% for FY25
items.quote: So it will be in the range of 11% to 13% for the full year.

items.statement: R&D expense expected at 4.5%-5% of sales for FY25
items.quote: The annual spend will be within the range of 4.5% to 5% and in terms of absolute.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 700 bps YoY to 20.1%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin improved by 700 basis points as compared to last Q1. So from 13.1%, we have improved it to 20.1% for the quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement of ~150 bps expected for full year FY25
items.quote: we see it improve -- further improvement of around, say, 150 basis points in our gross margin for the full year.

items.statement: API price reductions in dapagliflozin, sitagliptin, and paracetamol benefiting margins
items.quote: We had, say, for example, dapagliflozin, we had sitagliptin. These are now substantial value products for us, and we have a significant reduction in some of these molecules on the API pricing.

items.statement: Penicillin G prices seeing marginal increase, no softening yet from Chinese suppliers
items.quote: In fact, in the recent times, I'm seeing that Pen G prices are even seeing a marginal increase. So unless we see the large Indian players coming up in market with the offerings, I don't think we are seeing softening in the China suppliers on the PenG.

items.statement: Non-NLEM portfolio price increases realized at 5%-6% annually vs 10% allowed
items.quote: Generally, we get 5% to 6% increase on the annualized basis.

items.statement: Domestic acute seasonality in Q2 better than last year per early trends
items.quote: But again, it will be too early, but it's much better than what it was last year.

items.statement: Q1 domestic growth driven by volume 1.5%, new launches 2.5%, price 2.5%
items.quote: So in domestic, we have had a volume growth of close to some 1.5%. We have -- the new launches have contributed to around 2.5%. And balances are, I would say, price growth, which is again close to 2.5%.

items.statement: Mirabegron launch delayed until patent litigations resolve, expected FY26-27
items.quote: So unless the final outcome of all the litigations on the patent are clear, we would not be -- because we are bound by the settlement agreement, I don't see it getting launched in -- before the agreement date and which will be somewhere, I would say, 26 or 27, somewhere around that time.

items.statement: Expects volume growth of ~18% and revenue growth of ~35% in Visa & Consular business to continue for the rest of FY25
items.quote: we have done a growth in this quarter about 18% in the volumes. And overall, about 35% on the revenue, we believe that will continue and the growth in the EBITDA should also be on the same line as for the existing business is concerned.

items.statement: Visa & Consular EBITDA margin expanded 600 bps to 29% in Q1 FY25 driven by self-run model transition, higher service fees, and value-added services
items.quote: EBITDA grew by a robust 71% Y-o-Y to INR 121.3 crores in Q1 FY '25 with a margin of 29%, which expanded by 600 basis points as compared to 23% in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Management sees further upside in blended EBITDA margins for FY25 after iDATA integration, though exact number not quantified
items.quote: The exact number, we don't know. But definitely, we see further upside in our margins. If you see last year, we did 21%, year before we were at 15%-16%. So constantly, the EBITDA margins have been growing and definitely, after this acquisition, we definitely feel that EBITDA margins can grow further.

items.statement: Capex incurred for self-run model transition reflected in higher depreciation and employee costs, not directly in EBITDA
items.quote: if you see, our depreciation and our employee costs have gone up compared to the last quarters, and only due to this that we have got people on our own payroll as well as we have invested in new facilities. Therefore, the depreciation has also gone up.

items.statement: Won 14-15 new contracts in last 1-1.5 years, mostly from competitors; more governments outsourcing for first time in pipeline
items.quote: If you see our competitors, we have won 14 to 15 new contracts in the last 1 to BLS International Services Limited August 06, 2024 1.5 years, and most of it was from the competition. Some governments have outsourced for the first time also, that most of this was winning more market

items.statement: iDATA acquisition completed for INR 720 crores; will consolidate from Q2 FY25; iDATA did INR 246 crores revenue and INR 144 crores EBITDA in CY2023
items.quote: We have also announced the completion of iDATA acquisition recently, for a consideration of INR 720 crores. This is a large milestone for the company and we will witness the synergystic benefits from Q2 onwards. iDATA is a profitable company and recorded INR246 crores revenue with INR144 crores in EBITDA in calendar year 2023.

items.statement: Board passed enabling resolution to raise up to INR 2,000 crores via equity (QIP/other modes) for future acquisitions; no concrete M&A plan yet
items.quote: this was an enabling resolution that we passed in the Board meeting and in the follow-up AGM we wish to take that up. But definitely, we are constantly looking at growth opportunities of the company. Organically, we are looking at new contracts, newer geographies and inorganically these acquisitions.

items.statement: Anticipates significant boost to international tourism and visa demand from travel-facilitating measures, rising air capacity and connectivity
items.quote: With increased business confidence and travel-facilitating measures and rising air capacity and connectivity across the globe, we anticipate significant boost to the international tourism and corresponding demand of visa applications.

items.statement: No sizable revenue exposure to countries with current geopolitical tensions; operates in 70+ countries providing diversification
items.quote: We operate currently in a global scenario, where there is every year or every quarter or somewhere we have geo-political tension keeps happening. So, I don't think on an annual basis, this affects our business. We are operating in 70-plus countries.

items.statement: Service fee increases from new contracts at higher charges and re-tendered existing contracts at higher charges driving margin expansion
items.quote: We have gotten an increase in service fee. We have won new contracts at higher service charges, even though existing contract that we re-tendered we have won at higher service charges. So the service fee has increased.

items.statement: Digital Services EBITDA margin expanded 358 bps to 15.2% in Q1 FY25 despite flat revenue; added new banks and CSPs
items.quote: The EBITDA surged by 31% Y-o-Y to INR 11.9 crores in Q1 FY '25, against INR 9.1 crores in Q1 FY '24. The EBITDA margins at 15.2% were up 358 basis points from 11.6% in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents of INR 1,290 crores as of June 30, 2024; used for iDATA and Aadifidelis acquisitions post quarter-end
items.quote: The company continues to maintain a strong balance sheet with cash and cash equivalent of INR1,290 crores as on 30th June 2024, and strong return ratios with ROE of 29% and ROCE of 32% on an annualized basis.

items.statement: BLS E-Services IPO funds (INR 300 crores unutilized) to be used for Aadifidelis acquisition, IT infrastructure, e-stores, and further acquisitions
items.quote: the IPO funding we are going to use for this acquisition, which is in the final stages now. We are signing a definitive agreement. And once that happens, we will be utilizing for that as well as the balance will be used for the growth capital of the BLS e-services.

items.statement: Company has natural FX hedge as all contracts are in USD or Euro; collects local currency equivalent at achieved rate
items.quote: as far as the exchange rate, we have a natural hedge that our all contracts are in USD or in Euro. So, we collect the equivalent local currency matching with the achieved rate. So, we don't have an exchange rate risk inherited into the system.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR900 crores plus for FY25 with EBITDA margin of 19% to 20%
items.quote: We are quite confident that we should be able to achieve what we have projected since potential of about INR900 crores plus in FY '25.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR1,200 to INR1,300 crores for FY26 with 90%+ capacity utilization
items.quote: We are expecting a revenue between INR1,200 crores to INR1,300 crores in FY'26 because of the selling price.

items.statement: Pakhajan facility commissioned April 9, 2024 with 20,000 MT capacity; total capacity now 32,500 MT
items.quote: I am pleased to announce the successful completion and commissioning of our Pakhajan facility on April 9, '24. This facility is spread over 42 acres with an initial install capacity of 20,000 metric tons per annum. With this facility, our total capacity now stands at 32,500 metric tons.

items.statement: No major capex planned for remainder of FY25 beyond INR5-10 crores maintenance; next expansion after 70%+ utilization
items.quote: Well, generally company spend on a repair capex is about INR5 crores to INR10 crores not more than that for this year. And for the further capex we have not planned anything yet.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to stabilize to previous levels by Q3-Q4 FY25; FY25 margin 19-20%; FY26 margin 19-20% at company level
items.quote: We expect the EBITDA margin will stabilize back to the previous level by Q3-Q4 of this year, which we expect it to grow further.

items.statement: Selling prices and raw material prices under pressure; container availability issues expected to resolve by end of Q3/early Q4
items.quote: Well, there is a current pressure on the selling price and so does also the raw material prices are also under pressure. Number two, there is some kind of a delay happening in export getting container availability all that thing. We believe that that should be over by the end of Q3 and early Q4 things should start stabilizing.

items.statement: Industry growing at 3-4% YoY; demand driven by alternate supply chain preference and specialty chemistry focus
items.quote: And the industry is growing healthy growth of 3% to 4% year-on-year. So, it's not a question of we are snatching somebody's business but we are also getting a small pie of the growth of the market itself.

items.statement: Pakhajan has dedicated lines, no product change; mix optimization only at Vapi facility; new products at Pakhajan currently insignificant
items.quote: Well, the product mix optimization can happen only from Vapi. Pakhajan has a dedicated line. We don't change the product at Pakhajan.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty may affect container availability and pricing stabilization timeline
items.quote: But we can't say due to the geopolitical situation what is going on currently. 100% nobody can say what is going to happen.

items.statement: No plans for equity dilution via QIP; debt peaked, no further increase intended; target debt/EBITDA close to 3x by FY25 end, then 2-2.5x
items.quote: We understand that the current debt level has peaked and we do not intend to increase it any further. We expect that the debt to EBITDA will be close to three by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: US subsidiary to be operational in few months to expand sales network and improve margins by 3-5%
items.quote: We have also opened a subsidiary in the USA which will be operational in a few months time to expand our sales network in the region.

items.statement: Long-term supply agreements expected with new customers after trials; volume growth of 27% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: No, there will be definitely a long-term supply agreement with the various customers.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve gradually from H2 FY25 as cost reduction initiatives take effect
items.quote: All these initiatives are expected to gradually improve our margins starting from half 2 of this year.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 668 million in Q1 FY25; net debt to equity improved to 0.59
items.quote: This resulted in a n et debt reducing by further INR 668 million in quarter 1 of FY '25 and our net debt to equity has improved to 0.59

items.statement: Lifetime new business wins of INR 7,959 million in Q1 FY25 with annual peak revenue potential of INR 1,416 million
items.quote: In quarter 1 of FY'25, our lifetime new business wins was over INR7,959 million, the cumulative order wins are expected to result in an annual peak revenue levels of around INR1,416 million.

items.statement: Renewable energy Phase 1 (36.6 MW) from Q2 FY25 to yield INR 200 million annual savings; Phase 2 (14 MW) to add INR 70-80 million
items.quote: The first phase of this initiative is expected to result in 36.6 megawatts of power of sourcing from solar power starting from quarter 2 of this year and is expecte d to give us an annual recurring saving of around INR 200 million

items.statement: Overseas markets (US, Europe) showed negative 2-wheeler growth; Asian growth driven by low-end segments; premium segment struggling
items.quote: The overseas market especially the U.S. and the European market also showed negative growth for 2-wheelers. In the Asian region, the growth was largely driven by low-end segments and the premium segment continues to struggle for growth in this region.

items.statement: EV revenue reached 7.8% of total in Q1 FY25; 48% of new order wins from EV players; 4-wheeler share 71% of new wins
items.quote: Revenue from supplying to EV players in quarter 1 FY '25 was approximately 8% of our overall revenues.

items.statement: Overseas recovery expected to take 1-2 years; negative operating leverage impacting overseas profitability
items.quote: As far as the overseas thing is concerned, as we indicated earlier, the negative operating leverage is coming and hitting us, which is what we indicated in the previous quarters also. That will take some time. I think it should slowly improve, but for us to see any concrete improvement, I think it will take anywhere between 1 to 2 years.

items.statement: Startup costs from two new Maharashtra plants to significantly reduce in Q2 FY25; margins expected from Q3 FY25
items.quote: But going forward, we see that these losses in Q2 will be sig nificantly reduced. And then we start making margins from Q3 onwards

items.statement: Average quarterly debt reduction of INR 50-60 crores expected to continue; may invest in land for future growth
items.quote: So on the average, anywhere between INR50 crores to INR60 crores reduction per quarter has been the trend. So we should be able to continue this. Except that in between, we may have to invest some amount in terms of buying some additional land for our future growth.

items.statement: Commodity price adjustments impacted revenue in Q1 FY25; described as transitory phase expected to correct in outer quarters
items.quote: These are some of the normal adjustments or price changes which keep happening in this industry, as you know. So this is again a transitory phase. So it should get corrected in the outer quarters.

items.statement: India business gross margins improved ~1% YoY excluding government incentive; overseas margins to stay flat while India improves
items.quote: If you eliminate the impact of the government incentives in Q4, I think there was some improve ment, some reasonable improvement in the gross margins already in this quarter

items.statement: 2-3 wheelers now 78% of total revenue; Bajaj share at 44.6%; non-Bajaj share 85% of new order wins
items.quote: In terms of segments, 2- and 3-wheelers add up to now 78% of the total loan. And Bajaj business is now at 44.6%, close to 45%.

items.statement: Interest cost reduction delayed due to lease accounting changes, loan prepayment costs, and new plant lease arrangements
items.quote: Some of these lease interest also got added, like what we mentioned, some of these new plants had leasing arrangements, plus we have an R&D center also which got into a leasing arrangement or renewed it.

items.statement: Free cash flow generation and debt reduction to continue; credit rating upgraded to AA- long term, A1+ short term
items.quote: In the past 2 years, we have seen our efforts resulting in a strong free cash flow generation and debt reduction, thereby tendering our balance sheet. This improvement has resulted in an upgrade to the credit rating of the company by 1 notch to AA minus for long term, and our short-term rating is at a top notch, which is A1 plus.

items.statement: Management says 20% topline growth is a sensible way to model the company for the next few years and will continue to improve margins.
items.quote: I think that 20% topline growth is a sensible way to model our company at this moment, and we will continue to improve our margins, thus hopefully deliver higher growth on the bottomline.

items.statement: Management expects gradual increase in operating profit margins for the rest of FY2025.
items.quote: As we look ahead to the rest of FY2025, we are poised to further accelerate our growth trajectory with gradual increase in operating profit margins and will continue to deliver greater value to all our shareholders.

items.statement: Management expects employee expenses to remain largely flattish for the foreseeable future while revenue grows much higher.
items.quote: So as business expands, I would expect to keep our employee expenses largely flattish, at least for the foreseeable future. You will see much higher growth in revenues and a flattish to low growth in the employee expenses.

items.statement: Management sees potential lift in CPCU rates from premium inventory investments but expects the benefit to reflect in margin expansion.
items.quote: I see that effect being utilized from a margin perspective, right . Overall, the way Affle is strategizing itself is that we are going more and more premium in a way we are working with different strategic platforms, be it the app stores or the alternate of app stores.

items.statement: India and Global Emerging Markets growth was 24.8% y-o-y and contributed 73.2% of quarterly revenue; market tailwinds remain intact.
items.quote: Our strong anchoring across India and Global Emerging Markets continues to be resilient and it contributed 73.2% to our quarterly revenues. Our growth for India and Emerging markets combined, was about 24.8% y -o-y. The market tailwinds remain intact affirming our positive outlook for continued growth across India and Global Emerging Markets.

items.statement: Developed Markets growth was 36.9% y-o-y and contributed 26.8% of quarterly revenue; management is confident of sustaining momentum.
items.quote: Our growth in Developed Markets was about 36.9% y -o-y and it contributed 26.8% to our quarterly revenues. We are strengthening our foundation through continuous enhancements to our Consumer Platform and are confident of sustaining the existing growth momentum.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 20.1% in Q1 FY2025, delivering strong operating margin expansion.
items.quote: We achieved an EBITDA margin of 20.1%, delivering a strong operating margin expansion.

items.statement: Management states Google's Privacy Sandbox and GAID deprecation are delayed/deferred for several years; Affle is fully prepared and not worried.
items.quote: So at the moment, it seems that cookies, which I thought was a very simple thing for them to do, technically at least, and for 4.5 years, they have essentially said that is not going to happen for now. We were not too worried about the cookies at all. We are fully prepared and ready for Privacy Sandbox.

items.statement: Gaming vertical led significant growth in both emerging and developed markets in Q1 FY2025.
items.quote: We are seeing a n overall broad-based growth. But I would say that the growth in the gaming vertical, both in emerging markets and developed markets has been quite significant.

items.statement: Effective Tax Rate of 18.7% in Q1 FY2025 is expected to be the new standard going forward.
items.quote: Moving forward, we see this Effective Tax Rate to be a new standard for us.

items.statement: Management is investing in premium inventory and deeper ecosystem partnerships (e.g., TCL, OEM app stores, iOS/CTV) to drive higher CPCU rates and margin expansion.
items.quote: We are investing into that aspect, so as to raise the profile of our company, deliver higher value to the advertisers, create that validation interdependent so that we have a competitive moat, and can get higher wallet share and achieve higher CPCU levels and better pricing / better margins.

items.statement: Management is not in a rush for M&A despite strong cash generation; will pursue acquisitions only if they add disproportionate value.
items.quote: We have just completed YouAppi's integration. YouAppi is 1 year and full integration has been done in less than a year. So if we find the right acquisition target, we certainly would but we are not in a rush.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth of over 20% y-o-y in Q1 FY2025; extrapolating Q1 run rate to Q2 suggests more than 20% organic y-o-y growth even without sequential uptick.
items.quote: Further, if you take our last year's Q2 numbers and you applied our current Q1 numbers run rate, assuming this coming quarter, which is July, August, Affle (India) Limited August 05, 2024 16 September, let's say, we do exactly the same Q1 numbers in Q2 as well, and there's no sequential sort of uptick, which is not how we are. I mean we typically see Q1 to Q2, there is some sequential uptick. But

items.statement: Management is comfortable defending current inventory and data cost at 61.6% of revenue; sees sustainable margin profile and will endeavour to improve long term.
items.quote: I think I've already answered in the previous question, and we are where we are and comfortable to defend that range and position at the moment.

items.statement: Real Money Gaming (RMG) impact in India is neutralized and over; current growth is the new normal.
items.quote: We are going more broad-based. Even in India, realigning the definition of gaming for us. I mean, looking at it in a much broader way than just RMG. We are neutralizing that impact. Yes, I would say for now that impact is over and this is our new normal, and we will continue to grow sensibly from here.

items.statement: Direct business mix remains in 70%-75% range; quarterly fluctuations not meaningful as advertisers may shift between direct and agency channels.
items.quote: Now direct versus agency, it's within that range, 70% to 75% direct business. It is all in that range. So please don't read into 1 quarter or the other.

items.statement: Base business ex-Cenexi full-year revenue growth guided at mid-teens
items.quote: The mid-teens, that's what we guided.

items.statement: Base business EBITDA margin guided at 32-33% for full year
items.quote: So, EBITDA around 32%, 33%.

items.statement: Cenexi positive EBITDA expected in Q4 FY25 and next fiscal year with revenue exceeding €200 million
items.quote: we reaffirmed the outlook communicated during the last investors call, a positive EBITDA for Q4 of this Fiscal Year and a positive EBITDA for the next fiscal year driven by increased revenue exceeding the €200 million threshold.

items.statement: New ampoule line at Fontenay to be commissioned in August shutdown with commercial production in early 2025 generating ~€10 million revenue
items.quote: This line will be commissioned during the summer shutdown period of August, with commercial production slated to begin in early 2025. We antic ipate this new line will significantly increase capacity, improve customer service, and generate approximately €10 million in revenue in 2025

items.statement: Capex of INR 637 million invested in Q1 FY25 largely for Cenexi upgrade and maintenance
items.quote: We invested INR 637 million in capital expenditure during the current fiscal year, largely allocated towards upgrading and maintenance capex of Cenexi business.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 60% in Q1 FY25 vs 63% prior year; base business gross margin impacted by product mix
items.quote: Our gross margin for Q1 FY25 was 60%, compared to 63% in Q1 FY24, impacted by the product mix at the base business for us.
