items.statement: Recruiting experienced BDMs for SPM, heavy machinery, utilities and industrial machinery to diversify beyond BIW and poles/towers
items.quote: We have now taken people who are to join. Hopefully they join in the next one, two months. And we continue to hire BDMs with experience in U.S. markets, especially.

items.statement: 25% of employees added in last 18 months are still in training and not fully billable, increasing cost base
items.quote: I would not say 30% to 40%, but definitely 25% of the employees who joined last 18 months, they may be just learning the fundamentals and able to do some basic work.

items.statement: EV domain stagnation due to automobile industry indecision between EV and hydrogen fuel engines
items.quote: Unfortunately, that is going through ups and downs due to the indecision of some automobile companies whether to move completely to EV, or wa it for hydrogen -based fuel engines

items.statement: Company has INR40-50 crores in deposits; bankers ready to support; investor interest available for acquisition funding
items.quote: We have more than INR40 crores to INR50 crores worth of funds stacked in our various deposits. And apart from that, company bankers are ready to support, and a lot of investor interest is also there.

items.statement: Attrition rate at 15-16%; employee strength close to 1,200 including new trainees
items.quote: Attrition rate is somewhere around 15% to 16% like in the industry. And the employee strength is now close to 1,100. With the new trainees, it may be now close to 1,200.

items.statement: Implemented Performance Improvisation Plan (PIP) to identify and retrain or exit underperforming employees
items.quote: We also now introduced a very efficient way of PIP, that is Performance Improvisation Plan, wherein we are identifying laggards who are not able to perform even after a couple of years.

items.statement: Signed agreement with Spanish company for SPM work; revenue ramp-up expected over couple of quarters
items.quote: We have signed an agreement with a Spanish company for SPM work. But that to become a true big number, it might take a couple of quarters.

items.statement: Utilities opportunity in poles/towers and transmission lines; initial deals 50-100K with 2-3 million potential in 2-3 years
items.quote: They all will start in 50 and 100K in the beginning with the overall potential of 2 million to 3 million within a period of two, three years.

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue guidance as per company policy
items.quote: I don't think we would be in a position to provide any guidance first. That's something that is a policy we do not do.

items.statement: Full year CAPEX planned at Rs 125 crores including Rs 50 crores for Albumin project, Rs 50 crores maintenance, Rs 25 crores for Tranexamic Acid expansion
items.quote: I think we have mentioned that for the year we have about Rs 125 crores kind of CAPEX requirements in toto, about Rs 50 crores for our Albumin project, about Rs 50-odd crores for our maintenance CAPEX and all and around Rs 25-odd crores for our Tranexamic Acid expansion, that's the full year number.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 28% in Q1 FY25 from 19% YoY driven by licensing income mix and formulation growth; expect similar range to continue
items.quote: So, this is a combination of all these efforts which you are seeing in the improvement in the EBITDA, and we expect that the EBITDA should remain in similar kind of range.

items.statement: Secured pre-launch order for NDA molecule #1 with breakthrough designation; supplies over current and subsequent quarters
items.quote: We have already secured a pre-launch order in this quarter for which the supplies will be done over the current quarter and subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Licensing revenue in Q1 was 50:50 mix of existing contract milestones and new contract signings
items.quote: So, currently in this quarter, it's a mix of both; it's a ratio of maybe around 50:50.

items.statement: UDCA with European CEP approval expected to grow in export markets in large volumes in coming quarters
items.quote: With the approval of CEP, it opens a big opportunity for Shilpa Medicare in export markets, and in the quarters to come, we are confident that this molecule is expected to grow in export market in a large volume.

items.statement: Plan to prepay Rs 300 crores of NCD long-term debt in August from QIP proceeds
items.quote: We are on track to prepay as we had mentioned earlier. We have earmarked Rs 300 crores out of the QIP raise that we had done and that is something that we would prepay during this particular month.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 CAPEX was Rs 58 crores mainly driven by Albumin facility investment
items.quote: Our CAPEX for the 1st Quarter was Rs. 58 crores, which was again mainly driven by our investment in our Albumin facility that we are setting up.

items.statement: Amneal sold more than 1,000 vials of Pemetrexed in US market; K Code approval expected this quarter to drive further sales
items.quote: Post launch currently Amneal has already sold more than 1,000 vials currently in US market and they are waiting for K Code which is again very important for insurance reimbursement which is expected to come in this quarter.

items.statement: Signed key CDMO deal with Unicycive Therapeutics for Oxylanthanum Carbonate; US$ 10 million milestones; dedicated facility to be funded by customer
items.quote: We are delighted to announce a key CDMO signed during the quarter with Unicycive Therapeutics for Oxylanthanum Carbonate. We will be supplying to them the finished formulation along with our own API. We will be receiving US$ 10 million milestones for this deal.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to normalize around 35% for FY25 after higher Q1 rate due to intercompany interest structure
items.quote: Typically, our tax rates are in the region of about 35%-odd. For the quarter it has been on a bit higher side mainly on account of intercompany interest which has been there where the income is getting accrued in a higher tax Company as compared to the expenditure getting booked in a lower tax Company.

items.statement: USFDA formulation facility review expected to complete in Q3 FY25 after appointing subject experts; will re-apply to USFDA post review
items.quote: So, we have finished the meeting with the USFDA, and they have suggested us to appoint some subject experts for which the appointment is completed, and the review has started, and we are expecting to complete the review in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Liraglutide plant validation completed; DMF filing expected Q3 FY25; formulation scale-up planned Q3 FY25 for ROW markets
items.quote: With respect to the first molecule, Liraglutide, we have now finished the plant validation. So, now we will be promoting this molecule to various customers, and we will have some customers seeded in this financial year.

items.statement: Semaglutide large-scale development finished; target to complete plant validation and DMF readiness in FY25
items.quote: And on the second molecule, Semaglutide, currently, the large-scale development is completed. And once we finish the plant validation with drug master file, that is when the commercial feature will start coming in.

items.statement: Two new CDMO projects likely to be signed in Q2 FY25 in biologics space
items.quote: And apart from that, we have two new CDMO projects which are likely to be signed in second quarter FY25.

items.statement: Albumin Phase-III human study expected to start Q4 FY25 for India/emerging markets (12 months) and Europe (15 months) in parallel
items.quote: We are expecting to start the Phase-III human study in Q4 FY25 and the study duration is for one year and the Phase-I study what we have completed was against the European reference product.

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: Overall consumption environment remained weak; apparel market impacted by subdued wedding season and prolonged heat wave reducing consumer activities.
items.quote: As we look back at the first quarter of this fiscal, the overall consumption environment has remained weak. The apparel market, in particular, was further impacted by a subdued wedding season, prolonged heat wave, all of which have contributed to reduced consumer activities.

items.statement: Demerger expected to complete by end of fiscal year 2025.
items.quote: For demerger, we have filed the application with the stock exchanges and hopefully we'll be able to complete it within the timeline indicated earlier, that is by end of fiscal year '25.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 11.8%, up 15% YoY in absolute terms; Lifestyle EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 18.8%; Pantaloons EBITDA margin expanded 470 bps to 17.6%.
items.quote: Company achieved consolidated EBITDA of INR406 crores with 11.8% margin. EBITDA increased 15% year-on-year in absolute terms. Both our established businesses, that is Lifestyle and Pantaloons witnessed margin expansion led by gross margin improvement and effective cost control measures.

items.statement: Anticipate improved demand environment during upcoming wedding and festive seasons in H2 FY25.
items.quote: As we look ahead, we anticipate an improved demand environment during the upcoming wedding and festive seasons that will hold us in a much stronger position to capture the opportunity in the market.

items.statement: Bangladesh unrest not material; sourcing from Bangladesh is 2-3% of overall sourcing.
items.quote: No, it's not material. It's between 2% to 3% of our sourcing comes from there on an overall basis. So there might be individual business, some segment, a little bit of it. But at overall level, it's not significant for us.

items.statement: TCNS EBITDA losses expected to turn positive in H2 FY25; gross margins to recover to 65-67% range; EBITDA margin recovery to high teens targeted in 12-18 months.
items.quote: We expect this business to come closer to where Lifestyle brand margins are on an overall level in 12 to 18 months. Now if it takes a couple of quarters more or less, that's something that we have to see. But that's really where it would come back to, which is high teens in terms of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: TMRW fundraise targeted ideally by end of FY25, but first half of next year also acceptable; acquisitions paused until fundraise completed.
items.quote: Ideally would be end of this year, but first half of next year is also fine for us. Till then, therefore, our acquisitions as far as TMRW is concerned, will have to wait until the fundraise actually comes through.

items.statement: Pantaloons private label share increased to ~66%; private label plus ABFRL brands ~76-77%; aim to improve by a couple of percentage points further.
items.quote: If you look a t the share, as we've given you, of private label plus the ABFRL brands, that totally comes to about 76%, 77%. And I think we'll continue to strive to improve that further by a couple of percentage points

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands SSG low-single-digit negative in Q1, primarily impacted by reduced wedding days and consumption occasions.
items.quote: First question, low-single-digit negative, okay, for the quarter. Primarily impacted by wedding days. While definitely our suits and blazers business and categories which are more impacted by weddings, had that impact more. But overall itself consumption o ccasions had reduced

items.statement: TCNS merger approved by NCLT; awaiting court order to make scheme effective.
items.quote: The amalgamation of TCNS with ABFRL is on track as the honourable NCLT has approved the merger. We are awaiting the court order and then we will work towards making this scheme effective.

items.statement: American Eagle posted 35% YoY growth led by strong distribution expansion; Reebok maintained profitable growth trajectory.
items.quote: American Eagle posted 35% Y -o-Y growth led by strong distribution expansion. Reebok following a successful first year with ABFRL maintained its trajectory of profitable growth year-on-year.

items.statement: TMRW portfolio grew 2x YoY; now consists of 7 brands including minority investment in Wrogn; top 3 brands potential INR800-900 crores NSV.
items.quote: TMRW portfolio grew to 2x of last year as the brands continued to benefit from operational and business model announcements provided by the center of excellence. TMRW expanded its portfolio with minority investment in Wrogn.

items.statement: TCNS inventory correction largely complete; old inventory problems behind; organic performance showing improvement with 5%+ L2L across 500 stores.
items.quote: And Gopal, I can assure you that journey is more or less over as far as the inventory correction is clear. Our organic performance has already started to show improvement for the first time after multiple quarters, TCNS as a network, which is W plus Aurelia across 500 stores delivered 5% plus like -to-like in a very tough market environment.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance band of 12% to 14% for FY25
items.quote: Overall, we are in that band of 12% to 14%, which we have been guiding on the EBITDA margins, while continuing to grow our volumes, investing back in brand, a lot of digitization and transformation efforts which the company is embarking on.

items.statement: Lubricant industry volume growth expected at 3% to 4% for next decade
items.quote: As you look at lubricants, as we have communicated, this industry is going to grow at least 3% in volume for the next decade, at least that in the normal circumstances, unless something goes wrong macro so this is a growth industry in terms of lubricant consumption.

items.statement: Company aims to grow 2x to 3x industry volume growth rate
items.quote: We try to grow 2x, 3x the industry growth rate, which is going to be around 3% to 4%, which is what we generally also track.

items.statement: Annual capex guidance of INR 25 crore for lubricant business
items.quote: On a yearly basis, we have given a capex guidance of around INR 25 crore which is largely to get some filling lines and some auxillary.

items.statement: Gross margin improved ~200 bps YoY and ~50 bps QoQ in Q1 FY25
items.quote: You will also see from the result that we have grown our gross margin by nearly 200 basis points Y-o-Y over last year June quarter and eve n from March quarter, we have grown our gross margins by another 50 basis points nearly so that has translated into excellent EBITDA growth of 25% and profit after tax of 29% nearly

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 13.1% in Q1 FY25, within guided 12-14% band
items.quote: I think we spoke about EBITDA margins , while the gross margins have seen an im provement, we have invested back in the brand mo re because this being the IPL quarter as well and also, there has been increase in freight and some of the OEM royalties in line with our volume growth so that's the primary reason

items.statement: Small retail price increase taken in mid-May 2024 after crude rose above $90
items.quote: Yes,we took a small price increase in retail in mid-May. Obviously, it takes some time to realize the price increase,I think all the participants will recall that crude went above $90 in April and that's where base oil also follows with a lag of one month or so, and the price increase was taken in mid-May.

items.statement: If crude sustains below $80, input cost reduction may allow margin improvement
items.quote: As I mentioned in one of the previous questions that if the crude sustains for a reasonable period below $80 and all, there can be recalibration in some of the schemes and all, but that input cost also will come down with the lag base oil also reacts so we'll keep managing our margins to see that overall, we deliver what we are guiding.

items.statement: Core lubricant volumes grew 5.7% YoY to 37,000 kl in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Core volumes for Q1 FY '25 was INR 37,000 kl with a growth of 5.7% year -on-year.

items.statement: AdBlue volumes grew 26% YoY to 38,000 kl in Q1 FY25
items.quote: AdBlue volume for the quarter has been 38,000 kl, which is roughly 26% growth over the last year same quarter.

items.statement: AdBlue market expected to grow at least 10-15% annually with BS-VI vehicle growth
items.quote: This will grow. If the BS-VI vehicle goes up, it should have at least 10%, 15% growth minimum.

items.statement: Premiumization drive across retail, OEM and industrial segments improving product mix
items.quote: The product mix is also improving across segments like channel retail. Our focus is on premiumization. The product mix enrichment is happening retail channel, OEM business, industrial B2B, of course, supported by the demand for quality products, which help to create value.

items.statement: Premium products currently single-digit percentage of revenue, target to grow 2x faster
items.quote: Each of the segments, it could be a single -digit percentage now. We want to obviously try to get into that so that's the endeavor and also introduce products which are going to be more of the new technology pieces. So both are there and I would say we'll be happy to share with you. Currently, we want to get this premiumization piece it is part of our DNA now. We are pushing it and that's one of t

items.statement: Factory fill volumes declined 10-11% YoY due to OEM production cuts
items.quote: The factory fill segment was the only segment which probably saw some declin e around 10%, 11% due to a decline in production by some OEMs, which clearly is not in our control, but impacting our volumes slightly

items.statement: EV charging investments (Tirex, ElectreeFi, Indra) total ~INR 150 crore; Tirex targeting EBITDA neutral to positive in FY25
items.quote: we have invested close to INR 150 crore in all the 3 investments put together and out of this Tirex transmission, which is a DC fast charger company, we have 51% stake, ElectreeFi, which is a software as a service company, we have 26% stake and Indra Technologies, which is a UK-based company manufacturing slow AC home chargers there, we have 7.5% stake from India balance sheet so t hat's our inves

items.statement: Management expects to beat FY24 revenue growth of 10.4% in FY25 without price increases
items.quote: I think FY25, I told you last time we will try and beat the FY24 number. This quarter is 11.3, its better than 10.4%. I have a feeling we will continue to do better and then definitely beat 10.4% of last year.

items.statement: Establishing 20 new labs primarily in Tier-3 and Tier-4 towns of North and East to broaden reach
items.quote: We are establishing 20 new labs to broaden our reach with plans to add more labs as the year progresses.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable EBITDA margin seen around 27% due to investments in new markets, awareness, digital and automation
items.quote: On a longer term , we said in the last call around 27% kind of margins because we also are doing lot of investment s, we are going deeper, we are spending more and lot of new investments are required which will give obviously top line in a longer period

items.statement: No price increase taken since February 2023 and no intent to take one currently; realization growth driven by mix
items.quote: We took last price increase, that was in February 2023, and we completed one full year of cycle of that in Feb '24 and we have not taken any price increase and neither we have intent to take as of now.

items.statement: Sample volume growth of 9.6% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by volume gains and favorable test and geographic mix
items.quote: sample volume growth is 9.6% over Q1 Classification: Restricted FY24. Notably, we saw a 10.4% increase in patient numbers in Q1 FY25 as compared to Q4 FY24

items.statement: Specialized portfolio contributes ~23% of revenue, up 1-1.5 percentage points YoY; Swasthfit contributes ~25% of total revenue
items.quote: The specialized portfolio is again the way we define it, because specialized portfolio definition can vary from organization to organization, the way we define it, it currently contributes about 23% of our revenue v/s let's say similar period last year, the contribution would have grown by about 1-1.5% points.

items.statement: Suburban Diagnostics revenue grew ~8% YoY in Q1 FY25 with EBITDA margin ~14%; core DLPL business grew ~13%
items.quote: Suburban revenue growth for this quarter is about 8% and EBITDA is about 14%.

items.statement: Competitive intensity from predatory pricing and high promotional spend has eased; hospital forward integration limited to 4-5 km catchment areas
items.quote: I think competition became visible because a lot of private equity money and I think there were different format s of cash burn, etc., they were spending a lot of money on promotions which to me has eased off. That's why they are not that visible now

items.statement: Net cash and equivalents of Rs. 1,044 crore as of June 30, 2024; interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share approved for FY25
items.quote: Net cash and equivalents as on June 30th, 2024 is Rs. 1,044 crore. We are pleased to announce that the board of directors has approved an interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share for FY25.

items.statement: Priority for cash deployment is strategic acquisitions in South and West regions; also investing in new labs, technology and higher dividend payout
items.quote: Our priority #1 is to look for strategic assets, inorganic which are in South and West Region, in West we have done Suburban. If you look at contribution wise, region wise obviously South is still very weak. We would want to fill that gap.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex of INR 2.8 billion for Bangalore land purchase, maintenance, biomedical upgrades, and interior transformation; confident of realizing projected full-year capex with more Greenfield projects
items.quote: We have incurred a capital outlay of INR 2.8 bill ion directed towards purchase of land in Bangalore for Greenfield expansion, regular maintenance, biomedical upgrades, and interior 3 transformation work within existing hospitals.

items.statement: Kolkata Greenfield first phase estimated at INR 950-1000 crores for ~350 beds and infrastructure for 1000 beds; Bangalore land cost ~INR 500 crores for 1.5 acre HSR layout extension (~200 beds) and cardiac annex
items.quote: For the Kolkata Greenfield one, the first phase project estimate is almost around INR 1000 crores, which includes the building of around 350 beds in the first phase and there will be a lot of infrastructure development for the entire for the 1000 beds as well, but the first phase will cost around INR 950 crores. For the Bangalore land, cost will be around INR 500 crores.

items.statement: No forward revenue guidance; organic growth in line with market until new capacities (Kolkata, Bangalore) come online in 3-4 years; next inflection point when new hospitals operational
items.quote: The growth will be organic in the short term. The next big inflection point will come when our capac ities come online. Until then, we will grow in line with the market and in line with our own efforts that we are putting in in terms of throughput maximization as well as quality of revenue

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 24.4% in Q1 FY25 vs 23.2% in Q1 FY24; India EBITDA margin improved from 18.3% to 19.4% YoY; focus on quality of revenue over volume growth
items.quote: Narayana Hrudayalaya generated a consolidated EBITDA of INR 3,274 million at a margin of 24.4% against 23.2% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Cayman existing facility at saturation with mid-single digit growth; new Camana Bay hospital (50 beds, daycare-focused) inaugurated July, patient inflow expected before end of Q2 FY25; next growth wave from new facility
items.quote: We've already inaugurated it. We have about 50 odd beds, that’s our official bed count. You know, we hope to be occupied from the early quarters, but at the end of the day, this is something we'll have to wait for a few months to see

items.statement: India IP volumes flat for 3 quarters due to elections, seasonality, bed reconfiguration; Q1 FY25 IP discharges 59,000 vs 56,000 in Q3/Q4 FY24; focus on quality of revenue, double-digit revenue growth expected
items.quote: we saw about 56,000 patients in our inpatient, and this quarter we saw about 59,000 patients in our inpatient. So even though Q1 is a wea k quarter for us in terms of inpatient volume, we were okay

items.statement: Cardiac share of IP down from 35% to 33% YoY as ortho/oncology grow faster; conscious rebalancing, not demand decline; cardiac remains flagship anchor business
items.quote: That is a conscious effort. See the cardiac, it's a disproportionate component of our business compared to all the other listed hospital groups, predominantly because we have this very, very large, the largest cardiac hospital in this part of the world, which does only one specialty.

items.statement: Not aggressive on pricing; normalized prices between domestic and international patients; payer mix choices balancing cash flows, margins, capacity utilization, social relevance; scheme share ~21% flat
items.quote: We are also not very aggressive on the pricing. Therefore, our buildup has always been very slow or has been slow, but very steady.

items.statement: Cayman new facility will have initial operational losses and margin dilution due to high fixed costs; no quantification provided; existing facility growth limited until new hospital commissions
items.quote: Initially there will be obviously, certainly margin dilution and operational losses. We are not in a position to, you know to give out a particular number or a hard value to quantify that, but they're actually, you can obviously expect operation losses and margin dilution for sometime.

items.statement: No equity raise planned; capex funded 80% debt, 20% internal accruals; net debt INR 1.55B (0.05 D/E) as of Jun 2024; leverage to increase as Greenfield capex spends
items.quote: You can assume that at least 80pc of the capex we are indicating will come through debt and to that extent, the leverage will be, it will increase.

items.statement: Insurance business launched in Mysore (Aditi product: 1 Cr cover for ~INR 10k/family); INR 100 Cr capital committed; narrow network (Narayana facilities); early days, systems working well
items.quote: I’m pleased let you know that we launched Na rayana Health Insurance in Mysore ass we have said in late June with our first product it’s called Aditi, the headline feature which is providing 1 crore cover for surgeries for a price of about ₹10,000 for a family of four

items.statement: Integrated Care revenue crossed INR 80M in Q1 FY25 (highest), 51,000+ transactions across 8 clinics; cash burn continues, targeting clinic-level breakeven in reasonable timeframe
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter has crossed INR 80 million, which is the highest so far with more than 51,000 patient transaction across 8 clinics.

items.statement: Capex run rate INR 1500-1600 Cr/year for next 3 years; Kolkata construction start end of Q3 FY25, Bangalore couple months later; full operational in 3.5-4 years
items.quote: We have indicated a certain capex for the current year and we are expecting that we will spend a similar amount as capex over the next 2-3 years and therefore, there will be significant investment that will happen.

items.statement: IndAS 116 impact: EBITDA increased by INR 148.7M, PAT decreased by INR 19M in Q1 FY25; lease unwinding mostly done, slight further decrease next 2 quarters then normalize
items.quote: Our EBITDA will increase by, because of IndAS our EBITDA has increased by INR 148.7 million, and our PAT has decreased by INR 19 million for Q1 FY25 on a like to like basis.

items.statement: Bangladesh patient flows disrupted during elections/festivals; consciously reducing reliance on international medical tourism, expect share to trend to zero over 5 years
items.quote: consciously as a company we're moving away from a reliance on international medical tourism and more towards domestic patient s. So, this is the number over five years, we expect to go down to zero

items.statement: Tax rate steady state ~13% (Q1 FY25); varies with India/Cayman profit mix; last year 11.13% included deferred tax credit from regime change
items.quote: If you see, last year in the 1st quarter was 10.6pc. 2nd and 3rd quarters were 8.7 and 9.8. For the full year, last year we were at 11.13pc. That was the effect of the deferred tax credit that came in in last year. So that is not repeating. Therefore we have kind of come on to that 13pc kind of range.

items.statement: India midnight occupancy 60-65% range (Q1/Q3 lower end, Q2/Q4 upper end); daytime/daycare occupancy much better; not sharing separate occupancy number as not representative
items.quote: Having said that, we always operate in the range of between 60-65pc on midnight occupancy basis. Daytime occupancy and day care occupancy will be much better, so in Q1 and Q3 quarters, we kind of end up in the lower end of the range and in Q2 and Q4 quarters, we normally hit the upper end of the range.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance for FY25 maintained at 6-8%
items.quote: Yes, fixed rate percent. Yes, that remains. That remains.

items.statement: EBITDA per metric ton guidance for FY25 maintained at INR20,500-21,500
items.value: INR20,500 to INR21,500 per metric tonne
items.quote: We increased the guidance last quarter to INR20,500 to 21,500 per metric tonne. So the industry builds on that as a volume growth plus increase in EBITDA means that we have more amount of specialties that should contribute, which we said should happen from H2, that the rational, we increased it. And we continue with the same guidance.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA per metric ton at INR20,197, slightly below guided range
items.quote: the EBITDA for per metric ton came in at INR20,197 per metric ton, slightly below the guided band of INR20,500 to INR21,500 per metric ton.

items.statement: Demand scenario robust across geographies, volume momentum expected to sustain
items.quote: So what I'm saying is that the demand scenario looks robust across geographies. The supply chain situation, though not improving, at least should not deteriorate. If it doesn't deteriorate today, we don't see any reason why we can't have a good volume growth next quarter as well.

items.statement: India volume growth expected to recover to mid-single-digit from Q2 FY25
items.quote: It should. But as all of them, all our customers come in to see -- they're seeing that the rural demand is coming up in last quarter, and they expect that to continue given the good monsoon that we have had and the budget that has put more money in the hands of the rural consumers.

items.statement: AMET market targeting double-digit growth for remaining 3 quarters if supply chain normalizes
items.quote: Yes, that is what we are aiming at. We do hope that the environment supports us. That's what is our endeavor.

items.statement: Specialty volumes grew 13.3% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by masstige categories
items.quote: Even segmentally while our performance of surfactants grew at 5.4%, specialties driven by masstige recorded 13.3% growth.

items.statement: Premium specialty product launches by customers expected to resume from H2 FY25
items.quote: Improving consumer sentiment should accelerate new launches of premium specialty products, which in turn, should aid our premium specialties from H2 FY'24-'25.

items.statement: Specialty capacity expansion under implementation, commissioning targeted by end of FY25
items.quote: So there is one which is already under implementation and execution. I think we're looking at getting it commissioned by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions (container shortage, port congestion, elongated lead times) impacted volumes in Q1
items.quote: Unavailability of containers, port congestion and some of the major ports in the world, combined with higher lead times and rationalized availability of raw materials, adversely impacted the volumes in this quarter.

items.statement: Lauryl alcohol prices increased ~10% QoQ in Q1 and ~30% in last month, creating feedstock volatility
items.quote: See lauryl-alcohol prices have been -- it's been -- it is only increasing, in fact, increased by about 10% compared to the previous quarter in this quarter. But if you see the last one month, it has gone up significantly, aided by the increase in the oil price. So it's like -- it's going to be another about 30% in just about 30 days.

items.statement: Logistics cost increases passed on to customers with a lag; expect to manage further increases judiciously
items.quote: I think we have been -- obviously, it gets passed on with the lag. So I think with the increases, there are no further increases that happened. I think we would have been successful in passing on all the increase.

items.statement: Q1 volumes include 2,500 MT deferred from Q4 FY24; some Q1 volumes deferred to Q2
items.quote: Yes, it does. And some volumes from this quarter also have deferred next quarter in terms of whatever we could not sell because of supplier ratio. This continues. So this includes both.

items.statement: Rest of World markets grew 24.5% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by Europe, Latin America, Asia-Pacific
items.quote: This quarter saw our company growing by 24.5% in rest of the world markets driven by strong growth seen in Europe and Latin America.

items.statement: Innovation funnel split approximately 50-60% internally driven, 40-50% customer driven
items.quote: So you can say, just to be back of the level of calculation, I can tell you about 50% -- 50% to 60% can be what is initiated by us and the balance, 40%, 50% can be what the customers then brought us into thinking.

items.statement: Expect FY25 revenue similar to FY24 level

items.quote: The numbers that you see and that have been reported which is typically INR1,497 crores which is a 4% YoY growth is after the adjustment of the RBI circular. While you have indicated a number of INR400 crores-INR500 crores, I would want to say that this 4% would have been upward of 25% growth if it were not for the circular in position.

items.statement: Stage 3 provision coverage at 34%-35%, target range 32%-36%; management overlay INR45 cr retained
items.quote: This year, because the incremental NPA movement will probably come in at a rate of around 22%-24% when they actually come into Stage 3. That is why the percentage would have come down from 40% to 34%-35% in the Q1. But, yes, we would like to be in the same range as you correctly said. We would like to be in the range of around 32%-36%.

items.statement: Top-up loans ~3% of AUM (~INR600 cr); end-use monitoring via undertaking, Udyam certificate for LAP
items.quote: Top-up loans today stand at about close to 3% of our AUM, which is approximately about INR600 crores. What do we do in terms of end-use monitoring? Today we typically take an undertaking from the customer on where he's going to use the funds.

items.statement: FY25 budgeted capex over ₹4,500 crores with ₹3,000 crores for growth capex in new businesses (66% of total)
items.quote: On the capex front, we continue to focus on growth capex for FY'25 budgeted capital expenditure is over ₹4,500 crores, of which growth capex in new businesses is planned at ₹3,000 crores, which is 66% of the total capital expenditure.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals now contribute 30% of chemical business revenue with highest ever sales volume and revenue
items.quote: We have clocked highest ever sales volume and revenue for the specialty chemical business, which now contributes 30% to the chemical business revenue.

items.statement: Cellulosic fibre volumes at highest quarterly level of 200 tons; revenue highest in 7 quarters
items.quote: Our CSF volumes stood at highest levels of quarterly number of 200 tons and revenue stood at highest levels since past 7 quarters.

items.statement: Paints business on track for high single-digit market share exit target for FY25
items.quote: Raashi Chopra: Got it. And you're still maintaining the high single-digit market share exit target, right, for FY '25? Rakshit Hargave: Yes.

items.statement: Paints capex of ₹10,139 crores excludes working capital; includes IDC, tinting machines, IT systems
items.quote: Yes. Navin. So, ₹10,139 crores, I think is the number is the capex only, which, of course, includes the IDC, the tinting machines, the IT system, everything. Working capital is not included. Okay.

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity to double from 1 GW to 2 GW by end of FY25; aim to add 1 GW annually for next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, I think we have earlier also shared this that firstly, we aim to double the capacity by this financial year, okay? And the projects are already under implementation. So from 1 -GW to 2-GW in this financial year, and then our aim is to add maybe 1-gigawatt every year for next 2, 3 years

items.statement: Birla Pivot B2B e-commerce quarterly revenue run rate over ₹550 crores; targeting $1 billion revenue in 3 years
items.quote: Revenue of our B2B e -commerce business, Birla Pivot is gradually ramping up. The current quarterly run rate of revenue is over ₹550 crores with increasing trends in total number of buyers.

items.statement: VSF margins expected to remain range-bound; raw material prices mixed with slight increase tendency
items.quote: Raashi Chopra: Okay. So you're expecting margins to remain at this level? Harikrishna Agarwal: Range bound, that is what the best assessment.

items.statement: Chemicals ECU realizations at ₹32,529 in Q1 FY25, highest since Q2 FY24; caustic prices improved for fourth consecutive quarter
items.quote: Improved caustic reductions, coupled with uptick in demand and realization for chlorine derivati ves had led to improvement in eco realizations, which stood at ₹32,529 for Q1 FY '25, highest since Q2 FY '24.

items.statement: Chlorine prices under downward pressure due to competitor capacity addition in Gujarat without integration
items.quote: Chlorine is a somewhat different story because chlorine is more domestic. As you know, one of our competitors have guided significant capacity in Gujarat, without an integration. So chlorine for sure is under downward pressure.

items.statement: Paints business commercialized 3 plants in April 2024; >80% of 145 planned products placed in distribution channels
items.quote: Paints business under brand Birla Opus has started its commercial production at 3 plants in April 2024 and more than 80% ra nge of 145 planned products have been placed in the distribution channels.

items.statement: Paints KPIs on track: 3 plants commercialized, >102 depots (target 150), targeting 50,000 active dealers by year-end
items.quote: We have been able to place out of the 125-odd products we talked about, more than 80% is already there in the market. We had talked about reaching 150 depots by the end of the year. We are already beyond 102. We have talked about reaching 50,000 dealers. We are in sync with the plan to hit 50,000 active dealers by the end of the year.

items.statement: Paints retail sellout exceptional; inventory at stores is small part of what sold; tinting machine data gives real-time demand insights
items.quote: Our retail audit of stores where we have gone and seen stocks sold till date and taken inventory of stocks lying in the store, suggest that the inventory lying in the store is a small part of what we have sold till now, which means majority of it has been sold out.

items.statement: Paints trial production revenue goes to CWIP for 3-4 months per plant; Chamarajanagar trial started, Mahad Q3, Kharagpur Q4 FY25
items.quote: So Mahad and Kharagpur will be in somewhere in Q3 and Q4. So first Mahad in Q3 and then in Q4, the Kharagpur plant. Chamarajanagar has already commenced trial run production. So I think in Q3, we should be capitalizing that.

items.statement: Birla Pivot gross margins 1.5-4% across categories; losses not very large as business scales
items.quote: You see, the gross margins, as we have earlier said, will be in the range of about 1.5% to 4% in different product categories, okay. So that is the situation as far as gross margins are concerned.

items.statement: Chemicals outlook cautiously optimistic; depends on Chinese consumer demand and Middle East supply chain risks
items.quote: I would say that I'm cautiously optimistic on chemicals as a sector. With the disclaimer that a lot will depend upon what happens with the Chinese consumer and nothing funny should happen either in the global supply chain because of the crises in the Middle East.

items.statement: Underlying volume growth target for full year is double-digit; Q1 was 9.6%
items.quote: our Q1 underlying volume growth was 9.6%, not very far from the double-digit target that we have for the year

items.statement: EBITDA margin band maintained at 20-24%; currently at higher end but will invest back if stability continues
items.quote: we will be in the 20% to 24% range, probably a little more at the higher end. But as we see signs of stability, we will invest back more aggressively for growth

items.statement: No significant pricing rollbacks in Q1; further cuts depend on input price reductions
items.quote: As of now, in the first quarter, we have not taken any significant pricing rollbacks. What you are seeing is really the impact of what we have done over the course of all of last year

items.statement: Current VAM price fluctuating between $850 and $1,000 per ton due to force majeure
items.quote: Currently, the VAM price is fluctuating because one of the big guys had a force majeure, so on. I would say it's between $850 and $1,000 depending on where you are

items.statement: Kerala market soft due to lower foreign remittances and government spending; will assess after Onam season
items.quote: Kerala vis-à-vis other markets has been soft. There is clearly an issue of demand in Kerala vis-à-vis the normal buoyant conditions

items.statement: Rural growth outpacing urban for 8th consecutive quarter; 90% of rural growth is same-store
items.quote: this is the eighth quarter where we have had double-digit growth in rural India

items.statement: Rural to outpace urban by 1.5x for next 2-3 years; covering 28,000 villages directly
items.quote: Our internal objective is 1.5 times

items.statement: Core:Growth+Pioneer mix shifted from 80:20 to 55:45 over 7-8 years
items.quote: when we started on this journey, Percy, we were 80-20, 80 was core and 20 was growth and pioneer. We are now close to 55-45

items.statement: Capex to be 3-5% of sales annually while maintaining double-digit growth ambition
items.quote: we are now in a stable equilibrium place, where you will find us spend capex between 3% to 5% of sales every year as long as we maintain our double-digit growth ambition

items.statement: Capacity utilization 70-75%; 20 plants undergoing brownfield expansion
items.quote: we remain between 70 and 75. The moment, we crossed 75, we start looking at fresh capacity. So as we speak, actually 20 of our current plants are undergoing some form of brownfield expansion

items.statement: Real estate boom benefits to accelerate from year 3-4; currently in year 2 seeing waterproofing uptick
items.period: end of this year, beginning of next year
items.quote: starting maybe the end of this year, beginning of next year, you will start seeing the multiplier as long as real estate continues to boom

items.statement: VAM prices near bottom as largest producer declared force majeure at current levels
items.quote: the largest one of them actually declared a force majeure in its U.S. and Mexico plants because they found these levels itself not satisfactory. So I would say we are very near the bottom

items.statement: Paints foray progressing organically; will assess after one festive season
items.quote: I would be best equipped to answer this question after these markets have gone through one festive season and we see where we settle

items.statement: B2B targeting double-digit UVG for next 2-3 years through value-added portfolio transformation
items.quote: on a 2 to 3 year basis, as we keep transforming this portfolio into a more value-added portfolio, the objective here also is very clearly double-digit underlying volume growth

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 14.4% in Q1 FY25, down from 16.4% in Q4 FY24 due to raw material cost pressures.
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 9.1 billion, a margin of 14.4% compared to 16.4% in the last quarter.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin was 13.8% in Q1 FY25, down from 15.6% in Q4 FY24 due to rising raw material costs.
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at a margin of 13.8% compared to 15.6% in the last quarter, given the pressure from rising raw materials.

items.statement: Europe EBITDA margin improved to 13.7% in Q1 FY25 from 13.4% in Q1 FY24 due to mix improvement.
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter at E UR 20 million was a margin performance of 13.7% compared to 13.4% for the same period last

items.statement: Raw material basket increased 5% Q-o-Q in Q1 FY25; expect further mid-single digit increase in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: We expect the raw material cost to go up further by mid-single digits in Q2 on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Natural rubber prices around INR 180/kg; no near-term respite expected, potential relief from Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Maybe we will start seeing some respite from Q4 onwards.

items.statement: Expect demand momentum to improve going forward with robust replacement demand and strong farm tyre segment signs.
items.quote: In terms of demand outlook, we expect the demand momentum to get better going forward, continued robust replacement demand, and strong signs from the farm t yre segment as well

items.statement: Europe expects mid to high single digit top-line growth Y-o-Y in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Next quarter, as of now, our expectation would be a mid to high single digit top line growth.

items.statement: India replacement growth expected at high single digits for FY25; exports to grow but face freight challenges.
items.quote: The overall replacement growth should be a high single digit. As I mentioned, we have not done in line with our peers. So, the replacement demand overall should be at high single digits and we would recover some of the lost ground.

items.statement: Truck OEM volumes declined double-digit in Q1 FY25; expected to remain negative for better part of FY25, recovering in H2.
items.quote: Particularly on the truck OE side, the demand is significantly lower than what it was being projected out to be. And that probably a better part of the year would still be in the negative zone. It would recover towards the second half.

items.statement: No change in capex guidance for FY25; continue to be judicious about capex outflow.
items.quote: There is no change in our capex guidance for the current year and we will continue to focus on profitability, free cash flow generation and improvement in the return ratios.

items.statement: Targeting >15% EBITDA margin in line with long-term vision; current margins not satisfactory.
items.quote: No, absolutely. And in line with our long-term vision, we will continue to target higher than 15% EBITDA margin. The current level of margins that we have reported in this quarter is not what we are happy with.

items.statement: Europe 16% EBITDA margin sustainable with potential to go up; demonstrated historically.
items.quote: We believe, Jinesh, that the 16 odd percent margin that you mentioned on EBITDA is quite a sustainable margin within that industry structure.

items.statement: Shut down Trumigo doorstep car servicing venture due to significantly lower financial performance than expectations.
items.quote: However, the financial performance of the venture was significantly lower than expectations and hence we took the decision to shut this right off on account of this.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt reduced by >10% Q-o-Q to INR 2,250 crores; net debt/EBITDA at 0.6x.
items.quote: We reduced our net debt by more than INR 280 crores in Q1 to a figure of INR 2,250 crores. The net debt to EBITDA for the consolidated operations stood at 0.6x at the end of June '24.

items.statement: EPR expense of INR 27 crores in Q1 FY25 is recurring, not one-off.
items.quote: No, Basudeb, the INR 27 crores of EPR expense is a regular item, that's not a one-off.

items.statement: Received new multi-year orders worth Rs. 1,000 crores from a leading European OEM through JV Marelli Talbros Chassis Systems; some orders commercializing now
items.quote: During the last year, we received orders over Rs. 1,000 crores during the last quarter in April 24. We received new multi-years orders worth Rs. 1,000 crores from a leading European OEM through our joint venture, Marelli Talbros Chassis Systems Private Limited.

items.statement: Full order book is about Rs. 2000 crores over 5 to 7 years; execution ramps from Rs. 150-155 crores to Rs. 190-220 crores annually
items.quote: The full order book is about Rs. 2000 crores. These are over 5 to 7 years. So, let's say Rs. 155 crores, Rs. 150 crores, then go to 190, then 220, like that.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 16.5% in Q1 FY25, up 150 bps YoY; management aspires to maintain around 16.5% for full year
items.quote: During the quarter, we have focused on cost optimization as well as a good product mix of domestic and export, which has led to an improved EBITDA of 16.5%, an increase of 150 basis points. We aspire to maintain these margins for the full year as well.

items.statement: Export EBITDA margin generally 2% higher than domestic, ranging 16-19% depending on customer
items.quote: EBITDA margin is generally 2% more than the domestic business, so it depends on the customer to customer. Sometimes it is 16%, sometimes 18%, in some cases 19% also.

items.statement: Targeting export share increase from current ~27% to upwards of 30% in next three years
items.quote: We are consciously working on increasing our exports from current levels of about 27% to upwards of 30% in the next three years.

items.statement: CV demand sluggish in Q1 with high dealer inventory; pickup expected post Q2 with infra projects and replacement demand
items.quote: Demand for CVs is likely to pick up pace post Quarter 2 of this year, with an uptick of infra projects post the monsoon. Replacement demand and mandatory scrapping of older government vehicles expected to support volume in FY25.

items.statement: EV revenue contribution rose from 3% to 3.3% in Q1; target 12% of total revenue with orders in hand, though some launches delayed 3-6 months
items.quote: In fact, if you see, in the last year, my EV contribution was 3% of our total revenue. In this quarter, we have achieved 3.3%. Going forward, we are committed to achieving a target of 12% of our total revenue, and orders are in hand.

items.statement: Potential Rs. 20-30 crore capex for new orders; not major Rs. 100 crore capex; depends on order finalization
items.quote: We are working on some orders where we require some decent CAPEX, not major, not Rs. 100 crore CAPEX, maybe Rs. 20 to Rs. 30 crore CAPEX in one day.

items.statement: Price increases pending 8-9 months received in last weeks; will reflect in Q2 results
items.quote: Here I want to add that there was some price increase pending with our major customers for last 8 to 9 months. That price increase has been received by the Company in the last weeks, which we did in this period also, which was not accounted in the results, which you will see in the second quarter.

items.statement: Exchange rate volatility (Dollar, Yen, Euro) creates pressure; recovery from customers takes time
items.quote: Of course we are importing also, and especially in the gasket division and in Marugo, we import a lot of stu ff. But you know how Dollar, Yen and E uro is moving. Of course, that pressure is on us and of course we recover from all customers, but it will take some

items.statement: Pune plant Phase 1 machines installed by September; volume Rs. 3 crore/month from October, ramping to Rs. 5 crore/month by Q4
items.quote: We have started some production also, but I think all the machines will be by September. But in the first phase, the machine will be installed, which I think the good volume will start coming up to Rs. 3 crores per month. Volume will come from October onwards from that plant. And it will go up to Rs. 5 crores in the last quarter.

items.statement: Marugo Rubber JV EBITDA target 13-14% in next 3 years; price increase from Maruti received, will reflect in coming quarters
items.quote: Our expectation is by next 3 years it should be around 13% to 14% EBITDA. See the EBITDA at the end of the year, don't see for this quarter, please. I request you. It will improve.

items.statement: Gasket & heat shield division anticipates 15% growth in FY25; heat shield revenue Rs. 50-60 crores
items.quote: Yes, if you see this division, we anticipate a growth of (+15%) in this financial year. Out of which, I think the heat shield this year will be around Rs. 50 crore plus. Rs. 50 to Rs. 60 crore will be heat shield.

items.statement: New products: large gaskets for heavy duty, plastic gaskets for EV, transportation gaskets for EV, heat shields for Tata/Mahindra, heavy forged components for excavators/highway equipment
items.quote: So, in gaskets, we are working on large gasket for heavy duty applications, we are working on some plastic components for EV, plastic gaskets for EV. We are working on some transportation gaskets for electric vehicles, new heat shield for Tata M otors, Mahindra's. And in forging, we are working on very heavy components now for excavators and the construction of highway equipment

items.statement: Rs. 65 crores from Nippon stake sale (after tax) placed in FDs at 8%; reserved for potential big project/JV, not normal operations
items.quote: That Rs. 65 crores, we have put in the FDs which is carrying an average interest of 8%, okay? And this money will be used, number one, if we come out with a big project. We are talking about, we will take out some money out of that.

items.statement: Marugo JV 90% of shifting issues resolved; remaining manpower issues to be resolved within one quarter
items.quote: No, 90% issue have been resolved, there are some manpower issues still, manpower is a little high, it should have been lower. We are working on that. I think within one quarter, that issue will also be resolved.

items.statement: Middleweight motorcycle segment grew 4-4.5% in Q1 FY25; Royal Enfield retail grew low-single-digit despite market confusion from new entrants
items.quote: Middleweight, what is happening, the middleweight the entire motorcycle, which has seen only almost about 4 - 4.5 percentage of growth over the first quarter of FY 24.

items.statement: Management expects middleweight segment growth to recover in coming months driven by new launches and festive season
items.quote: Very positive, it will start picking up in a few months' time, Pramod.

items.statement: Sherpa 450 platform (Himalayan 450 and Guerrilla 450) running at 8,000-8,500 units per month including initial Guerrilla ramp-up
items.quote: K platform as a whole, if I have to tell you Pramod, which is what, six months old, six months young baby, it is almost about 8,000 to 8,500 numbers per month is what we are tracking.

items.statement: Royal Enfield commodity benefit of 0.6% YoY on gross cost; Q-o-Q largely stable
items.quote: As far as commodities are concerned, I think we've got an impact of about 0.6% as far as commodities are concerned. So that benefit is flowing through in the GC.

items.statement: Spare parts and accessories share trending at around 15%, supporting gross cost
items.quote: I think the share of spare parts and accessories are doing well continues to be trending at around 15%.

items.statement: Royal Enfield capacity modularly expandable from 1.2 million to 1.3 million; K platform supply to meet demand in 1-2 months
items.quote: Overall capacity is 1.2 million Chandramouli, so 1.2 million to 1.3 million because capacity can be modularly increased.

items.statement: International retail sales increased in Q1 FY25 over Q1 FY24; green shoots visible but cautiously optimistic
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, our retail sales have increased over Q1 FY '24, that's why our wholesale also has been becoming better.

items.statement: LatAm and Europe showing good signs in exports; APAC picking up; new model launches in Brazil and other markets from now on
items.quote: In the international markets, especially LatAm is doing very well because our CKD plant is also fully in operation. And Europe started showing good signs.

items.statement: VECV expects commercial vehicle industry growth in balance of FY25 driven by government capex of ₹11.11 lakh crores and festive season
items.quote: And we should also note that due to elections, nothing much has happened on the investments on the capital spends from the government. And of course, now it will also be a challenge that they will have to do this entire spend in the remaining part of the year.

items.statement: VECV EBITDA margin at 7.7% in Q1 FY25 vs 7.9% last year; expects price management to improve margins as heavy-duty truck mix improves
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin in quarter one is 7.7% against 7.9% last year.

items.statement: VECV Q1 growth of 10% flattered by low base due to OBD2 transition preponement in Q4 FY24; July market dropped due to monsoons
items.quote: Even in the first quarter, even though the growth looked good at 10% in the first quarter. But that also we have to see that. Last year in the first quarter, the numbers were very low; base was small, because we had just moved to OBD2.

items.statement: VECV switched to new 25% tax regime from 35% after MAT credit utilization, resulting in deferred tax write-back and higher PAT
items.quote: Our PAT has significantly increased because of the write back of deferred tax, because now we have opted for the new tax regime at 25% tax rate. Earlier, we were at 35% tax rate.

items.statement: Hunter 350 attracting 19-25% first-time buyers; brand building and college connect programs planned to drive growth
items.quote: First-time buyers, maybe about 13%. 12% - 13% roughly in the portfolio level, and Hunter may be slightly higher, maybe about 19 to 25 percentage level first-time buyers.

items.statement: Marketing and brand building spend to increase as planned in P&L for FY25 across Classic, Hunter, Meteor and Continental GT
items.quote: Which is actually planned, Jinesh. So that's all planned in our P&L for the whole year. So you will see our investments, which will be there, but there will be an increased spend on the marketing and brand building.

items.statement: Expect 5-10% revenue growth and EBITDA margin of 13-13.5% for FY25, with potential upside if volumes pick up
items.quote: The outlook for thi s year is going to be maybe a small amount of growth, both in revenue and profitability. We are expe cting that, 5% to 10% growth is what we expect

items.statement: Order intake of Rs 882 crore in Q1 FY25 is highest in eight quarters; order backlog up 5% to Rs 1,777 crore
items.quote: Order intake improved significantly this quarter, mainly driven by Heavy Engineering, Mixing and Systems businesses. The last two quarters have now seen a strong order intake, and this quarter Rs.882 crores of order i ntake is the highest order intake in the last eight quarters. Our order backlog is also up by 5% to about Rs.1,777

items.statement: No expansion capex planned for FY25 or FY26; maintenance capex around 2-2.5% of revenue but likely lower
items.quote: the capex front, basically we don't have any expansion capex comi ng up this year, and most likely nothing in the next financial year as well. The maintenan ce capex we have alluded to towards some like 2%, 2.5% but will be much lower than that any which ways in this year

items.statement: Q1 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 11.3% due to lower volume absorption and pricing pressure; target FY25 margin 13-13.5%
items.quote: In terms of financial performance, our consolidated revenue for the q uarter was at Rs.785 crores, and EBITDA stood at Rs.89 crores, with a EBITDA margin of 11.3

items.statement: Pricing pressure persists in glass-lined business due to competitive intensity; margin improvement to come from internal cost efficiency program
items.quote: Plus also keep in mind, just because of the slowness in demand, the competitive intensity is much higher, an d hence there is definitely pricing pressure as

items.statement: Chemical and agrochemical sectors remain weak; agrochemical slowdown expected for 6-9 more months due to Chinese competition; specialty chemicals and pharma showing some recovery
items.quote: I feel that there is going to be still about six to nine months of further, slow down in this sector mainly driven by the Chinese competition. So, the Chinese are still dumping and still competing at a cost structure that the Indian companies are not being able to ki nd of compete at

items.statement: Mixing business at 8% of consolidated revenue in Q1; targeting $100M+ revenue in 3 years from current $45M base
items.quote: On the numbers front mixing for Q1 accounts for 8% of the total con solidated numbers. And of course, but of course being the focus area the growth trajectory will be faster in times

items.statement: Geopolitical impact minimal; interest rate cuts benefit international debt (SOFR-linked); China slowdown affects glass-lined demand
items.quote: The geopolitical impact not so much. The only thing that we have heard is that, from some of our customers that shipping costs for some of the chemicals and stuff has increased.

items.statement: India capacity utilization ~55-60%; Heavy Engineering plant at 90-100%; cost efficiency program underway for 9-12 months
items.quote: Today, we would be around in India, maybe 55%, 60% ,I would think maybe in Europe a little bit more, in the Europe and the US. China has been slow for us, so China would be a bit less.

items.statement: Three-year strategic plan to be communicated in 3-6 months focusing on diversification beyond chemical/pharma and glass-lined
items.quote: So, at least in the next maybe three to six months we should have something out there for you all, if not earlier, but we spent the last maybe four or five months working on this.

items.statement: Fertilizer segment EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs 4,500-5,000 for manufactured products remains intact
items.quote: That is intact. We spoke about Rs. 4,500 to Rs. 5,000 for manufactured products. I think that's pretty much intact.

items.statement: Approved 1 million ton brownfield granulation capacity expansion at Kakinada; final investment decision after intermediate capacity execution
items.quote: we have got approval during this quarter to expand our capacity at Kakinada by another million ton. So, as and when the right opportunity comes, we will be looking to expand the capacities as well for granulation

items.statement: Kakinada phosphoric and sulphuric acid plant construction commenced; major orders released; fixed processing plant at BMCC Senegal expected commissioning in Q2
items.quote: Further the Company has received all the statutory clearances for its proposed phosphoric acid and sulphuric acid plant in Kakinada and we have commenced activities during the quarter and major orders have been released.

items.statement: Q2 fertilizer margins expected to improve vs Q1 due to better procurement, captive production, Senegal rock blending, and demand normalization
items.quote: So, all this will help us to have an improved margin in the Q2. So, going forward, we have to see in terms of the subsidy rates for Rabi, how the commodity prices behave. But definitely, it will be much better than what we witnessed in Q1.

items.statement: Phosphoric acid contracted at $950/t for Q2 (up $2 vs Q1); potash at $283/t vs $319/t last year; ammonia and urea prices hardening
items.quote: We have finalized the PA price at $950 for Q2. This price will prevail up to September. There is a marginal increase of $2 over the previous quarter price.

items.statement: Industry phosphatic consumption up 11% in Q1 led by 42% NPK growth; reservoir levels up 52% YoY; sowing at 90M ha (83% normal); expect good Rabi season
items.quote: Phosphatic consumption for the industry increased by 11% during the quarter. This was led by improved NPK consumption, which went up by 42%, indicating a positive shift towards balanced nutrition.

items.statement: NPK share increased to 87% of nutrient sales; unique products 31%; manufacturing sales share improved; POS sales up 32% to 4.8 lakh tons; market share 11.7% vs 9.7%
items.quote: Between the NPK and DAP sales, the Company has increased the NPK sales share to 87%. Unique product sales stand at 31%. The share of the manufacturing sales also improved in the overall mix.

items.statement: Crop protection new products 22% of domestic formulation sales; 10 new products launched in Q1 including 4 patented; formulation share ~30% of crop protection sales
items.quote: we have seen that almost 22% of the sales in the domestic formulation today is coming from new products. When I say new product, these are products that have been introduced in the last 3 years.

items.statement: DMPAT plant for acephate backward integration approved; 6-8 months to commission; will cover 20-25% of requirements
items.quote: very recently we have got the business case approved. And it's a smaller capacity plant, which will come up in the next 6 to 8 months' time. This will help us to be a little more competitive in the Acephate space.

items.statement: Invested Rs 150 cr in Dhaksha (drone mfg) raising stake to 58%; invested Rs 24 cr in Ecozen raising stake to 5.54%
items.quote: Coromandel increased the shareholding in Dhaksha. This is a drone manufacturing company, where Coromandel had invested earlier. The overall stake has moved up to 58% through fresh issue of shares with an investment of Rs. 150 crores.

items.statement: Nano DAP facility commissioned at Kakinada; crossed 10 lakh litres volume; expect improved traction in Q2; industry substitution potential 20-25% over 3-5 years
items.quote: right now, Coromandel have crossed 10 lakhs litres of Nano, which is a very significant volume, and we do it in a very systematic way in terms of convincing the farmers and doing education across the country.

items.statement: Mill site services revenue potential INR 2-6 crores per mill per year; running one SAIL site; business growing as steel companies outsource more

But anywhere between INR 2 crores to INR 6 crores is generally a yearly potential out of that.

items.statement: Imports from China (INR 359 crores in FY24) will continue for large bore bearings not yet localized; localization depends on critical mass; wind bearings up to 1.5m needed for 5MW turbines
items.quote: But still, there is a consumption in India, which is large bore, which is not produced in India and you still get a very good cost for these bearings which are not tooled up in India from our Chinese counterparts. So that is there and will remain there.

items.statement: Employee cost lower due to gratuity adjustment last quarter not repeating this quarter; merit increases offset
items.quote: So gratuity, last quarter was there, this quarter was not there. That is the short answer.

items.statement: Non-bearing portfolio (belts, couplings, lubrication) from parent under discussion; no announcement or firm plan; parent evaluating ease of doing business, tax environment
items.quote: So the endeavour is on. But, again, no announcement or no firm plan, which I can say that, hey, next we'll do that. But yes, this is certainly a possibility. The parent has changed. The parents have belts. The parents have couplings. The parent has lubrication system, all this is there. They have the technology.

items.statement: Freight cost increase due to Red Sea adding 6 days transit; contributes ~3% to other expenditure; not a big needle mover; freight cost largely borne by end user
items.quote: It is -- my CFO, Mr. Avishrant, is saying it is 3%. Definitely, the cost has gone up compared to, say, last year with now -- with 6 days more on the water. So that cost has certainly gone up. Overall, it is 3%.

items.statement: Maintain FY25 revenue growth guidance of 15%-20% but will review after Q2FY25
items.quote: While the global industry landscape remains challenging, we maintain our growth outlook for the year, aggressively pursuing available opportunities to sustain momentum. We shall, however, closely monitor the emerging business scenarios and review our growth guidance after Q2FY25.

items.statement: Maintain FY25 gross margin guidance of 50%-51% and EBITDA margin guidance of 25%-26%
items.quote: So, we maintain our guidance that we expect to achieve a 50% to 51% gross margin, 25% to 26% EBITDA margin and these variations quarter-on-quarter will keep on happening depending on the product mix. But we maintained our earlier guidance of maintaining a 25% to 26% margin.

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs. 800-900 crore for FY25
items.quote: We have a plan of close to Rs. 800 crore – Rs. 900 crore CAPEX this year and we are moving in that direction.

items.statement: Order book currently around $1.5-$1.55 billion, mostly Agchem
items.quote: It is around $1.5-$1.55 billion.

items.quote: The gross margins and EBITDA improved mainly due to favorable product mix and operating leverage.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for FY25 expected at 22%-23% due to SEZ exemption change
items.quote: The ETR for FY25 is expected to be around 22% to 23% due to the tax exemption of our second SEZ at Jambusar moving from 100% to 50%.

items.statement: Domestic sowing momentum caught up in last 3-4 weeks, healthy Kharif recovery expected
items.quote: As the monsoon has progressed well, in the last three to four weeks, the sowing momentum has c aught on and is expected to achieve a healthy recovery in Kharif

items.statement: Launched 2 domestic brands in Q1 (PRESSEDO, OSHEEN ULTRA); pipeline of 20+ products for the year; Jivagro to launch 6 products in rest of year

Our product pipeline for domestic launches comprises more than 20 products and marks a healthy visibility of growth in the coming year.

items.statement: Pharma segment impacted by high customer inventory on 2 products; revenue visibility low for near term
items.quote: In our case, this is a long-term customer and one of the products is a new drug for that they have already build good inventory and now they are positioning the product. They are now going a little slow forf further procurement till the time they kind of come to a reasonable level of inventory.

items.statement: Plant Health Care acquisition on track for court approvals completion in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We are on track with obtaining the requisite court mandated approvals and hope to complete this process in the current quarter.

items.statement: Commercialized 2 new molecules in Q1 FY25; targeting 6-7 more for the year
items.quote: For the current fiscal, we have already commercialized two new molecules in Q1 and are looking to commercialize another 6 to 7 molecules for the sustained growth trend.

items.statement: Management expects to reach INR 1,000 crore run rate by end of FY25 if external factors improve
items.quote: I don't see no reason why by end of this year, we will not be able to start hitting close to the INR1,000 crores run rate.

items.quote: It is for capacity expansion and to the -- like I said, it is in a mandate for faucets, built in appliances, fabrications, nothing for inorganic, yes.

items.quote: No, these are absolutely new contracts. Fresh contract, they're going to bring in fresh revenue to the company.

items.quote: EBITDA margin for quarter 1 FY '25 stood at 18.3%. There is a marginal impact of integration of our U.S. subsidiary, United Granite LLC and the increase in export freight costs due to Red sea and container availability issues on the quarter 1 FY '25 EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Freight costs increased due to Red Sea crisis; management passing on costs gradually while maintaining margins

items.quote: Our business in the US and UK remain strong, with an increasing demand from existing customers, signaling positive plans. Europe continues to face persistent challenges due to high inflation, interest cost and geopolitical issues.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis, container availability, longer sailing times, high inflation, interest rates, geopolitical issues and US elections cited as external risks
items.quote: While the challenges lies, geopolitical situation and the crisis, which is some external factors, which are beyond our control.

items.statement: Completed QIP raising INR 125 crores for capacity expansion, new moulds, manufacturing lines, brand building and working capital
items.quote: We recently completed our successful QIP, raising INR125 crores, this fund will be allocated to expand manufacturing capacity, acquiring new moulds for our existing customers, to increase quartz sink business as well as for the manufacturing lines of appliances, faucets and fabrication.

items.statement: Domestic business targets INR 300 crore revenue in 5 years from current INR 150 crore run rate
items.quote: We would like to shape up and our vision is to be a INR300 crores company in five years' time.

items.statement: Faucet factory Phase 1 completed with 50,000 units annual capacity; Phase 2 under implementation

items.statement: No inorganic growth planned currently; focus on organic expansion in quartz sinks, faucets, built-in appliances and India market

items.statement: Strong demand across packaging, FMCG, pharma; rural demand resurgence; growth in paper and textile sectors
items.quote: Our outlook remains strong, supported by robust demand across key sectors such as packaging, FMCG and pharma. We are witnessing a resurgence in rural demand as alluded to by the FMCG majors and promising growth in the paper and textile sectors as well

items.statement: Industry growth typically at or above GDP rate; minimum GDP growth expected for industry verticals

items.statement: Value-added products (chocolates, beverages, oral care) expected to see renewed demand with rural recovery
items.quote: we hope that a renewed demand of our value add products whether which goes into recreational choices such as chocolates and say, beverages or even oral health care, higher end toothpaste, etc., we hope to see a better demand

items.statement: FY24 volume growth >5%; Q1 FY25 volume growth not disclosed

items.quote: It would be coming interest for 5-6 crores. Exact figures I do not have but yes, it is between 5-6 crores in Q2.

items.quote: But definitely 2nd Quarter on we will be doing as normal as last year or maybe 5% above on it. It is not going down.

items.quote: Because 2nd Quarter, we are looking as normal as last year or little bit 5% more than that. So, according to me 2nd Quarter would be the correct position where we can say occupancy will be 65% or 70% for Orchid.

items.quote: Due to the Pollution Board. That is a Maharashtra Pollution Board which they used to come and to raid the things. So, to avoid all these things we have voluntarily submitted our application. Application is approved by the Maharashtra Pollution Board, and they have almost Rs. 1.10 crores we have paid for the Pollution Board as one-time fees.

items.statement: Redeemed balance 10,000 convertible debentures (face value Rs 57,983 each) for Rs 63.78 crore; funded by Rs 20 crore Axis Bank loan and internal accruals; debt now ~Rs 130 crore at 10.75% from Axis Bank only
items.quote: We have successfully redeemed the balance 10,000 outstanding convertible debentures of the face-value of Rs. 57,983 each. The redemption of the value was total 63.78 crores in which we have taken 20 crores loan from Axis Bank. Rest of the whole amount is paid from internal accruals.

items.statement: SBI Special Situation Fund converting warrants to equity; Kaushal Biyani appointed Additional Director (Non-Executive Non-Independent) effective 12 Aug 2024
items.quote: I am also excited to share that a SBIFM Special Situation Fund which was our previously NCD holder in KHIL will be entering as an Equity Holder consequent upon the conversion of the warrants into equity.

items.statement: Revenue target of ₹1,800 crore for FY25 representing around 15% growth
items.quote: we continue to anticipate revenues of ₹1,800 crore this fiscal representing around 15% growth for the fiscal year

items.statement: Expect CAGR of approximately 15% to 16% in top line beyond FY26
items.quote: we are expecting a CAGR of approximately 15% to 16% in the top line

items.statement: Full year capex target of roughly ₹151 crore for FY25
items.quote: For the full year, we have a target of roughly ₹151 crore for FY25, reflecting the heightened level of activity

items.statement: New orders of ₹650 crore booked in Q1 FY25

items.quote: With this, our total new order booking has surpassed ₹.9,500 crore which is executable over a period of 6 years from 2023-24 upto 2028-29

items.quote: So, in quarter 1, we noted yes, there was a good increase in two-wheeler segment around 20%, but still our contribution was just 37%. So, we have ideally reduced our contribution from last year's 40% to 37%

items.quote: So 17-20% is our CAGR, kind of a guidance which we have given for the next 3yrs. So we will be like on track. Yes.

items.statement: Export revenue surged 26.3% YoY, export share increased to 18% from 16.9%
items.quote: On the export front , we are excited to report a significant uptick in performance with export and overseas revenue surging by 26.3% year over year in Q1FY25. This has increased the share of export sales in our top line to 18% in this quarter , up from 16.9% in the previous year.

items.statement: Expect glass prices to moderate from Q2 onwards
