items.statement: RBI special audit completed on May 27 was satisfactory and compliance certificate submitted
items.quote: A s pecial audit was commissioned by RBI and that has been completed on May 27, a couple of months ago. And we believe that it was satisfactory, and verified and validated all the compliances that we had done

items.statement: Management expects RBI to lift gold loan restrictions at an early date but cannot give certainty on timing
items.quote: And we expect that RBI will lift the restrictions in a short time from now. The RBI processes are involved and therefore we cannot have any certainty of when this will happen. But we anticipate that to happen at an early date.

items.statement: No employee retrenchment or branch closures despite gold loan embargo
items.quote: We have not retrenched any employee, nor have we shut down any branch. So, we continue to be confident and optimistic about our resumption of normal business as soon as possible.

items.statement: Home loan business had slack quarter in April-June but expects stronger growth due to government affordable housing push
items.quote: Our home loan business has seen a slack quarter in April to June. But the government has come out with very strong support and impetus for this business. They allocated significantly higher resources for affordable housing. So, we expect that this business, which had a relatively slow growth rate in last one or two years, will also have stronger growth.

items.statement: Microfinance impacted by bank credit line squeeze after gold loan embargo and election-related asset quality stress
items.quote: In microfinance, business has also been impacted by the squeeze of credit lines by banks in the wake of orders on our gold loan business. Also, in the last quarter due to election, the asset quality has suffered, and the provisions and losses remain at an elevated level in this business in this quarter also.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT before non-controlling interest was Rs 338 crore, down 28% YoY and 21% QoQ
items.quote: At a consolidated level for the quarter Q1 FY '25, the profit after tax before non-controlling interest was Rs. 338 crores, down by 28% Y-o-Y and down 21 % on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Pre-provision operating profit was Rs 647 crore, down 18% YoY and 35% QoQ
items.quote: We recorded pre-provision operating profit of Rs. 647 crores, down 18% Y-o-Y and down 35% on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Consolidated loan AUM grew 2% YoY but degrew 12% QoQ to Rs 69,610 crore
items.quote: On a consol basis, we degrew by around 12% on quarter-on-quarter basis, touching AUM of around Rs. 69,610 crores.

items.statement: Core product AUM (Microfinance, Gold loan, Home loan, Digital finance, LAP) grew 4% YoY but degrew 12% QoQ to Rs 67,853 crore
items.quote: If I further dissect the AUM on our core products, which is largely Microfinance, Gold loan, Home loan, Digital finance and LAP, there we grew Y-o-Y by around 4%, and degrew by around 12% on quarter-on-quarter basis to Rs. 67,853 crores.

items.statement: Gross NPA at 2.2% and net NPA at 1.1%, up 40 bps and 4 bps YoY respectively; provision coverage ratio at 128%
items.quote: Our gross NPA stood at around 2.2% and net NPA was around 1.1%, which is up by around 40 basis point and 4 basis points respectively when compared to the same period last year. With the implementation of the expected credit loss under IndAS, provision coverage ratio on NPAs stands at 128%.

items.statement: Raised Rs 2,886 crore through term loans, bonds, refinance and assigned Rs 1,769 crore of other loans in Q1
items.quote: also raised funds in aggregate to around Rs. 2,886 crores through term loan , bond, refinance. And also assigned around Rs. 1,769 crores of other loans

items.statement: Repaid Rs 15,700 crore to all lenders since embargo including Rs 2,239 crore to capital market lenders
items.quote: Just to add to what Nirmal highlighted, we additionally also repaid to our capital market lenders close to around Rs. 2,239 crores. So, in aggregate the entire repayments since the embargo to all our lenders have been around Rs. 15,700 crores.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents including committed credit lines at Rs 6,853 crore; positive ALM with inflows exceeding outflows across all buckets
items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalents including committing credit lines from banks and institutions was around Rs. 6,853 crores adequate to meet not just some near-term liabilities but also to support growth in some of the other businesses which continue to operate. We have a positive ALM whereby inflows cover exceeds the outflows across all buckets.

items.statement: Net gearing at 2.8x after May 2024 capital infusion; capital adequacy: NBFC 27.8%, HFC 46.5%, Samasta 27%
items.quote: With the infusion of capital that we raised in the month of May of '24, our net gearing stands around 2.8x. Supported by that, our capability NBFC entities stood at around 27.8%, for HFC it was 46.5%, and for Samasta it was 27%.

items.statement: Management will wait at least one more quarter before giving clear volume guidance for the year due to logistics uncertainty.
items.quote: we want to wait and watch at least for one more quarter before we give you a clear volume guidance, at least for this year.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion at Kerala GIDC for composite mill rubber and composite liner plant with Rs. 65 crores capex, expected commissioning by end of year.
items.quote: This CAPEX has required us to spend about Rs. 65 crores. We expect this facility to be commissioned towards the end of this year.

items.statement: Total capital outlay for the year is about Rs. 250 crores including Rs. 35 crores captive power, Rs. 65 crores mill liner composite facility, and Rs. 150 crores grinding media phase one.
items.quote: total as we speak , our outlay remains at about Rs. 250 crores, and we will keep updating as things evolve from here.

items.statement: Approximately 5,000-6,000 tonnes of orders could not be shipped this quarter due to container unavailability and extended supply chain times.
items.quote: at around 5 ,000 tonnes, 6,000 tonnes of orders which were supposed to be shipped this quarter, could not be shipped.

items.statement: Product mix improved with higher casting and higher priced products, reflected in higher selling price realization this quarter.
items.quote: Overall, if you have seen the numbers, the product mix is better where there is higher casting, higher priced product . A nd you ar e right , that is reflected in the higher selling price, yes , higher realization.

items.statement: Freight cost is a complete pass-through on cost-plus basis; freight from India to Latin America rose from $100 to $400 per tonne.
items.quote: the freight cost for sending a container from here to say Latin America, which was about $100, has gone up now to $400 per tonne. And more importantly, the container availability is just not there

items.statement: Targeted volume growth opportunity remains unchanged but logistics uncertainty may delay conversions; management evaluating long-term options including potential overseas manufacturing.
items.quote: targeted volume growth year-over-year target and the opportunity remains the same. But in all honesty, we want to wait and watch at least for one more quarter before we give you a clear volume guidance

items.statement: Added rubber and composite liner capability to complete full product suite; 20,000 tonnes additional capacity expected, targeting niche efficiency solutions not price competition.
items.quote: We expect about 20,000 tonnes of additional capacity in this configuration to be available to us. Of course, mill liner sales and penetration and all of that we have discussed at length in the past few quarters.

items.statement: Container shortage and Red Sea crisis causing 2-3 month shipping delays vs 30-40 days previously; customers on wait-and-watch for new conversions due to unpredictable pricing and timelines.
items.quote: What we used to do in 30- 40 days is now taking more than two, two and a half to even three m onths. So, that's indeed a challenge which we are trying to circumvent.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of Rs. 500 crores; net cash stands at about Rs. 3,500 crores before buyback and dividend outflows.
items.quote: We have also done a buyback; Board approved a buyback of Rs. 500 crores. So, that should be getting through in the next few days , next few weeks . Our net cash stands at about Rs. 3,500 crores

items.statement: Brazil anti-dumping duty terminated (11.8% reduced to 6.5% CVD); countervailing duty sunset review outcome expected in 2-3 months; expect Brazil volumes upwards of 20,000 tonnes in next 12 months.
items.quote: Going forward, in next 12 months, it will be surely upwards of 20,000 tonnes is what we expect in the market.

items.statement: Copper mine penetration ramping up; currently heavyweight on gold, catching up on copper; all three metals (copper, gold, iron) expected to equally drive growth long-term.
items.quote: over a longer period, all the three would be more or less equally driving our growth, that is what we perceive.

items.statement: Customer value addition from integrated solutions ranges from $2-5 million annually on low end to $150 million on high end for copper mines through throughput, recovery, and power savings.
items.quote: for a copper customer that can vary from , on the lowest side it is only $2 million to $5 million, on the higher side to maybe $150 million a year.

items.statement: Company on track to achieve volume guidance given at beginning of year
items.quote: I am delighted to share that the Company is on track to achieve the volume guidance given at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Expect to achieve 3 million tons mining capacity in Q4 FY25 if approvals in place by end of Q3
items.quote: If a guidance, we have given 3 million basis, we have assumed there will be some production of additional capacity in Q4 of this financial year because the current mining capacity is 2.35-2.4. So, we expect we should be able to achieve 3 million if that was in place by the end of Q3.

items.statement: Mining capacity expansion approvals expected by December 2024
items.quote: Basically, approvals are expected to be placed by December 2024.

items.statement: Pellet capacity expansion from 2.7 to 4.7 million tons on schedule for commissioning by June 2026
items.quote: The project of increasing pellet capacity from 2.7 to 4.7 is running on schedule and same is expected to be commissioned by June 2026.

items.statement: Integrated steel plant 2 million ton capacity environmental approval process expected to complete by December 2024
items.quote: Environment impact assessment study is now finalized and being filed with MOEF for final presentation. The process is expected to be completed by December '24.

items.statement: Integrated steel plant project will take about 36 months from ground breaking ceremony
items.quote: The project will take about 36 months from the ground breaking ceremony.

items.statement: Rolling mill modification for structural steel completed and production started
items.quote: I am happy to announce that modification of Rolling Mill for manufacture of its structural steel has been completed and production of structural steel has started.

items.statement: Strip mill commissioning expected by September 2024
items.quote: The Strip Mill, we are also commissioning Strip Mill along with this Rolling Mill with a separate line and that is expected to be commissioned by September.

items.statement: 70 MW solar power project for pellet plant expected to commission by Q1 FY26
items.quote: GPIL has planned to set up an additional 70 MW solar power project to meet the power requirement of the upcoming pellet plant, which we expect to commission by Q1 FY26, coinciding with the commissioning of pellet plant.

items.statement: Board approved Rs. 75 crores investment for energy efficiency project generating 11 MW additional power with 2-year payback
items.quote: The Board has approved an investment of Rs. 75 crores for this energy efficiency project which will generate an additional power of 11 MW without requiring any additional fuel. The project expected payback for this project is about 2 years, with cost saving of Rs. 38 crores per annum and this is expected to result in additional carbon reduction intensity by 2,59,415 tons.

items.statement: EBITDA margin increased significantly to 30% in Q1 FY25 from 23% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin increased significantly to 30% as compared to 23% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Iron ore pellet realization increased 3% Y-o-Y and 4% Q-o-Q to Rs. 10,500 per ton
items.quote: The realization of iron ore pellet increased by 3% and 4% respectively on Y-o-Y and quarter-on-quarter basis to Rs. 10,500 a ton.

items.statement: Finished steel products realization decreased 5-6% Y-o-Y but increased 7-8% Q-o-Q
items.value: 5% to 6% decrease Y-o-Y, 7% to 8% increase Q-o-Q
items.quote: Realization for finished steel products decreased in the range of 5% to 6% on Y-o-Y and increased 7% to 8% quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Domestic iron ore pellet market strong due to shortage in Chhattisgarh region, not planning exports currently
items.quote: There has been no addition of backward integration in terms of pellet supply or additional iron ore. The sources will be the same, which is NMDC, ONGC and the pellet makers. So, we feel there will be a shortage of iron ore in this area, the pellet prices will be on the higher side irerespective of the international market

items.statement: Supreme Court ruling allows states to levy tax on mineral rights; Jharkhand already imposed Rs. 100 tax, Chhattisgarh may follow
items.quote: We should be, to be honest, something we never would like to, but we really can't comment because it is a state matter. It is up to the state government, Jharkhand just passed in the assembly to impose Rs. 100 tax on the mine industry. So, we really can't comment. Hopefully, nothing imposes but if there is an imposition, we have to comply.

items.statement: Pellet production guidance lowered from 2.6 to 2.45 million tons for FY25 due to annual shutdown in Q2
items.quote: Yes. So, there is an annual shutdown plant for one or two plants which will take about 50 years of operation that happens every 4-5 years in cycle. So, that is why we have lowered the guidance in this financial year from 2.6 to 2.45.

items.statement: Management expects to sustain adjusted EBITDA margins in the high 15s or early 16s percent range, prioritizing growth investments over margin expansion.
items.quote: But, we're not banking them for any kind of margin improvement projections because we are in the growth phase, we are also continuing to invest in our sales a nd marketing efforts in our partnerships like being out there with our partners for events and other things. So , we hope to sustain our margin levels at reasonably in the high 15s or early 16s, kind of levels

items.statement: Management is optimistic about H2 2024 market sentiment improving, citing early signs of deal activity across sectors and geographies, while monitoring US elections and Middle East uncertainty.
items.quote: So overall, we are optimistic of the market sentiment improving in the second half of the calendar year. We are seeing early signs of deal activity in the market. We are seeing traction, which is actually across sectors and geographies.

items.statement: Discretionary spend revival is unlikely in 2024 as US clients are at budget year-end; decision-making may improve for 2025 budgets post-election.
items.quote: Looking at massive or significant increase in discretionary spend this year is a little unrealistic. What we are seeing is where there were project decisions that were pending that were put on hold or people were unsure and were undecided, some of those have opened up, and those are things that we are capturing.

items.statement: AI and GenAI work is being won at higher price points but is not yet material enough to impact overall EBITDA margins.
items.quote: We have started winning some of AI related work, which comes at a higher price point but it is really not material enough to make a difference on our final EBIT DA margin at this point

items.statement: Velotio acquisition earnout of INR 241 crores via optionally convertible preference shares is redeemable after 2 more years; funding may involve stock swap subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: Those are redeemable after another 2 years. So , there is 3 year window for the shareholders of Velotio to stay in the company. So ultimately, kind of the vesting or the final issuance will happen after another 2 years because 1 year has already passed.

items.statement: Pipeline activity and TCV/ACV conversion rates have increased versus 6 months ago, though management wants more high-value conversions before higher confidence.
items.quote: From TCV, ACV activity from where we were 6 months back or 3 quarters ago, we're clearly seeing a higher activity. I would love to see more higher value conversions before I can feel far more confident.

items.statement: US election outcome and Middle East situation could create uncertainty; telecom/high-tech vertical weakness persists with no significant revival yet.
items.quote: Very clearly, we'll watch out for the elections in the U.S. and kind of developing situation in the Middle East because those could cause some uncertainty. But overall, so far, we are optimistic.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 35.5% in Q2 from 33.7% in Q1 and 34.8% a year ago, driven by utilization and billable days, offset by salary increases.
items.quote: The gross margin was 35.5% compared to 33.7% last quarter and 34.8% same quarter last year. Gross margin is resultant of improved utilization, higher billable days as offset by increas ed average salary at our offshore

items.statement: No specific revenue or margin guidance provided; management hopes to sustain adjusted EBITDA in high 15s/early 16s and aims for industry-leading growth in CY25 if momentum continues.
items.quote: And if we do get that momentum over the next 2 or 3 quarters, then absolutely, we will exit strong, and it will give us a good foundation to build towards industry leading growth for the next year.

items.statement: Company added more than two dozen new logos in Q2, including two from Blackstone portfolio; tracking pipeline strength, average deal size, win rates, and deal-to-revenue velocity.
items.quote: Overall, the Company has added a significant number of logos. We've added more than 2 dozen logos across the Company . And I think we've also added, if I'm not wrong, 2 new logos from a Blackstone portfolio perspective.

items.statement: Management says visibility is not there and it is very difficult to say if positive numbers will come in coming quarters
items.quote: So challenges are there, visibility is not there. So it is very difficult to say. We have been improving quarter-on-quarter, let's see how does it work out.

items.statement: Domestic demand increase ahead of festival season is lower than expected
items.quote: While the Indian domestic story remains largely intact, we are witnessing a lower-than-expected increase in demand ahead of the festival season.

items.statement: Export demand for home textiles is growing 5-10%
items.quote: home textile, yes. In exports, so far, our products, which we manufacture curtains and upholstery, our exports are growing little bit there. We are seeing better demand there

items.statement: Planned INR 800-900 crore project dropped due to lack of market visibility; only routine capex continues
items.quote: We have already dropped that because it was INR 800-900 crores project. And since the visibility of the textile market is not there, and we may think of something else, we keep on evaluating.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross margin at 44%, up 4% quarter-on-quarter; EBITDA INR 25 crores vs INR 13 crores in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 44%, which is higher by 4% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. EBITDA for the quarter was INR 25 crores as against INR 13 crores in Q4 FY24.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, Red Sea crisis, high ocean freights, Bangladesh turmoil, and recession fears in USA creating challenging environment
items.quote: The recent developments of heightened geo-political tensions in West Asia, political turmoil in neighboring Bangladesh, increased ocean freights, supply chain disruptions and recession fears in USA have exacerbated the already challenging business environment.

items.statement: Launching 12 new Nesterra collections annually; maintaining 50-60 collections in market with 5-year lifecycle
items.quote: We have already launched 36 collections and every year we are launching 12 new collections. So this year also, we will be launching 12 new collections and normally one collection has a life cycle of 5 years.

items.statement: Home textile business now EBITDA positive; cut service picking up; Panipat warehouse improving North market delivery
items.quote: In home textiles we have curtains and upholstery. 3 years back, we had started our own cut service, and that is picking up. If you take 3 years data, you will find that our losses have been going down, and now we are EBITDA positive in that business also.

items.statement: Total long-term debt reduced by INR 22 crores and working capital borrowing reduced by INR 27 crores in Q1 FY25; debt-to-equity at 0.81
items.quote: Total long-term debt further reduced by INR 22 crores and working capital borrowing also reduced by INR 27 crores in Q1 FY25. Our debt-to-equity is maintained constantly below 1, around 0.81 as of now.

items.statement: Expect double-digit EBITDA margin and healthy substantial topline growth, targeting around Rs 2,000 crore for FY25
items.quote: But certainly we should be going into the double digits for the EBITDA margin and growth of topline also will be healthy and substantial as we had guided for the year. So, we are on target for that, to get to that around 2,000 mark.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross margin at 44.9%, stable vs Q4 FY24 adjusted 44%, supported by blends momentum
items.quote: Gross margins are at 44.9% which is stable when we compare it to Q4FY24's adjusted margins of 44%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 7.2%, significant improvement vs last quarter
items.quote: The resultant EBITDA stood at 7.2%, which is a significant improvement as compared to the last quarter.

items.statement: Global industrial growth stable but weaker demand in many markets; US resilient, China stagnant, Europe soft, LatAm returning to normalcy
items.quote: Global industrial growth was stable but remained hampered by weaker global demand in many of our markets. Regional demand remains resilient in USA. China seems to be stagnant and struggling with its local economic weakness. Softness in Europe is more than evident as you know.

items.statement: Catechol at sub $1 sale price impacting topline and margins; Hydroquinone chain prices in negative trend last month; Vanillin price steadily moving up in recent weeks
items.quote: Catechol remains at sub $1 sale price, which not only impacts topline but also our margins.

items.statement: Hydroquinone chain prices in negative trend last month; raw material prices rising with crude
items.quote: Hydroquinone chain, the prices are in negative trend in last one month.

items.statement: Blends revenue grew 13.4% QoQ, sustaining momentum and supporting margins
items.quote: The revenue from blends have grown at a rate of 13.4% as compared to last quarter.

items.statement: Europe Diphenol facility under shutdown; negative EBITDA of Rs 10 crore in Q1 likely to continue next quarter; repurpose to take six months, negative drag for couple more quarters
items.quote: Negative EBITDA of around Rs. 10 crores in this quarter in Europe and a loss of 15%.

items.statement: Europe repurpose activity to take six months; negative drag expected for a couple more quarters
items.quote: It's too early because the repurpose activity itself is going to take six months. So, we think that there will be a negative drag for a couple of more quarters from this Company.

items.statement: Italy plant repurpose CAPEX Rs 2-3 million, 6-9 months timeline, revenue from next year, minimum EBITDA 10-12%
items.quote: It's an anticipated cost of Rs 2 to Rs 3 million on CAPEX. It will take six to nine months to complete the project. And the revenues will start from the next year. The minimum expected EBITDA is around 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Heliotropin plant repurpose in China expected cost Rs 20-30 crore, borne by partner, no cash flow to company
items.quote: So, we are expecting cost between Rs 20 to Rs 30 crores on repurposing the plant. These costs have to be borne by our partner. This will not be to the company.

items.statement: Lockheed Martin commissioning first commercial battery this year; substantial potential in 2-3 years but too early to estimate near-term contribution
items.quote: I think it's too early in the day to estimate what that business will look like in the near future. Yes, but two to three years out, the kind of numbers that could potentially be substantial.

items.statement: Vitafor acquisition acquired June 11, 2024; current run rate ~1 million Euros/month topline, low EBITDA margin, expected to improve to group levels over next few quarters
items.quote: currently the run rate is abo ut a million Euros a month, topline and low EBITDA margin. I think that will improve as we go along in the next few quarters to more like what we see in the other

items.statement: US and EU anti-dumping actions against Chinese Vanillin likely positive; buyers already developing Camlin as long-term supplier
items.quote: the initiation of anti -dumping action by local manufacturers in US and Europe against the dumping and predatory pricing by Chinese manufacturers is likely to have a positive impact on our business whe never this anti-dumping regulation is promulgated by the US and European governments

items.statement: Vanillin legacy inventory liquidated; new Methyl Vanillin campaign started end-May with process stability and quality; customer response more than encouraging
items.quote: have now liquidated almost the entire legacy inventory of Vanillin. The revenues of aroma were Rs. 13.42 crores in current quarter. The new campaign of Methyl Vanillin was commenced as we had declared in the last investor call also by the end of May. This new campaign has resulted in process stability as well as quality of the product

items.statement: Q1 was expected to be soft; confidence in full-year guidance from Vanillin green shoots and operating efficiency improvements
items.quote: Yes. Quarter 1 was going to be soft.

items.statement: Crude oil production target 4 MMT+ and natural gas 5 BCM within next 2-3 years; trajectory on track
items.quote: we can very much assure you that the trajectory we have projected in the last year is, in fact, and we have been moving in that trajectory only.

items.statement: Planning 78 wells in FY25 and 100 wells each in FY26 and FY27; workover growth ~20%
items.quote: this year, we were plan -- we are planning 78 wells. And if I talk about the next year, then we are planning 100 wells. So if you can talk about '26, '27, we are planning 100 drilling -- new drilling to be completed.

items.statement: Capex FY25: Oil India INR6,880 crore, NRL INR9,650 crore
items.value: Oil India INR6,880 crore, NRL INR9,650 crore
items.quote: For Oil India, it is -- '24, '25, it is INR6,880 crores. That is the Cap ex. The NRL '24, '25 is available, INR9,650 crores.

items.statement: NRL expansion project cost INR28,000 crore, 65% physical progress, completion expected December 2025
items.quote: As you know, this cost for this NRL is -- this is INR28,000 crores. Currently, the physical progress is 65%. And we are expecting that the completion will be by end 2025, that is December 2025.

items.statement: NRL expansion equity contribution INR8,500 crore total; Oil India share 69%; ~INR19,000 crore already invested
items.quote: INR8,500 crore will be total equity part because INR18,000 crores has been -- as borrowings.

items.statement: APM gas price to increase by $0.25/MMBtu from April 2025 (from current $6.5/MMBtu)
items.quote: There is a $0.25 increase MMBtu. Right now, it is 6.5 MMBtu. That is what we are realizing, and as per the guidelines that will be increasing by $0.25 from first April '25.

items.statement: Indradhanush Gas Grid first sales expected December 2024; will enable gas evacuation to mainland via Urja Ganga
items.quote: This pipeline, we are expecting the first sales by December this year.

items.statement: NRL expansion to add ~2 MMSCMD gas demand once fully operational
items.quote: For NRL, it will be close to, once the expansion is received and the production would be 2 MMSCMD for expanded capability.

items.statement: Gas offtake potential 3-3.5 BCM within Northeast; additional volumes can go to mainland via Urja Ganga
items.quote: Some broad indication, if I have to say that as of now, I can say that from 3 BCM to 3.5 BCM can be within the area and rate, whatever we produce, we can dispose it to the mainland India.

items.statement: EBITDA margin Q1 FY25 43.79% vs 53.49% Q1 FY24; decline due to SAED increase to $10.27/bbl and INR204 crore GST on royalty provision
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q1 FY '25 is 43.79%, vis -a-vis, 53.49% for Q1 FY '24. The reduction in EBITDA margin is mainly due to the increase in SAED from USD2.59 per barrel in Q1 FY '24 to USD10.27 per barrel in Q1 FY '25 and provision made towards service tax GST on royalty during Q1 FY '25 amounting to INR204 crores, vis-a-vis, nil for Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: GST on royalty provision INR3,300 crore total; Supreme Court 9-judge bench ruling under MMDR Act does not cover Oil India case; separate judgment needed
items.quote: So total amount, we have already provided is roughly about INR3,300 crores till now. But accordingly, any decision of the Supreme Court, although it may go against us, it will not have any impact on the bottom line of the company, first of all.

items.statement: Bangladesh unrest impact on NRL offtake/exports too early to assess
items.quote: Actually, it is too early to comment on this. But anyway, we'll just take the data from NRL, and we can come back on that.

items.statement: Exploration success rate 50-60%; development wells near 100%; aspiration to raise exploration success to 80-90%
items.quote: in terms of ex ploratory wells, our success rate over the years have been hovering in the range of 50% to 60%. So that number still holds actually

items.statement: Operating wells 150-200; majority associated (oil+gas); few non-associated gas wells
items.quote: total number of wells varies from 150 to 200. And some of the wells -- majority of the wells are producing oil and gas, both. Associated well, we call it because it produce oil and gas, both.

items.statement: Upstream cost inflation expected 5-6% at $80/bbl crude; potential GST inclusion could yield input tax credit savings
items.quote: we can expect a normal increase over the current prices but like right now, the crude price is hovering around $80 per barrel. So we expect that the prices, whatever increase will be say, 5% to 6%...

items.statement: Network guidance reaffirmed; targeting 180 Domino's India store openings in FY25 with pace increasing in Q2
items.quote: So this year I think we have stated we are targeting 180 stores opening. And I think, at the moment, we feel confident we'll increase pace in Q2.

items.statement: Hong's Kitchen to add 20-25 stores in FY25, but focus is on customer satisfaction and store profitability rather than store count
items.quote: So about Hong's we'll add 20 to 25 stores. But again, these are not like a number that we are chasing as a goal. Rather we are chasing customer satisfaction scores, store throughput in terms of revenue and the restaurant level profitability.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin at 19.3% in Q1 FY25, down 178 bps YoY but up 22 bps QoQ; expect improvement from Q4 FY24 lows
items.quote: In India, the revenue at Rs. 14.4 billion was up by 9.9% yoy. EBITDA margins at 19.3% while was lower by 178 bps yoy, it was sequentially up 22 bps.

items.statement: DP Eurasia EBITDA margin at 25% in Q1 FY25, up 871 bps YoY but down 150 bps QoQ; PAT margin at 9.2%
items.quote: EBITDA margin came in at 25% (+871 bps YoY and -150 bps QoQ). PAT margin was strong and accretive to Indian business, at 9.2% (+660 bps YoY and +300 bps QoQ)

items.statement: No price increase in Domino's India for 8 consecutive quarters; absorbed cost inflation via internal optimization and Project Vijay; free delivery with Rs.150 threshold
items.quote: It is important to emphasize here that its now 8th straight quarter of no price increase in Domino's and by waiving off delivery fee we have significantly enhanced value quotient for our consumers further.

items.statement: Domino's India LFL growth at 3% in Q1 FY25; delivery LFL grew 12.1%; dine-in LFL grew 1.7% QoQ; growth driven by execution not macro tailwinds
items.quote: We are excited about the vast opportunity for our brands and have ambitious plans for all brands and markets in which we operate. And through commensurate ahead-of-the-curve investments in supply chain and technology, building on consumer love, we are confident that we will achieve newer records and milestones in the future.

items.quote: The average selling price stood at INR 585 in Q1, driven by higher saliency of open footwear, which was close to 22% versus 18% last year.

items.statement: Economical portfolio below INR 1000 increased to 30% saliency from 27% YoY, semi-premium INR 1000-1500 rose to 30% from 25%, premium 1500+ dropped to 40% from 46%
items.quote: So, our ratio to economical has actually also slightly gone up for below 1000 to 30%. salience versus 27% year on year and 1000 to 1500 for your semi premium has gone up actually from 25% to 30% again year on year, but our 1500 plus portfolio premium segment has dropped from 46% to 40% year on year.

items.statement: Anticipate demand resurgence post monsoon with additional momentum from festive season
items.quote: We anticipate a resurgence in demand post monsoon with additional momentum expected from the festive season.

items.statement: Expect category growth in lower double digits for FY25 and aim to grow in line or faster than category
items.quote: We anticipate I think in lower double digit for sure like kind of category growth this year, FY25 to happen, just waiting for the markets to sort of demand scenario to come back.

items.statement: Aspire to return to 17-18% EBITDA margins in normalized demand scenario, up from 15.8% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: If you really want me to call it out, we will be aspiring to get to those numbers for sure. There is no doubt even in a very tough macro to be very honest, whatever one was highly muted in terms of demand and in spite of that, we've been able to deliver 15.8% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Added 1 new LFS account in Q1 FY25, expansion to all stores of that chain will be gradual over 3-4 quarters
items.quote: The growth in the L FS is a gradual progression. I mean, we do get an entry into certain number of test stores and then eventually it amplifies based on the success of our product or the particular category

items.statement: BIS compliance fully effective from August 1, non-BIS inventory liquidation allowed till June 2025, smaller players face significant cost impact
items.quote: BIS is fully in effect now as of 1st of August and you know the government has mandated time till end of June 2025 for everyone to liquidate their non

items.statement: Sneakers portfolio grew ~120% YoY in Q1 FY25, identified as key growth lever alongside women and kids category
items.quote: The sneakers portfolio has basically grown by almost 120% ev en though the base is obviously smaller compared to the sports portfolio. But the demand and the acceptance in the market is very

items.statement: Open footwear ASP is INR 150-200 lower than closed footwear, open category sold at INR 499-999 range
items.quote: The ASP difference in the range of ₹150 to ₹200. The difference would be 150 to 200.

items.statement: Channel inventory at 60-80 days in distribution channel, largely normalized and in line with market demand
items.quote: Currently, we continue to hold around 60 odd days of inventory in the distribution channel anywhere between 60 to 80 days and that continues to be the norm considering the peak time for production of the NPDs.

items.statement: Employee cost increased 21% YoY due to front-end headcount additions in distribution and stores plus annual increments
items.quote: OK, so this is primarily driven by our additional headcounts primarily in the front-end function, the distribution business and also in the stores with the addition of new floors over period. And so of course the year-on-year inflation through the increment so these two after the driving, the higher employee cost.

items.statement: July onwards seeing decent recovery in demand, no further ASP drop anticipated
items.quote: we don't really see a big increase in our ASP in FY25 if you recall, because we anticipated the demand scenario, but we d o see you know demand getting back on track very soon like even July onwards we've seen a decent recovery in demand

items.statement: New multi-year 4WD transfer case order from existing customer with ~INR800 cr life-cycle revenue, SOP H2 FY27
items.quote: It's a multi-year contract that, as per the indications that have come from the customer, has a life cycle of about seven years, and based on the volume projections that they have given for capacity planning, has a life cycle revenue of about slightly over INR800 crores.

items.statement: Exports expected to be at least 15% of revenue in FY25 and well beyond 20% in FY26
items.quote: I think for FY '25, exports should be at least 15% of our revenue. And in FY '26, as we begin to see businesses that have been awarded and are under development come to production fruition, we will see that percentage go well beyond 20 %.

items.statement: Domestic business targeting at least 20% growth in FY26 on development accomplishments of FY25
items.quote: I am quite optimistic that we will be able to deliver in FY '26 on the foundation of the development accomplishments of this financial year, at least a 20% growth.

items.statement: Business expected to pick up and stabilize from H2 FY25 (October) driven by exports, EV new platforms, and transfer case recovery
items.quote: We foresee that this, before we come out of these headwinds, you know, there will be a little bit of continuation through Q2, but we are expecting the business to pick up and stabilize from H2, so that's from October.

items.statement: Pursuing dedicated hybrid transmission for strong hybrids; expect strong hybrids in India beyond Toyota/Maruti from 2027, aim to be supplier from 2027
items.quote: Our best forecast on this technology is that we will see strong hybrids in India in 2027 beyond just Toyota and Maruti, who are currently the exclusive providers of this feature in India's automotive industry. And we are looking forward to Divgi-TTS being one of the suppliers from 2027 onwards.

items.statement: Maharashtra mega project approval for Shirwal EV facility grants electricity duty exemption for 7 years, 100% stamp duty exemption, SGST benefits up to capital investment
items.quote: we have received formal approval from the letter from the government of Maharashtra for the mega project under the electric vehicle policy. This will offer various incentives like electricity duty exempt ion for about seven years, 100 % exemption from payment of stamp duties, and benefits under the SGST, the state part of the GST, to the extent of our capital investment at our brand -new Shi rwal

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA INR13.9 cr (23.4% margin) vs INR17.8 cr YoY, down 22% due to mix change and Shirwal plant costs
items.quote: EBITDA for Q1 FY '25 stood at INR13.9 crores as against INR17.8 crores in Q1 FY '24, a year-on-year degrowth of 22%. Due to the change in product mix along with increased cost of Shirwal plant impacted the operating profitability of the company.

items.statement: Export orders under execution annualized at ~INR80 cr; China business resuming ~20k units/month in H2 FY25 worth INR4-6 cr over 6 months; China+Thailand potential >INR50 cr
items.quote: If I take the current pricing we have and the RFQ volumes, the annualized value of the current orders under execution is about INR80 crores.

items.statement: EV demand slower than expected due to consumer range/charging concerns; technology cycles short requiring supply chain agility
items.quote: Those of you who watch the space are aware that the numbers continue to disappoint in the battery electric vehicle, and perhaps the industry as a whole has underestimated the impact of how the consumer community is perceiving range and availability of charging infrastructure.

items.statement: Higher-end 125kW EV transmission for Tata Nexon/Curvv developed with encouraging NVH results; target supply from FY26
items.quote: We have successfully developed that product. It has -- the NVH results for that are extremely encouraging, I would say quite spectacular. And that product is under development right now.

items.statement: Mahindra 5-door Thar Roxx launch August 15; exclusive 4WD transfer case supplier; expect surge toward high-end variants at launch
items.quote: is going to be launching the five-door Thar Roxx, which is a significant upgrade from the three-door Thar. This is the five-door model, and we are the exclusive four-wheel drive transfer case supplier on this, what we think is quite a spectacular model

items.statement: MG Motors transfer case volumes down due to low-cost variant without 4WD; inventories being liquidated; EV side more competitive but 4WD exclusivity remains
items.quote: Two of our transfer case contracts ran into serious headwinds, one at MG Motors, and the second one was on the defense side for various reasons. They have not revived in the first half, so we see some of that beginning to happen actually starting this month and next month.

items.statement: Automatic transmission strategy shifting to dedicated hybrid transmission to meet CAFE III norms from April 2027; prototypes needed by mid-2026
items.quote: So we therefore believe that a more prudent product development strategy is to deliver a hybrid automatic or an automatic hybrid, whichever way you put it that gives the OEM not only the convenience of an automatic but is a double whammy and delivers a considerable improvement in fuel efficiency.

items.statement: Component business grew 57% YoY in Q1 FY25; strong domestic order book for manual transmission components and systems
items.quote: The component business has seen uptake in this quarter, grown by 57% year -on-year basis. It will continue to grow further on the back of strong domestic order book and top -notch technology for manual transmission components and systems.

items.statement: EV transmission business grew 10x YoY in Q1 FY25 but flat QoQ; expected pickup on new launches and FAME III subsidy restoration
items.quote: Our EV transmission business did exceptionally well and has grown by 10x on year -on-year basis. Although it was expected to be more than this, but due to the industry-wide slowdown in EV, it remains flat on quarter -on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Toyota Supplier of the Year Award won for second time in three years in powertrain systems
items.quote: I'm very pleased to share with you that this quarter that is under review, we won for the second time in the last three years the Toyota Supplier of the Year Award.

items.statement: Commissioned 22 additional beds in Pune on 1st July 2024; Indore expansion of 75 beds commenced, expected ready by end of FY25 and operational in early Q1 FY26; Dombivli construction progressing as per plan; second Pune hospital regulatory
items.quote: We have commissioned an additional 22 beds in Pune on 1st July'24. The construction activity for our expansion in Indore has also commenced. We will be adding about 75 beds there. They are expected to be ready by the end of this financial year and commence operations in early Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Indore 75-bed expansion capex estimated at INR 20-25 lakhs per bed
items.quote: So, forIndore, we'll probably incur INR 20, 25 lakhs sort of capex for the new beds being constructed

items.quote: So, we have incurred about INR 95 crores on Dombivli so far.

items.quote: In the current quarter or two we have probably spent about INR 10 lakhs, INR 15 lakhs per bed for the finishing of these beds.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin around 25% give or take as hospitals mature over next three years
items.quote: Yes. So around 25% give or take something is a respectable margin according to us and that can be expected.

items.statement: Q1 traditionally weaker quarter due to seasonality (~10% impact) from vacations and elective procedure deferrals; Q3 also weaker due to weddings and festivals
items.quote: So, over the past calls and whenever we have spoken, it has been discussed that the seasonality as far as our business goes is to the tune of maybe around 10% or so, with Q1 and Q3 being relatively weaker quarters.

items.statement: Pune occupancy grew from 53% to 62% YoY with ~10% headroom; Indore occupancy grew from 46-47% to 57% YoY with headroom plus 75 new beds coming
items.quote: still being at 53% of occupancy last year in Q1 has grown to 62% in this quarter. So it still has about a 10% headroom for growth in terms of occupancy. So Pune should contribute to growth over the next year and a half. Indore similarly from last year around 46%, 47% has grown to 57% in this quarter in terms of occupancy

items.statement: Indore case mix to drive ARPOB growth for another 1-2 years as transplant and tertiary programs mature; Thane and Pune ARPOB growth mainly inflation-linked thereafter
items.quote: So, currently, Indore is in that second phase. The first phase of introduction of new specialties is pretty much over. The second phase of, getting matured into doing more tertiary and quaternary work is underway. So, maybe for another year or two, Indore will see this case mix driver.

items.statement: No self-payer price hike planned for FY25; may consider at end of year or beginning of next year
items.quote: So, I do not think there is a plan of self-payer price hike currently in this year. We may do it at the end of the year or beginning of next year as far as the self-payers are concerned.

items.statement: Desire to add one more hospital in FY25 in Western India (Maharashtra/Gujarat); negotiations underway but land acquisition timelines uncertain; optimistic to close in FY25
items.quote: We have a desire to add one more hospital in this financial year. We have a couple of negotiations underway, but Greenfield projects mean that you have to first buy land and in India that comes with its own set of timelines. So today I can't give you a definitive answer about where it is and when it will come up. But we are quite optimistic that in this year, we should be able to do one more.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 22.6%, PAT margin 15.5%; average occupancy 63.9% vs 57.2% YoY; ARPOB INR 59,700; ALOS 3.76 days

items.statement: Net cash at end of Q1 FY25 between INR 250-300 crores
items.quote: So, net cash at the end of this quarter should be something between INR250 crores to INR300 crores.

items.statement: NABH Digital Gold accreditation not for pricing negotiations but for quality improvement and digital framework commitment
items.quote: No. So, this is not done with a pricing angle in mind. It is more of continual quality improvement. So, we have always been NABH accredited for the healthcare services.

items.statement: Doctor attrition very low single digits; strong team across units; cultural engagement practices for retention
items.quote: And we have a very, very low attrition rate in doctors, maybe very low single digits. So, I don't know if that helps you.

items.quote: So, no, we haven't started engaging with doctors yet. It is too early for that. We'll probably start one quarter before we are ready to operationalize. So, that should be a good enough of a time to start team building.

items.statement: Annual pre-sales guidance of INR10,000 crores for FY25 with 35%+ sales growth target
items.quote: we feel much more confident achieving the INR10,000 crores annual guidance which we have given. It is significant because if you look at the last 4-year trend, we have grown at about 60%-odd plus sales CAGR. Even in this year, this target was quite stiff. We are planning to achieve about 35% plus sales growth for this year.

items.statement: Annual launch guidance of INR16,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: This year, what we are very confident is to create the supply of INR16,000 crores of fresh inventory.

items.statement: Revenue recognition target of INR3,800 crores for FY25 from 5.5-6 million sq ft completions
items.quote: We stand by our targeted number of about INR3800-odd crores of completion during this particular financial year, wherein, we'll be completing projects anywhere between five and a half to six odd million square foot.

items.statement: Embedded EBITDA margin of ~35% on current FY25 pre-sales of INR10,000 crores
items.quote: we stand comfortable with this guidance of about, 35%-odd EBITDA, embedded EBITDA being earned on these sales, which will, of course, get recognized as per accounting policy in years to come.

items.quote: And the EBITDA margin on this should come anywhere between 20% to 25%-odd. items.quote: On an yearly basis, we do anticipate this per square foot realization to settle anywhere between INR13,000, INR14,000 a foot. But it is going to be upwards of INR13,000 is what we anticipate

items.statement: Market remains supply-constrained; demand is significant if right product at right location and price is offered
items.quote: Honestly, the experience of the last decade is that the market is hugely supply constrained. And like Pradeepji was saying that if you are offering the right product at the right location at the right price, if you can manage to create that balance within the broader sort of industry contours, the demand is significant.

items.statement: Upcoming Sohna launch: low-rise floors (primary), convenience retail (build-to-sell), and industrial/business-use plots
items.quote: The most important one is the, low-rise floors, which we've very successfully done over the last three, four years. In addition to that, there'll be a retail component, which will be typical convenience retail and we'll do a build to sell over there. Also, we have certa

items.statement: Land acquisition on replenishment basis only; INR290 crores spent in Q1 for 2.6M sq ft in Sector 37D; no large BD expenditure needed
items.quote: Since the company has good levels of yet to be launched projects, which is almost like 30-odd million square foot of land inventory still exists with us, we only intend to do land acquisition going forward on a replenishment basis. And we do not need to do any large expenditure or significant expenditure on the business development side.

items.statement: Government G+4 approval for low-rise floors in Sohna is clear; legal challenges/PILs may cause temporary confusion but strategy remains intact
items.quote: See, we don't think government's backtracking on that G plus four, approval strategy. Of course, I think whenever there are these changes taking place, there could be certain sort of, PILs getting filed or some sort of, this legal environment, few things, confusions happen. But we feel governments, taken its time and come up with, very clear notification around it.

items.statement: Net debt reduced 16% to INR9.8B in Q1 FY25; will continue declining quarterly as operating surplus funds land replenishment and debt service
items.quote: created a surplus of about INR530-odd crores. About 55% of that surplus went towards new land acquisition. About INR290-odd crores went in an acquisition which we did in Sector 37D. That's why we saw that the net debt came down from about INR1150

items.statement: Operating cash flow collection target >INR6,000 crores for FY25; Q1 surplus INR530 crores vs full FY24 surplus INR911 crores
items.quote: For this year, we anticipate to collect in excess of INR6,000 crores through operating cash flows. We had anticipated a surplus of about 45% of that collection at the start of the year. items.statement: 51M sq ft total portfolio: 16M sq ft advanced completion (INR12,000 crores revenue potential), 5M sq ft recently launched, ~30M sq ft yet to launch
items.quote: Overall, about 51-odd million square foot of portfolio is there. 16 million at very advanced stages of completion. 5-odd million which we've recently launched and is being developed and starting around that. And about close to 30 million square foot which is yet to be launched.

items.statement: Premium project general contractors will be best-in-class Grade A, not makeshift; mid-income/affordable projects continue with in-house team
items.quote: We do intend to bring in good quality grade-A general contractors. These are not makeshift guys. These would be the best-in-class sort of general contractors, with whom one can work in the country right now. So, these are good quality contractors being onboarded.

items.statement: Informal IFM revenue growth guidance of 13-14% for FY25
items.quote: So, this year we will guide you about 14% growth, between 13% and 14% growth for this year in the IFM.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth target of 15-16% for FY25
items.quote: Overall, I think what we have actually earlier also commented was we are looking at a 15%-16% console all businesses put together.

items.statement: BSS revenue mix target of 40-42% in next 1-2 years
items.quote: So, this 36% revenue split could actually go up to about 40%-42% in the next year, year and a half, 2 years.

items.statement: IFM standalone EBITDA margin outlook of 4.5-5% near term
items.quote: So, going forward, we believe that this margin of around 4%-4.5% easily should be there. And in fact we believe that overall it can be better.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improvement of 0.2-0.3% per year
items.quote: Console margins will grow between 0.2% and 0.3%.

items.statement: BSS EBITDA margin improvement of 0.2-0.3% year-on-year on cost arbitrage basis
items.quote: We will grow at about 0.2%-0.3% year-on-year as far as the margin is concerned.

items.statement: Airport ground handling requires equipment investment per new airport with 2.5-3 year gestation
items.quote: Every new airport that we enter, we have to invest in equipment like a ground power unit, there is a ground, there is an air handling unit.

items.statement: Strong government push for employment and GCC buildup supporting BSS growth
items.quote: With strong government push for boosting employment and large buildup of global capability centers, we are confident in sustaining a strong growth trajectory going forward.

items.statement: IFM segment mix: soft services ~40%, engineering ~25%, production support ~15-20%, catering ~10%, staffing ~10%
items.quote: Engineering services and soft services would be about 30% each. Soft would be about 40. Engineering would be about 25 say, so that would be about 65 and production support services will also be about 15 or 20.

items.statement: EBGC business under stress due to weak IT hiring, diversifying into BFSI and retail
items.quote: The EBGC business has been under stress for the past few quarters. That is basically because as we had already commented earlier the EBGC business is very closely linked to hiring and IT hiring in particular.

items.statement: Airport ground handling turned EBITDA and PAT positive in Q1 FY25 across 22 airports
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that our Q1 FY25 Airport Ground Landing business has turnaround EBITDA positive and PAT positive, which is in line with our previous commentary.

items.statement: Avon Logistics at Rs 100 crore revenue run rate shortly
items.quote: Avon is currently on a revenue run rate of get to on Rs. 100 crore very shortly.

items.statement: ESOP cost Rs 1.1 crore in Q1 FY25, Rs 5 crore expected for full year
items.quote: The ESOP cost for this particular period is Rs. 11 million for this quarter, the full year we are expecting it to be around Rs. 5 crores.

items.statement: Tax rate expected at 15-16% for FY25, not dependent on 80JJAA
items.quote: So, our tax rate roughly is about 15% and we look at about 15%-16%. And the thing to note over there is that we are not dependent on 80JJAA.

items.statement: Korea market not material in near term but could be significant in 2-3 years
items.quote: It will not be a material number in the near future, but Korea is a large market and in the future 2-3 years down the line, it could be a significant revenue and EBITDA generator.

items.statement: Aspires to achieve mid-teens revenue growth in FY25 backed by new store openings and subject to recovery in overall industry demand for mid-premium to premium brands
items.quote: Looking ahead, for FY '25, the company aspires to achieve mid-teens revenue growth backed by new store openings in new and existing geographies and subject to recovery in overall industry demand for mid- premium to premium brands.

items.statement: Targets to improve profitability through implementation of various cost efficiency measures in FY25
items.quote: The company is also targeting to improve profitability through implementation of various cost efficiency measures.

items.statement: Plans to open 25 to 30 new stores in FY25, with EBOs central to growth strategy
items.quote: We are optimistic about our continued store expansion efforts and aim to open between 25 to 30 new stores this year during FY '25.

items.statement: Expects to maintain EBITDA margin between 28% to 30%
items.quote: EBITDA margin also as we have said in the earlier calls we expect to maintain between 28 % to 30%.

items.statement: Gross margins will remain around 58% level
items.quote: I think last year we did a little north of 56 -odd crores as a gross margin -- 57-odd crores and this year we've done -- 58-odd percentage I'm sorry not crores . So gross margins will remain there and thereabouts .

items.statement: Plans to spend approximately 5% of revenues on branding and advertising for the full year
items.quote: For the full year, we plan to spend approximately 5% of revenues on branding and a dvertising.

items.statement: Market for premium and mid-premium branded apparel continued to be subdued due to inflationary environment and nationwide heat wave
items.quote: The market for premium and mid -premium branded apparel conti nued to be subdued due to the consumer behaviour influenced by an inflationary environment and a nationwide heat wave we experienced this summer.

items.statement: Hoping festival season and marriage season pick up well after elections and stable prices
items.quote: we are hoping that the festiva l season and the marriage season should pick up well and we should have a good season.

items.statement: Product mix shift toward premiumization may take up prices, not pure price escalation
items.quote: Maybe 2%-odd. It does not necessarily reflect price escalation it also reflects the product mix the ratio of what else and as we are going toward premiumization there might be some premium products that get added etcetera and that may take up prices.

items.statement: Market conditions remain volatile and difficult to predict; not putting gun to head to grow at any pace but focusing on profitability and same-store sales growth
items.quote: Given that it's very difficult to look into the crysta l ball today and gaze there and give an exact idea of what will happen , but we are very positive and hopeful and hoping now that the elections also are behind us and prices have been stable now for all the last few seasons so we are hoping that the festiva l season and the marriage season should pick up well and we should have a good season.

items.statement: Working capital days decreased by 5 days to 161 days as of 30 June 2024; aims to reduce by another 5-7 days by year-end
items.quote: Business we are in, in retail we need -- I mean that does not give an absolute true reflection of how the brand is doing. But give or take five, seven days here or there

items.statement: Intends to double business in next four to five years, calibrated through profitability lens
items.quote: Why not certainly we intend to you know double in four to five years is what we had mentioned earlier also however all of that will be done depending on the market conditions and we have always grown the through the profitability lens and that is something we will continue to do we will calibrate the growth of the through the profitability lens.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth for Q1 FY25 stood at 3% year-on-year
items.quote: Despite a difficult market, our same-store sales growth for the quarter stood at 3%.

items.statement: Added five new stores in Q1 FY25, increasing total store count to 430
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, we added fi ve new stores to our portfolio, increasing our total strength of stores to 430.

items.statement: Provision for returns increased to 25% from 22% last year due to shift to SOR basis from outright
items.quote: last year in Q1 the provision for returns was 22% and this year the provision for returns has been consistent 25 % as per the provision made in Q4 of last year.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue growth guidance of 25% to 30% alongside anticipated margin improvement
items.quote: Finally, we are pleased to reaffirm our guidance of 25%, 30% revenue growth for FY '25 alongside an anticipated improvement in our margin profiles.

items.statement: Long-term sales growth guidance of 25% to 30% year-on-year for a longer period
items.quote: Our long -term guidance to the market for sales growth will be in the range of 25% to 30% on a year -on-year basis for a longer period of time.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance range of 33% to 36% depending on product and sector mix
items.quote: Our long -term guidance to the market for EBITDA margins will be in the range of 33% to 36%, depending upon product and sector mix.

items.statement: Order book stands at over Rs. 3,300 crores, up from Rs. 2,000 crores a few quarters earlier
items.quote: Our order book has skyrocketed from Rs. 2,000 crores a few quarters earlier to over Rs. 3,300 crores today, driven by strategic contracts and key customer acquisitions

items.statement: New facility 10x existing size on track to be ready by FY26 with high visibility on first phase utilization
items.quote: We are on track to complete the expansion phase and will be ready by and from FY '26. With orders in hand and pipeline of validations, we have high visibility on the utilization of the first phase.

items.statement: Aerospace and Defense contributed ~19% of Q1 FY25 revenue, in line with diversification plan
items.quote: During the quarter, Aerospace and Defense contributed around 19% of our total revenue, which is in line with our long -term diversification plan.

items.statement: GTRE/DRDO order for complete turbojet engine assembly marks entry into propulsion systems as single-source industry partner
items.quote: An order from GTRE/DRDO for manufacturing and assembly of a turbojet engine. Now, this is a very, very exciting opportunity and this is going to take Azad into a very different league.

items.statement: Seven-year contract with Rolls-Royce for Defense and military aircraft engines; two major contracts with Baker Hughes; contract with GE Vernova for high-complexity rotating airfoils
items.quote: A seven-year contract with Rolls-Royce for the Defense and military aircraft engines. Two major contracts from Baker Hughes. A contract from GE Vernova for supply of high -complex rotating airfoils for the Nuclear, industrial, and thermal power industries.

items.statement: Added subsidiary Azad VTC for special processes and coatings to reduce job work charges and external dependency
items.quote: Likewise, we have added a subsidiary Azad VTC, for special processes and coatings, which will help us reduce job work charge as well as the dependency.
