items.quote: On the account of that, we have acquired a company, VTC, where we started qualifying for those particular process es. And going forward, we see that this cost will normalize again.

items.statement: Employee expenses 20.5%-21.2% of sales; raw material and other expenses 45.1%-45.7% of sales, showing consistency
items.quote: Employee expenses as a percentage of sales were between 20.5% to 21.2%, which are quite consistent. The raw material and other expenses put together have been in the range of 45.1% to 45.7%, which again show a mark of consistency in our performance.

items.statement: First batch of fully integrated ATGG engines targeted for delivery in first half of FY26
items.quote: So, in terms of the timeline, we are looking at FY '26 for delivering the first set of engines, right? So, that is correct. So, we cannot share when exactly we will be doing it, but yes, it is towards the first half of FY '26 is what we are looking at

items.statement: Indigenized 2-3 raw material grades with Sunflag and Star Wire to reduce import content from 50-55% toward 40% target
items.quote: We have been able to successfully indigenize two or three raw material grades with two companies. One of them is Sunflag and the other one is Star Wire. So, you will see that gradually our import percentage of raw materials will come down.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 240 crores primary capital for FY27 infrastructure and capacity deployment; now planning CAPEX beyond FY27 given contract wins
items.quote: And for FY '27 we had raised a primary of Rs. 240 crores and this was to be deployed towards infrastructure and capacity. And now, we are planning how do we go beyond FY '27 ?

items.statement: Targeting INR 1,000 crore revenue for FY25 with 18% EBITDA margin; Q1 behind but confident to get close
items.quote: That's the objective, Prathik. Q1, we are a little behind. We are hopeful we can make it up. The whole idea is if you aim big, you will get close to the target. So it's an aggressive goal but as of now, at the end of Q1, we are confident that we'll get close to it, if not at it.

items.statement: Revenue gap of INR 150 crore to reach INR 1,000 crore target including Augmento; weighted pipeline INR 50 crore
items.quote: If I look at our pipeline today, Vikas and our order book, we have from a INR 1,000 crores, we have a gap of INR 150 crores. This is including Augmento.

items.statement: Unweighted pipeline INR 150 crore, weighted pipeline INR 50 crore to close revenue gap
items.quote: So the un-weighted pipeline would be INR 150 crores, but the weighted pipeline would be in the range of INR 50 crores.

items.statement: Digital engineering contributes 45% of revenue, QA/testing 15%, balance data and infrastructure
items.quote: So Amit, digital engineering, which is a product capability, that shows almost 45% of our revenues. The QA and the testing, that's about 15% and the balance comes between data and infrastructure.

items.statement: Augmento Labs acquired June 2024; expected INR 50 crore revenue in FY25 at 20%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: Approximately INR 50 crores.

items.statement: Augmento expected to deliver at least 20% EBITDA margin, above company average
items.quote: Yes, 20% at least. At least.

items.statement: High technology spend in Fintech, Hi-Tech, and Retail e-commerce verticals driving growth
items.quote: Technology spend today globally is moving I mean, is increasing in these business verticals, in these verticals. So the ability for us to grow becomes better because we have targeted high growth areas.

items.statement: Fintech startup clients pose payment risk due to funding-dependent spending patterns
items.quote: What we have to be careful about is, and this is a fine line that we have to ride is, since a lot of these are startups, we have to be careful that w e don't get stuck with them

items.statement: Utilization at 85%, expected to remain flat with 100-200 bps variation
items.quote: I think this is pretty much maxed out. Maybe 100-200 basis points in either direction is probably what you will see, but 85% is pretty much where we will remain.

items.statement: Hired 3 salespeople in US (2 in June) and 1 in UK (June) to drive US revenue mix toward 45-75%
items.quote: We have hired 3 new sales guys in the U.S. 1 is the guy who brought this Hi-tech company and this was 7 months ago, and 2 have joined in the month of June.

items.statement: Augmento integration painless; support functions integrating, delivery teams folded into Hi-Tech vertical
items.quote: So I would say, so far no surprises, quite a painless integration.

items.statement: No focus on HealthTech/MedTech; sector parked for now
items.quote: Correct. That didn't work out. And, I think this is a sector, which we are sort of parked, not going to focus on it excessively for now.

items.statement: Future acquisitions limited to small capability players due to capital constraints
items.quote: We're always talking to potential targets, hopeful something will come out. But, you know, we don't have that much money with us now to make a big play.

items.statement: Billing rate improvement dependent on rupee-dollar movement
items.quote: One big area they'll come from is our finance minister, if the rupee dollar benefits.

items.statement: DSO increased marginally to 65 days; no significant collection issues
items.quote: Marginal I think, Niraj is saying it's a marginal increase.

items.statement: Targeting breakeven in Jeevansathi this year with high growth and aggressive monetization
items.quote: So, in Jeevansathi we are targeting breakeven this year. So we would like to get as close to breakeven as possible.

items.statement: Targeting breakeven or profit in Shiksha this year while investing in platform and content
items.quote: In Shiksha, can we continue to be profitable? The domestic business grew very well in Q1. Study abroad is struggling a little bit because of what we're seeing are happening around the world. So even in Shiksha, we would want to at least, target breakeven or make make some profit this year.

items.statement: Willing to invest more in 99acres even if it means taking losses for longer to capture long-term opportunity
items.quote: We would want 99acres to grow faster going forward. We are doing whatever we can and if that requires us to invest a lot more in the business, and if that means taking a loss of some more time, that's fine with us.

items.statement: Continuing to invest in recruitment verticals including JobHai, AmbitionBox, iimjobs, hirist and Naukri Gulf
items.quote: Even in recruitment, we will continue, we continue to invest in our JobHai business. We continue to invest behind the AmbitionBox platform. We continue to invest behind iimjob and hirist. Even our Naukri Gulf business has been doing well, We continue to invest in the business.

items.statement: Gestation projects in recruitment verticals costing Rs. 20-25 crores per quarter
items.quote: In the range, you said, Rs. 20-25 crores a quarter, around that much.

items.statement: 99acres advertising spend higher than last year; manpower costs under control
items.quote: We are actually spending more than we spent last year. I don't know exactly how much. Right now, as we speak, we have a higher budget than we spent last year. On the other hand manpower costs, etc. are under control.

items.statement: IT hiring showing early recovery signs with July Jobspeak up 12% YoY and 11% MoM; some large IT clients renewed and upgraded
items.quote: The July 2024 Jobspeak report has also been very encouraging. The Jobspeak index grew by 12% Y-o-Y in July and M-o-M grew by 11%.

items.statement: Non-IT billing growth at 14% YoY driven by healthcare, infrastructure, transport, real estate, media & telecom
items.quote: Growth momentum in the Non-IT segment continued, with billings growing at 14% year on year. This was largely driven by sectors such as healthcare and life sciences, infrastructure, transport, real estate and media & telecom.

items.statement: Niche verticals iimjobs, NaukriGulf, Naukri Fast Forward grew billings 26%, 25%, 29% YoY respectively
items.quote: Our niche and adjacent business verticals, including iimjobs, NaukriGulf, and Naukri Fast Forward also maintained healthy billings growth with Y-o-Y increases of 26%, 25%, and 29%, respectively.

items.statement: JobHai expanding to ~60 cities with product-market fit; freemium model targeting 1M SME customers in 5-7 years; monetization started few months ago
items.quote: We've worked very hard on the product for the last three years. And we seem to have got product market fit. There's a lot of traction. We're getting a lot of job seekers, we're getting a lot of jobs. We're getting a lot of recruiters advertising on the platform. And it's a freemium model.

items.statement: 99acres growth hit in June possibly due to election uncertainty; state government changes delaying project approvals
items.quote: Now, again, anecdotally, what I can tell you, the business took a hit in June. Maybe again, it had to do with some uncertainty around the elections. And often when state governments change and all these things happen in real estate some of the projects get delayed. Approvals take longer as people adjust to the new environment.

items.statement: No plan to exit Zomato or Policybazaar holdings; taking long-term view on value creation
items.quote: As of now, there is no plan to exit.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 20% for FY25 maintained but management is cautiously optimistic
items.quote: I would still do not want to jump into any change in numbers, but we are quite cautious and we keep ourselves cautiously optimistic on this year's performance.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs. 16.9 billion as of June 2024 with 63% international and 37% domestic
items.quote: In terms of order book, it stood at Rs. 16.9 billion as of June '24. Out of which, 63% of orders are from international business and the rest 37% are domestic orders.

items.statement: Capex of approximately Rs. 4,500 million planned for FY25 towards brownfield expansion
items.quote: We are looking at a CAPEX of approximately Rs. Rs. 4,500 million during FY '25. This is towards brownfield expansion projects for which we are looking at our existing facilities.

items.statement: Special process facility for aerospace approved with Rs. 30 crore investment, operational by mid-FY26
items.quote: So, this would mean that in over 12 to 15 months, this facility will come up adjacent to our existing machining facility, and this would have an overall investment of about Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded ~200 bps YoY to 41.8% in Q1 FY25 due to favorable product mix
items.quote: During this quarter, the gross margin grew from 39.9% in Q1 of FY '24 to 41.8% in the Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Targeting 20% EBITDA margin through mix improvement, Sweden turnaround, 2-wheeler premiumization and operating leverage
items.quote: These factors aided with the operating leverage on better capacity utilization on various product lines will actually help us to achieve or get closer to the 20% goal of operating margin.

items.statement: Emerging segments (non-auto, tech-agnostic, xEV) grew 34% YoY; tech-agnostic up 68% to Rs. 712M, xEV up 29% to Rs. 421M
items.quote: Together, these segments have expanded by 34% on a year-on-year basis during this quarter. We have registered a top line of Rs. 712 million in auto tech-agnostic products with a year-on-year growth of 68%. Our xEV business grew by 29% on a year-on-year basis to Rs. 421 million

items.statement: Aerospace revenue growth target 30-35% for FY25 (base Rs. 110 crore); exports from India grew ~28% YoY in Q1
items.quote: For this year, for Aerospace, we are looking at between 30% to 35% growth as it stands today.

items.statement: Swedish subsidiary EBITDA margin to reach 12-13% from next financial year with two new engine program wins
items.quote: we have worked, and we have acquired 2 key business wins for our Swedish subsidiary, which will enable us to go back to 12% to 13% EBITDA starting from next financial year.

items.statement: Non-auto, tech-agnostic and xEV segments targeting 40-50% CAGR over next 2-3 years
items.quote: we are looking at a CAGR growth in this by about 40% to 50%.

items.statement: International business outlook slightly worrisome for H2 FY25 due to global slowdown concerns
items.quote: While I would be cautious to say that international business is looking in the second half of this year, especially the international business looks to be slightly worrisome.

items.statement: MOU signed with Karnataka government for 55 acres land for future greenfield expansion
items.quote: we have recently signed an MOU with the government of Karnataka to acquire 55 acres of land. Over the years, we will be looking at greenfield expansion in the area of our current expertise in this piece of land.

items.statement: Aluminum forging production reaching ~1.5 million parts this year; margins in line with domestic products but still on learning curve
items.quote: This year, we will be doing almost close to 1.5 million aluminum parts, which is quite a good progress given the fact that this has been only about 2.5, 3 years of this thing.

items.statement: MMRFIC radar business EBITDA margins expected upwards of 50% upon full integration and field testing
items.quote: generally speaking, the average, the EBITDA numbers on this business would be upwards of 50%.

items.statement: Off-road segment growth to moderate to ~14-15% in FY25 after 66-67% growth in FY24
items.quote: Yes, it may be in that range.

items.statement: Full year FY25 expected to be flattish with Q2 sequentially flat, H2 higher than H1, and Q4 highest run rate; full year could be flat to minus 2-3%
items.quote: I would think the full year outlook would be more flattish for this year. I expect maybe quarter 2 to be sequentially flat. And the half 2 probably -- the second half would be higher than half 1. And with quarter 4, I expect to have the highest run rate.

items.statement: Full year FY25 EBITDA margin target of 18%, long-term target remains 20%
items.quote: But 18% is what I'm looking at for this full year. But my longer-term stand on the 20% margin remains because right now, it's basically the operating leverage causes an issue is when the volumes are down.

items.statement: Capex outlook for FY25 between INR35 crores to INR40 crores, Q1 was about INR8 crores
items.quote: I think the capex outlook is going to be between INR35 crores to INR40 crores. This quarter, was about INR8 crores or so.

items.statement: Early signals of slowdown in U.S. construction equipment end market; Europe also witnessing softness in construction equipment end market
items.quote: There are some early signals of slowdown in U.S. construction equipment end market. Europe, as alluded earlier as well, is also witnessing softness in construction equipment end market.

items.statement: India domestic tractor market steady after previous fiscal softness; midterm expectations linked to monsoon 2024 and festive season demand
items.quote: India domestic tractor market is looking steady after the softness in previous fiscal year. Midterm expectations were now more linked to the monsoon 2024 performance and the festive season demand.

items.statement: New awards pipeline remains encouraging with added traction in all product verticals including PMP, large agricultural equipment assembly, agriculture machinery in India, high-horsepower 3PL, and geographical expansion in below 70-horsepowe
items.quote: New awards pipeline remains encouraging with added traction in all product verticals including PMP, large agricultural equipment assembly, agriculture machinery in India, high-horsepower 3PL as well as further geographical expansion in below 70-horsepower tractors.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 reported EBITDA margin at 17.6%; operating cash flow generation approximately INR50 crores
items.quote: Reported EBITDA for Q1 was INR46 crores, which is a quarter-on-quarter change of minus 10.6%, and year-on-year change of minus 23.6%, while reported EBITDA margin was at 17.6% for the quarter. Operating cash flow generation for the quarter was approximately INR50 crores.

items.statement: Inflationary pressure on operating costs remain in medium term to be partially mitigated through operating efficiencies
items.quote: Inflationary pressure on operating costs remain in the medium term to be partially mitigated through operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Macro concerns over global economic slowdown, geopolitical uncertainties and impact of worldwide high interest rates continue to remain a key monitorable
items.quote: Macro concerns over global economic slowdown, geopolitical uncertainties and impact of worldwide high interest rates continues to remain a key monitorable.

items.statement: Large ag segment (approx 20% of revenue) seeing 20-25% reduction due to end market decline of 10-12% plus inventory correction; construction equipment (37% of revenue) flat to low single digit down; small ag (30% of revenue) slightly better
items.quote: large ag that used to form about 18%, 20% of our business, that even though the market – end market is down by about 10% to 12%, we are seeing almost a 20%, 25% reduction. So the impact -- even though it's a small one, the impact over there is fairly large. In the small ag, it forms almost about 30% of our business, but it's – the inventory corrections are out, but the market is still slow. So we

items.statement: Long-term revenue growth expectation of 15-16% vs market growth of 5-6%, driven by new product platforms and market share gains
items.quote: No. I think our expectation on these two -- markets are going to be 5% to 6% growth go forward. We are looking at growth by longer term. This thing is to stay at about a 15% to 16% growth. So we expect to beat it by a significant larger number. But it won't be just by increased market share, it's by adding more products as well.

items.statement: Capacity utilization overall in range of 55% to 60% currently; not product-specific as factories produce both 3PL and PMP with common processes
items.quote: So to your first question, the capacity utilization overall is in the range of 55% to 60%, currently. It is not product-specific. Pretty much all our factories, except the U.S. one, which produces only PMP. All our India factories produce both 3PL and PMP.

items.statement: Interest rate cuts expected to drive recovery in small ag and small construction equipment; large ag recovery may take about a year due to low commodity prices and stretched farm income
items.quote: I don't see the serious farmer buying large equipment at least for about a year because this cycle will play through for the moment. But I do expect interest rates to kind of start showing up something on the small ag and the small construction equipment. And aftermarket has already come out in any case.

items.statement: Crude steel production target of 20.87 million tons and sales volume target of 19.26 million tons for FY25
items.value: 20.87 million tons crude steel; 19.26 million tons sales
items.quote: Volume target for this year, we are planning a crude steel production of around 20.87 million tons and sales volume of around about 19.26 million tons.

items.statement: FY25 capex projected at INR6,300 crores; similar range of INR7,000 crores for FY26; real jump from FY27 onwards
items.quote: For FY 2024-25, we have projected around about INR6,000 crores. It's actually INR6,300 crores, which we have given to the ministry. And the expenditure in the coming year also will be in the similar range around about INR7,000 crores or something. The real jump in the capex will come from, you can say, 2026-27 onwards.

items.statement: Debottlenecking to add 3 million tons capacity over 3-4 years with INR10,000-11,000 crores investment
items.quote: So we are planning to bring it up by 3 million tons in the next 3 to 4 years by putting in something like INR10,000 crores to INR11,000 crores of impact.

items.statement: IISCO 4 million ton greenfield expansion approved at Stage 1 with INR37,000 crores investment; tendering starting shortly
items.quote: One particular plant, IISCO plant, already the Board has accorded stage 1 approval for that. And it is that -- it's a 4 million ton plant, and the total investment will be around INR37,000 crores.

items.statement: Bokaro expansion to 7 million tons (+2.4 mt) and Durgapur to 3 million tons (+0.9 mt) under evaluation; consultant costs being reworked
items.quote: And the other 2 plants which are there, they are basically brownfield expansion in which Bokaro is going to be ramped up to 7 million tons. And Durgapur, we'll be going up by around about, you can say 1 million -- around 1 million tons.

items.statement: Hopeful of realization and margin improvement in coming quarters; cost reduction efforts ongoing via coal diversification and techno-economic parameters
items.quote: Going forward, the boost from the various measures being taken by the government on infrastructure spending orders well for the steel demand in the country with the overall outlook positive for the sustaine d growth in domestic consumption. We are hopeful of the realization and consequently the margin will improve for the company in the quarters to come

items.statement: Q1 blended NSR INR53,700/t; July decline INR500-600/t; August further decline INR1,000-1,500/t; Q2 NSR expected lower than Q1
items.quote: The NSR for Q1, it's in the range of INR53,700. Going forward, like we are -- it has declined further in the month of J uly by, you can say, around about INR500 to INR600. And there is a further reduction in the month of August also

items.statement: Long product NSR INR54,000/t, flat product NSR INR53,500/t in Q1; July drop INR700-800/t long, INR1,500/t flat; August drop ~INR1,000-1,500/t both
items.quote: In the long segment, the NSR was in the range of, you can say, around about INR54,000 crores. And in the flat, it was INR53,500 crores. Then the average was coming to around about INR53,700 crores.

items.statement: Imported coking coal landed cost INR24,500/t, indigenous INR13,500/t, blended ~INR23,000/t in Q1; expected similar in Q2 due to inventory consumption
items.quote: The imported coking coal was in the range of around about INR24,500 per ton landed at our steel plant and the indigenous was around INR13,500 per ton. So the average is working out to around about INR23,000 per ton.

items.statement: Q3 coking coal cost reduction expected if spot rates sustain; depends on August-September finalized rates
items.quote: Yes, Q3, there will be a reduction of around about you can say -- But then again, it depends on the supply or the rates which are being finalized in this August, September quarter -- in this August, September month.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand outlook positive driven by infrastructure investment; India projected >8% growth; long segment to benefit from infra spend, flats challenged by imports
items.quote: Going forward, the boost from the various measures being taken by the government on infrastructure spending orders well for the steel demand in the country with the overall outlook positive for the sustaine d growth in domestic consumption

items.statement: Semis share in production 15%, sales 7%; will remain at similar levels for ~3-3.5 years until new mills commission; then virtually zero
items.quote: The semis will remain at almost at the same levels. It will not come down drastically. The only thing is that our basic target is to maximize conversion through our conversion agents and wet leasing agents. So this we'll be doing it. But I don't see much of a reduction in the percentage of semis.

items.statement: Supreme Court judgment on state levies: Jharkhand INR100/t on iron ore/coal (~INR100-200 cr impact); Odisha clarity awaited; no major contingent liability currently
items.quote: and Madhya Pradesh. And i n case of Jharkhand, we have recently announced that they'll be imposing INR100 per ton -- per ton for iron ore and coal. Steel Authority of This is going to have a prospective effect of around INR150 crores to INR100 crores -- you can say, under INR200 crores

items.statement: Coke rate improved to 428 kg/thm in Q1 vs 440 kg FY24 average; target further 6-8 kg reduction in balance year; CDI rate to increase 10-12 kg
items.quote: This year we have targeted 440, but we may not be ab le to achieve that. We may not be here. But I'm sure that another you can say 6 to 8 kg of coal will be during the balance period

items.statement: Pellet plant at Gua mines 4 million tons in 3.5-4 years; COM basis pellet plant in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: We have our own plans of setting up a plant at Gua Ore Mines, a pellet plant at Gua Ore Mines of 4 million ton. So this should take around of 3.5 to 4 years from now.

items.statement: IISCO expansion IRR ~18% based on 3-year average steel prices and stamp charge battery cost savings; to be reworked before Stage 2
items.quote: It's IISCO plant and we have made an analysis. It's quite favorable. I think it's 18% -- 18% is IRR.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers revenue target ~Rs 200 crore in FY25 with ~40% EBIT margin and 20-25% annual growth
items.quote: Going by the 1st Quarter, we are very confident that we shall achieve ballpark Rs. 200 crore turnovers with EBITDA margins or EBIT margins in the region of about 40%. And we expect a 20%-25% growth rate year-on-year on this business.

items.statement: Film business value-added/specialty share target 40% by FY26 from 30% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Share of value-added and specialty products stood at 30% during the quarter and we are hoping to scale it up to 40% by FY26.

items.statement: Ester Filmtech revenue target Rs 450-500 crore at optimal utilization by FY26
items.quote: We expect the entity to generate revenues of a bout Rs. 450 to 500 crore upon achieving optimal utilization at reasonable prices /margins by next fiscal

items.statement: Loop JV capex $165 million funded 60-40 debt-equity; equity split 50-50 between Ester and Loop; minimal FY25 spend as groundbreaking in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, very simple, we have a CAPEX of about $165 million which is going to be funded at 60 - 40, outside could be 70-30. If we take 60-40, $66 million will be the equity which will be shared 50-50 between Ester and Loop and the balance about $100 million will be raised as debt in the joint venture company.

items.statement: Loop JV commercial production target first half of calendar 2027
items.quote: Our target timeline is to commence commercial production in the first half of calendar 2027.

items.statement: Domestic polyester film demand ~65,000 tons/month; exports ~20,000 tons/month; total demand ~85,000 tons vs effective capacity ~100,000 tons; gap narrowed to ~15,000 tons
items.quote: Domestic demand is estimated at about 65,000 tons per month a nd export is taking away about 20,000 tons. So, total demand for Film, domestic plus exports is about 85,000 tons against the effective operational capacity of 100,000 tons. The demand supply gap has now narrowed to about 15,000 tons

items.statement: Current BOPET spread Rs 37-38/kg vs Q1 FY25 average Rs 17-18/kg; June exit at Rs 26/kg; July at Rs 35-38/kg
items.quote: So, the spreads over PTA MEG would be in the region of about Rs. 37 to 38 per kilo as we speak now.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers Q1 FY25 EBIT margin 43% on Rs 45 crore revenue; 982 tons volume vs 526 tons YoY
items.quote: Q1 registered revenues of Rs. 45 crore with an impressive EBIT margin of 43% largely on the back of higher off -take of our marquee products, namely M B03 and Innovative PBT.

items.statement: Ester Industries value-added/specialty films 30% of volume (3,200 tons) and 42% of value in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Ester Industries, the total quantity of Films told was about 11,250 tons, out of which value-added and Specialty Film was close to 30%, 3200 tons. In terms of value quantity, it was 30%, but in terms of value, it was 42% of the sales made by the company.

items.statement: Value-added film spreads Rs 55-65 over base; export blended spreads Rs 65-75; commodity domestic spread Rs 17-18 in Q1
items.quote: As I have told you the differential will be around Rs. 55 to Rs. 65.

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization target 75-80% for FY25; Ester Filmtech volume 32,000-34,000 tons vs 25,600 tons FY24
items.quote: On a consolidated basis for year as a whole we are estimating our capacity utilization at 75% to 80% or a little better than that.

items.statement: Plastic Waste Management Rules effective April 1, 2025 mandate 10% recycled content in flexible packaging; expected to shift demand from BOPP to polyester
items.quote: Plastic waste management rules are scheduled to come into force from April 1, 2025. These rules will mandate utilization of 10% recycled content in flexible packaging laminate. This is expected to lead to increased demand and consequent better margins for Polyester Film with conversion taking place from other substrates like BOPP to Polyester.

items.statement: One BOPET line (3,500-3,700 tons) starting in next 2-3 months included in 110,000 tons capacity; another line in FY26; next after that in 2027
items.quote: is coming next year, how much would the capacity be approximately? Arvind Singhania: 3,500-3,700 tons. It is not going to make basic growth in demand. I don't think that is going to upset the apple cart

items.statement: Ester Filmtech Q1 FY25 positive EBITDA; revenue Rs 81 crore on 6,501 tons
items.quote: Better pricing environment resulted in positive EBITDA for the quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 overall company margin was about 13% and electrical cable segment margin slightly over 11%
items.quote: So, we closed the quarter with about 13% margin overall for the company and slightly over 11% for the electrical cable segment.

items.statement: Copper prices touched a high of $10,857 and low of $8,809 on LME in Q1 FY25, a difference of almost 20%
items.quote: Copper, for instance, touched a high of $10,857 on LME and also a low of $8,809 on the LME in the same quarter. So, that’s a difference o f almost 20

items.statement: Price cuts of about 10% were taken from June onwards in electrical wires due to copper price decline
items.quote: I think we took overall from then till now about 10%.

items.statement: Demand expected to pick up once copper prices stabilize around $8,800-$9,000 levels; festival season expected to boost auto demand
items.quote: I think demand will start to p ick up maybe once there is stability at the price level. If people see that the prices remain at 8,800, 9,000 levels, probably demand will pick up immediately afterwards

items.statement: Total CAPEX outflow for FY25 and FY26 around 500 crores, bulk spent in FY25; E-beam equipment installed awaiting AERB clearance, auto cable expansion at Roorkee by mid-Oct to mid-Nov, Goa compounding plant by May-Jun next year
items.quote: Overall expenditure until next year would still be around 500 crores. Bulk of it would be spent this year.

items.statement: EHV order book close to 300 crores; target revenue for FY25 is 240 crores
items.quote: We have a fairly decent order book there. Our current order book is close to 300 odd crores.

items.statement: FMEG business at 68 crores quarterly revenue, annualized ~272 crores, breakeven expected around 250 crores annual revenue
items.quote: 68 crores is what we have done in this quarter, times 4 is just over 250. And I think at this speed, we will be breaking even, barring any blips.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin range for consolidated entity (ex-dividends) is 13-13.5%
items.quote: But if you exclude that, 13%, 13.5% is something that you should work on.

items.statement: Aim to more than double revenues at attractive margins within this decade (next 4-5 years)

items.quote: Maybe couple of INR100 crores. We don't have a huge debt. We have told you before. We don't have and our intention is not to have any long term debt.

items.statement: Aiming to almost double AUM from INR 730 crores to around INR 1400 crores in FY25.
items.quote: We are again aiming to almost double our AUM in this financial year from INR 730 crores to around INR 1400 crores this year.

items.statement: Targeting 150 to 175 branches and expansion to 12 states by adding Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh with 25 branches in southern states.
items.quote: As we speak, we have 113 branches, and we are on track to achieve 150 to 175 branches. Currently, we have presence in 8 states and soon in this quarter, we will expand our presence to 12 states.

items.statement: Secured loans share increased from 8% to 27% of AUM; targeting over 40% by end of 2025.
items.quote: Last year, it was only 8% of our AUM, which as on June stands at 27%. We will continue to increase contribution from secured loans, and it will be over 40% by end of 2025.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost reduced to 12.05%; expect further 50 bps reduction in H2 with equity infusion and credit rating upgrade.
items.quote: Incremental borrowing costs reduced to 12.05%. If you see that, you know, in H2 of last year, it was 13%, while our average borrowing rate is around 13.7%, but incrementally the decline is sharp. And with increasing capital base by end of this month, we believe further in H2 we should be able to bring down cost by another 50 basis points.

items.statement: Credit cost at 2.36% in Q1 vs 1.88% in Q4; guided blended credit cost to remain 2-3% (unsecured 2-3%, secured up to 1.5%).
items.quote: Historically, the company credit cost was less than 3%, including pandemic. And that's what we still maintain as we always say that on unsecured, we believe credit cost to remain between 2-3% and in secured portfolio maybe up to 1%, 1.5%, which will mean on a blended level, we should be around 2% of credit costs and not crossing that asset class portfolio increases.

items.statement: Targeting ROE of around 12% for FY25, up from 10% in FY24.
items.quote: We feel that ROE should reach which was about 10% in last year, we should see an elevation maybe somewhere around 12% is our idea that we should see.

items.statement: FY25 AUM guidance INR 1,300-1,400 crores; branch target 160-175; disbursement target INR 1,100 crores.
items.quote: FY25, as we guided, we in terms of AUM, we believe that anywhere between INR 1,300 crore and INR 1,400 crore, we should reach in terms of AUM. In terms of branches, the target is to have 175 branches, with the minimum number to be at 160.

items.statement: Leverage to be maintained below 4x on balance sheet; net worth expected to exceed INR 500 crores by mid next year to support INR 2,500 crores AUM in FY26.
items.quote: Largely, if you see that we are sorted, I'm definitely not saying that we will not raise equity next year. But with INR 175 crores of existing equity, INR 270 crores of infusion over the next 18 months, maybe a PAT of, say, minimum within next 1 year of INR 60 crores. I mean, in terms of going to next year as well, say, middle of next year, we'll have a net worth of INR 500 crores, which is enough

items.statement: Q1 muted due to seasonality (30% of yearly disbursement in H1); expect pickup in H2 with branch expansion, monsoon improvement, and festival season.

items.statement: Maintaining spread of at least 15% over medium to long term; Q1 incremental spread improved 49 bps despite secured loan growth.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded by CRISIL from BBB- to BBB Stable; expect another upgrade within calendar year driven by AUM growth, secured lending, improving ROA, and equity capital.
items.quote: The other thing which happened in this quarter is improvement in our credit rating by CRISIL from BBB minus to BBB stable, which will now we expect that in another 5-6 months' time, maybe within this calendar year, we should see one more upgrade, especially driven by increasing AUM, increasing secure lending, improving ROA and most importantly equity capital.

items.quote: And the collection efficiency for the month of June is above 95%. It's about 95.5%.

items.quote: But for the whole year, we would still expect that 12% to 14% kind of growth on the whole year basis to come through?

items.statement: Sanctions in hand of over INR 3,000 crores available for drawdown
items.quote: Apart from that, we have more than INR 3,000 crores of sanctions i n hand, which we can draw

items.statement: Collection efficiency at 96% in July due to excessive rains; expect return to 98-99% by end of Q3
items.quote: So we feel that by the end of Q3, we should be back to around 98%, 99%. By the end of the year, we should be back to normal.

items.statement: Karj Mukti Andolan impact largely stopped; limited to 4 districts in Punjab with INR 31 crore exposure
items.quote: Yes, so that majority of that activity has stopped. It was almost linked with the election activity that was going on during that period in Q1. So now we don't have too much of activism. In Punjab, of course, there are certain districts, there are four districts which are affected. They remain affected, but there is no further deterioration of those portfolios.

items.statement: No exposure to Wayanad landslide affected area
items.quote: We are really concerned about the Wayanad development, but we as an entity do not have any exposure to Wayanad. We have been prudent in that policy. And considering Wayanad is a hilly area, we have not exposed ourselves there. So we don't have any branches or portfolio there.

items.statement: South portfolio now 51% of AUM after entering Andhra and Telangana
items.quote: With this entrance, south contributes around 51% of the portfolio for the company. And it's a more evolved market.

items.statement: Digital collections at 26% currently; targeting 30%+ by end of FY25
items.quote: We should be able to go this year around 30%-plus in terms of digital collection by the end of the financial year, definitely.

items.statement: Corporate agency license from IRDA obtained; expect 5-10% commission on INR 600-650 crore insurance premium in FY25
items.quote: Depending upon the agreement, I think definitely there's a scope of around 5% to 10% commission income that will come through this arrangement. We process around -- last year we processed around close to INR 500 crores of insurance premium. Considering our 25% growth, we should be processing somewhere around INR 600 crores or INR650 crores of premium this financial year.

items.statement: Co-lending agreement signed with State Bank of India for consistent credit line
items.quote: We have also entered during the quarter into a co-lending agreement with the largest bank in the country, State Bank of India. The aim is to empower the microfinance borrower, and this will also allow us to continue a free flow of disbursement to our customers.

items.statement: Full year revenue growth expected at 20% plus and EBITDA margin between 20% and 21%
items.quote: For the full year, we expect overall revenue growth of 20% plus. Even on margin front, we expect full year margins to be between 20% and 21% as we see operating leverage play out.

items.statement: Four new facilities operationalized in FY24; Kadu plant at 60% utilization, expected breakeven in Q3; Mehsana solids at 40%, injectables and biologics in filing stage; Oncology at 20% utilization
items.quote: on the new plants, if you look at it, three of them have started operations and we started supplying from them. So, if you look at Kad u, which was more focused on global oral solids, there we are now reaching about a 60% utilization. So, that should b e breakeven from third quarter

items.statement: Gross margin declined to 62.4% from 63.6% due to Sanofi mix; ex-Sanofi gross margins improved 100-150 bps; EBITDA margin 19.8% in Q1, targeting 20-21% for full year
items.quote: Gross margins for the quarter stood at 62.4% against 63.6% in quarter 1 of FY '24. The decline is due to business mix. Sanofi business is at a lower margin.

items.statement: India base business (ex-FCM, ex-Sanofi) grew 7% YoY and 8.4% QoQ; acute grew ~8%, chronic ~6%; target to grow 200 bps ahead of industry
items.quote: Ex-FCM and ex-Sanofi registered a steady growth of 7% Y-o-Y and 8.4% Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Emerging markets have healthy order book in non-ARV and ARV; ARV orders more back-ended this year, uptick expected going forward
items.quote: Emerging markets, we have a healthy order book both in non -ARV and ARV segment. In our non-ARV segment, w e are seeing traction for our differentiated products, and we saw robust growth in this segment

items.statement: Differentiated products contribute 53% of domestic revenue and ~one-third of international; Tenectase included in national essential list and state procurement expanding
items.quote: For the FY '24 in terms of the, if I look at the domestic business, about 53% of our revenues came from these differentiated products. In terms of the international market, that would have been roughly about one-third of the business there.

items.statement: Tax dispute of ~250 crores under appeal, no provision taken; US litigation settlements cash neutral as liability sits with demerged entity; loan guarantees to US entity retired in Q1
items.quote: It's under appeal and we have not taken any provisions, and we don't feel the need to take any extra provisions for that.

items.statement: IPO proceeds reduced net debt from 1,550 crores to 850 crores and gross debt from 2,000 crores to 950 crores; interest cost benefit fully from Q3/Q4
items.quote: So, our debt today is close to 850 crores. Prior to the IPO, it was around 1,550 crores.

items.statement: Canada targeting steady-state double-digit growth vs mid-single digit market; Mantra integration and cross-selling driving growth; margins sustainable in short-medium term
items.quote: So, you know, for us, our aspiration is to continue to grow on a steady-state double digits for the Canadian market for the short to medium-term. While the market, as you rightly said, continues to grow probably mid single digits.

items.statement: MR productivity target of ~7 by year-end vs 6.3 in Q1; field force expanded by 1,200 in last 18 months to ~5,000 (4,100 excluding managers)
items.quote: We believe our productivity levels will be closer to 7 by year end versus the 6.3 that we delivered in Q1.

items.statement: New facilities causing ~75 bps margin drag; expected to recover by year-end or early next year as utilization ramps
items.quote: I think, overall, just to add, we think that there is probably, cumulatively from these four facilities, the way you just described it in more detail, still about a 75-basis point margin drag on account of, obviously, th em ramping up

items.statement: ARV segment seeing green shoots on pricing and internal costing; bids aligned to margin threshold; selective participation
items.quote: Having said that, I think this year we are seeing some green shoots out there in terms of both the pricing and also from our internal costing also. So, we are seeing orders which are meeting our margin threshold picking up.

items.statement: Biologics plant audited by European authorities, positive outcome expected; focus on MENA, Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia for biologics; Tenectase global patent for stroke indication
items.quote: So, as far as biologics are concerned, what has really happened recently, our plant was audited by the European authorities and we expect, positive outcome going forward.

items.statement: MR attrition rate 20-30%, in line with industry
items.quote: I think it is in line with the industry between the 20% and 30% around that figure.

items.statement: Domestic-international revenue split to remain roughly 50-50; India organic growth target 200 bps above industry
items.quote: But I think if you look at domestic international, our split should roughly remain at 50%-50%.

items.statement: Management refrains from giving sugarcane crushing guidance for 2024-25 season, will provide better guidance in September-October-November results
items.quote: We will refrain from making a guess this time because last time when we did try to give a guidance, it did not work out, but I have outlined the headwinds and tailwinds, and I believe the tailwinds should outplay the headwinds is all I can tell you today.

items.statement: PLA project capex of Rs. 300 crore spent as of June 30, 2024, commissioning targeted for October-November 2026
items.quote: As of 30th June 2024, we have approximately spent Rs. 300 crore from internal accruals on the project.

items.statement: PLA project capex to be spent gradually over two years and three-four months until commissioning in October-November 2026
items.quote: So, I can only tell you that because we are looking at commissioning in October, November 2026, so it will be a gradual spend of money as capex gets spent in any project.

items.statement: India sugar production for 2024-25 projected at 32 million tonnes pre-diversion, domestic consumption at 29 million tonnes
items.quote: As per the latest estimates, India sugar production for the ensuing season that is 2024-25 is projected at 32 million tonnes pre-diversion.

items.statement: India inventory on September 30, 2024 expected at 8.5 million tonnes, government comfortable with 5.5 million tonnes closing stock
items.quote: India's inventory on 30th September 2024 is expected to be around 8.5 million tonnes or 85 lakh metric tonnes with the domestic consumption of 29 million tonnes.

items.statement: Ethanol diversion of 4 million tonnes expected to produce 400 crore litres for 2024-25 season
items.quote: From this 4 million tonnes diversion, we will be able to produce 400 crore litres. So, 400 crore litres of ethanol is what the sugar industry should be able to tender for the year in various tenders.

items.statement: Balrampur can run distillery at 100% capacity with unhindered juice and B-heavy ethanol diversion
items.quote: 100%. All juice, B-heavy, everything unhindered as per past.

items.statement: Management expects return to 2022-23 ethanol pricing regime for upcoming contracts
items.quote: So, we hope to get back to 2022-23 pricing regime, relationship regime, pricing regime, whatever is that. Last year wiped out as a bad dream.

items.statement: International raw sugar price floor at 18 c/lb, upside limited to 21-22 c/lb
items.quote: So, 18 c/lb should act as a floor and very honestly, there is no great upside beyond 21-22 c/lb, but this is because you're asking us to reply it is just a guess.

items.statement: Domestic sugar prices in UP around Rs. 38-39/kg ex-factory, white sugar export around Rs. 40/kg
items.quote: So, domestic prices are around Rs.3 8-39/kg in UP ex -factory, and international prices, we as a country are not exporting as of now, it is under restricted list, but maybe white sugar export will fetch around Rs.40 /kg

items.statement: Government policy decisions on ethanol diversion, pricing, MSP and exports expected before October-November crushing season
items.quote: So, the logic is everything should happen before October because everything is applicable something from 1st November, something from 1st October, types. So, prior to that, we hope, and we are working very hard and engaging with the Government so that it should happen.

items.statement: MSP revision expected to provide bottom protection of Rs. 2-2.5/kg above MSP during December-March season
items.quote: It could be Rs.35-36-37/kg, whatever it is. UP gets a Rs.2.5/kg bottoming above that. One should look at this for bottom protection, not for top creation and which is very important.

items.statement: Dual feed distillery capacity of 330 KLPD produces 5.5 crore litres ethanol from alternative feedstock in off-season
items.quote: So, we have dual feed capacity at one of our distilleries which has a daily distillation capacity of 330 KLPD. So, on an annual basis in the off season it can produce around 5 to 6 crore liters of ethanol out of alternative feeds.

items.statement: No plans for additional capex beyond PLA project, not investing in SAF, biodiesel, or CBG capacity expansion
items.quote: Having deployed our capital into this PLA project, as Balrampur, we are not looking at any more capex. With just capex within our company for balancing , etc., which is essential, rest we are not looking at any capex

items.statement: Maize feedstock at Rs. 72/litre not viable at current prices, FCI rice could help ethanol supply
items.quote: Currently, maize is at Rs. 72/litre. So, we do not know how the Government will react to maize pricing. We do not get into that. We run our business.

items.statement: Committed to sustained double-digit revenue growth with 20% plus EBITDA margin
items.quote: we are firmly on track to deliver on our commitment of sustained double -digit revenue growth with 20% plus EBITDA margin

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 19.1%, up 160 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has expanded to 19.1%, marking an improvement of 160 basis points year -on-year

items.statement: Europe margins increased 230 bps over past year to mid-teens; Americas margins rose from single-digits to high-teens
items.quote: In Europe, margins have increased by 230 basis points over the past year, reaching the mid-teens level. Similarly, in the Americas, margins have risen from single-digits to high-teens

items.statement: Strong organic oral care demand and wallet share gains from sustainable tube transition
items.quote: There was an enhanced oral care demand this quarter, driven by strong organic momentum. But also importantly, wallet share gain with a few customers as we transitioned to sustainable tube

items.statement: Sustainable tube mix reached 29% of total volume in Q1 FY25 vs 21% in FY24; anticipate further growth
items.quote: Our sustainable tube offerings now represent 29% of our total volume. And we anticipate this proportion to grow further as customer commitments align with our sustainable solutions

items.statement: Brazil plant at 65-70% utilization with modular design allowing plug-and-play capacity additions
items.quote: Currently, probably that will be somewhere around 65% to 70% of the utilization levels. But we still have headspace. But the plant is b uilt modular. As we start getting more traction on the market demand, we will just plug and play kind of a situation that we can add any time capacity

items.statement: Global double-digit revenue growth commitment; not providing region-specific growth guidance
items.quote: We've given you guidance on our global growth ambition. I would not like to get into a region-by-region growth ambition because every company, and we included, run a portfolio. But our ambition is to continue to drive growth in all regions, but deliver double -digit growth globally

items.statement: Brazil debt at local rates optimal after hedging costs and tax benefits; treasury constantly optimizing
items.quote: Brazil as a country has a volatile currency. And hence, the moment you add, if you take, let's say for example INR loan or USD loan or Yen loan, or we have looked at various currencies, the moment you add the forward covers to that, the landed cost in that country comes to be the same

items.statement: Effective tax rate steady state 21-24%; Q1 rate 17% due to profit mix
items.quote: in the long term we have said that our effective tax rate will be, let's say, anywhere between 21% to 23%, 24%. I think it's likely to be there

items.statement: EAP at 22% EBITDA margin in target zone; margin compression not a challenge per management
items.quote: a 14% revenue growth and a close to 22% EBITDA margin and 16% EBIT margin I think is the kind of P&L that we believe is a very strong P&L. Now, 22% EBITDA margin is in the target zone for EAP

items.statement: Management refuses to provide production or revenue guidance, stating it would be incorrect due to monetization dependencies
items.quote: See, Riddhesh, fundamental fact is in this business, we're continuously creating the value of the underlying assets. The monetization depends on many important drills, and it would be bad to me to give any guidance, and that will be either way incorrect.

items.statement: Capital outlay of Rs. 250 crores for North-Eastern region over next 2 financial years, may increase with sustained gas demand after grid connectivity
items.quote: In North-eastern region, our capital outlay for the next 2 financial years is about Rs. 250 crores, which would further be increased if there is sustained demand for gas after the establishment of grid connectivity.

items.statement: Capital program of about Rs. 1,000 crores for next 3 years to ensure sustained production with increased reserves, funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Capital program of about Rs. 1,000 crores for the next 3 years would ensure our sustained production with increased reserves and resource base of the Company. Our planned capital spend will be met through internal accruals.

items.statement: Dirok field production restricted to 20 mmscfd due to lack of demand; expects 40-45 mmscfd immediately once North-Eastern gas grid connects to national grid
items.quote: We believe that once the IGGL lays its own line from Duliajan to Numaligarh for about 180 kilometers, the demand constraint may move to supply constraint. This will ensure that an increased and stabilized offtake from financial year '25-'26 onwards to achieve the production to the full potential of the field.

items.statement: Dirok gas sales maintained at 0.55 bcf in Q1 FY25; condensate at 10,578 barrels vs 10,917 barrels previous quarter
items.quote: Dirok gas sales for the last quarter was 0.55 bcf, the same level is maintained in the 1st Quarter of '24, '25 for our share. Condensate is 10,578 barrels compared to 10,917 barrels in the previous quarter.

items.statement: B-80 gas price realized at US$10.34/mmbtu in Q1 FY25 vs US$17.54/mmbtu previous quarter; Western region gas price moving akin to imported LNG at ~US$13/mmbtu
items.quote: During this quarter, the average gas price realized is US$10.34 per mmbtu compared to US$17.54 per mmbtu in the previous quarter. Now the gas price in the Western region is moving akin to imported LNG price, which is about US$13.

items.statement: B-80 gas contract priced at 12% of oil price with floor at PPAC price (~$6.5/mmbtu) and no ceiling
items.quote: I think the floor, we put it as PPAC price that whatever it comes on it, that to my mind, the floor price should not be less than $6.5 and there is no ceiling as such because it is fixed with the 12.1% for one Company, another one is 12% or something.

items.statement: B-80 production in Q1 FY25: 67,351 barrels oil and 0.40 bcf gas vs 83,290 barrels oil and 0.42 bcf gas previous quarter
items.quote: Production in the current quarter is 67,351 barrels of oil and 0.40 bcf of gas, while it was 83,290 barrels of oil and 0.42 bcf of gas in the last quarter.

items.statement: B-80 production shut for ~14 days due to hawser parting in monsoon; new hawser ordered from Denmark, expected in 7-10 days, cost <Rs. 60-70 lakhs
items.quote: It's about 10 to 14 days. I think it's about 14 days, a little more than that.

items.statement: B-80 wells capable of 1,400 bpd oil and ~9 mmscfd gas (2,400-2,500 boepd); plans to drill 3 new wells in 2026-27 to ramp up full potential
items.quote: We will continue with that. And I don't think we plan to have any workover in these wells. We'll drill 3 new wells at the appropriate time, as we plan for it about 2026 and '27 to ramp up the full potential of the block.

items.statement: PY-1 offshore: 3 development wells planned, first well drilling to commence April-June 2025 after third-party expert review of gas-water contact
items.quote: We plan for 3 development wells and if everything goes as per plan, drilling of the first well will commence in April to June 2025.

items.statement: Kharsang block: Environmental clearance pending for 15 wells in Upper Girujan; revised EIA submitted July 25; exploration well to 4,000+ meters planned after partner approval
items.quote: Drilling 15 wells to increase the production from Upper Girujan will start as soon as we get the environmental clearance. Revised environmental impact assessment report is submitted. We will try to get the clearance at the earliest to embark on drilling.

items.statement: AA-ONHP-2017/19 block: GTO approved for 1 exploration well with 7 seismic signatures; 2-year RSC extension applied; drilling delayed due to heavy rains
items.quote: GTO has been approved to drill one exploration well with 7 seismic signatures. Due to heavy rain, drill pad and approach road could not be constructed in time to move the rig for drilling before August 2024. We have made an application for a 2-year RSC extension and once the extension is received from MoP&NG, we will drill one exploration well and on success, we will drill the second well.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution for debt up to Rs. 750 crores subject to shareholders' approval for oil & gas service sector opportunities with hard assets
items.quote: Board has approved an enabling resolution for debt up to Rs. 750 crores subject to shareholders' approval. This will enable us to scout for new opportunities in oil and gas service space with hard assets to widen our scope in the service sector.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA Rs. 20.97 crores vs Rs. 29.45 crores previous quarter; PAT Rs. 11.39 crores vs Rs. 19.1 crores; reduction mainly due to B-80 gas price drop
items.value: EBITDA Rs. 20.97 crores, PAT Rs. 11.39 crores
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA for the current quarter is Rs. 20.97 crores compared to Rs. 29.45 crores in the previous quarter. Profit after tax for the current quarter is Rs. 11.39 crores compared to Rs. 19.1 crores in the previous quarter. Major reason for reduction in profit is due to reduction in the gas price of B-80 field from US$17.54 per mmbtu to US$10.34 per mmbtu.

items.statement: B-80 oil inventory at ~165,000 barrels; will sell when reaching 400,000 barrel threshold to optimize tanker costs; FSO capacity 900,000 barrels
items.quote: As we speak, it should be around 165,000 barrels.

items.statement: Expect OPEX to AUM to keep moderating over medium term; reiterate goal of 3.5% to 4% in medium term
items.quote: We expect OPEX to AUM to keep moderating over the medium term and reiterate our goal of 3.5% to 4% in the medium term.

items.statement: Focus to bring legacy AUM to below 10% of total AUM in FY25 and make it further insignificant in FY26
items.quote: Our focus is to bring the legacy AUM to below 10% of total AUM in FY '25 and make it further insignificant in FY '26.

items.statement: Stick to guidance of collecting about Rs. 1,200-odd crores of AIF gain this year
items.quote: We continue to stay put with our guidance where we said that we would collect about Rs. 1,200-odd crores of AIF gain this year. So, we stick to that.

items.statement: Raised $300 million through maiden US dollar denominated sustainability bond in July, oversubscribed by four times
items.quote: Following the $100 million social impact loan in May, we raised $300 million through our maiden US dollar denominated sustainability bond in July, it was oversubscribed by four times.

items.statement: Growth AUM grew 51% year-on-year to Rs. 57,601 crores, now 82% of total AUM
items.quote: Within this, growth AUM grew by 51% year-on-year to Rs. 57,601 crores. It now accounts for 82% of our total AUM versus 34% at end FY '22.

items.statement: NIM for growth business was at 6.7% in Q1 FY25; expect some pressure in NIM for another quarter or two due to rising cost of borrowings and increasing leverage
items.quote: The NIM for growth business was at 6.7% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Increased pricing starting April 1 on most secured product lines; starting August 1, increased RPLR by 25 basis points on all variable rate portfolio
items.quote: Starting August 1, we have increased our RPLR by 25 basis points. So that is another indication to you of where yields are headed, given what we are seeing on the cost of borrowing environment.

items.statement: Retail disbursements grew 19% year-on-year to Rs. 6,816 crores; mortgage disbursements temporarily impacted by Rs. 255 crores due to regulatory changes
items.quote: 1st Quarter disbursements stood at Rs. 6,816 crores, growing by 19% year-on-year.

items.statement: Shifted focus towards non-metro geographies; reduced digital lending disbursements by over 50% over last 5 quarters; cross-sell at 7% of disbursements, expected to improve steadily
items.quote: We have been able to staff a sizable proportion of our customer base for future cross-sell. Current levels of cross-sell for us are still relatively modest at 7% of disbursements in this quarter. However, you should expect to see this improve steadily in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Retail 90+ DPD contained at 60 bps vs 80 bps YoY; business loans at 140 bps 90 DPD but priced at ~20% yield; digital lending disbursements cut by half over 4 quarters to manage risk
items.quote: On the asset quality front, retail has shown robust performance with overall 90-plus days past due contained at 60 basis points versus the 80 basis points same time last year, and the 50 basis points in the fourth quarter of the previous financial year.

items.statement: Securitization at 12% of overall borrowings vs 3% at end of prior period; fixed to floating rate debt mix improved to 52:48
items.quote: On diversification of borrowings, securitization is about 12% of overall borrowings versus 3% at the end of

items.statement: Merger of PEL and PCHFL progressing on track; scheme filed with stock exchanges after Board approval
items.quote: The merger of PEL and PCHFL is progressing on track. Following the Board approval, the scheme has been filed with the stock exchanges.

items.statement: Q2 aluminum consumption cost expected flattish to 1% up vs Q1 due to monsoon coal auction prices and higher caustic prices
items.quote: I think that in Q2 versus Q1, it will be flattish to 1% up because normally during monsoons, the s pot auction prices of coal tend to go up, and caustic prices have also gone up a little bit

items.statement: Copper business sustainable EBITDA baseline at ₹600 crores per quarter; Q1 ₹805 crores includes derivative accounting noise
items.quote: So I think that what you should be modeling going forward is more like the ₹600 crores.

items.statement: Downstream aluminum EBITDA per ton expected to bounce back in Q2 after Q1 product mix impact
items.quote: So the outlook for Q2 is extremely strong. So we have already seen July. So you will see the EBITDA per ton bouncing back in quarter 2.

items.statement: Downstream aluminum steady-state profitability at 600 Kt capacity estimated at $200 per ton EBITDA
items.quote: So once we have fully commissioned the FRP phase A and Silvassa is fully ramped up. So 600 kt into $200 per ton is roughly the number you should work with.

items.statement: India capex guided at ₹5,500-6,000 crores for FY25; Novelis capex guided at $1.3-2.1 billion for FY25, currently tracking near $1.8 billion
items.quote: So for the India side, this year, we'll be at ₹5,500 crores to ₹6,000 crores.

items.statement: Three upstream projects identified: alumina refinery expansion, copper smelter (280-300 Kt), 180-pot aluminum smelter expansion; each ~₹8,000 crores
items.quote: we will be looking at the alumina expansion in Odisha. We will be looking at a copper smelter -- I'm giving it in the sort of terms of priority. And then we are looking at 180 pot smelter expansion in Aditya with the renewable hydrid starting there i n January. So these are the 3 large upstream projects that are on our radar screen now. And each one of them is about an ₹8,000 crores project

items.statement: Alumina refinery project to break ground after bauxite contract with OMC signed; 24-26 months to full production from ground-breaking
items.quote: So look, we need to sign the contract that we are expecting to sign in the coming months, then we'll break ground, and we have done a lot of the parallel work already. So it will probably be another 24 to 26 months from that point.

items.statement: Copper recycling project (50 Kt) public hearing concluded; ground-breaking expected by October 2024
items.quote: Yes, the copper recycling project, the public hearing was concluded successfully 2 weeks ago. So we are now expecting to break ground by October for the copper recycling project.

items.statement: Indian FRP aluminum demand expected to grow 7-8% YoY in FY25 led by packaging, automotive, building & construction
items.quote: The Indian FRP demand in financial year '25 is expected to grow by around 7% to 8% on a year-on-year basis. This increase is led by strong demand from packaging, automotive and Building & Construction segments.

items.statement: Global aluminum FRP demand ex-China expected to grow 4% in CY24 with 4-7% CAGR over next 3-4 years across beverage packaging, automotive, specialty, aerospace
items.quote: The global aluminum FRP demand excluding China is expected to grow by 4% in calendar year '24 with demand recovery across all major segments of beverage packaging, automotive, specialty and aerospace between CAGRs of 4% to 7% over the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Novelis Sierre, Switzerland plant halted since June 30 due to unprecedented flooding; estimated restart by end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: However, an unprecedented weather event in Novelis Europe at the end of June, caused significant flooding at its Sierre, Switzerland plant. Fortunately, all of our employees were safely evacuated, though production has been halted since June 30. We currently estimate the plant to be back up and running at the end of the second quarter.

items.statement: Coal block clearances (Chakla, Meenakshi) facing difficult Stage 1/2 forest clearance process; met Ministry to expedite
items.quote: So we are working through it and let -- it'd fair to say that the going is quite difficult. I mean we are trying to get the Stage 1 and Stage 2 forest clearances, trying to get the CA land. We have actually just met the Ministry and the minister to ask for help in expediting this process.

items.statement: Supreme Court verdict on mineral taxation: negligible retrospective liability for Hindalco; ongoing impact from higher state tax rates
items.quote: No, no. There is -- for us from a retrospective basis, we have negligible liability. I think that for us, we will only be concerned on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: Downstream aluminum Q1 EBITDA per ton down 32% YoY due to unfavorable product mix fulfilling lower conversion premium orders in-house
items.quote: What happened is the product mix. So we had to fulfill some orders of products that were at a lower conversion premium. Normally, we would have done it through outsourced vendors, but this time, we had to do it wit h our

items.statement: Indian aluminum hedged 22% commodity at $2,550/t and 15% at zero collar ($2,258 floor, $2,539 ceiling) for FY25; 11% currency hedged at ₹88.43/$
items.quote: Our Indian aluminum business is currently hedged at around 22% commodity at a price of $2,550 per ton for the financial year 2025 and around 15% of the commodity at a zero collar with the bottom of $2,258 and a ceiling of $2,539 per ton. 11% of the currency is hedged at ₹88.43 per dollar.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt ₹35,530 crores (net debt/EBITDA 1.24x); India net cash ₹1,770 crores; Novelis net debt ₹38,226 crores as of June 2024
items.quote: On the balance sheet, our consolidated net debt stands at ₹35,530 crores. In the India operations, we have net cash of ₹1,770 crores, while the Novelis net debt stands at ₹38,226 crores at the end of June 2024. Hindalco, at the consolidated level maintained a strong balance sheet with net debt-to-EBITDA well below 2x at 1.24 at the end of June 2024

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected to remain similar to FY24 spend of around INR140 crores
items.quote: So if you look at our financial year '24, we have increased our capex kind of spend around INR140 crores on capex. And for financial year '25 as well, we expect our capex to more or less remain in a similar way.

items.statement: Manufacturing mix improved to 64% in Q1 FY25 from 60% in FY24
items.quote: Our manufacturing mix was around 64%, whereas traded product sale was 36%. So we are seeing improvements in our manufacturing mix if you compare year on...
