items.statement: Warehouse count increased 2.4x from 18 in FY21 to 44 in Q1 FY25; capacity up 2.5x to 1.5M sq ft; average order-to-delivery reduced 45% to 2.2 days.
items.quote: We've increased the number of our warehouses by almost 2.4x in the last three years. So from 18 warehouses in FY '21 to 44 warehouses in Q1 of this year. Capacity has also increased in a very similar amount, 2.5x. And today, we have over 1.5 million square feet of warehouse capacity.

items.statement: Acquired additional 39% stake in Dot & Key for INR 265 crores, raising total stake to 90%; also acquired majority stake in Earth Rhythm.
items.quote: And this growth continues to accelerate. And if you were to look at quarter 1 of financial '25, the GMV is now at annualized run rate of INR 750 crores. So, this has been a fantastic investment by Nykaa, and Nykaa has decided to go ahead and acquire additional 39% stake at a cost of INR 265 crores for 39% stake.

items.statement: Physical beauty store count reached 200 across 72 cities (1.9 lakh sq ft), doubling in 2 years; stores contribute ~8% of omnichannel beauty GMV and hosted 70+ brand events in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: we have 200 stores across 72 cities, and we covered a total retail l area of about 1.9 lakh square feet, which has doubled what it was just 2 years ago. If you look at the bar chart on the top right, you see that it took us about 8 years to build our first 100 stores. And we've managed to build the next 100 stores in just about 2 years

items.statement: Superstore transacting retailers grew 65% YoY to 210,000 across 1,000+ cities; orders grew 45% YoY to 383,000 with rising AOV and premium brand mix.
items.quote: You can see that transacting retailers have gone up by 5x in 2 years and a 65% growth year-on-year. We now have 210,000 transacting retailers and we serve now 1,000-plus cities, so we are really scaling up this business very well.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin improved 90 bps YoY to 6.2% in Q1 FY25; reported EBITDA margin 5.5% up from prior year.
items.quote: So corrected for that, the adj usted EBITDA stands at INR 109 crores, which is a 44% year-on-year growth and adjusted EBITDA margin would be at 6.2%, which would be a 90-basis point improvement over the previous

items.statement: Fashion fulfillment expenses reduced 167 bps YoY via air-to-land optimization and lower RTOs; marketing expenses improved 101 bps via better repeat ratio and conversion.
items.quote: Our fulfillment expenses have reduced by about 167 bps, this is a gain a concerted effort where we've been working on optimizing delivery from certain legs from air to land, faster deliveries, which has also reduced leakages, which we spoke about earlier, reduce RTO, has also reduced fulfillment expenses. So all moving again in the right direction. The marketing expenses improved by about 101 bps.

items.statement: Fashion owned brands GMV declined 14% YoY on 3P channels in Q1 FY25, partially offset by 10% growth on Nykaa Fashion platform; management calls performance disappointing but not a long-term trend.
items.quote: However, this is due to channel degrowth in 3P channels where we're degrown at 14% year -on-year. However, this is compensated by th e GMV growth and Nykaa Fashion platform where they grew 10%. Again, I think this performance is a bit disappointing. I wouldn't read into it as a long -term trend and efforts are on to increase the innovation and performance of the fashion owned brands

items.statement: Fashion 'First in Fashion' new launches contributed 24% of GMV in Q1 FY25, up from prior year, growing 37% YoY; Luxe Indian wear added 200+ brands in 6 months.
items.quote: We've seen a 37% GMV growth year-on-year of these new launches that all the brands in the country have done and its contribution to our total GMV was 24% in this quarter. Again, this is higher than it was last year. Last year, again, cementing our belief in creating newness conversation and excitement in fashion as a category.

items.statement: Beauty annual unique transacting customers grew 21% YoY to 13.1M; orders grew 26% YoY to 12.4M in Q1 FY25; new customer acquisition grew 27% YoY.
items.quote: In terms of annual unique transacting customers, this grew at 21% taking us to 13.1 million unique transacting customers for the year. And the number of orders that were placed on the platform for the quarter was about 12.4 million orders, which is a 26% growth year-over-year.

items.statement: Nykaa Play relaunch drove 35% higher cart additions and 30% higher visits per visitor for engaged users vs non-engaged users in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: And you can see that Nykaa Play's relaunch has led to a 35% higher cart addition by those who are actually actively using the Nykaa Play feature on the app versus those who are not, and also 30% higher visits per visitor of those who are actively using and engaging with Nykaa Play.

items.statement: Marketing expense for Beauty segment expected to remain range bound at 8.5% to 9.0% of sales
items.quote: I think somewhere around the 8.5% to 9.0%.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expanded 30 bps YoY in Q1 FY25; normalized expansion 90 bps excluding GCC and restructuring expenses
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded by 30 basis points during the quarter with a higher than revenue growth of 31%.

items.statement: Fashion gross margins improved 360 bps YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by higher marketing and servicing income
items.quote: Our fashion gross margins in Q1 improved by 360 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis, primarily driven by higher marketing and servicing income.

items.statement: Beauty BPC gross margins remained largely steady YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: While gross margins in BPC remained largely steady.

items.statement: Heavy lifting on warehouse expansion for express delivery largely behind; incremental last-mile fulfillment cost may come but not very meaningful
items.quote: I do believe a lot of the heavy lifting is now behind us.

items.statement: Optimistic on services income recovery in H2 FY25 driven by festive season and D2C brands returning to advertising
items.quote: So that's a positive trend, which we think should strengthen as we get into the second half of the year, which tends to be where most of the festive occasions are and a lot of the seasonal, and festive shopping for this category will occur.

items.statement: Expect discounting to moderate in H2 FY25 if demand revives during festive season
items.quote: And I think if that happens, you will see the discount ing should moderate, and that should, again, help reduce the buildup

items.statement: Owned beauty brands growing across all channels; channel mix shifts reflect Dot & Key rollout in stores and GT/MT expansion for Kay Beauty
items.quote: All the beauty on brands are growing across all the channels. It just might happen to be that, for example, others, it's coming off of a smaller base, right?

items.statement: Foot Locker e-commerce partnership launch scheduled for October 2024
items.quote: We've announced a Foot Locker Association, where we are going to represent all the Foot Locker's e-commerce demand in the country, and that launch is going to happen in October of this year.

items.statement: Acquired majority stake in Earth Rhythm; board approved increasing stake in Dot & Key to 90% and making Earth Rhythm a subsidiary
items.quote: The Board of Directors at its meeting held today has also approved acquisition of further stake in Dot & Key, which will take our stake to 90% as well as in Earth Rhythm, which will make it a subsidiary of the company.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of western wear and accessories business from Nykaa Fashion via slump sale in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Completed the acquisition of western wear and accessories business from Nykaa Fashion by a slump sale in quarter 1 FY '25.

items.statement: Fashion growth impacted by seasonality and step-function dynamics; Indian wear weakness and western wear underperformance on third-party platforms in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The quarter was tough due to two elements, mainly on third-party platform where it has been listed on Myntra few other platforms. We didn't perform as well.

items.statement: Packaging cost reduction in eB2B driven by reuse and recycling of outer packaging materials over last 6-7 quarters
items.quote: What we have been driving for last, I think, 6-7 quarters is that a lot of our outer packaging, we are reusing recycling materials for the brand boxes.

items.statement: No incremental guidance provided; management cautions against reading too much into quarterly margin fluctuations
items.quote: I would just like to caution that, yes, Fashion gross profit margin looked very good, but there are quarter-on-quarter differences. And I would say that some of it is definitely noncore.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain ~20% growth at least till H1 FY25; internal targets split between H1 and H2 with high hopes for Diwali
items.quote: We've still been able to post a 20% growth. So, I think we will try and maintain this at least till H1. Once the market conditions improve, things start happening, then probably internally also we're looking at H1 separately, and then we're looking at H2.

items.statement: Total FY25 capex ~Rs 30 cr for hard luggage plant plus Rs 5-6 cr for warehousing phase 1 plus regular store capex
items.quote: overall project was about ₹30 odd crores, and we're deploying that. Apart from that, there's some CapEx that we are also deploying towards our warehousing that will also entail about anywhere between ₹5 crores to ₹6 crores of CapEx.

items.statement: Juicy Couture license signed for 10+5 years with lower royalty; women handbags expected to reach 15-20% of portfolio in next couple of years
items.quote: the contract is 10 plus five. So, we get a 15 -year license ideally. 10 years is the contract period, and there's an auto renewal clause of another five years. So, we get a long-term contract. And the royalty percentage is also quite lucrative.

items.statement: Margins improved sequentially from Q4 but remain below year-ago quarter due to subdued same-store sales, higher royalty on old inventory, and pre-operative expenses; expects recovery in coming quarters if market improves
items.quote: The margins have been improved from Q4, of course, the last preceding quarter, but still subdued from the previous same year quarter. The reasons remain to be the same as I had explained even during my last call that a same -store sales, the growth has been subdued.

items.statement: Adding Juicy Couture as super premium bridge-to-luxury women's handbag/accessories brand; also exploring marketplace model on bagline.com for curated premium brands; UCB small leather goods now #2 at Shoppers Stop
items.quote: Juicy Couture is a very, very, strategic addition to our portfolio. We've been eyeing this space, where we look at our women handbag kind of a brand. And the price point is going to be more in the super premium bridge to luxury kind of a category

items.statement: Bangladesh unrest impacting competitors who source heavily from there; management sees this as positive for Brand Concepts
items.quote: all the big-ticket players were sourcing a lot from Bangladesh. Yeah, there is going to be an impact for them. Good for us.

items.statement: IFF merger in NCLT; shareholders meeting end of September, completion expected by end of Q3 FY25; operational integration already underway with new client wins
items.quote: IFF, I think we are already in NCLT. And if I'm not mistaken, towards the end of September is when the Shareholders Meeting is supposed to happen. And I think after that, it'll take another couple of months , so four months max.

items.statement: CSD channel showing brilliant sell-through in limited depots; margins currently lower due to locked-in pre-COVID pricing but price escalation allowed after one year; focus now on expanding points of sale
items.quote: The traction is very good actually. The sell through is very good. Sales are in whatever limited number of th is thing that canteen that we've gone, we've seen a brilliant response over there. So, now is the time when we geared up, and we will sort of start expanding on that entire segment.

items.statement: Vertical brand experimenting in mass-market luggage distribution with good initial response; leveraging upcoming in-house manufacturing for pricing power; Sugarush confined to EBOs
items.quote: We've experimented with two models in Vertical in distribution space, in MBO space. And we've taken a very, very different sort of route, very different strategy. And I'm happy to share that the markets have responded pretty well, very good, actually to those strategies.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target 10-12%; management prefers reinvesting profits for growth over margin maximization; aims to scale from ~Rs 70 cr quarterly run-rate toward Rs 2,000-3,000 cr potential
items.quote: I believe there are 12%, 13% , anything between 10 % to 12% of an EBITDA is a good EBITDA, right? It's a decent EBITDA. We're not very extremely good, but we're not extremely bad also. Let's maintain that and then plough back that whole money to grow.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected in late teens for FY25
items.quote: I think, Damayanti just to anticipate that , our growth (Revenue) probably for this year will be kind of late teens.

items.statement: Matured hospitals revenue growth expected to reach double digits in coming quarters
items.quote: Typically, the quarter first remains very muted. Still, we could show gro wth of 7.3% year -on- year basis and as we enter into the season which is September and December, you'll see more healthy growth in the double digits going forward

items.statement: Invested INR 56.7 crores in capex during Q1 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, the company invested roughly INR56.7 crores in ongoing capital expenditures.

items.statement: Gurugram flagship hospital capex per bed around INR 1.5 crores
items.quote: I think it will be around 1.5 Cr. Yes, for sure.

items.statement: Rajahmundry and Hennur Bangalore hospitals expected to commence operations in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Both are expected to commence operations in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Coimbatore regional hub hospital project started, expected completion in 24 months
items.quote: The project work for the regional hub hospital in Coimbatore (~ 130 beds) has just started and is expected to complete in 24 months' time.

items.statement: Matured hospitals EBITDA margin slightly improved year-on-year, no erosion
items.quote: We are not seeing any margin erosion. In fact, in the matured hospitals they operate on the operating leverage. So any incremental revenue growth will always improve the EBITDA or EBITDA margins.

items.statement: New hospitals cost structure 90-95% settled, minimal incremental cost expected
items.quote: more or less I think 90%-95% the cost is settled there. As we grow these units and new clinical teams join, there may be some impact but not major

items.statement: Hydernagar, Himayat Nagar, Sarjapura hospitals to achieve EBITDA breakeven by end of FY25, Chennai by H1 FY26
items.quote: So then potentially the Hydernagar, Himayat Nagar and the Sarjapura Hospital should achieve EBITDA break even by end of this year. And Chennai, you are possibly targeting break even in first half of next year.

items.statement: Three new hospitals commissioned in Q4 FY24 adding 280 beds, total capacity over 2,000 beds
items.quote: In the last quarter, we marked a significant milestone by commissioning three new hospitals, one each in Hyderabad, Bangalore and Chennai, adding a total of 280 beds. This brings our total capacity to over 2,000 beds, including managed beds in New Delhi.

items.statement: Outpatient footfalls, inpatient admissions and deliveries showing significant improvement
items.quote: Our outpatient footfalls, inpatient admissions and deliveries are all showing significant improvement.

items.statement: IVF program expanded to 11 units with impressive organic footfalls
items.quote: Now we've got to about 11 total. Now I think all of them are commissioned, all the embryology services have started, the doctors have been recruited, the business plan is laid out. And I think whatever the early footfalls that we are seeing are pretty impres sive and are pretty organic

items.statement: New hospitals priced attractively initially, insurance tie-ups take 6-9 months to settle
items.quote: One is that you want to be attractive for the patients. Generally, in a new hospital, people see how expensive it is. First thing is you don't want to get that in major name. So, you will definitely price it attractively in the beginning.

items.statement: Gurugram project may face 4-6 month delay due to government approval processes
items.quote: I think there may be a four to six months delay because we didn't expect that it will take about a year to get the land parcels registered and now we applied for the permissions.

items.statement: New hospitals breakeven at ~35% occupancy, Hyderabad within 12 months, Bangalore 12-15 months, Chennai 15-18 months
items.quote: Usually about 35% occupancy we break even. And a t a place like Bangalore, it will take about 12 to 15 months time. Chennai might take about 15 to 18 months

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 518 crores as of June 30, 2024, sufficient to fund all planned capex without debt
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with a net cash position of INR518 crores as of June 30, 2024 which will support our ongoing capital expenditure plans. Given our current cash flow and anticipated internal accruals in the coming years, we are confident in our ability to complete all planned capital expenditures through internal accruals without acquiring debt financing.

items.statement: Topline growth guidance of 18-20% for FY25 maintained; bottom line growth now expected at 15-18% due to duty cut impact
items.quote: we are confident that we will achieve overall 18% to 20% growth throughout the year subject to quarterly variances.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 at 7-8%; gross margin guidance at 14-15%
items.quote: We have said 14% 14.5% to 15% and EBITDA we have said 7 % to 8%.

items.statement: Plan to open 18-20 stores in FY25; 6 stores opened in Q1 (4 COCO, 2 franchisee, 1 in Dubai)
items.quote: we have been planning and aiming to open about 18 to 20 stores for the whole financial year and in Q1 we have opened six stores out of the 18 to 20 stores

items.statement: Q1 gross margin expanded ~500bps YoY due to better business quality, franchisee pricing tweaks, and rising gold price benefit on making charges
items.quote: gross margin has also been in a good range, primarily because what we see is that subsequent to the earlier quarters, like last year's Q1, or Q1 FY 22-23, we've seen an improvement in the quality of our business.

items.statement: Customs duty cut (9%) creates ~Rs 50 crore inventory loss on gold loan portion; impact spread over Q2-Q3
items.quote: we are analysing and assuming that approximately 50 crores of financial impact would be there due to the duty that has already been paid and the market value that has been coming down.

items.statement: Post duty cut (last 15-20 days), footfalls and sales up sharply; Q2 YTD growth ~25-30% implying 18-20% YTD
items.quote: growth number as on date can be assumed to be at 18% to 20

items.statement: Studded ratio fell to 9.6-9.7% in Q1 (vs 11.5% FY24); target 12-13% for FY25 via inventory build and attractive pricing
items.quote: our target remains the same. It is only one or two quarters, as you said, do not decide the journey. The journey very clearly remains a confident journey. And more so, since our diamond prices are quite attractive, we are with the competition. We are sure that we will achieve the 12.5% to 13% this year. But surely, we will touch 12%.

items.statement: Gold metal loan portion (~40-45% of hedging) unhedged to duty changes; further duty cuts would hurt
items.quote: But we need to keep in mind that GML will not have an impact of that, if there is any further duty cut, then GML will not be the right way to hedge.

items.statement: Hedging at ~95% in Q1 (MCX ~50-55%, Gold Metal Loan ~40-45%); gold loan portion exposed to duty changes
items.quote: hedging percentage has been, we said in the press release also, has been ~95%.

items.statement: Gold exchange rising due to higher gold prices and trust shift from unorganised to organised; target 40-45% of sales
items.quote: Higher gold exchange clearly is for two reasons. One is the increasing gold price and which is a major reason the customer has to buy gold he doesn't have money and he brings the old gold. Secondly, the trust and movement from unorganized to organized in the respective market.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond pilot in 3-4 stores; not yet breakeven; FY25 revenue contribution Rs 50-100 crore
items.quote: in the current year, in 24-25, when we talk about the Sennes segment, which consists of lab-grown perfume and the leather bags, the contribution is not likely to be more than Rs 100 crores. I have said earlier Rs 50 crores. I think between Rs 50 crores to Rs 100 crores.

items.statement: International expansion calibrated; first store in Dubai opened; focus on brand building before scaling
items.quote: we will be in a very methodical and a calibrated manner doing our expansion abroad.

items.statement: FY28 revenue aspiration of Rs 2000 crore if roads and building segments expand
items.quote: And if we increase the building a little and increase the road, if we go to the highway, then it will be 2000 plus, very easily.

items.statement: Order book stands at over Rs 1800 crore unexecuted work
items.quote: Sir, in excess of 1800 crores unexecuted work is with us.

items.statement: Bid pipeline exceeds Rs 4000 crore with 10-15% expected conversion rate
items.quote: The bid pipeline is more than Rs. 4000 crores, where we have participated and the maximum result should be within one to two months.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 24-26% considered sustainable across water, road HAM and building projects
items.quote: Yes, sir, these are all projects with the same margins.

items.statement: Significant increase in water sector works expected from government entities post-budget
items.quote: I think there's going to be a significant increase in the water sector works that are going to come out of the government entities.

items.statement: Order book split 75% water segment, 25% other segments
items.quote: 75% water segment, 25% from other.

items.statement: Acquired manufacturing property in Fatehpur, UP for Rs 50-60 crore to use as bank collateral for BG facilities
items.quote: We have acquired a manufacturing entity in Fatehpur, UP. We have told in our board meeting that our plan is to shut down by December. Ultimately, we will use that property as collateral which we need for banking facilities.

items.statement: No payment delay issues anticipated; projects funded by World Bank, ADB or central government
items.quote: We are not facing any payment delay issues. The nature of the business is such that we almost 10% to 15% of the amount gets withheld by the department in shape of retention money that is released after commissioning of the project.

items.statement: H1 revenue expected at 30-40% of annual, H2 at 60-70% due to seasonality
items.quote: So I think it would be anywhere around for H1 it would be based on year-to-year 30% to 40% and for H2 it would be 60% to 70%.

items.statement: No fundraising requirement currently; working capital sufficient for project execution
items.quote: Now the requirement is not there. It depends on how many project gets converted, it is based on that too, but as of now there is no requirement. We have working capital available and we can do in that.

items.statement: Cash realization of Rs 125-150 crore from trade receivables in Q1 FY25
items.quote: It will be around Rs. 125-150 crores.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15-17% for FY25
items.quote: Last year also we had a revenue growth of 15% to 17%, which would be in overall lines. This year, in terms of revenue growth, Q1, we are around 6% in terms of the passenger vehicle segment and about 14% in commercial vehicle segment. Going forward, Q2, Q3, Q4, and the larger numbers coming from these three quarters, we would be at an overall of about 15% to 17% overall growth.

items.statement: Service business revenue growth target of 20-25% for FY25
items.quote: Service business, we target to grow by approximately 20% to 25%, and that will be the guidance for the year also.

items.statement: Q2 expected to cover Q1 volume shortfall with festival season starting August 17
items.quote: We are confident that Q2 will cover up the shortfall of Q1 in terms of volume sales.

items.statement: EV two-wheeler sales expected to recover from August with Ather Rizta launch
items.quote: We are expecting the sales, the amount of booking, the number of bookings that we have is quite considerable. And we are expecting sales as soon as supplies happen, starting from August through the next three quarters to be very robust.

items.statement: EBITDA margin depressed at 4% in Q1 due to weak service business from climatic conditions
items.quote: Service being a main driver of EBITDA margin, these conditions led to a depressed margin in this quarter. EBITDA reduced by approximately 3% compared to last year.

items.statement: Average selling price increased across new vehicles, pre-owned, and service segments
items.quote: We have seen an uptrend in our average selling price, increased from INR 8,54,057 to INR 9,62,403.

items.statement: EV investments negligible at ~INR 1.5 crores for Piaggio across seven centres
items.quote: We have made approximately just about INR 1.5 crores of investments in Piaggio across seven centres per se.

items.statement: Credit rating upgrades for two subsidiaries: Popular Auto Works BBB- to BBB+, Prabal Motors BBB to A-
items.quote: two of our subsidi aries, one is Popular Auto Works Private Limited, got double notch credit rating upgradation from BBB - to BBB+. Whereas the other subsidiar y, Prabal Motors Private Limited, also got a double notch rating upgradation from BBB to A

items.statement: Revenue mix: PV 5.4% growth, CV 14% growth, EV -39.5% decline in Q1
items.quote: PV revenue .i.e., passenger vehicles revenue was INR 734 crores versus INR 696 crores in Q1 FY '24, which is an increase of about 5.4% year-on-year. Commercial vehicle was INR 479.9 crores versus INR 420.8 crores in Q1 FY '24, an increase of 14% Y-o-Y. EV revenue was INR 13.6 crores versus INR 22.4 crores in Q1 FY '24, a decrease of 39.5% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Bookings nearly double July daily average in last 4-5 days ahead of Onam festival
items.quote: In the last four-five days, we are seeing that the bookings are almost double of what has been the July daily average.

items.statement: Appointed Chief Risk Officer effective August 13
items.quote: We are pleased t o announce the appointment of our Chief Risk Officer with effect from 13th August, that is yesterday. So Jarly, who is the Head Finance of our Pop ular Vehicles and Services division, has been given the additional responsibility of CRO

items.statement: Adding seven new service centers in FY25 after adding seven in FY24
items.quote: Last year we have built about seven new service centers. And I mean, like I said, this year too, we have another seven centers coming up.

items.statement: Honda ASP grew 12% in Q1; revenue grew 8% despite only 2% volume growth
items.quote: In fact, Honda ASP has gone up by 12%. So overall the revenue of Honda actually grew up by 8% in Q1 compared to previous year.

items.statement: Annual EBITDA margin guidance of around 18% and PAT margin of 11-12%
items.quote: In the past also, we have given a guidance of 18% EBITDA and around 11% to 12% of PAT. And that's how historically our margin profile has been.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 25-30% year-on-year for next couple of years
items.quote: From the revenue perspective, we are definitely looking at around 25 to 30% increase year on year. That is what has happened in the last year as well. And we should be able to exceed that in the next couple of years as well.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs. 12,461 million with 91% domestic, 9% international; 95% heating equipment, 5% waste gas handling
items.quote: Our order book remains strong, standing at Rs. 12,461 million with a well-diversified composition. Geographically, 91% of our current order book is driven by the Indian customer requirement and 9% orders coming from the international markets.

items.statement: Complete Rs. 1,246 crore order book should ideally get executed in FY25 and FY26
items.quote: So, just to answer your question in short, the complete Rs. 1,246 crores order book should ideally get executed in this year and next year.

items.statement: Bid pipeline roughly Rs. 4,000 crore with Rs. 1,000-1,500 crore domestic and Rs. 2,000-2,500 crore export opportunities
items.quote: So, basically, the bid pipeline roughly stands at something like Rs. 4,000 crore, wherein maybe about Rs. 1,000-1,500 crores is for domestic and Rs. 2,000-2,500 crores is for exports.

items.statement: Expect order inflow to be better in FY26 vs FY25 considering announced projects in India and abroad
items.quote: It is a bit difficult to comment on that as of now. But, yes, generally it looks like that considering the projects announced in India and also the projects expected abroad. It looks like that. The inflow should be better in FY26 vs 25, yes.

items.statement: No additional capex needed for Reliance cracking furnace order; existing facilities sufficient
items.quote: And we don't need any additional capex to execute this project. Whatever the existing facilities we have, that is sufficient. We might have to create some facilities at the site to execute the job.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 13.4% down from prior year due to lower quarterly revenue, ESOP provision of Rs. 54.6 million, and revenue mix
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has gone down as compared to the same period last year. This is mainly due to the increased operational cost as we scale up our business and invest in future growth. Also, the creation of ESOP reserves to the tune of Rs. 54.6 million for the employee benefit.

items.statement: ESOP provision of Rs. 5.46 crore made in Q1; similar provisions expected each quarter in FY25 depending on share price
items.quote: Yes, Sagar, this provision is made for this quarter and every quarter there will be a provision, and that provision corresponds to the market value at the end of the quarter.

items.statement: No price escalation clauses; raw material ~10% of order value; critical materials procured immediately or back-to-back to hedge fluctuations
items.quote: Generally, we do not have the price escalation clause in the purchase orders, but what happens is that the raw material purchased by us from a percentage perspective is quite low. It is, not even maybe 10% of the order value.

items.statement: Export project finalizations delayed but expecting closures in FY25; CPCL project may spill to FY26
items.quote: Yes, there has been a bit of a delay in terms of the finalization on the export project which we have quoted. So, the big pipeline stands as it is. So, we are definitely expecting certain closure in this fiscal, no doubt about it, it did get delayed.

items.statement: Historical revenue execution: ~1/3 in H1, ~2/3 in H2; Q3 and Q4 roughly double Q1 and Q2
items.quote: Historically, what has been the case is whatever we had done in Q1 and Q2, almost double we have done in Q3 and Q4. That has been the historical trend.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs. 300 crores primary capital strengthening balance sheet for working capital and growth
items.quote: The past year has been particularly noteworthy for us, culminating in our IPO which has raised Rs. 300 crores in primary capital. So, this IPO marks a new chapter for JNK India, providing the capital required for our support to grow future ambitions.

items.statement: Targeting Rs 900-1,000 crores top line in next 3-4 years with parallel bottom line growth
items.quote: That's the target. That's a very clear target, primarily. And more than the top line also, we are focused on making sure that we're able to get our bottom line also growing parallelly.

items.statement: Planning 11 new stores across three formats in FY25, targeting 100 stores in 3-4 years
items.quote: We are planning 11 stores this financial year. We are more or less on track for that. Having said that, we are not one of those companies who want to rush into store opening because real estate plays a very important role in our business and finding the suitable real estate still remains a very big challenge.

items.statement: Gross margin dropped to 53.2% in Q1 from 56.5% in Q4 due to sea freight costs, airlifting leather, forex impact and bulk sale at lower margin
items.quote: On gross margin, Q4, gross margins were 56.5% and current Q1 is about 53.2%. What really impacted was because of sea shipment, which is we import leather from sea, because of the sea freight going up and also the delays in arrivals of these shipments, we had to airlift a lot of leather or a lot of imported goods for our supply chain.

items.statement: Expect gross margin to recover to 56% range from Q2 onwards through price hike, shipment cost stabilization, localization and operating efficiency
items.quote: What we believe is from Q2 onwards, we should come back to our 56% range I mean, you know, like all the scenarios and those one-time bulk sale that we had in Q1. Without that, we should go back broadly to our Q4 margins.

items.statement: Leather localization at 30-33% currently, targeting 75% in 18-24 months for 20-22% overall cost savings
items.quote: Currently, around 30 %, 33% of our leather has been localized. My target is to get to a point of 75% localization in the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Expect solid housing delivery to start H2 FY25 with 30,000 units sold above Rs 3 cr in past 4 years, 85% delayed
items.quote: We are expecting solid delivery to start happening perhaps by H2. And most of the projects that were delayed are now coming almost into completion stage. And we expect a very good housing handover to happen in H2, starting from H2 of this year.

items.statement: KCD (kitchen) pilot in Bangalore executed 100 projects, planning gradual pan-India rollout over 1.5 years
items.quote: While we have successfully launched our KCD in Bangalore only Bangalore last year in September and we have done the pilot marketing here, we are happy to say that we have taken close to about 150 projects and executed close to 100 projects in Bangalore.

items.statement: Took small price hike to offset cost pressures, plus shipment cost stabilizing and localization benefits
items.quote: No, I think it will definitely improve because we have taken a small price hike, point number one. Point number two, we also see the shipment cost stabilizing just at this point in time plus also the localization.

items.statement: B2B contract manufacturing at 20% of revenue, added Steelcase as new client, maintaining 80-20 B2C-B2B split
items.quote: Contract manufacturing has something been there from a legacy perspective. We will continue to do contract manufacturing and currently it's 80 -20 split between B2C and B2B. We see that being similar going forward also.

items.statement: Store openings delayed due to construction labour shortage, 3 mature stores relocated due to metro disruption and fire incident
items.quote: We encountered delays in opening of new stores due to non-availability of construction labour and we had to relocate three ma tured stores due to disruption caused by metro lines and a fire incident in one of the stores.

items.statement: New homemakers constitute 65-70% of business, premium housing handover delays of 18-24 months causing purchase postponement
items.quote: New homemakers constitute majority of our customer base and we are witnessing postponement of purchase due to this handover delay.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs 200 crores allocated for retail network expansion, new stores and renovation of existing locations
items.quote: We raised RS. 200 crores in primary capital which we plan to be utilizing for expansion and ensuring Stanley capitalizes on the growing premium and luxury markets.

items.statement: Mature Stanley Level Next stores (2+ years) showing 20-25% SSSG driven by complete home solution pivot including kitchen and wardrobes
items.quote: Stanley Level Next , which is my luxury format store this more than two years store format is showing an average growth of 20% to 25%. Again to understand here, this growth is coming in mainly because we have pivoted to a more complete home solution offering.

items.statement: Stanley Level Next grew 35% YoY in Q1, while Stanley Boutique and Sofas & More were flat to negative 5%
items.quote: Of all the three formats, Stanley Level Next has reported a growth of from Q1 to Q1 almost 35% and Stanley Boutique and Sofas and More have almost been flattish to negative to almost like negative 5% growth in other two segments.

items.statement: BIS certification for furniture imports expected to be fully implemented in 12-24 months, providing tailwind for domestic manufacturers
items.quote: So, we believe that while this process of what you call as blocking free import has already started, it will definitely come into full play probably 12-24 months from now.

items.statement: Advertising spend reduced to 3.4% in Q1 due to subdued markets, H2 seasonally stronger than H1
items.quote: In fact, I think we have been restrictive and reduced our advertisement spend in Q1 considering that markets were fairly subdued and we didn't get initial response. So, I think we have ended up spending 3.4%

items.statement: Production guidance of around 50 million tons for FY25 maintained
items.quote: Number two, of course, we still keep a guidance of around 50 million tons.

items.statement: NSL monthly breakeven targeted by end of Q2 FY25, quarterly breakeven in Q3 FY25, annual breakeven in FY25
items.quote: On a monthly basis, we'll be able to break even. Quarterly breakeven will come, of course, in Q3 and annual breakeven will come in this financial year.

items.statement: Capex spend of around INR384-400 crores up to August against annual target of INR2,200 crores; expect to exceed target by substantial margin
items.quote: Up to August spend, we have spent around INR384 crores or almost INR400 crores in NMDC for against an annual target of around INR2,200 crores.

items.statement: Lump mix expected to decline to 20-25% in 5-7 years as larger blast furnaces increase pellet usage; expansion plans factor this shift
items.quote: We expect that in 5 to 7 years especially around '31, '32 or maybe somewhere around '35 with the bigger blast furnaces coming in which has higher capacity of pellets, the lump demand itself might go down to around 20% to 22% or 25%.

items.statement: Supreme Court retrospective tax judgment: MP diamond mine liability ~INR21 crores (hard to recover); Karnataka potential liability ~INR2,500 crores (mostly recoverable from existing customers); Chhattisgarh ~INR144 crores (already paid/reco
items.quote: So far as Chhattisgarh is concerned, we are already recovering it and -- from our customers and paying it. So there will be hardly any retrospective effect. There was some about INR144 crores old demand which we have paid in cash

items.statement: Pricing terms exclude all taxes and duties; any new levies recovered from customers in addition to base price
items.quote: Yes, it is excluding all the taxes and duties. Even now when we have the consolidated pricing it is inclusive of royalty, DMF and annuity and additional royalty. Any new taxes and duties are always in addition to that.

items.statement: Pre-demerger expenses of INR2,500 crores owed by NSL to NMDC; INR100 crores paid last month; expect full liquidation within 12 months
items.quote: This is a pre-demerger expenses at INR2,500 crores. Last month INR100 crores has been paid with the improved -- as and when we reach breakeven and we'll have enough cash surpluses to pay. Hopefully, within a 12-month period, we should be able to liquidate that.

items.statement: Karnataka Monitoring Committee dues of ~INR1,890 crores pending; review petition filed in Supreme Court; no adverse P&L impact as tax already paid and amount booked
items.quote: That left about INR1,890 crores of still a recoverable amount. The Supreme Court initial judgment declined to refund that, but we have now made a review petition for that, and we've gone to the higher bet.

items.statement: Average sales realization was INR5,304/t in Q1; after two INR500/t price cuts, expected to fall to ~INR4,304/t in Q2, in line with market trends
items.quote: Our prices, we have taken 2 price cuts in the last 2 times. That's about INR500 and INR500, about a INR1,000, we have taken a price cut. And that is why our average sales realization which was Q1, it was around INR5,304. Now it should come down to around INR4,304

items.statement: Royalty accounted based on production, not sales; Q1 royalty down 13% YoY in line with 14% production decline
items.quote: royalty, ultimately, what we book, although it is paid based on sales, but the booking is based on production. So that is why the royalty came down by 13%, which is in turn -- which is in tune with the reduction in production

items.statement: NSL losses halved in first year; produced >1.5 million tons hot metal; targeting 1 million tons HRC by Aug 24 anniversary
items.quote: Financially, we've been able to cut down our losses to half. And once the 5-kilometer electrification is done by the end of next month, we will be able to dispatch 2 rigs daily against the 1 rig currently

items.statement: Q1 production down 4% YoY (~1.5 million tons) due to May go-slow and heavy monsoons/flooding (254mm rain in 3 hours at Kirandul); confident of making up shortfall by Oct 10-15 and exceeding prior year in H2
items.quote: Because of some go slow in month of May and then very heavy monsoons this year. As you know, there has been some flooding. There had been some flooding in one of our mines in Kirandul, etc because we received 254 millimeters of rain in 3 hours itself.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY25 to be significantly better than H1 and remains confident of meeting full-year revenue, EBITDA and PAT guidance.
items.quote: We expect our second half of the year to be significantly better than the first half. We are still guiding within our revenue guidance range for the year. We are confident of meeting our EBITDA and PAT norms for the year that we've had before.

items.statement: Management targets exit EBITDA margin of 9% for FY25.
items.quote: We are further marching towards FY25 exit at 9% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Order book stands at $475 million as of June 30, 2024 with a robust pipeline, particularly in data center solutions.
items.quote: Our backlog stands steady at $475 million as of June 30, 2024, bolstered by a robust pipeline, particularly in data center solutions.

items.statement: INR410 crores raised via preferential warrants will be invested in data center expansion, network infrastructure, innovation in cloud, cyber security, AI, IoT, and go-to-market expansion in North America and emerging markets.
items.quote: We're excited to report a significant funding boost of INR410 crores to drive growth in key focus areas within the digital infrastructure sector. This capital will be invested strategically in: Data center expansion, enhancing our capabilities to capitalize on the exponential growth in data center, demand driven by cloud and AI.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 240 bps YoY to 8.1%; PAT margin improved 110 bps YoY to 2.6%.
items.quote: For quarter one FY25, EBITDA margins increased to 8.1%, which is a growth of 240 basis points year -on-year compared to EBITDA margins of 5.7% in quarter one of FY24.

items.statement: Muted demand from federal partners in product business (~15% of revenue) and delayed project execution due to customer site readiness and macro uncertainty impacted Q1 revenue.
items.quote: The top line is affected due to our strategic exit from low -value, non -accretive customers coupled with some delay in decision-making leading to delayed project execution and with muted demand for our product business from some federal partners during the quarter.

items.statement: Strategic exit from low-value, long-tail customers (90% revenue from top 250-300 customers) to focus on high-value accounts; exercise to continue through FY25.
items.quote: We have made a strategic decision to exit low-value long-tail customers. Black Box is serving over a few thousand customers over the last many, many years. We have instituted a strategic program to assess our customer base. 90% of our business comes from top 250-odd customers who are large multinationals.

items.statement: Data center revenue was ~$175 million in FY24; Q1 FY25 estimated at $40-45 million. India and North America are the two focus geographies for hyper growth.
items.quote: number for this quarter? Deepak Bansal: We, this quarter it should be around $40 million or $45 million, but yes, we don't have the exact numbers but yes, it should be around $40 million , $45 million

items.statement: Organic growth target to reach $1.2-1.3 billion revenue in coming years; $2 billion target in 4 years includes inorganic acquisitions.
items.quote: We are expecting organically to take this business to $1.2 billion, $1.3 billion with a double-digit growth going forward for the next several years. And yes, we will be looking at, to be able to go to 2 billion, we will have to look at inorganic growth.

items.statement: H2 FY25 expected to be higher than H1 due to seasonality (budget utilization in India Jan-Mar and US calendar year-end).
items.quote: We expect that H2 to be higher than H1. There is an element of seasonality to an extent that there is a budget and a fiscal year norm. In India largely, the fiscal year ends in March. So, therefore, if you have an India-specific business, people want to utilize their budget in the Jan, Feb, March period.

items.statement: Technology Product Solutions (TPS) business breaks even at $20M revenue; targeting >20% growth in FY25 to be accretive at or above 9% EBITDA margin; shifting mix toward own IP-led products (Emerald brand) with R&D expansion in Bangalore.
items.quote: Our business technology products breaks even at about $20 million. So every dollar outside of that is highly accretive. As we move forward, we plan to grow the business in this current year over 20-odd percent. So if you look at the current fiscal year, it will be equal accretive or more from our 9% guidance perspective.

items.statement: No significant inorganic acquisitions in past year (only ~$4M); current focus is organic growth; inorganic is opportunity-based for $2B target.
items.quote: We haven't done any inorganic in the past year or so. So, barring a small $4 million or so that we did, this is largely organic. Going forward, as you said, in two parts, we expect our current focus is on organic growth.

items.statement: Project delays linked to Fed rate uncertainty; improvement expected once Fed cuts rates (anticipated by September).
items.quote: We are expecting that as soon as Fed starts reducing the interest rates, these environments will improve. And because the customers are also prudently going on with respect to spending, because if they go slow on the work, obviously, their spending a little bit gets slowed.

items.statement: Management reiterated guidance to retain high single-digit profitability margins in UCP segment
items.quote: whatever we have always been giving guidance that we will retain - the high single-digit profitability % which we have been ensuring all along. And our endeavour going forward also will be to retain that high single-digit profitability.

items.statement: Management maintained guidance of high single-digit profit margins for UCP segment
items.quote: We maintain our guidance or indication of overall single-digit -- high single-digit profitable margins -- profit margins. And that kind of remain.

items.statement: Company earmarked Rs 800-1,000 crores capex for factories
items.quote: Each, we have earmarked large sums of capex, almost Rs 800 crores to Rs 1,000 crores which we have earmarked for our factories.

items.statement: UCP segment EBIT margin was 8.6% in Q1 FY25 vs 9.2% in Q4 FY24, impacted by higher ad spend, subvention costs, and lower CAC/CR margins
items.quote: So partly, yes, because of Commercial AC and Commercial refrigeration, for sure. But in this first quarter, there is a heavy advertisement cost. We have to advertise a lot. IPL etc., is being happening around that time. Then because the sales are higher, therefore, also our subvention costs, for consumer financing, rebates are higher. So everything goes up relatively and therefore, I think that ha

items.statement: Projects segment typically delivers 4-5% margins; Q1 FY25 saw 7% due to no provisions and milestone accruals
items.quote: projects generally give us margin of between 4% and 5% only all along. So that's what we have been trying, that it should continue.

items.statement: Voltas Beko achieved over 50% volume growth YoY, reducing losses per unit and targeting EBITDA breakeven in near future
items.quote: Voltbek has delivered a volume growth of over 50% compared to corresponding period in the previous year. With regard s to the bottom line, with increased volume and gradual reduction in losses, Voltbek continues to reduce loss per units and move towards our goal of achieving EBITDA breakeven in near future

items.statement: Channel inventory at normal to below-normal levels after hand-to-mouth supply situation during peak summer demand
items.quote: Secondly, on the inventory front with the trade, it is not high because the channel and all the brands were struggling. And so were we also to cater to the demand, it was hand-to-mouth kind of a situation in the last 1 or 2 months because nobody could have planned a growth of 60%, 70%. So inventory is not much in the neither with the trade nor with the brands.

items.statement: Pre-sales growth guidance of 30% to 35% for FY25
items.quote: With a strong start to this financial year, we remain confident to achieve 30% to 35% growth in pre-sales for FY '25, as we had guided at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Pre-sales growth target of 30% to 35% year-on-year on continuous basis
items.quote: Riddhi, on a continuous basis, we are looking at 30% to 35% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Total GDV excluding pre-sales already done stood at Rs. 37,480 crores
items.quote: Our total GDV excluding pre-sales already done stood at Rs. 37,480 crores.

items.statement: Dubai project construction cost around Rs. 2,000 crores including approvals, sales and marketing
items.quote: And cost, obviously, the cost of the project is around Rs. 2,000 crores. And which should, most of it should come from the pre-sales.

items.statement: Dubai project potential of generating over Rs. 9,000 crores of sales with Rs. 250 crores investment for 50% profit share
items.quote: Our project in Dubai is likely to be launched in the next 12 to 15 months in FY '26. It has the potential of generating over Rs. 9,000 crores of sales, and our investment in the project is just around Rs. 250 crores for 50% of the profit share.

items.statement: Nepean Sea Road project potential of Rs. 2,500 crores gross development value
items.quote: The project has a potential of Rs. 2,500 crores of gross development value.

items.statement: Combined launches planned for FY25 with GDV value close to Rs. 5,000 crores
items.quote: The combined launches of the Sunteck for this year what we are planning is close to the GDV value of Rs. 5,000 crores

items.statement: Core EBITDA margin close to 50% adjusted for one-time charge, reported EBITDA margin close to 40%
items.quote: Adjusted for this, our core EBITDA margin is close to 50%, and reported EBITDA margin shall be close to 40%.

items.statement: BKC project momentum picked up significantly with Rs. 355 crores pre-sales in last 12 months vs Rs. 203 crores in previous three years
items.quote: So, if you see in BKC in the last 12 months, we have done a pre-sales of close to Rs. 355 crores, and this is against Rs. 203 crores that we did in previous three financial years all put together.

items.statement: Dubai project to be launched as single project in one go, not phase-wise
items.quote: Dubai, it's a one single land parcel, and you cannot have the phase-wise kind of a thing. So I think we will launch at a time, it's a one single project with maybe one tower or two towers.

items.statement: Nepean Sea Road launch expected in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: As far as launch timeline, I have already mentioned in my last quarter call that we should be looking to launch this in either Q4 of FY '25 or Q1 of FY '26.

items.statement: Balance cost to be spent on business development of existing projects is zero
items.quote: So, Puneet, the balance cost to be spent on our BD of our existing projects is zero, is nothing.

items.statement: Receivables from ongoing projects close to Rs. 2,300 crores to Rs. 2,400 crores
items.quote: The receivables from the ongoing projects is close to around Rs. 2,300 crores to Rs. 2,400 crores.

items.statement: Dubai project completion timeline of three to four years
items.quote: So, time to complete should be three to four years.

items.statement: Operating cash flow surplus growth expected to be stronger in FY25 with two big project completions and higher pre-sales
items.quote: With the higher sales in BKC, two big project completion in FY '25, and higher pre-sales, I am confident Sunteck will deliver a stronger operating cash flow surplus growth in FY '25.

items.statement: Gross debt down over 60% since FY22, currently at 0.09x of equity and less than one quarter cash collection
items.quote: Gross debt is down over 60% since FY '22, today at 0.09x of the equity and it is less than one quarter cash collection.

items.statement: Target INR 3,000 crores revenue within next two years
items.quote: Our next goal is to reach INR 3,000 crores of revenue within the next two years, our focus on growing the business, launching new products, and enhancing supplies from our new facility will be instrumental in achieving this target.

items.statement: Capex incurred in Q1 FY25 was INR 31 crores
items.quote: The capex incurred during the period was INR31 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 432 bps YoY and 386 bps QoQ to 55.7% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter expanded by 432 basis points year-on-year and 386 basis points quarter-on-quarter, primarily due to the reduced raw material pricing and the depletion of old high-cost inventory.

items.statement: Additional freight cost of INR 12 crores YoY due to Red Sea crisis; freight costs creeping up again
items.quote: Niharika, we incurred an additional freight of INR12 crores if you see the year-on-year freight number. So, we incurred INR12 crores extra in freight.

items.statement: Mixed demand in U.S. this quarter; anticipate upcoming quarters to be far better based on historical trends
items.quote: This quarter, we faced a mixed demand scenario in the U.S. region. However, based on historical trends, we anticipate the upcoming quarters to be far better.

items.statement: Favorable product mix boosted margins in Q1 FY25
items.quote: A favorable product mix also boosted our margins.

items.statement: Elevated freight costs due to Red Sea crisis, container shortages, and port congestions continue
items.quote: However, we continue to face elevated freight costs, mainly due to the ongoing Red Sea crisis, container shortages, and port congestions.

items.statement: Goa facility current sales INR 750-800 crores; Teva plant expected to overtake it
items.quote: It is in the range of INR750 crores to INR800 crores.

items.statement: U.K. growth expected at 10-12% going forward due to larger base
items.quote: But we will see a 10% to 12% growth happening from here. And our team is working hard to supply shares and move ahead of that. But realistically, I think pretty much what you have said is what we believe will continue moving forward.

items.statement: Exploring M&A in Europe for market authorizations and geographic spread; not seeking manufacturing facilities
items.quote: We would like a company with more market authorization and more time in Europe spread. And we would like to leverage low-cost manufacturing based out of India.

items.statement: Signed one DMF for API in-housing; working on second DMF
items.quote: So, we have signed, you know, one DMF, and we are working on setting another one right now.

items.statement: U.S. market to lead growth to INR 3,000 crores; U.K. to bridge the gap
items.quote: Obviously, the immediate growth of the fastest-growing market will be the U.S. market. We see the growth drivers in the U.S. market. But that said and done, the U.K. market will also add value to this growth. But in absolute numbers and comparison, it will be the U.S. market that will take us faster and closer to the INR3,000 crores, with the U.K. market bridging the gap to hit that number.

items.statement: Production guidance of around 50 million tons for FY25 maintained despite 1 million ton shortfall in Q1
items.quote: Number two, of course, we still keep a guidance of around 50 million tons. I know we are running about 1 million tons plus on shortfall as compared to last year because of 2 reasons.
