items.statement: Targeting order inflow of INR6,000 crores to INR8,000 crores by end of FY25.
items.quote: we are targeting an order inflow of around INR6,000 crores to INR8,000 crores by the end of FY '25.

items.statement: Capex of INR10 crores in Q1 FY25; full-year FY25 capex expected around INR80-100 crores.
items.quote: First quarter, we did capex of INR10 crores. And this year, because as our ED sir is telling that we are trying to get new projects definitely based on them and which quarter we are getting to the project. Based on that capex requirement may change, but if we go in a normalize way, there will be somewhere around INR80 crores-INR100 crores addition will be there in this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 15-16% for FY25/FY26 assuming normal input prices, including irrigation and BOT EPC projects.
items.quote: If the all input prices are normal, definitely, we are going to deliver around 16% to 15% kind of level.

items.statement: Expect new order awarding to pick up post-elections with strong budgetary allocation; MoRTH plans to award INR3 lakh crores in next 3 months targeting INR5 lakh crores for FY25.
items.quote: Now with this election behind us and the strong focus on roads and highway development as indicated through budgetary allocation towards the sector, we expect new order awarding to be picked up, and we are targeting an order inflow of around INR6,000 crores to INR8,000 crores by the end of FY '25.

items.statement: Actively pursuing BOT toll EPC (26-27% equity), MSRDC subcontracting (~INR2,000 crores), irrigation (Telangana, MP, AP, Jal Shakti), metro (NCC JV), mining, railways, and mass earthwork contracts.
items.quote: Further, we are also very keen in working on some Maharashtra MSRDC projects we're also working. That means I'm not straight away qualified into it because we couldn't finish our express highway projects timely. I mean to say The time the tender is quoted. That time, our projects are not ready. So we could not qualify on that. So we are starting some sort of back-to-back arrangement with Patel Inf

items.statement: Telangana irrigation receivables of INR900 crores (INR600 crores certified, INR300 crores unbilled); government targeting payment by September end; court case filed for delayed payments.
items.quote: As of date actually Telangana has certified receivables of INR600 crores, but with unbilled it will be around INR900 crores as of date. Receivables are pending from the Telangana.

items.statement: Two HAM projects (Mysore-Kushalnagara, ~INR1,200 crores) await appointed date pending environmental clearance; EC meeting expected 20th/22nd, appointed date likely mid-September to October.
items.quote: Actually, Mysore project is pending for the EC that environmental clearance. So I think the tribunal meeting is going to happen or the board meeting for the EC is going to happen in 20th or the 22nd, I'm not very sure about it the date and all, but approximately around that there is a meeting for them. And once that is through with that, I think circulation of minutes would take another 15 days th

items.statement: Revenue growth uncertain for FY25; Q2 disappointing due to rains, targeting to match FY24 revenue if new orders execute in Q3/Q4; FY26 expected better if INR6,000-7,000 crores orders secured.
items.quote: So if I'm able to execute all these, then definitely, we will try to touch the last year results. I'm not very sure about growth on the revenue side this time. But however, we try our best in getting those things in order.

items.statement: Equity infusion of INR335 crores, INR72 crores, INR67 crores in 9 months of FY25, FY26, FY27 respectively for eight HAM projects (balance INR474 crores of revised INR992 crores equity).
items.quote: Out of balance, equity requirement of INR474 crores for these eight HAM projects, INR335 crores, INR72 crores and INR67 crores will be infused in 9 months of FY '25, '26 and '27, respectively.

items.statement: Monetization of 4 HAM assets: Palani in FY25, Kerala 2 and Chittoor-Thatchur by September 2025; bulk deal with one investor under discussion.
items.quote: So if we monetize the project then whatever the debt is there, it is taken there by the investor. So that is one thing that we are trying to do it. And this year, actually, because one project that is KNR Palani we already got the PCOD. So we expect that monetization will definitely happen in this year. And the other three assets, monetization is in discussion and we expect that this Kerala 2 and

items.statement: BOT toll projects have no escalation; bidding assumes 5-6% annual cost escalation; margins targeted at 15-16% if input prices normal.
items.quote: So what happens once there is no escalation factor we put around every year overall 5% growth on every year we take it. So on average around 5% to 6% we will take towards the entire contract size if you take it, that's going to be around 5% to 6% we would try to be putting it.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR1,532 crores (June 30, 2024) vs INR1,220 crores (March 31, 2024); net debt/equity 0.41x vs 0.36x; standalone cash INR33 crores, consolidated cash INR70 crores.
items.quote: The consolidated debt as of June 30, 2024 is INR1,532 crores as compared to the INR1,220 crores as of March 31, 2024. The net debt to equity on consolidated basis as of June 30, 2024 has stood at 0.41x as compared to 0.36x as of March 31, 2024.

items.statement: Vivad Se Vishwas claims: Odisha projects INR25 crores admitted, INR70 crores agreed (50% expected post-VSV); AP-07 claim ~INR200 crores pending VSV/EC.
items.quote: I think the claim is around INR200 crores plus, sir. So after VSV calculation we have to see how much it will get.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh targeting INR1,000-2,000 crores orders (1-2 projects); contracts grouped above INR800 crores; hybrid/HAM model suggested over VGF.
items.quote: So actually, my target is about, say, INR1,000 crores to INR2,000 crores only. Lower side, I'm keeping it around INR1,200 crores, I'm keeping it. Only 1 project or 2 projects because I cannot get more on that as you know that.

items.statement: Irrigation revenue target INR200-250 crores for FY25; high-end engineering projects ~60-70% of order book.
items.quote: For the year, maybe around INR200 crores to INR250 crores will be for entire year.

items.statement: EPC revenue to cross Rs 1,000 Crores in FY25, grow 25% YoY to Rs 1,250 Crores in FY26 and Rs 1,500 Crores in FY27; EPC PBT to stretch to 9% in FY25 and 10% in next 2 years
items.quote: EPC will do -- will cross the Rs 1,000 Crores mark this year. Again, it's a guidance, I mean fingers crossed we are on track to do that. We want to do that. And going forward, we want to ensure that EPC grows at least 25% year-on-year, so Rs 1,250 Crores next year, upwards of Rs 1,500 Crores a year after that.

items.statement: Real estate revenue recognition of Rs 125 Crores expected in FY25 from project completions
items.quote: But -- once again, it depends upon the -- how the approval and that the completion gets done irrespective of our execution capabilities, there are -- government also that appropriate authority also have to give the completion certificate. So all the live -- not only execution to liasoning and everything. But still, we expect around Rs 125 Crores kind of revenue to be booked -- likely be booked in

items.statement: EPC order book at Rs 3,482 Crores (4.9x FY24 EPC revenue); 82% government projects; Rs 2,979 Crores external, Rs 503 Crores internal
items.quote: Looking ahead, our outlook for the EPC segment remained robust, backed by a strong order book of Rs 3,482 Crores, which is 4.9x the FY '24 EPC revenue, which reflects a strong foundation for growth and execution. Of this, the order book was Rs 2,979 Crores are attributed to external EPC orders, while the remaining Rs 503 Crores are internal projects. About 82% of these orders are from government p

items.statement: New order intake of Rs 331.38 Crores for medical college from PWD Sindhudurg in FY25 YTD; target Rs 1,000 Crores more by March 2025
items.quote: In terms of order intake, the company has received new orders from PWD Sindhudurg for the construction of a medical college worth Rs 331.38 Crores in this year FY '25 till date. Our bank guarantee limits have increased in the last fiscal and led by our strong balance sheet and financials. And with this, we are looking forward to continuing growth in the EPC division.

items.statement: EPC gross margin target 14-15%; EBITDA margin 10-11%; PBT 8-9% currently, targeting 9-10% in next 2 years
items.quote: I will reiterate that all our gross profit of it, on an average in EPC will be in the range of 14%, 14% - 15%. And this will not translate to 13% - 14% EBITDA, it would translate to about 7-12. And we expect -- our PBT in EPC currently is at around 8, stretching towards 9. And our focus is to get the EPC PBT towards between 9 and 10 in the next year.

items.statement: Real estate gross margin 28-30% on Rs 1,700 Crores unrecognized revenue; PBT 15-18% at scale
items.quote: And in terms of profitability, at gross profit level, our EPC book exactly double the expectation of profit from our -- sorry, our real estate book looks exactly double of our EPC books in terms of gross profits in the range of 28% to 30%. And with scal e that will translate to easily 15%, 18% PBT levels

items.statement: Sindhudurg medical college project gross margin 13-14% (1% below target); design-build model expected to recover to 15%
items.quote: See, we've taken -- as of now, the gross profit margins on this project will be in the range of 13% to 14%. And the time line, typica lly, we've seen that it takes at least 6 months because these are all design and build projects and certain approvals are also pending at site, even the government takes time to get their approval

items.statement: Government infrastructure allocation Rs 11.11 Lakh Crores (11% increase, 3.4% of GDP) driving EPC demand; construction industry 6% CAGR to Rs 1.39 trillion by 2033
items.quote: Let me take you through some of the key industrial updates in the recent union budget, which outlines a robust framework for infrastructure industry in India, which is focusing on significant capital investments and strategic initi atives aimed at fostering growth and sustainability that the government of India has allocated Rs 11.11 Lakh Crores for infrastructure development, marking an 11% incre

items.statement: Two real estate launches (Powai, OHM Sainath Santacruz) expected in Q3 FY25; three more in FY26 (Prakash, Baner-Pashan, Ajanta Kharadi); one per quarter over 5 quarters
items.quote: So the first launch that we expect to happen would be both Powai and The Prakash -- sorry, the OHM Sainath Housing Society at Santacruz. Both of these are in advanced stage of approval. So we expect before December, we do hope to launch in this Q3, we do hope to launch both these projects. And then the Prakash will be launched mostly post April or in the next financial year.

items.statement: GMP divestment to Shinryo for Rs 155-157 Crores; net cash flow Rs 100-110 Crores expected by end of month; QIP approved, Rs 100 Crores for 3 Mumbai projects, 6-8 months to complete
items.quote: During the fiscal year 2025, the company's Board of Directors has considered and approved a proposal for divestment of its 100% equity stake, which is an 85% holding in GMP Technical Solutions to Shinryo Corporation, a Japane se firm for an aggregate consideration in the range of Rs 155 Crores to Rs 157 Crores. As against the company's share of the Rs 155 Crores to Rs 157 Crores post tax and other

items.statement: Rs 170 Crores capital needed for 3 Mumbai projects (Rs 70 Crores already infused, Rs 100 Crores from QIP); additional investment for Thane 25-acre parcel aggregation and EPC collateral
items.quote: These three projects, which is almost at a defined level of approval, it is almost Rs 170 Crores kind of capital infusion is required. Out of which Rs 70 Crores we have infused earlier and Rs 100 Crores supposed to be integrated from QIP. And that QIP specifically for these three projects and apart from that, what is the sale of GMP that is meant for the -- you need some kind of capital infusion i

items.statement: Government project advances mostly interest-bearing; Rs 60 Crores outstanding mobilization advances; labor shortage mitigated by design-build focus (15-20% labor efficiency gain)
items.quote: So most government projects today have interest -bearing advances. Some private projects do offer zero interest advance against bank guarantee. Every now and then, some government project also offers zero interest, but by and large government p rojects are expecting or offering advantage with interest only

items.statement: Political risk mitigated by avoiding projects in election-bound states 12-18 months prior; focus on hospital projects in non-metro locations less prone to political interference
items.quote: Point number one, you will notice we are taking a lot of hospital projects which are not in a prime location in terms of a big city. What happens is these projects are generally not in the radar of politicians. The fund is allocated by the departments in their health care projects, there is very little risk of them being stalled or cancelled if there is any political change in the state.

items.statement: Net debt risen to Rs 38 Crores due to real estate JV investments; CRISIL BBB+/A2 stable rating; short-term bridge debt of ~Rs 40 Crores for project launches
items.quote: The status of debt. This fiscal year, we have seen our total debt go up because we are involved in new real estate joint ventures. As a result, our net debt has risen to Rs 38 Crores over the past last year. Even with this increase, we are committed to capital financial management and are focused on sustainable growth and creating value.

items.statement: GMP Q1 FY25 revenue Rs 79 Crores (42% YoY), gross margin 26%, EBITDA Rs 4 Crores (6% margin)
items.quote: GMP continues to deliver improved performance during the quarter. Revenue of Rs 79 Crores in Q1 FY '25, which is up 42% year-on-year and a healthy gross margin of 26%. The EBITDA was Rs 4 Crores with a 6% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Real estate Q1 FY25 sales booking 12,244 sq ft, Rs 7 Crores sale value, Rs 11 Crores collections
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, we achieved new sales booking totalling 12,244 Square Feet, generating a sale value of Rs 7 Crores and a total collection of Rs 11 Crores.

items.statement: TEU volumes grew 13% quarter-on-quarter and close to 80% year-on-year in Q1 FY25, reaching around 17,186 TEUs.
items.quote: If you look at the TEU numbers, the volumes have been seeing a steady growth in past quarters and if you look at the Q2 of FY24, so we've we started at 12,460 and now we've been consistently growing and now in the Q1 FY25, the numbers are close to around 17,186.

items.statement: Air freight volumes grew 60% quarter-on-quarter in Q1 FY25, supported by IATA accreditation received last year.
items.quote: Even on the air freight sector, we are seeing some good growth as you all are aware that we got IATA accreditation last year and that has helped us in growing our air freight volume also.

items.statement: Revenue was ₹102.8 crores in Q1 FY25, up 9.1% quarter-on-quarter and 2.4 times year-on-year.
items.quote: I think the overall top line has improved quite a lot in this quarter. we closed at ₹102.8 crores overall and which we've seen a 9.1% increase on quarter to quarter and almost 2.4 times increase year on year.

items.statement: EBITDA increased 10.6% quarter-on-quarter and nearly doubled year-on-year in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has also increased on quarter-to-quarter basis. EBITDA has increased by 10.6% and almost two times what it was year on year.

items.statement: Management expects growth to continue in the current and coming quarters due to a good pipeline and tailwinds.
items.quote: Overall, we feel that's the reason even the PAT margins have been better. So overall, we are seeing that the company has done well in last quarter and this growth is going to continue in this quarter and coming quarter as well because the pipeline is good.

items.statement: Management does not see major challenges in coming quarters and is focused on strengthening position beyond automobiles into electronics, solar, ceramics, and commodities.
items.quote: We are not seeing any major challenges in coming quarters. We don't see any major issues in the coming days and we are only looking at strengthening our position in the Indian logistics industry where we are seeing that other than automobiles, we are also focusing on other sectors like imports of electronic goods, imports of solar equipment's and working closely in the solar industry and also in t

items.statement: Cash reserves are being deployed for LCL acquisition targets mandated to consultancies over the last 1.5 years to fuel inorganic growth, with potential working capital needs as business grows.
items.quote: So, we are looking at some acquisition options that we've already mandated this to few companies, few consultancies where we are looking at LCL acquisition which we've been working on for last one and a half year which will fuel our inorganic growth.

items.statement: Management does not rely on disruptions like the Red Sea crisis or container shortages for growth, preferring a stable environment and long-term client acquisition in growing Indian sectors.
items.quote: We are not looking at any disruption to fuel our growth very, very clear. We are not because that all those disruptions are temporary. So, we are not looking at any disruption to help us grow. We want a stable environment because that is the long sustaining way of working.

items.statement: Freight Jar 2.0 is gaining customer traction, particularly in electronics, renewable energy, and solar sectors, serving as an entry vertical for new client acquisition.
items.quote: So, Freigsht Jar 2.0 has already been implemented where we are seeing a good traction of customers, which is happening. So that is going to continue with us because Freight Jar, the parent company is Tiger Logistics only.

items.statement: Automobile sector remains the main vertical with strong growth in 2-wheeler auto exports; focus continues on deep-selling existing clients and acquiring new ones.
items.quote: So, what has happened is that we are working very closely with developing and deep selling with our present customers, but are also looking at acquiring new customers, which is a regular process. So, the overall business, I would say has improved for auto sector also, where the auto exports is doing very well especially in the 2-Wheeler Auto sector market.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin is improving each quarter through cost and buying improvements; no specific target provided.
items.quote: Sustainable EBITDA Margin, I would say we are improving each quarter and that is the whole idea. We are working towards it trying to improve our cost overall and trying to improve our buying's overall so that is how it works.

items.statement: No major structural changes seen in the ocean freight industry; disruptions create unhealthy competition and contract dishonoring, which are not welcomed.
items.quote: No, we are not. See, of course those they made huge money after COVID. Then you know the rate drops below the COVID level pre COVID levels. They went down below that also. So, we are not seeing any major structural changes in our industry.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 8,032 million as of 30 June 2024, up from Rs 8,001 million as of 31 March 2024, further strengthened by recent Dow Chemical order
items.quote: As of 30 June, our order book stood at 8,032 million, up from 8,001 million as of 31 March 2024, while the recent order of US$40.71 million from Dow Chemical has further strengthened our order book.

items.statement: Secured $40.71 million order from Dow Chemicals Canada ULC for pipe spool fabrication, execution between September 2024 and December 2026, job-work value only
items.quote: We are extremely excited to announce that we have just last week secured a significant order valued at $40.71 million USD from Dow Chemicals Canada ULC for pipe spool fabrication.

items.statement: Anjar facility commercial production started with 3,000 MT capacity, additional 9,000 MT rolling out from 1 October 2024, targeting total 30,000 MT capacity at this facility
items.quote: So, Maheshji as we have already started our commercial production with introduction of 3,000 metric tons of capacity at New Anjar facility and with effect from 1st October, we shall be rolling out another 9,000 metric tons of capacity.

items.statement: Total capacity to increase from 6,000 MT to 15,000 MT at Anjar, bringing total company capacity to 112,500 MT, facility near Kandla Port to reduce logistics costs
items.quote: We are establishing the new Anjar facility which will boost our capacity from 6,000 metric tons to 15,000 metric tons, bringing the total capacity to 112,500 metric tons.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin expanded 445 bps YoY to 13.4% in Q1 FY25, PAT margin expanded 456 bps YoY to 1.7%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA in Q1 FY '25 saw a robust year-on-year increase of 76.1%, reaching 248 million , with an operating EBITDA margin expansion of 445 basis points to 13.4%.

items.statement: Anjar facility expected to improve margins through logistics savings, automation efficiency, and fixed cost absorption, visible from Q3-Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, these all three things will add to our margin profile, and it will be properly seen once we come down to third and fourth quarter.

items.statement: Full-year revenue, margin and order inflow guidance to be provided in about a month after Anjar capacity ramp-up and customer approvals
items.quote: So, in a month's time, we will make sure to give you a good guidance in this respect

items.statement: Expect strong top-line and bottom-line growth in near-medium term driven by strong order book outlook and customer capex cycles
items.quote: With a strong order book outlook, coupled with our strategy to capitalize on the increasing capex by our customer segments, we expect strong top-line as well as bottom-line growth in near-medium term.

items.statement: Power sector orders expected earlier than planned, possibly in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26, driven by government's 80 GW thermal energy announcement
items.quote: Now, we are expecting it to get those orders much earlier maybe in the last quarter of this fiscal or maybe the first quarter of the next fiscal.

items.statement: Heavy fabrication division revenue grew 295.2% YoY to 7.4% of sales, piping division grew 13.2% YoY to 81.3% of revenue
items.quote: Revenue from piping division saw a 13.2% year -over-year growth, contributing 81.3% over revenue, whereas heavy fabrication division saw a year -on-year growth of 295.2% with sales contribution of 7.4% of the growth.

items.statement: Export orders on FOB basis insulate from freight cost increases; import logistics cost impact not substantial
items.quote: So, as far as our orders are concerned, our orders are FOB basis. So, the impact of the cost increase in terms of freight cost does not come to us

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs 3,250 million: Rs 935.32 million utilized so far (Rs 179.82 million working capital, Rs 755.50 million debt repayment); Rs 175 crore debt repaid before 10 July 2024
items.quote: Of the total IPO proceeds of 3,250 million, we have already utilized 935.32 million so far, towards 179.82 million towards working capital needs and 755.50 million towards repayment of debts.

items.statement: New pilot plant vertical launched for design, engineering, fabrication and manufacturing of pre-commercial production systems
items.quote: As part of our growth strategy, the company has recently ventured into a new business vertical focused on design, engineering, fabrication, and manufacturing of pilot plants.

items.statement: Many large orders in advanced negotiation stage, expecting good inflow every month; Dow order first from this customer but more expected
items.quote: Many more orders are in the queue. Of course, they may not be as large as this particular order, but there are many large orders in the queue as yet.

items.statement: Fully qualified for supercritical power plants with BHEL and NTPC; nuclear approved by NPCIL but focusing on overseas nuclear opportunities
items.quote: We are qualified with BHL. We are qualified with NTPC. We are qualified as any other player in the Indian power sector market, who shall be putting up these supercritical power plants.

items.statement: Revenue potential from existing capacities guided at Rs. 1,600-1,800 crores in next couple of years, subject to raw material prices
items.quote: we had guided to around Rs. 1,600 crores to Rs. 1,800 crores of sales. The only caveat there is the raw material prices, because whatever we are trying to give you as numbers is based on an assumption of the raw material prices.

items.statement: Pastry line expansion planned with two more lines in immediate future, costing Rs. 3-4 crores
items.quote: We are just planning to add a couple of those lines, because that's a business that we see a lot of potential in, and there are not many competitors in India or globally. So, that's something that we are trying to expand. That should not be more than Rs. 3 crores or Rs. 4 crores

items.statement: Blended realization for Q1 FY25 at Rs. 88/kg vs Rs. 105/kg in Q1 FY24 due to lower raw material price inventory and product mix changes
items.quote: the average realization for this quarter was around Rs. 88 kg. All put together, the export and domestic put together. But I am sure you will not get much of a sense with respect to this, because our product mix keeps on changing.

items.statement: Totapuri raw material prices almost double FY24 levels, Alphonso slightly cheaper than FY24
items.quote: Totapuri raw material prices were almost double of what we procured in FY'24 and Alphonso was slightly cheaper than what we actually procured in FY'24.

items.statement: Export shipments deferred due to container unavailability and high freight costs; vessels skipping India for China due to higher freight rates
items.quote: since 15th of June onwards, we are having a serious issue in India on the shipment, because most of the vessels are skipping India and going to China because of much, much lucrative freight rate.

items.statement: Domestic volume growth only 5-6% vs targeted 20% due to brand facility breakdown and local brand dispatch deferrals
items.quote: we have landed around 5%, 6% growth in the domestic market. The reason behind that, in the month of, I mean, from June second week onwards, whatever target volume have been given to us by the brands where we supply the major volume, we can see a downfall in the volume.

items.statement: Tetra Recart traction slower than expected; concrete numbers expected by end of FY25
items.quote: With respect to what numbers, we can actually guide you with, for Tetra Recart, we would request you to give us time till the end of FY'25 to give you concrete numbers on the same.

items.statement: Pectin project trial runs completed; commercial production starting late August 2024; revenue generation expected early 2025 after brand audits
items.quote: in our pectin project, our main raw material is dried peel. So, during mango season, we have already dried whatever peel wastage was there. Now it will be converted into pectin. So, I think around fourth week, 26th of August or maybe 22nd or 23rd of August, the process will start to produce pectin.

items.statement: Exploring new geographies for tomato including Russia, Sri Lanka, UK, Spain; working on seed varieties to improve lycopene and color values for export competitiveness
items.quote: Russia is one of the markets that we are actually exploring. Sri Lanka is another market that we are exploring. The UK is another market that we are actually exploring for tomatoes. In FY'23, we even sold to Spain.

items.statement: Expect revenue CAGR of around 20% over next three years driven by ATBS, antioxidants and VOPL products
items.quote: We expect our revenue to have a CAGR of around 20% over the next three years, which will be mainly driven by ATBS, antioxidants, and other products from VOPL.

items.statement: Overall capex for FY25 approximately INR570 crores including VOPL and ATBS expansion
items.quote: The overall capex to be spent in FY '25 would be approximately INR570 crores. This includes VOPL.

items.statement: VOPL capex plan exceeding INR500 crores for MEHQ, Guaiacol, anisole, 4-meth and other Iso Amylene derivatives
items.quote: VOPL has outlined a capital expenditure plan exceeding INR500 crores, focusing on production of MEHQ, Guaiacol, anisole, 4-meth, and other Iso Amylene derivatives.

items.statement: ATBS expansion and remaining VOPL products scheduled for commissioning in second half of FY25
items.quote: Additionally, the remaining products under capex are scheduled for commissioning in the second half of FY '25. This period will also see the completion of the ATBS expansion, furthering our VOL's ATBS production capabilities.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margins expected at 26% to 27% on sustainable basis from Q2 onwards
items.quote: I think one can expect normalized EBITDA margins of 26% to 27% on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Prices presently stabilized, raw material price changes passed through contracts
items.quote: Prices are presently stabilized. It's not, there is not much of a moment as such, because anyway, we have our, you know, contracts in place. So whatever price change that happens in terms of the raw materials, that is passed on.

items.statement: ATBS demand exceeds supply, sold out with high-grade ATBS demand restricting production capacity
items.quote: See, in ATBS right now, the demand exceeds the supply. Because the demand, which is there, it's for a very, very high grade ATBS quality, which restricts our production capacity.

items.statement: Antioxidant capacity utilization expected to reach closer to 50% in FY25
items.quote: Secondly as far as 50% capacity utilization, yes, for FY25 I think we should be coming closer to that one year.

items.statement: MEHQ plant capacity on stream, commercial samples sent, some commercial sales done, plant not fully stabilized
items.quote: Capacity is on stream. Vinati Saraf Mutreja: Yes. We have send some commercial samples. Kaviraj Devaraj: Yes. Sampling work is going on along with that. Some commercial sales have also happened. But we are also working on improving the efficiency and yield of the plant. Vinati Saraf Mutreja: It's not completely stabilized

items.statement: On track for 20% CAGR revenue guidance over three years, Q1 year-on-year growth strong
items.quote: Yes, I think we are on track for that one. We have basically guided for a 20% CAGR over a period of three years. Vinati Mutreja: And even this quarter year-on-year

items.statement: Antioxidant business picking up, India showing good growth, ATBS strong based on present scenario
items.quote: And overall, it is robust. It's picking up. In fact, India has shown good growth in the last 3 years or so. While it has been slow in the last 2 years, we expect there to be some recovery on that end, and hence we expect the AO business to pick up. ATBS, yes, was in oil recovery. And just based on the present scenario, it is looking strong.

items.statement: IBB business remains steady with no significant volume or price improvement
items.quote: IBB remains just as is, to be honest.

items.statement: Electricity costs up ~10% per unit, coal prices risen, renewables cover 40-50% of energy needs
items.quote: One is the electricity cost itself has gone up because there is a raise in prices that has happened in electricity. So that's almost like a 10% kind of a raise that has happened on a unit basis. Secondly, there is also some rise in coal prices which is there, which is seen and that's essentially why the… Vinati Mutreja: So the renewable add only to 40%, 50% or… Kaviraj Devaraj: Yes, roughly around

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY25 remains north of 15% growth
items.quote: Our revenue guidance for the year though still remains at north of 15%.

items.quote: In our CAPEX outlay for the next 2 years, all of it will get committed in this financial year, but some will get spend this year and some in the year after. But we expect to spend about Rs. 30 odd crore in capacity expansion and brand b uilding. We are expecting to spend ~Rs. 5 odd crore in expanding area under cultivation. I mentioned already about Rs. 45 crore - Rs. 50 crore in building the hosp

items.statement: Winery capacity expanding 25% to 5.6 million liters by end of FY25, commercialization by December 2024
items.quote: Our existing capacity at the moment is roughly 4.5 million liters. This year we are looking to expand that by approximately 25% and that will be north of 5.6 million liters by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Premium and Luxury segments contribute 73% of revenue in FY24, up from 70% in FY21
items.quote: If you look at our numbers for FY21, we had 70% contribution from the premium and super premium segments, and this has risen to 73% in FY24 on an expanded operating base.

items.statement: Wine industry expected to grow ~15% CAGR, Fratelli grew ~25% CAGR over last 3 years
items.quote: The wine industry, as per all industry data available to us is expected to grow at about 15%. We have grown about 25% CAGR over the last 3 years.

items.statement: Added 150 acres of vineyard 200km away to derisk agro-climate exposure
items.quote: We have recently taken a new parcel of 150 acres of land under active farming which is approximately 200 kilometers away from our winery. Now, what that does is that it slightly derisks us from an agro-climate risk perspective.

items.statement: Current debt Rs 90 crore (Rs 15 crore long-term), may add Rs 10-15 crore long-term debt for capex
items.quote: At this point of time, we have roughly Rs. 90 crore of debt in our balance sheet. About Rs. 15 crore is long term debt, and the balance is working capital. We may take an additional Rs. 10 crore - Rs. 15 crore of long-term debt going forward to complete all the CAPEX that we have planned over this year and the next year.

items.statement: S&D spend at 28-30% of revenue for last 3-4 years, working to reduce it
items.quote: Basically we are at below 30% in the S&D trends and basically if you see from last 3-4 financial years, we are between 28% and 30%. Kavita: Any outlook for the future, sir? Hemant Arora: We continue to do efforts regarding the reduction of S&D spend and we will follow the same and employ different strategies to reduce our S&D

items.statement: Can segment gross margins slightly better than bottles due to lower packaging cost
items.value: a couple of percentage points better
items.quote: On a gross margin level, it is fairly consistent with bottles as well, slightly better. You can say a couple of percentage points due to the lower packaging cost which is there in Cans.

items.statement: HoReCa channel split 25% of revenue, growing from retail-heavy 75-25 mix
items.quote: Currently as of last year, the split is roughly 75-25 with 75% coming from retail and 25% coming from HoReCa.

items.statement: Trading business revenue ~Rs 100 crore in Q1 FY25, will reduce dramatically in Q2 and shut down in Q3
items.quote: While in Q1, the trading business of the listed entity contributed approximately Rs. 100 crore in reve nue, t his will reduce dramatically in Q2 and will completely shut down in Q3

items.statement: Kolkata plant for pulses and grains to be commissioned in February 2025
items.quote: we plan to commercialize our new plant in Kolkata, dedicated to pulses and grains. Within, I think, it will be commissioned in the month of Feb 25.

items.statement: Surat plant land acquired, commissioning expected next financial year
items.quote: Additionally, we are also trying to launch a new plant in Surat, for which we have already acquired land and it will be commissioned in the next financial year.

items.statement: Edible oil refining operating margin targeted at 2% to 2.5% on processing only
items.quote: our operating margin will be around 2% to 2.5%. We will be just trying to have that on processing thing only.

items.statement: Processing margins expected to increase profit by 1.5% to 2% of revenue once plants operational
items.quote: we think our profit may increase like 1.5%, 2% of the revenue. It may increase.

items.statement: Shift from exports to domestic market focus; exports were 22% of revenue in Q1 FY24
items.quote: reducing our Reliance on exports, which accounted for approximately 22% of our revenue in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Domestic demand for food grains and pulses increasing enormously
items.quote: our domestic demands have increased very much enormously. You can say like, yes, our domestic demands have increased very much.

items.statement: Government not encouraging agri-commodity exports; focusing on ethanol production from grains
items.quote: government is not encouraging the exports of agri-commodities. They are rather planning to convert the additional grain into ethanol so that they can save on foreign exchange on import of crude oil and all.

items.statement: Kolkata plant capacity 100,000 tons per year Masoor; edible oil capacity 50,000 tons per year
items.value: 100,000 tons per year of Masoor. And around, edible is around 50,000 tons per year
items.quote: Like we are already trying to install, we are installing 100,000 tons per year of Masoor. And around, edible is around 50,000 tons per year.

items.statement: Surat plant to process lentils, channa, and matar for domestic wholesale and retail
items.quote: We are putting for pulses. Like we can process three types of pulses in that unit. One is lentils. One is channa. And the third one will be matar.

items.statement: Plan to establish brand and expand retail presence over next two to three years
items.quote: once this plant is commissioned, our focus will also be there to establish our brand. So, we are going to register our brand and we will start marketing.

items.statement: Will continue export business if government provides quotas; not exiting sugar/rice exports
items.quote: We are not going to shut down our old business. We are not going to go away from that business because that is already there. That is already established. So, we are not going to switch off anything which we are having. Rather, we will be waiting for the opportunities.

items.statement: Future plan to add one more processing unit at Bombay after current two plants
items.quote: We plan to increase our processing units. One, after this two commissioning, we'll be planning to have one more unit at Bombay.

items.statement: Management will stay with previous guidance; Q1 on track and confident of market tailwinds to cover any minor deficit
items.quote: I think we will stay with the guidance we provided last time. There is nothing that requires a review at this stage.

items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA margin is a two-year journey, not expected in FY25 due to ahead-of-curve investments in brands, people and marketing
items.quote: No, I think the guidance I have been presenting, the double digit is about a two-year journey. And so, it was not for this year.

items.statement: Chennai AAC block plant commissioning in H2 FY25 adding 2 lakh tons in first wave with capacity for another 2 lakh tons; targeting India's largest single-location plant
items.quote: The Chennai plant that will get commissione d in the second half of this year, we are adding 2 lakh tons in the first wave of that expansion, and we have capacity for another 2 lakh tons after that, which can be quickly switched

items.statement: Pipes & Fittings capacity expansion on drawing board to reach Rs 1,500 crore revenue milestone; current capacity sufficient for Rs 800-1,000 crore
items.quote: We are already on the drawing board to plan for those capacity expansion. So, yes, getting to our final eventual goal, we will need to invest more on capacity.

items.statement: Parador order bookings remain strong; third straight quarter of positive momentum on billings and order bookings
items.quote: Despite ongoing market sluggishness, Parador's order bookings remain strong. We have also introduced several new products ac ross categories to capture a larger market share

items.statement: Contribution margins improved across most segments despite price realization drops: Blocks +220 bps, Boards +170 bps, Putty +90 bps, Construction Chemicals +1,000+ bps, Parador +370 bps YoY
items.quote: In Blocks, we improved our contribution margin by 220 basis points, in Boards by 170 basis points, in Putty by 90 basis points, in Construction Chemicals by over 1,000 basis points. And at Parador, the contribution margin improved by 370 basis points.

items.statement: Price realizations fell across categories: Pipes & Fittings -12%, Putty -6%, Parador -5.7%, Blocks -3%, Panels -3.5% YoY due to aggressive competitor pricing and sluggish demand
items.quote: In Blocks, the price realization dropped by about 3%, for Panels by about 3.5%, in Putty by nearly 6%, in P ipes and Fittings by about 12%, and in Parador by about 5.7

items.statement: Q2 demand expected moderate in India with pricing challenges continuing; bounce back from September driven by government infrastructure and housing spend
items.quote: Looking ahead in Quarter 2, we expect the demand scenario to be moderate in India and challenges on pricing to continue. However, we expect a bounce back from September onwards driven by government spends on infrastructure and housing.

items.statement: B2G/JJM pipe sales at only 30% of normal in Q1 due to elections; budget allocation up ~50% to Rs 75,000 crore; expect normal service from September
items.quote: Overall, what we estimate is, and Ajay, you can help me, I think from steady state, the revenue was only about 30% of normal. So, the erosion was to the extent of 70%.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted ~5% away from Roofing strategically; Pipes & Fittings crossed Rs 150 cr quarterly revenue for first time (78% YoY growth); Construction Chemicals grew 35% YoY
items.quote: Significantly, in this quarter, we at HIL have made a nearly 5% swing away from Roofing in our overall revenue mix. It's a metric that we had highlighted we want to strategically shift.

items.statement: PVC price declining trend since July creates headwind for Pipes & Fittings in Q2; Parador faces transient product/channel mix pressure and one-time wage provision impacting Q1 EBITDA
items.quote: However, we need to watch out for headwinds being created by the declining trend in PVC prices since July.

items.statement: Parador EBITDA positive guidance for FY25 maintained; contribution margin +370 bps, EBITDA margin +170 bps YoY despite strategic investments in teams and marketing
items.quote: At the EBITDA level, there is also an i mprovement of nearly 170 basis points. The delta that you see is essentially because we are investing in the teams

items.statement: Blocks business targets 500-600 bps margin improvement via material cost (increasing pond ash), conversion cost and logistics; already delivered 220 bps contribution margin gain in Q1
items.quote: Having said that, in our blocks business, we believe there is an opportunity for us to improve the marg ins by nearly 500 to 600 basis points

items.statement: FY25 production target of 20 lakh tons plus, representing 14-15% growth over FY24
items.quote: This year we are targeting a growth of around 14%-15% over the last year.

items.statement: FY30 production target of 3.5 million tons, increasing market share from 20-21% to 32%
items.quote: By the year 2030 when country is requiring around 11 billion tons of manganese ore, we have targeted that we would be contributing to the tune of 32% of requirement of country which is right now around 20%-21%.

items.statement: FY25 capex target of INR 328 crores, FY26 capex target of INR 340 crores
items.quote: For last 2 years, capex is, or maybe 3 years, capex is more than our profit after tax. And even this year we have planned INR 328 crores, next year INR 340 crores.

items.statement: Capex of INR 316 crore in FY24, exceeding profit after tax
items.quote: Capex, that is capital expenditure of INR316 crore was done, which is more than profit after tax of the year.

items.statement: Environmental clearance of 24.88 lakh tons as of April 2024, targeting 10 lakh tons additional EC applications in FY25 and 10-15 lakh tons in FY26
items.quote: Look, the beginning of this year that is 1st of April 2024, we had an EC of nearly 24.88 lakh tons. And for this year, financial year 2024-2025, we have planned to apply for nearly 10 lakh tons.

items.statement: Targeting 6-7% year-on-year reduction in production cost per ton through volume growth with same manpower
items.quote: Exactly, you cannot say target, but definitely as we are targeting a growth of around 14%, 15% every year, so you can presume that reduction in cost by 6%, 7% every, on year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 blended realisation growth of 13-14% despite 30% announced price hikes due to grade mix
items.quote: No, what you see, I mean, it is just one or two grades. But we have a lot many grades, so it is a mix of that. Which grade is having how much demand and how much could be dispatched.

items.statement: Q2 prices likely to continue at current levels, Q3 onwards prices will decline following regular seasonal pattern
items.quote: Prices what we have today, I mean in this Q2, I think most likely they will continue. But Q3 onwards, prices will go. And this is a regular pattern over years.

items.statement: India's manganese ore consumption expected to exceed 11 million tons by 2030 per National Steel Policy
items.quote: By 2030, it is envisaged to exceed 11 mi llion tons as per National Steel Policy

items.statement: Gujarat JV with GMDC identified 9.51 million tons of manganese ore resources, potential 2 lakh tons production starting FY26
items.quote: In Gujarat, I can share that we have explored, and we have identified about 9.51 million tons of manganese ore. Now based on the joint venture signing and then getting clearances perhaps the starting year we can say another 2 lakh tons, maybe next year there is '25-'26 but potential is 9.5

items.statement: No major impact from Supreme Court ruling on state mining taxes; no liability from Maharashtra or Madhya Pradesh state governments
items.quote: As far as the Sup reme Court decision is concerned, it is about the power of the states. The royalties are taxed or not. Royalty is not a tax. And if the state governments are imposing certain taxes, those taxes have to be paid since 2005, in the next 12 years. So, in case of MOIL, there are no taxes with respect to state governments. So, there is no liability from the state government

items.statement: Employee cost reset expected around 2027 due to pay scale revision
items.quote: That will be around 2027 or so.

items.statement: Exploration target of 1 lakh metres for FY25, added 7.98 million tons resources in FY24
items.quote: We are targeting aroun d 1 lakh metres to be explored and further we will add to our reserves and resources in the current financial year

items.statement: Targeting environmental clearance for 5 million tons by 2030 to support 3.5 million tons production
items.quote: By 2030, we are targeting environmental clearance for 5 million tons or 50 lakh tons, so that we can achieve our envisaged target of 3.5 million tons.

items.statement: Five new shafts planned across mines to support production growth
items.quote: So we have, and if you understand the language of mining engineers, that is number of shafts to be added. So it is under process, but we have decided on 5 shafts to be installed in different mines.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve from Q2 and surpass FY24 levels for full FY25
items.quote: it is expected that now from Q2, the margins will increase and it will surpass on Y-o-Y basis for FY25, the margin will surpass FY24.

items.statement: Order book of more than 50 MW captive projects, majority to be executed in FY25
items.quote: On the EP C front, we have very healthy order book for more than 50 megawatt of captive projects

items.statement: Evaluating investment opportunities in IPP segment including PM Kusum and C&I group captive projects
items.quote: We are looking for the investment opportunities as we have entered the IPP segment. We are evaluating the opportunities as and when like PM Kusum is one of the promising opportunity for investment.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of INR30 crore equity for INR150 crore PM Kusum IPP project with UGVCL PPA
items.quote: The purpose for going for QIP is to get an equity for investing into PM KUSUM projects where we have one project worth 26.56 megawatt and then the PPA with UGVCL. items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 5.58% vs 7.72% YoY due to salary, interest costs and high working capital orders
items.quote: Though the EBITDA margin contracted to 5.58 compared to 7.72 in Q1 FY24 due to investment in growth initiatives

items.statement: Solar panel prices stabilized in Q1 FY25 after volatility in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Q1 FY25 is steady. The prices of solar panel are steady and the volume is normally we are into capex.

items.statement: Solar sector growing at breakneck pace; PM Surya Ghar Yojana and state policies driving demand
items.quote: the solar energy sector is growing at a very breakneck pace. And the deployment of solar power in the country is rising exponentially.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 30% residential rooftop, 70% C&I, government and distribution business
items.quote: our rooftop, residential rooftop is around 30% of our revenue. And our commercial and industrial segment with government business and distribution business is contributing balance 70%.

items.statement: Informatics rating withdrawn after SEBI/RBI intervention; company did not engage for debt rating
items.quote: Ultimately, we complained to SEBI and RBI and after intervention for RBI and SEBI, Informatics has dropped our rating.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 90-100 days; working capital facility ~INR50 crore at 9.35% avg interest
items.quote: Current working capital cycle is roughly 90 to 100 days. Depending on the project, it may vary. But average current working capital cycle is around 90 to 100 days.

items.statement: Promoter stake ~72.8% pre-QIP, expected to marginally reduce to ~71.5-72% post-QIP
items.quote: before QIP, promoter stake was approximately 72.8%. With QIP, it will, I have not exact numbers, but it will marginally reduce to around 71.5% or 72%.

items.statement: Lucknow office operational for 4 months; Pune office to start within 1-2 months
items.quote: Lucknow office is operational and it is operational since last four months. And we are slowly and gradually gaining good orders from Lucknow office. Pune office is under process and soon it will be within a month or two, it will start operating

items.statement: FY25 revenue target INR305 crore (INR80 crore India, INR220 crore UAE)
items.quote: Revenue for '24-'25 yearly is INR80 crores for India operation and INR220 crores for UAE operation.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue expected INR63-65 crore
items.quote: And next quarter, this is the current quarter, Q2, we are expecting around INR63 crores to INR65 crores.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue expected around INR70-80 crore
items.quote: So, third quarter will be, we are expecting around, 75 to 80 Cr. Around 70 Cr.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target INR400 crore with same capacity
items.quote: And the next year, we are targeting around INR400 crores turnover with the same capacity.

items.statement: UAE plant to reach 100% capacity utilization in FY25-26
items.quote: In FY25 -26, we will be able to capture 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Total UAE capex invested INR105 crore including acquisition and working capital
items.quote: Total capex what we had invested in UAE is around INR105 crores, which includes the acquisition cost and the working capital together.

items.statement: Maintenance capex budgeted at 1.5-2% of turnover annually
items.quote: And maintenance is our, around 1.5% to 2% of the turnover, which we budget every year.

items.statement: Two acquisition proposals under discussion in India, may conclude this quarter
items.quote: Right now, there is no such expansion as we are filling our capacity. But definitely, once the demand will grow and the market size enlarge and we have a targeted turnover and targeted EBITDA naturally, we will expand.

items.statement: UAE order book ~40 million AED (75% UAE, 25% GCC/Africa); India confirmed project order book INR25 crore deliverable in 5-6 months
items.quote: The order book of UAE is around 40 million AED. And in India, it is like always month -on-month, the order book is there. But particularly for India, the project which we confirmed for supply of the glass and to be manufactured, there is around INR25 crores as on today.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 15-16% for FY25; UAE already at 15% EBITDA; India Q1 at 13.81% due to strike impact
items.quote: UAE market, we are already at 15 % EBITDA as on date also. India this quarter, as I said that because of that production loss, the margin were dipped by around 2% on EBITDA level. But average EBITDA is around 13.81 %, which is close to 14 %.

items.statement: Peak capacity EBITDA margin potential 17-19% (2-3% above current target)
items.quote: Right now, this year we are targeting around 15 % to 16% EBITDA. And maybe at the full potential, we can increase more by 2% to 3%.

items.statement: Selling price pressure from semi-organized competition; brand commands slight premium
items.quote: And because of this competitive environment, there is always a little bit of the selling price pressure. And we have also certain semi -organized competitions, where always there is a pressure on the pricing, though with our respectable brand, we have little bit of margin over competition.

items.statement: Architectural glass industry growing 35% CAGR driven by mandatory conversion from float glass and infrastructure growth
items.quote: Glass industry, the architectural glass is growing by 35% and the float glass industry is growing by around 12% to 15% compounding.

items.statement: Bulletproof glass sample under testing; UAE test certificate expected October, European certification by December; designer glass, ceramic frit to add margin
items.quote: Bulletproof glass, we already have a sample manufactured at our UAE plant and the same is under testing. So, we will be getting a local test certificate first in the first phase around in October. Then after we will further go for an European standard certification which generally takes three months.

items.statement: Key risk: real estate slowdown in India/UAE as 90% sales from architectural glass for commercial/residential buildings
items.quote: One key risk, if the economy of India and UAE can reduce, if the real estate can have the impact. Because our majority sale is coming around 90% from the real estate, architectural glasses for the commercial building, residential building.

items.statement: Acquisitions to be funded via debt-equity mix; will not increase interest burden significantly
items.quote: the debt and equity ratio we are expecting? Management: It's like again, once, we freeze on the valuation, then how the valuation payment structure are made, then we will decide. But yes, we will not, go more on the interest burden

items.statement: H2 FY25 expected to be 20-25% higher than H1 FY25; full-year FY25 growth will be below the previously budgeted 37%
items.quote: H1, which will close in September, we believe that H2 should be at least 20 or 25% higher than the H1, what we will close.

items.statement: Capex budget for FY25 under review and may be reduced from planned levels
items.quote: we are contemplating right now, we are doing each and every monitoring of the Capex which we have planned for this year and we may come with the reduction in our budgeted Capex plan for FY24-25

items.statement: European customers deferred orders due to high dealer inventory, US interest rates, and EV transition uncertainty; recovery expected post-August holidays
items.quote: are witnessing that there has been sudden reduction in customer orders because there has been huge inventory at dealer site and this most of the inventory reduction, I won't name the customers but most of our customers who have huge operations in the United States because of course the plants might be in Europe but they're higher customer base is

items.statement: EV demand volatility causing order cancellations and delays; customers lack new ICE/hybrid platforms after focusing on EV; US election and interest rate uncertainty
items.quote: consumers are not sure maybe should they go for hybrid, should they go for any other, the hydrogen is also being talked, so that is where I believe some of our projects did not pick up for which we have invested recently.

items.statement: RACL will still grow but at a reduced pace compared to past 35-30% growth
items.quote: RACL will still grow, but maybe not at the same pace where we were growing past three years and you know, pace of growth may change for growth will happen.

items.statement: Second half should be 10-20% better than first half
items.quote: I think the second-half should be ten 20% better than that.

items.statement: Revisiting and likely deferring non-critical capex; revised budget targeted by AGM
items.quote: We are in process of revisiting that CapEx budget. Since the as we have explained that European players are now opening up from the holidays, we are targeting to put up the revised CapEx budget contemplating to revive put up the revised CapEx budget by the AGM which we are planning next.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduction target for FY25; repayments exceed new borrowings
items.quote: Our target is that every year our repayments would be, yeah more than the more than the additional debt So that is also that those plans are already in place.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 22% currently; aspiration 20-23% maintained despite domestic mix
items.quote: If we are having 25% of EBIDTA even now we had a EBIDTA margin of 22%. It's not that we have. Gone upside down, we our beta margins are gone 3% if you see better in industry in India every time margin or not even 15%.

items.statement: European customers on holiday in July-August; real demand picture expected in 2-3 weeks after they return
items.quote: Eventually next two weeks will really give us a clear picture. Which way that the remaining months of the year have to go?

items.statement: Some customers cancelled/deferred orders due to inventory correction; one customer went from 4-month cancellation to restarting at reduced volume next month
items.quote: They said cancelling all orders for next four months and that is the kind of hustle we immediate. I mean the worry we immediately had. But then we went there, we understood the issue. They said there has been inventory correction.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility (military order hold, Red Sea crisis) causing demand volatility and inventory pile-up
items.quote: Suddenly these geopolitical things are really troubling. A lot of volatility. But I personally feel as vacation time is over, people are coming back, then they will be giving us a real stable demand for next one year at least.

items.statement: Domestic business growing with new substantial order (same product as European customer) and FCC India mass production started; margins between export and typical domestic
items.quote: This business is not very low margin business. This is actually a product which we are already producing for overseas, European customer, same product almost is going to adopted in the Indian motorcycle.

items.statement: ZF India sourcing plan intact despite short-term correction; China+1 and Europe FTA tailwinds expected
items.quote: India still remains their favourite country for sourcing. They have a big office, they're expanding their team and all that.

items.statement: May raise funds (preference shares/QIP) at right time for strategic decisions; not immediate
items.quote: These are all strategic surprise. Thanks for your message. But definitely these are our strategic decisions and yes, at the right time, the right decision will be on a take.

items.statement: Capacity utilisation currently 65-70%; peak 80-85% with given weeks
items.quote: In general we are right now operating with of course the reduced volumes we have around 65 to 70%.

items.statement: Solar captive power started July 20; expected saving ~1 crore annually on 1.4 crore equity investment
items.quote: I think its 1 Crore, because this this year we started only in July. We are 20th July, our captive power offsite generation started. So this year it will be lesser, but otherwise one crore will be the actual saving minimum at least.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 25% to 30% for FY25
items.quote: Despite a little slower in Q1, we are confident of achieving revenue growth in the range of 25% to 30% for FY '25.

items.statement: Order inflow target of INR11,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: On the order book side, we have set a target of INR11,000 crores for the financial year 24- 25.

items.statement: Order backlog of INR57,793 crores as of 12th August 2024
items.quote: The order backlog as of 12th August '24 is around INR57,793 crores.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book excluding 2 MDOs stands at INR18,115 crores
items.quote: If we exclude the 2 MDOs, the unexecuted order book stands at INR18,115 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 12.1% in Q1 FY25 from 12% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin has gone up from 12% in Q1 FY '24 to 12.1% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: MDO margins expected to improve after FY26-27, currently around 15% to 16%
items.quote: Until that time, it will be around 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Tracking INR75,000 crores of opportunities with hardcore opportunities of INR20,000-25,000 crores
items.quote: We are tracking about INR75,000 crores of opportunities and there are hardcore opportunities of nearly INR20,000 crores, INR25,000 crores.

items.statement: O&M revenue grew 52% YoY to INR341 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: O&M revenue of INR341 crores against INR224 crores in corresponding period last year, a registered growth of 52%.

items.statement: Civil business revenue grew 13% YoY to INR557 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Civil business, including railway, mining, water distribution contributed INR557 crores against INR493 crores in Q1 FY '24, an increase of 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: KBP MDO expected to break ground by end of September or beginning of October
items.quote: By end of September, beginning of October is when we expect to break ground, start the overburden activity.

items.statement: Supreme Court mine tax judgment will not impact MDO offtake due to contract clauses
items.quote: This is not going to impact the offtake at all. If it's going to impact the offtake, there are clauses that protect the offtake, as per the contract agreement.

items.statement: Overseas O&M revenue increased 27% YoY in Q1, expected to continue for 4-5 years
items.quote: Overseas O&M has increased compared to last year Q1 to this year's Q1, overseas O&M has increased by close to 27%. Revenue in this trend is expected to continue for the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to normalize to 26%-27% in FY25
items.quote: We are on 26% to 27% for this year.

items.statement: Secured orders worth INR1,746 crores so far in FY25
